# Phase 22 — Public Missionary & Project Pages: Primary Research Evidence

- **Evidence status:** complete supporting research for the implementation-ready
  specification; not implementation, certification, deployment, or production
  evidence
- **External-source access date:** 2026-08-03
- **Authority posture:** informative evidence only; ratified Phase 22 decisions,
  the checked-in [Phase 22 PRD](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages.md), active
  [`add-public-ministry-pages` OpenSpec deltas](../../../openspec/changes/add-public-ministry-pages/proposal.md),
  and ADRs carry product and architecture authority under the repository
  hierarchy
- **Specification status:** `/to-spec` and `/to-tickets` were completed after
  the D1–D27 closure. The PRD/OpenSpec package is implementation-ready planning,
  and parent specification issue
  [#1281](https://github.com/Asymmetric-al/core/issues/1281) owns 41 approved
  native child issues, #1282–#1322, with 116 native blocking relationships.
  P22-01/#1282 alone among the 41 implementation children is the current
  `ready-for-agent` frontier; Phase 22 remains unimplemented, undeployed, and
  not live
- **Scope:** public missionary and project page ownership, couples and teams,
  organization control, participant editing and review, donor-designation
  handoff, support-progress semantics, restricted-worker safety, public media,
  page lifecycle, retirement, search behavior, caching, accessibility, and
  implementation-adjacent Payload and Next.js constraints

## How to use this evidence

This appendix records a focused review of current mission-organization public
giving experiences, nonprofit fundraising products, CMS workflow products,
and official platform, search, accessibility, and security guidance. It uses
three labels:

- **DOCUMENTED** means the linked first-party or standards-body source directly
  states or visibly exposes the fact.
- **OBSERVED** means a current first-party public page demonstrates the behavior,
  but does not prove the vendor's hidden data model or internal authorization
  architecture.
- **INFERRED** means a proposed Phase 22 implication derived from the documented
  evidence and the phase boundaries. It is not a claim that a source mandates
  Asym's exact design.
- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY** means the inspected source does not establish the answer,
  the behavior may be tenant- or plan-dependent, or it must be proved against
  Asym's pinned runtime before release.

Comparator products are design evidence only. They do not authorize copying a
marketing-platform progress formula, page-level privacy toggle, broad CMS role,
or arbitrary workflow engine into Asym. Publicly visible behavior also cannot
prove backend ownership, tenancy, data isolation, or legal sufficiency.

Where historical research below uses `D17/D19 subject` as shorthand, the
controlling PRD means D17's exact source-qualified Page Subject Binding to a
Phase-9-owned Ministry Assignment or other eligible source. D19 owns separation
and orchestration semantics only; participant association, D1 display and Page
contribution, Phase 12 support access, Phase 21 support binding, and
notifications remain independently authoritative.

## Executive findings

1. **OBSERVED:** Mission organizations commonly present workers, projects, and
   organization-wide funds as different giving subjects. ABWE separates
   “Support a Worker,” “Support a Field Project,” and its Global Gospel Fund;
   TEAM asks donors to choose a worker, project, or TEAM generally.
   [ABWE Give](https://abwe.org/give/),
   [TEAM Give](https://give.team.org/campaign/give-now/c321842)
2. **DOCUMENTED:** Reliant says a missionary couple is supported “as a family”
   through the ministry fund the family is responsible for. **OBSERVED:** CTEN
   publishes couple pages. One public page therefore cannot safely be modeled
   as one person, one login, or one Party row.
   [Reliant Help](https://reliant.org/help),
   [CTEN Robert and Jenny Wheelis](https://www.cten.org/us-canada-missionaries/robert-and-jenny-wheelis),
   [CTEN Pedro and Ana](https://www.cten.org/guatemala-missionaries/pedro-and-ana)
3. **DOCUMENTED:** Raisely explicitly models fundraiser profiles as Individual,
   Team, or Organization profiles under one campaign template. Givebutter,
   Bloomerang, GoFundMe Pro, Blackbaud TeamRaiser, and CiviCRM all separate some
   participant customization from organization-admin control. This is strong
   evidence for a tenant-owned page with bounded participant proposals, not a
   participant-owned microsite.
   [Raisely fundraiser profiles](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649205175565-Understanding-Fundraiser-Profiles),
   [Givebutter team fundraising](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1749223-how-to-use-team-fundraising),
   [Bloomerang campaign builder pages](https://help.bloomerang.com/en/articles/13382504-peer-to-peer-campaign-builder-pages),
   [GoFundMe Pro classic peer-to-peer campaigns](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288738226587-Create-a-Classic-peer-to-peer-campaign),
   [Blackbaud personal-page administration](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_participants_personalpages.html),
   [CiviCRM personal campaign pages](https://beta.docs.civicrm.org/user/contributions/personal-campaign-pages/)
4. **DOCUMENTED:** Pioneers intentionally omits missionary names and project
   numbers from its website for safety. Reliant documents a secure-location
   case in which a person is not searchable and donors use a direct link. CTEN
   documents that a public bio URL can use an alias. These are distinct
   patterns—directory suppression, direct-link discovery, and public aliasing—
   and none proves that an unlisted URL is confidential.
   [Pioneers Giving Help](https://pioneers.org/give/givinghelp),
   [Reliant secure-location instructions](https://solomon.reliant.org/display/international/Support%2BRaising%2BInstructions%2Bfor%2BInternational%2BInterns),
   [CTEN USA Orientation Journal](https://www.cten.org/s/CTEN-USA-Orientation-Journal.pdf)
5. **DOCUMENTED:** Google says `noindex` controls search indexing only when a
   crawler can access the page; it is not a confidentiality control. Google
   recommends protecting confidential content with authentication. Phase 22
   must not label “unlisted,” an opaque slug, or `noindex` as private.
   [Google: control what you share](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/control-what-you-share),
   [Google: block indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing)
6. **DOCUMENTED:** Fundraising-platform progress definitions vary. Givebutter's
   campaign goal can count donations, tickets, offline/imported gifts, and paid
   auction bids and has no recurring/monthly-goal model. GoFundMe Pro documents
   legacy gross-donation progress behavior. Raisely exposes original,
   converted, gross, total, and net amounts as different reporting facts. A
   generic platform-style thermometer is not sufficient evidence for a
   missionary's monthly-support progress.
   [Givebutter campaign goals](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1761125-how-to-update-a-campaign-goal),
   [GoFundMe Pro progress metrics](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288737740187-Progress-metrics),
   [Raisely donation report guide](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/45346145513613-Report-Guide-Donations)
7. **DOCUMENTED:** Raisely allows offline donations to be attributed to a
   campaign or profile and included in totals. This supports including
   source-qualified offline truth when the owning phase permits it, but does not
   establish which Asym support metric, posting state, refund state, or currency
   treatment is correct.
   [Raisely manual and bulk offline donations](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649167360013-Adding-Offline-Donations-Manually-or-in-Bulk)
8. **DOCUMENTED:** Payload supports drafts, versions, autosave, relationships,
   and field access control. Its Local API skips access control by default unless
   a caller supplies a user and sets `overrideAccess: false`. Payload is a useful
   editorial substrate, but it is not by itself the Phase 10 safety boundary or
   Phase 22 publication authority.
   [Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts),
   [Payload versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview),
   [Payload relationship fields](https://payloadcms.com/docs/fields/relationship),
   [Payload field access](https://payloadcms.com/docs/access-control/fields),
   [Payload Local API access control](https://payloadcms.com/docs/local-api/access-control)
9. **DOCUMENTED:** Next.js `revalidateTag(tag, "max")` uses stale-while-
   revalidate, while `updateTag` immediately expires tagged data and is limited
   to Server Actions. Next.js also warns that CDN caching can continue serving
   stale content unless the CDN is purged. Safety revocation, page retirement,
   and CTA shutdown therefore need a hard invalidation and request-time safety
   gate; ordinary story refresh may use stale-while-revalidate.
   [Next.js revalidateTag](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag),
   [Next.js updateTag](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag),
   [Next.js CDN caching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/cdn-caching)
10. **DOCUMENTED:** WAI-ARIA defines a meter as a scalar measurement within a
    known range. WCAG 2.2 requires usable status communication, labels,
    non-color-only cues, and adequate target sizes. A public support amount or
    percent should have visible language and an accessible value such as “73%
    of monthly support goal, through 31 July 2026,” not only a colored bar.
    [WAI-ARIA meter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/meter/),
    [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/),
    [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages),
    [WCAG use of color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color),
    [WCAG target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum)
11. **DOCUMENTED:** Search engines distinguish a true permanent successor from
    missing content. Google recommends permanent redirects for genuine moves
    and 404/410 behavior for nonexistent content. Next.js provides a 308
    `permanentRedirect` and makes `notFound` responses non-indexable. Retirement
    cannot be one universal redirect-to-general-giving rule.
    [Google permanent redirects](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects),
    [Google soft-404 guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors),
    [Next.js permanentRedirect](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/permanentRedirect),
    [Next.js notFound](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found)
12. **INFERRED:** The highest-leverage first Phase 22 decision is the page's
    ownership and subject model. It determines how couples, teams, projects,
    editors, public identity, progress, checkout, privacy, and retirement fit
    without conflating them.

## 1. Mission-organization evidence

### 1.1 ABWE: worker, project, and organization giving are different subjects

- **OBSERVED:** ABWE presents separate routes for worker support, field-project
  support, and its organization-wide Global Gospel Fund. Its project pages pair
  presentation content with an explicit “Add to Basket” or “Give Now” action.
  [ABWE Give](https://abwe.org/give/),
  [ABWE Global Gospel Fund](https://give.abwe.org/projects/global-gospel-fund)
- **DOCUMENTED:** ABWE's giving instructions preserve a specific missionary or
  project selection through the giving process.
  [ABWE Donation Giving Process](https://abwe.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/ABWE-Donation-Giving-Process-July-2023.pdf)
- **INFERRED:** Phase 22 should use an explicit typed public subject and an
  explicit designation/checkout binding. It should not infer the financial
  destination from a page title, person relation, slug, or CMS folder.
- **LIMIT:** ABWE's public pages do not reveal its backend ownership, review,
  tenancy, or authorization model.

### 1.2 TEAM: giving subject and currency/legal context are visible choices

- **OBSERVED:** TEAM asks donors to select a worker, project, or TEAM generally,
  and separates worker-giving options by US dollars and Canadian dollars.
  [TEAM Give](https://give.team.org/campaign/give-now/c321842)
- **INFERRED:** Public presentation and checkout destination need exact site,
  legal-entity, locale, and currency context. “The same person” is not enough to
  infer one universal giving destination.
- **LIMIT:** The public flow does not establish whether TEAM stores one page per
  worker, household, fund, or legal entity internally.

### 1.3 Reliant: family funds, secure-location discovery, and bounded retirement

- **DOCUMENTED:** Reliant says donors search for a missionary and use Give Now,
  and explains that a missionary couple is supported as a family through the
  ministry fund that family is responsible for.
  [Reliant Giving Support](https://reliant.org/help/giving-support),
  [Reliant Help](https://reliant.org/help)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Reliant's secure-location instructions say a person may not be
  searchable and donors then use a direct link.
  [Reliant secure-location instructions](https://solomon.reliant.org/display/international/Support%2BRaising%2BInstructions%2Bfor%2BInternational%2BInterns)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Reliant's retiree program requires updating page title and bio
  to “Retiree,” provides donor-transition wording, permits continued gifts only
  within a bounded retiree program, and ends under stated conditions. Its exit
  prayer-letter guidance says recurring gifts may automatically stop after a
  specified date if the donor does not contact Reliant.
  [Reliant Post Employment Retiree Program](https://solomon.reliant.org/display/public/fieldbenefits/Post%2BEmployment%2BRetiree%2BProgram),
  [Reliant exit prayer-letter sample](https://solomon.reliant.org/display/public/employman/Exit%2BPrayer%2BLetter%2BSample%2BWording)
- **INFERRED:** A public page may represent a support household rather than one
  login. Retirement needs a bounded state and purpose-aware outcome. Existing
  recurring commitments remain independently owned; Phase 22 must not silently
  redirect or redesignate them.

### 1.4 Pioneers: directory suppression is deliberate safety behavior

- **DOCUMENTED:** Pioneers says missionary names and project numbers are
  intentionally not shown on its website for safety and explains that gifts
  remain under Pioneers' jurisdiction and control.
  [Pioneers Giving Help](https://pioneers.org/give/givinghelp)
- **INFERRED:** Search-directory membership and page publication are separate
  capabilities. Phase 10 must determine what public projection, if any, is safe;
  Phase 22 cannot downgrade a restricted worker merely because an editor knows a
  URL.

### 1.5 CTEN: couple pages, aliases, and distinct checkout rails

- **OBSERVED:** CTEN publishes public pages for couples as one presentation
  subject.
  [Robert and Jenny Wheelis](https://www.cten.org/us-canada-missionaries/robert-and-jenny-wheelis),
  [Pedro and Ana](https://www.cten.org/guatemala-missionaries/pedro-and-ana)
- **DOCUMENTED:** CTEN's orientation material says a public bio URL may use a
  first-and-last name or an alias and describes a Donate USA handoff to an
  external giving system. Its US and Canadian materials expose country-specific
  giving contexts.
  [CTEN USA Orientation Journal](https://www.cten.org/s/CTEN-USA-Orientation-Journal.pdf),
  [CTEN Canada Digital Orientation Journal](https://www.cten.org/s/Canada-Digital-Orientation-Journal-092023-jl-Website.pdf)
- **INFERRED:** Slug identity, public display participants, editors, and
  checkout destination must be separate records. An alias slug is a publication
  fact, not a Party identifier or an authorization credential.

## 2. Fundraising and CRM comparator evidence

### 2.1 Raisely: typed profiles under organization-controlled templates

- **DOCUMENTED:** Raisely fundraiser profiles can be Individual, Team, or
  Organization profiles. A campaign has a dynamic profile template; admins can
  view, edit, create, and archive profiles. Archived profiles are removed from
  campaign totals and public view.
  [Raisely fundraiser profiles](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649205175565-Understanding-Fundraiser-Profiles)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Manual or bulk offline donations can be attributed to a
  campaign or profile and included in totals. Raisely's reporting separately
  exposes original amount, campaign-converted amount, gross, total, net,
  status, source, and live/test mode.
  [Raisely offline donations](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649167360013-Adding-Offline-Donations-Manually-or-in-Bulk),
  [Raisely donation reports](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/45346145513613-Report-Guide-Donations)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Raisely's donation form can show campaign preview, funding
  progress, and recurring upsell; Stripe or PayPal remains the payment holder
  and settlement provider.
  [Raisely donation-form basics](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649206420365-Donation-Form-The-Basics),
  [Raisely payment setup](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649206846861-Setting-Up-Payments-The-Basics)
- **INFERRED:** A page template can be organization-controlled while profile
  facts vary by subject. Presentation attribution and payment truth stay
  separate. Raisely's campaign math is comparator behavior, not Asym's support
  definition.

### 2.2 Givebutter: contributor customization is not account authority

- **DOCUMENTED:** Givebutter distinguishes campaign team members from account
  admins. Team-member/custom links can attribute donations, and donors may give
  credit to a member.
  [Givebutter invite team members](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1813233-how-to-invite-team-members-to-join-a-campaign)
- **DOCUMENTED:** A member can edit bounded page facts such as display name,
  personal goal, and story. Only account admins can change team-level name,
  goal, logo, and deletion. Removing a member does not delete their login or
  the campaign's transactions; attribution can be unassigned or reassigned.
  [Givebutter member pages](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3270211-how-to-manage-your-team-member-page),
  [Givebutter team fundraising](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1749223-how-to-use-team-fundraising),
  [Givebutter Page campaigns](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3688273-how-to-configure-a-page-campaign)
- **DOCUMENTED:** A Givebutter goal is optional, appears only when configured,
  does not affect payouts, and can count multiple campaign activity types. It
  does not provide a recurring monthly goal.
  [Givebutter campaign goals](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1761125-how-to-update-a-campaign-goal)
- **INFERRED:** Public display membership, editing rights, donation attribution,
  and financial ownership are distinct. Deleting or removing a participant must
  never erase gifts or rewrite authoritative attribution.

### 2.3 GoFundMe Pro: bounded fundraiser edits under shared donation settings

- **DOCUMENTED:** GoFundMe Pro supports campaign, team, and fundraiser pages.
  Supporters can customize bounded fields, while organization-level donation
  page settings are shared and not editable by supporters. Admins can prevent
  supporters from changing headline or goal and can hide progress or comments.
  [Create a Classic peer-to-peer campaign](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288738226587-Create-a-Classic-peer-to-peer-campaign)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Its account manager lists fundraiser pages and teams created
  for the organization. A team captain can edit the team page.
  [GoFundMe Pro account manager](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288772410779-Intro-to-your-account),
  [Edit a team fundraising page](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288801799451-Edit-a-team-fundraising-page)
- **DOCUMENTED:** GoFundMe Pro documents progress behavior that may use gross
  donation amount and allows organizations to hide progress.
  [GoFundMe Pro progress metrics](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288737740187-Progress-metrics)
- **INFERRED:** Asym should preserve contributor-friendly editing without giving
  contributors authority over designation, safety tier, legal entity, public
  progress formula, or checkout controls.

### 2.4 Blackbaud TeamRaiser: approve participant-authored pages centrally

- **DOCUMENTED:** TeamRaiser lets administrators view, edit, approve, reject, or
  make participant personal pages private. It can require approval for new or
  modified pages; default content remains until approval.
  [TeamRaiser personal-page administration](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_participants_personalpages.html)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Event options can notify administrators, require page or
  modification approval, and control participant self-management, layout,
  styles, and status indicators. TeamRaiser distinguishes participant, team,
  company, and event pages.
  [TeamRaiser advanced event options](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_configuring_blueprints_03cselectingadvancedeventoptions.html),
  [TeamRaiser default pages](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_event_configuration_12bdefaultpages_understanding.html)
- **INFERRED:** “Missionary may propose changes; tenant publishes” is a proven
  workflow shape. Asym still needs immutable versions, scope-safe preview, and
  Phase 10 projection enforcement beyond these comparator controls.

### 2.5 Bloomerang: admin-controlled customization and separate lifecycle states

- **DOCUMENTED:** Bloomerang participants can have personal or team pages,
  goals, and thermometers, but nonprofit admins decide which elements they may
  edit and can reset content to the admin default. Team captains manage team
  page facts.
  [Bloomerang participant guide](https://help.bloomerang.com/en/articles/13382830-peer-to-peer-participant-user-guide),
  [Bloomerang campaign builder pages](https://help.bloomerang.com/en/articles/13382504-peer-to-peer-campaign-builder-pages)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Bloomerang distinguishes Active, Disabled (not visible), and
  Closed (visible but no registration or donation) campaigns.
  [Bloomerang campaign settings](https://help.bloomerang.com/en/articles/13382413-peer-to-peer-campaign-settings)
- **INFERRED:** Visibility and giving eligibility are different capabilities.
  Phase 22 should express them through a bounded lifecycle, not a collection of
  independent page-level booleans.

### 2.6 CiviCRM, Virtuous, Keela, and Salesforce

- **DOCUMENTED:** CiviCRM Personal Campaign Pages are linked to an existing
  contribution page or event. Administrators can require approval, notify
  reviewers, edit, disable, or reject pages, track totals, and enter offline
  gifts; participants edit bounded presentation facts.
  [CiviCRM Personal Campaign Pages](https://beta.docs.civicrm.org/user/contributions/personal-campaign-pages/),
  [CiviCRM contribution pages](https://docs.civicrm.org/user/en/latest/contributions/contribution-pages/)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Virtuous recommends distinct campaign segments for fundraiser
  or team attribution and documents mappings from external campaign, team, and
  fundraiser IDs into its campaign/communication/segment model.
  [Virtuous peer-to-peer fundraising](https://support.virtuous.org/hc/en-us/articles/29135845533325-How-Do-I-Manage-Peer-To-Peer-Fundraising),
  [Virtuous GoFundMe Pro mapping](https://support.virtuous.org/hc/en-us/article_attachments/37086251219597)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Keela provides distinct campaign and fundraiser experiences,
  but the inspected public documentation does not establish enough granular
  page-approval, safety, or ownership behavior to use it as a primary design
  authority.
  [Keela peer-to-peer campaign](https://support.keela.co/hc/en-us/articles/43096248800781-Create-a-Peer-to-Peer-Campaign),
  [Keela fundraiser account](https://support.keela.co/hc/en-us/articles/43096249746445-Navigating-your-Peer-to-Peer-Fundraiser-Account)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Salesforce CMS approval workflows distinguish author,
  reviewer, revision, and ready-to-publish stages, lock publication during
  review, and preserve version history. Nonprofit Cloud describes gift
  designations as funds or purposes.
  [Salesforce CMS basic approval](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=xcloud.cms_workflows_basic_approval.htm&language=en_US&type=5),
  [Salesforce CMS workflow enablement](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.cms_workflows_enable.htm&language=en_US&type=5),
  [Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud fundraising](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sfdo.NPC_FR_Nonprofit_Cloud_Fundraising.htm&language=en_US)
- **INFERRED:** External attribution IDs and CMS workflow states may inform
  integration and UX, but neither becomes Asym's public identity, designation,
  finance, or safety authority.

## 3. Implementation-adjacent primary evidence

### 3.1 Payload is an editorial substrate, not the public authorization boundary

- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload supports draft versions, autosave, and a `_status`
  distinction between draft and published content.
  [Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts),
  [Payload versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview),
  [Payload autosave](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/autosave)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Relationship fields and field access can restrict editorial
  relationships and individual fields.
  [Payload relationship fields](https://payloadcms.com/docs/fields/relationship),
  [Payload field access](https://payloadcms.com/docs/access-control/fields)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload Local API calls skip access control by default. To
  invoke access rules on behalf of a user, the caller must supply that user and
  set `overrideAccess: false`.
  [Payload Local API access control](https://payloadcms.com/docs/local-api/access-control),
  [Payload Local API overview](https://payloadcms.com/docs/local-api/overview)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload warns that long-running work in hooks should be moved
  to jobs and that read hooks can add cost to every read.
  [Payload hooks](https://payloadcms.com/docs/hooks/overview)
- **INFERRED:** Payload drafts and versions can store approved narrative and
  assets, but Phase 22 needs an Asym domain projection that joins only approved
  Phase 10 fields, exact public-page version, approved progress projection, and
  active CTA binding. Public routes, metadata, sitemap, OG generation, preview,
  and search must all read that same safe projection.
- **INFERRED:** Missionaries should use a purpose-built workspace editor rather
  than broad Payload Admin access. Any server-side Payload Local API call on
  behalf of a tenant participant must explicitly enforce access or use a
  narrower domain service with independently checked authorization.

### 3.2 Next.js cache and metadata are part of the public disclosure surface

- **DOCUMENTED:** Next.js supports static and generated metadata and Open Graph
  images.
  [Next.js metadata and OG images](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images)
- **DOCUMENTED:** `revalidateTag(tag, "max")` uses stale-while-revalidate;
  `updateTag` immediately expires data and is available only from Server
  Actions. Downstream CDNs may continue to serve stale content unless purged.
  [Next.js revalidateTag](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag),
  [Next.js updateTag](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag),
  [Next.js CDN caching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/cdn-caching)
- **INFERRED:** Normal narrative updates may use ordinary cache refresh. A
  restricted-worker escalation, publication revocation, page retirement,
  designation disablement, or CTA quarantine must use immediate invalidation,
  purge any external cache, and fail closed through a request-time safety and
  destination check. Old HTML, RSC payloads, JSON endpoints, metadata, OG
  images, sitemap entries, alternate locales, and image derivatives are all
  disclosure surfaces.

### 3.3 Search and retirement

- **DOCUMENTED:** Google treats permanent redirects as a strong canonical
  signal for a genuine replacement. It recommends 404 or 410 for content that
  no longer exists and identifies unrelated redirect targets as a source of
  soft-404 behavior.
  [Google permanent redirects](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects),
  [Google soft-404 guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors)
- **DOCUMENTED:** `noindex` is an indexing instruction, not access control;
  confidential content should be protected from unauthenticated access.
  [Google noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing),
  [Google control what you share](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/control-what-you-share)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Next.js `permanentRedirect` returns 308 outside Server Actions,
  and `notFound` injects a robots `noindex` marker for the segment.
  [Next.js permanentRedirect](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/permanentRedirect),
  [Next.js notFound](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/not-found)
- **RATIFIED BY D8:** Retirement needs an exact, audited outcome: `308` only to
  an eligible new canonical route for the same immutable Listed-public Page;
  the same real privacy-safe `404` plus `noindex` for every unknown or tombstoned
  route; or a substantive Transition Notice Release whose current Giving state
  remains D7/Phase 13-owned. A different successor presentation is a fresh
  explicit link, never an automatic redirect or inherited donor intent.

### 3.4 Uploads, images, and review links

- **DOCUMENTED:** OWASP recommends file-extension allowlists, MIME and signature
  validation, generated filenames, size limits, storage outside the web root or
  mediated access, malware scanning, and content disarm/reconstruction where
  applicable.
  [OWASP File Upload Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- **DOCUMENTED:** OWASP recommends deny-by-default authorization, least
  privilege, checking every request, relationship- or attribute-based access
  where appropriate, and authorization tests and logging. Opaque identifiers do
  not replace authorization.
  [OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html),
  [OWASP IDOR](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/insecure_direct_object_reference),
  [OWASP Top 10 2025 A01](https://owasp.org/Top10/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/)
- **DOCUMENTED:** For sensitive bearer links, OWASP's password-reset guidance
  recommends cryptographically random, securely stored, single-use, expiring
  tokens, HTTPS, trusted-host URL construction, and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
  [OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Forgot_Password_Cheat_Sheet.html)
- **INFERRED:** Public photo processing should quarantine originals, verify
  content and dimensions, decode and re-encode approved derivatives, remove
  metadata including EXIF/GPS, scan according to the accepted upload contract,
  generate non-revealing filenames, and never expose the original object. Image
  filenames, CDN keys, alt text, captions, metadata, and OG derivatives must all
  follow the Phase 10 public projection.
- **INFERRED:** An expiring review link is a bounded bearer capability, not a
  staff login. Bind it to Tenant, Legal Entity, site, page, exact draft version,
  permitted action, and expiration; make it revocable and read-only unless a
  separately authorized action is explicit. Restricted content may require
  authenticated review rather than a bearer link.

### 3.5 Accessibility and plain-language progress

- **DOCUMENTED:** WCAG 2.2 requires labels or instructions where user input is
  required, identification of errors, non-color-only communication, status
  messages available to assistive technology, and minimum target sizing under
  the applicable criterion.
  [WCAG labels or instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions),
  [WCAG error identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification),
  [WCAG use of color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color),
  [WCAG status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages),
  [WCAG target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum)
- **DOCUMENTED:** The WAI-ARIA meter pattern represents a scalar measurement
  inside a known range.
  [WAI-ARIA meter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/meter/)
- **INFERRED:** A support percentage is a meter, not task-completion progress.
  Its visible copy and accessible value must identify the measure and through
  date. Color cannot be the only signal. If source coverage is incomplete or a
  compatible goal does not exist, show a truthful unavailable/hidden state,
  never a fabricated zero.

## 4. Recommended first decision for the grill

### Option A — Person-owned page per Party

Each eligible individual Party owns one page, one primary editor, and one
designation inferred from that person.

- **Benefit:** superficially simple for a single missionary.
- **Failure:** breaks couples, project teams, shared ministry funds, multiple
  logins, restricted aliases, legal-entity/currency destinations, and lifecycle
  changes. It also makes a Party relation an accidental publication,
  authorization, and financial binding.
- **Recommendation:** reject.

### Option B — CMS-page-owned arbitrary relationships

A flexible CMS page relates to any number of Parties, designations, editors,
and progress sources through configuration.

- **Benefit:** maximum apparent flexibility.
- **Failure:** converts CMS configuration into security and financial truth,
  permits contradictory or dangling relations, increases cross-tenant and
  restricted-worker exposure risk, and makes staff learn a page builder and a
  policy engine.
- **Recommendation:** reject.

### Option C-prime — Tenant-owned, purpose-bound Public Ministry Pages with participant-scoped proposals — Recommended

One Tenant, Legal Entity, and Site owns every page. Each page has:

1. exactly one typed presentation and fundraising subject: a worker-support
   purpose/assignment, a project or campaign purpose, or an organization fund;
2. one bounded set of Phase 10-approved public presentation participants,
   supporting an individual, couple/household, or team;
3. one independently authorized set of page contributors and their allowed
   proposal fields;
4. one explicit, server-resolved active designation/checkout binding for the
   exact site, locale, currency, and source-attribution context;
5. one tenant-owned template and bounded page variant contract;
6. one immutable published revision plus independently versioned drafts and
   review evidence; and
7. one bounded lifecycle with immediate safety and CTA containment.

Missionaries, spouses, and authorized teammates propose changes only to the
fields the tenant allows. Staff can review a coherent diff against the live
version, request revision, edit directly with attribution, publish, pause, or
retire. Public rendering composes only approved CMS narrative, the Phase 10
public identity projection, an explicit source-owned progress projection, and
the server-resolved CTA. It never exposes or copies raw Party, Field Account,
support-access, designation-ledger, commitment, or contribution records.

**Critical separation:** Support Assignment membership, finance access, donor
attribution, public display membership, editorial contribution rights,
publication authority, and the giving destination are different relationships.
None may be inferred from another.

This option is the best fit because it supports Reliant-style couples,
CTEN-style couple/alias pages, distinct worker/project/general subjects,
participant-friendly edits, and organization control without turning Payload
or one Party record into the safety boundary.

## 5. Adversarial risk register and permanent controls

| Concern                               | What could go wrong                                                                                                                                 | Severity | Likelihood without control | Permanent prevention                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Page/Party conflation                 | A spouse, teammate, or project participant inherits publication, editing, finance, or designation rights merely by being related to a page subject. | Critical | High                       | Persist separate typed relations and authorize every action against the exact tenant/page/version/capability.                                                                                   |
| Cross-tenant or restricted-data leak  | Public route, Payload Local API, metadata, sitemap, OG image, localization fallback, or image CDN bypasses the safe projection.                     | Critical | Medium–high                | One public projection used by every render channel; deny-by-default RLS/service authorization; explicit Payload access; exhaustive leak tests.                                                  |
| “Unlisted means private”              | A direct link, opaque slug, or `noindex` page exposes a worker thought to be confidential.                                                          | Critical | Medium                     | Label unlisted as public-without-directory-discovery; require authentication for confidential material; publish only Phase 10-safe alias content.                                               |
| CTA tampering or stale destination    | Query parameters or stale page cache sends a donor to the wrong tenant, legal entity, designation, locale, or currency.                             | Critical | Medium                     | Resolve destination server-side from an active versioned binding; validate attribution context; fail closed; hard-invalidate on disablement.                                                    |
| Donor-intent corruption on retirement | Old worker URL silently gives to the organization or another worker/project.                                                                        | Critical | Medium                     | Use `308` only for a new route of the same immutable Page; make every different successor a fresh explicit link; preserve D7's current Giving state and never redesignate recurring gifts here. |
| Misleading progress                   | Page mixes gross, net, posted, provisional, refunded, offline, pledged, annualized, or converted amounts and calls the result “raised.”             | High     | High                       | Version one named metric per page type; show units, currency, source scope, through date, and explanatory details; hide when proof is incomplete.                                               |
| Restricted metadata leakage           | Real name or location appears in slug, JSON-LD, OG title, image name, alt text, analytics event, translation fallback, or cache.                    | Critical | Medium                     | Treat every emitted channel as public; derive all labels and assets from the same Phase 10 projection; test the complete response graph.                                                        |
| Draft overwrite race                  | A missionary submits from revision N after staff publishes N+1, silently erasing work or restoring unsafe content.                                  | High     | Medium                     | Base-version CAS, coherent revision diffs, conflict/rebase UX, immutable submissions, and no mutable in-place publish.                                                                          |
| Broad CMS access                      | A participant can browse other tenant records or edit protected relations through Payload Admin or a Local API bypass.                              | Critical | Medium                     | Purpose-built workspace editor; narrow domain commands; `overrideAccess: false` where user-context Local API is appropriate; explicit tenant tests.                                             |
| Dangerous uploads                     | Forged images, GPS metadata, parser exploits, decompression bombs, or public originals leak data or harm the service.                               | High     | Medium                     | Quarantine, signature/type/size/pixel checks, decode/re-encode, metadata stripping, malware checks, generated public derivatives, bounded processing.                                           |
| Review-link leakage                   | A forwarded bearer link reveals an unpublished restricted story indefinitely.                                                                       | High     | Medium                     | Exact-version, short-lived, revocable, least-capability token; no-referrer; authenticated review for restricted content; audit use.                                                             |
| Cache survival after revocation       | A restricted identity or Give CTA remains live in HTML, RSC, CDN, OG, or alternate locale after staff revokes it.                                   | Critical | Medium                     | Request-time safety/destination gate plus immediate cache invalidation and CDN purge; never use SWR for revocation.                                                                             |
| Locale fallback exposure              | Missing restricted-safe translation falls back to an unrestricted name, story, region, or photo.                                                    | Critical | Medium                     | Validate complete public-safe locale coverage or use an explicitly safe fallback revision; never field-merge locale content.                                                                    |
| Page-builder overengineering          | Per-worker layout, workflow, and field knobs create inconsistent sites and ongoing admin burden.                                                    | Medium   | High                       | Tenant template plus a small bounded set of slots and variants; advanced capabilities appear only when enabled and qualified.                                                                   |
| Lifecycle toggle contradictions       | Page is simultaneously searchable, retired, donation-enabled, redirected, and hidden due to independent booleans.                                   | High     | Medium                     | One bounded lifecycle whose states deterministically derive visibility, indexing, CTA, redirect, and cache behavior.                                                                            |

## 6. UX implications supported by the evidence

### Missionary, spouse, or teammate

- A single **Edit public page** action opens bounded content sections, not a CMS
  collection or arbitrary page builder.
- The header states one plain-language status: **Live**, **Draft**, **In review**,
  or **Changes requested**. It also says which live version donors currently
  see.
- Desktop, mobile, and social-card previews use the production-safe projection
  and synthetic/private-safe context. Preview never grants publication.
- Inline guidance distinguishes public fields from private CRM information and
  explains why a safety warning appears.
- One **Submit for review** action submits a coherent version. Staff feedback is
  attached to the revision and relevant section; contributors never have to
  reconcile hidden partial approvals.
- Separate logins for spouses or teammates can contribute without sharing
  credentials. Concurrent edits surface a base-version conflict rather than
  silently winning last-write.

### Staff reviewer and publisher

- A quiet, exception-first queue shows pages needing review, safety resolution,
  missing CTA binding, stale progress coverage, or retirement action. Healthy
  pages do not generate repetitive work.
- Review shows a diff against the current live version, public-safety tier,
  exact display participants, exact contributor identities, site and locales,
  the server-resolved designation/currency, progress definition and through
  date, mobile rendering, and social metadata.
- Staff approve one coherent revision or request changes. Direct staff edits
  create a new attributable version and do not destroy the contributor's draft.
- High-consequence actions use literal language: **Publish this version**,
  **Pause giving**, **Remove from public view**, or **Retire page**. The
  confirmation states the exact public, checkout, search, cache, and redirect
  consequence.

### Donor

- The page presents one coherent public identity/story and one primary Give CTA
  bound to the intended designation. The checkout handoff preserves valid site,
  locale, currency, and source attribution without trusting editable client
  parameters.
- Progress is optional. When shown, it states what is being measured, in which
  currency, and through what date; the details explain inclusions without
  exposing private finance facts.
- A retired or unsafe page never presents a functioning stale CTA. A donor is
  not silently moved to a different charitable purpose.

## 7. Progress contract questions for a later decision

The evidence establishes that “progress” is not one universal fact. Phase 22
should later decide, without changing financial ownership:

1. **Worker-support page:** whether the public projection uses an approved
   monthly support measure versus an approved monthly support goal, and how a
   tenant that does not use commitments or public balances disables the measure.
2. **Project page:** which posted/eligible contribution amount and reversals count
   toward a project goal, and whether a multi-currency project publishes one
   exact currency or no combined total.
3. **Coverage:** the exact as-of/through watermark and what happens when data is
   stale, incomplete, quarantined, or unavailable.
4. **Presentation:** whether values may exceed 100%, whether amounts are shown,
   and the bounded explanation available to donors.

The safe default is hidden progress until the page has one compatible,
source-owned, versioned projection. Missing or incompatible data never becomes
zero and no public page calculates directly from ledger tables, Field Accounts,
or arbitrary commitments.

## 8. Lifecycle direction resolved by D1-D8

A minimal capability-consistent lifecycle remains preferable to independent
public, searchable, editable, and donation-enabled toggles. The early sketch
below is superseded by the ratified separation of D2/D4/D7/D8:

- **Draft:** no public output.
- **In review:** exact draft under staff review; current live version, if any,
  remains separately authoritative.
- **Released:** the exact D2 release is current; D7 Giving is reported
  independently and may be ready or contained by its owning facts.
- **Transition notice:** one substantive D2 release may explain a current
  transition while preserving D7's exact binding and Phase 16's independent
  recurring truth.
- **Same-Page canonical move:** one originally Listed-public route may return a
  direct `308` to an eligible new route for the same immutable Page.
- **Removed:** every tombstone and unknown route returns the same real
  privacy-safe `404` plus `noindex`; a different successor Page can appear only
  through a fresh explicit link from a transition notice.

This is not one configurable lifecycle state machine. D2, D4, D7, and D8 remain
separate source-owned contracts, supported by comparator separation of page,
new-Giving, recurring, and discovery behavior and by Google/Next.js redirect and
missing-content semantics.

## 9. Required production-shaped verification

The eventual Phase 22 contract should require at least:

1. a Tenant × Legal Entity × Site × role × subject × page × action
   authorization matrix, including authenticated preview and anonymous public
   reads;
2. cross-tenant and IDOR tests, including Payload Local API calls with explicit
   access posture;
3. restricted-field leak snapshots for HTML, React Server Component payloads,
   route handlers, metadata, OG images, sitemap, JSON-LD, analytics labels,
   alternate locales, image URLs, errors, logs, and cached responses;
4. couple, household, team, and project cases proving that display membership,
   editorial rights, Support Assignment membership, finance access, donor
   attribution, and destination binding remain independent;
5. draft base-version conflicts, staff edits during contributor review,
   resubmission, rejection/request-changes, and immutable publication history;
6. tampered tenant, designation, site, locale, currency, return URL, and source
   attribution inputs failing closed at the checkout handoff;
7. progress fixtures for offline gifts, refunds, reversals, commitments disabled,
   missing/stale coverage, no goal, over-goal results, and incompatible or
   multiple currencies;
8. upload tests for forged MIME/signature, oversized bytes and dimensions,
   malformed decoders, metadata/GPS stripping, generated filenames, and public-
   derivative-only access;
9. immediate publish, pause, restrict, retire, and CTA-disable cache behavior
   across server cache, CDN, metadata, OG, sitemap, and locale routes;
10. review-token expiry, revocation, exact-version scope, reuse behavior,
    referrer protection, and restricted-content authentication policy;
11. accessibility tests for keyboard and focus order, visible errors and status,
    target size, reduced-motion behavior, contrast, color independence, and
    properly named/value-described support meters; and
12. lifecycle/SEO tests proving same-Page `308` versus uniform privacy-safe
    `404` versus transient no-store `503`, no soft-404 or cross-page redirects,
    no stale retired CTA, and safe historical slug handling.

## 10. What the evidence does not establish

- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY:** No inspected mission-organization public page proves its
  internal database ownership, RLS, editorial approval, cache, or audit model.
- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY:** “Direct link,” “unlisted,” and an alias do not establish
  confidentiality. The tenant's Phase 10 rule and resulting public projection
  must decide what is safe.
- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY:** Comparator platform progress cannot establish Asym's
  monthly-support, commitment, settlement, refund, assessment, or multi-currency
  formula.
- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY:** Payload drafts and access controls do not prove that
  every Next.js public, preview, metadata, or background-job path enforces the
  same projection. Release tests must prove it.
- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY:** Public documentation for Keela and several mission
  organizations is too sparse to support fine-grained backend or approval
  conclusions.
- **UNKNOWN / VERIFY:** Search-engine removal and CDN invalidation are not
  instantaneous universal guarantees. Phase 22 must prevent new disclosure at
  Asym's request boundary immediately and disclose downstream limitations
  accurately.

## Bottom line

Current mission practice and comparable fundraising products support a public
experience that is easy for a missionary to contribute to and firmly controlled
by the organization. They do not support collapsing a page into one person, one
editor, one fund, or one generic progress number. The durable Phase 22 model is
a tenant-owned, typed Public Ministry Page whose participants, contributors,
publication authority, financial destination, progress source, safety tier, and
lifecycle are explicit and independently authorized.

That ownership decision should be resolved first. It is the smallest decision
that prevents the largest class of later privacy, couple/team, checkout,
progress, review, and retirement redesigns.

## 11. D1 follow-up evidence: missionary-dashboard editing across assigned pages

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. This section responds to the founder's D1
clarification: an authenticated missionary should be able to find and propose
updates to the missionary-ministry and project/campaign pages for which that
person is an authorized subject. The sources below are current official product
or platform documentation; their product behavior is evidence, not an Asym
authority boundary.

### 11.1 Current comparator behavior

- [Raisely's fundraiser management documentation](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649207914637-Managing-Fundraisers)
  gives a logged-in fundraiser a dashboard for editing the fundraiser's profile,
  while organization administrators can edit the same fields, archive the
  profile, move it between teams, and transfer the profile to another owner.
  Raisely explicitly defines the profile owner as the person who can log in and
  control that profile. This supports self-service editing plus organization
  custody and explicit transfer; it does not support inferring authority from a
  person's appearance on arbitrary pages.
- [Givebutter's Page campaign documentation](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3688273-how-to-configure-a-page-campaign)
  lets an invited team member with a login edit that member's own picture, name,
  page link, goal, and story. A manually added member without a login cannot do
  so. [Givebutter's account-user documentation](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/2118934-how-to-manage-account-users)
  separately distinguishes peer-to-peer members from account users, provides a
  Campaign Editor role, permits campaign-scoped access, and lets an administrator
  change or revoke that access. Its [team-fundraising documentation](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1749223-how-to-use-team-fundraising)
  reserves editing of a team name, goal, or logo to an account administrator.
  The durable lesson is that personal-profile contribution, campaign editing,
  team administration, and account authority are different capabilities.
- [GoFundMe Pro's team-page editor documentation](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288801799451-Edit-a-team-fundraising-page)
  permits the team captain to manage the team's story, updates, picture, name,
  headline, goal, thank-you message, URL, and notifications, but requires the
  organization to delete the page. Its [fundraiser-management documentation](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288766899867-Manage-fundraisers-and-teams)
  lets staff edit supporter pages, change a team captain, move a fundraiser, or
  archive a page. Its [roles documentation](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288801410331-Roles-and-permissions)
  separates Campaign Editor, Campaign Publisher, Campaign Administrator, and
  Viewer permissions. This is strong evidence against treating edit, publish,
  lifecycle, and broad administrative control as one role. It also exposes a
  comparator limitation Asym should not copy: GoFundMe Pro documents only one
  team captain and no co-captains.
- [Blackbaud TeamRaiser's participant-center documentation](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_pc3features.html)
  lets an authorized team captain edit bounded team-page content. Its
  [advanced event options](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_configuring_blueprints_03cselectingadvancedeventoptions.html)
  allow the organization to require approval for a new or modified participant
  page, notify staff when a participant modifies a page, limit participant
  layout choice, and expose team self-management separately. The evidence
  supports a tenant-selected review lane, but Phase 10 safety remains mandatory
  regardless of that choice.
- [CiviCRM's Personal Campaign Page guide](https://docs.civicrm.org/user/en/latest/contributions/personal-campaign-pages/)
  lets both the page owner and administrator edit a page, while optional
  moderation requires an administrator to approve, reject, enable, or disable
  it before public use. Again, authoring and release are separate facts.
- [Salesforce Experience Cloud sharing sets](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.networks_setting_light_users.htm&language=en_US&type=5)
  grant authenticated external users Read Only or Read/Write access to exact
  related records through explicit mappings. Salesforce's
  [external-sharing guidance](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.mfg_experience_cloud_sharing.htm&language=en_US&type=5)
  separates object-, field-, and record-level access. This supports explicit
  page-scoped entitlements rather than a global "missionary editor" role.

### 11.2 Platform controls the implementation must respect

- [Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts) preserve the live
  document while newer draft work is saved and can restrict publication by
  access control. [Payload versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview)
  retain author-attributed history, diffs, restore points, and separately
  controllable version reads. These are suitable CMS mechanics, but the Phase 22
  Publication contract remains the product authority.
- [Payload document locking](https://payloadcms.com/docs/admin/locked-documents)
  prevents concurrent Admin Panel edits by default, but API callers can bypass
  locks. [Payload's Local API documentation](https://payloadcms.com/docs/local-api/access-control)
  likewise states that Local API operations bypass access control by default.
  Every missionary-dashboard operation therefore needs authenticated context,
  `overrideAccess: false`, `overrideLock: false`, and a durable base-version or
  compare-and-swap guard. A UI lock alone is insufficient.
- [Supabase's current RLS guidance](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)
  requires RLS for exposed-schema tables, recommends explicit `authenticated`
  roles, requires both `USING` and `WITH CHECK` for safe updates, notes that an
  UPDATE also needs a SELECT policy, recommends indexes and explicit query
  filters, and warns that authorization in JWT claims can remain stale until a
  token refresh. [PostgreSQL 18 row-security documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html)
  establishes default deny when RLS is enabled without an applicable policy and
  explains permissive versus restrictive policy composition. Editorial access
  should therefore resolve from an indexed, tenant-scoped membership relation,
  not a mutable client claim or an unbounded JWT array.

### 11.3 Hardened implication for Phase 22 D1

The founder's desired dashboard experience is sound, with one crucial domain
distinction:

1. **Public subject membership and editorial authority remain distinct facts.**
   A person shown incidentally in a photograph, family list, team roster, or
   project story must not gain edit access. Phase 22 needs an exact
   **Public Page Contributor Assignment** for each authenticated person who may
   contribute to a page.
2. **The ordinary missionary-subject path creates both facts atomically.** When
   a tenant explicitly assigns an active authenticated missionary as a
   `missionary_subject` of a Missionary Ministry Page or Project/Campaign Page,
   the same authorized operation creates that person's page-scoped contributor
   assignment. This makes the founder's expected path automatic without
   deriving rights later from Party, household, Support Assignment, Designation,
   donor, or finance relationships. A separate non-editorial
   `display_participant` role covers children, guests, inactive people, featured
   partners, and other people who may appear but must not edit.
3. **One dashboard enumerates exact assignments, not inferred relationships.**
   The missionary sees a quiet **Public pages** area containing every currently
   assigned page across both families, grouped as **My ministry page** and
   **Projects and campaigns**. Each card shows title, site/locale, page family,
   public status, whether donors currently see an older live version, last
   published time, and one primary action: **Edit**, **Continue draft**,
   **View feedback**, or **View live page**.
4. **Contributor scope is deliberately bounded.** A contributor may view the
   safe working projection, edit tenant-enabled story fields, propose media and
   updates, preview the exact safe rendering, save a draft, submit or withdraw
   that revision from review, and respond to feedback. Contributor status alone
   never permits changing Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, page family, canonical
   operational subject, restricted-worker classification, contributor list,
   Designation/checkout binding, progress source, financial facts, canonical
   slug/redirect, publication policy, page retirement, or deletion.
5. **Multiple contributors use their own identities.** A spouse, teammate, or
   project leader receives a separate assignment and login; credentials are
   never shared. One coherent working revision exists per page. Document locks,
   base-version checks, named presence, section-level attribution, and a clear
   conflict flow prevent silent last-write-wins behavior. Multiple contributors
   do not require one fictional owner or GoFundMe-style single captain.
6. **Saving, submitting, approving, and publishing are separate facts.** Editing
   a published page creates a newer draft while the current approved version
   remains live. The final button says **Submit changes** when review is required
   and **Publish eligible changes** only when the tenant's prospective release
   policy permits automatic promotion. Both paths run the same non-waivable
   Phase 10 projection, media, consent, destination, and publication checks.
   Automatic publication is a system execution of tenant policy, not a direct
   contributor write to live CMS state.
7. **Staff retain organization custody without overwriting authorship.** Staff
   may review a diff, request changes, edit through a separately attributed
   revision, approve/publish when authorized, add or revoke contributors,
   reassign coordination, pause or retire through the governing lifecycle, and
   recover an orphaned draft. A contributor cannot grant access to someone else
   or make themselves a publisher.
8. **Revocation is immediate for future authority and non-destructive for
   evidence.** Removing the operational subject, deactivating the user,
   revoking the contributor assignment, or a Phase 10 containment signal denies
   new draft reads/writes, preview, submission, and notification delivery at the
   smallest affected scope. It does not erase attributed versions. A pending
   draft is quarantined for staff reassignment or disposition; the already-live
   version changes only through the independently authoritative safety or page
   lifecycle transition.
9. **The page-scoped authorization key is structural.** At minimum it binds
   Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, page ID, authenticated participant/user ID,
   contributor role/scope, status, effective interval, and revocation facts.
   Database policies, the application service, Payload access, preview, uploads,
   review actions, notifications, and background work must all evaluate that
   same current assignment. No tenant-global `missionary_editor` role is enough.

### 11.4 UX details that prevent the feature becoming a miniature CMS

- Open the editor from the missionary workspace, not the Payload Admin Panel.
  Keep tenant templates and protected structure out of the ordinary workflow.
- Use a short section navigator: **Story**, **Photos**, **Updates**, and
  **Preview**. Show exact field-level guidance and character/media limits where
  needed; do not expose empty CMS configuration panels.
- Keep the live/draft distinction persistent: `Live page unchanged` while work
  is saved, then one plain-language release status. The preview must identify
  the page, site, locale, safety tier, and exact revision being previewed.
- Explain protected fields in situ: `Your organization manages the giving
destination and support-progress source.` Do not merely disable unexplained
  controls.
- Show collaborator names and current editing presence without exposing private
  account details. A contributor can see who else may edit but cannot change
  permissions.
- Send one actionable notification for review feedback, approval/publication,
  access removal, or a material conflict. Do not notify every contributor for
  autosaves or routine staff inspection.

### 11.5 Production-shaped proofs added by this clarification

The eventual Phase 22 acceptance suite must prove at least:

1. one missionary dashboard lists one Missionary Ministry Page and multiple
   assigned Project/Campaign Pages without exposing an unrelated page;
2. two spouses or teammates with separate logins can contribute to the same page
   while an unassigned household or Support Assignment member cannot;
3. a `display_participant` cannot read drafts, preview, edit, submit, receive
   editorial notifications, or discover the page through authenticated APIs;
4. subject-plus-contributor creation is atomic and cross-tenant, cross-Legal-
   Entity, cross-Site, forged-ID, stale-session, expired, and revoked access
   fail closed;
5. subject removal and contributor revocation immediately stop every write,
   preview, upload, notification, and background-operation path while preserving
   immutable authorship history;
6. one editor cannot silently overwrite another editor's newer revision, and a
   Payload Local API call cannot bypass access or document locks;
7. contributor edits cannot mutate protected identity, safety, designation,
   progress, lifecycle, slug, contributor, or publication-policy fields;
8. review-required and policy-authorized automatic lanes reach the same safe
   published projection and never confuse draft save with publication;
9. staff can request changes, publish, revoke, reassign, quarantine, and recover
   an orphaned working revision without becoming the original author; and
10. RLS policy plans remain indexed and tenant-fair with realistic page and
    contributor volumes, not only single-row fixtures.

**Result:** The D1 clarification should be adopted, but hardened as explicit,
page-scoped contributor assignments automatically created for authenticated
missionary subjects. That gives missionaries the expected one-dashboard editing
experience across both typed page families while keeping appearance, editing,
publication, safety, finance, and organization custody independent.

## 12. D2 follow-up evidence: publication reach is not confidentiality

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. This section distinguishes a normally
discoverable public ministry page, a direct-link public page using only a safe
alias projection, and no anonymous page. It also tests whether Phase 22 should
offer a generic password/authentication switch. Sources are current official
search-platform, mission-organization, regulator, and access-control
documentation; product behavior is evidence, not authority over Asym's Phase 10
contract.

### 12.1 Search and link semantics are unambiguous

- [Google's current content-control guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/control-what-you-share)
  says confidential or private content needs password protection so that only
  authorized users can access it. The same guidance says a `noindex` page can
  still be linked from another page and visited directly by anyone with its URL.
  **DOCUMENTED:** `noindex` is a search-discovery instruction, not an
  authorization or confidentiality control.
- [Google's robots metadata specification](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag)
  says crawler rules are usable only when the crawler can access the resource,
  and that non-HTML resources such as images and PDFs need an `X-Robots-Tag`
  rather than an HTML meta element. Its
  [robots.txt guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro)
  warns that other crawlers may ignore `robots.txt` and recommends password
  protection for private files. **DOCUMENTED:** blocking a direct-link page in
  `robots.txt` can prevent a conforming crawler from seeing the page's
  `noindex`; neither mechanism makes the page private.
- [Google's sitemap guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/overview)
  says sitemaps and ordinary site links help search engines discover URLs.
  **INFERRED:** a direct-link page should be absent from the public directory,
  site search, navigation, sitemap, JSON feeds, alternate-locale discovery, and
  other Phase 22 discovery surfaces. That reduces accidental discovery but is
  still not an access check.
- [YouTube's official visibility comparison](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/157177)
  says anyone with an unlisted URL can view and reshare it without a Google
  account; it is excluded from the channel and normal search but is not private.
  [YouTube's older-unlisted guidance](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9230970)
  expressly recommends treating unlisted content like public content.
  **DOCUMENTED:** the established user-facing meaning of "unlisted" is
  public-by-link, not confidential.
- [Google Search Console's Removals documentation](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9689846)
  says its tool hides results only temporarily, for about six months, does not
  remove content from the Internet or other search engines, and must be followed
  by removal, authentication, or `noindex` for a permanent source-side outcome.
  **DOCUMENTED:** a search-removal request is useful incident response evidence,
  but cannot be Phase 22's publication-revocation truth.

### 12.2 Current mission practice uses several genuinely different patterns

- [Pioneers Giving Help](https://pioneers.org/give/givinghelp) says it
  intentionally omits missionary names and project numbers from its website for
  safety. **DOCUMENTED:** for some organizations, the correct public result is
  no worker directory or worker page at all, even though an independently owned
  giving process remains available.
- [Reliant's support-raising instructions](https://solomon.reliant.org/display/public/international/Support+Raising+Instructions+for+International+Interns)
  say that for a secure location the missionary's name is not searchable and
  donors need the direct giving link. **DOCUMENTED:** direct-link public giving
  is a real missions workflow, but the source does not call the page private or
  prove that it contains confidential content.
- [CTEN's Canadian orientation journal](https://www.cten.org/s/Canada-Digital-Orientation-Journal-092023-jl-Website.pdf)
  directs supporters to a public biography URL that may use the missionary's
  name or an alias before handing off to the giving provider. **DOCUMENTED:** an
  alias can be the approved public presentation identity. It is not an
  authentication credential and does not establish the page's discovery reach.
- These examples prove three separate controls: **public identity** (legal name
  versus approved alias), **discovery reach** (directory/search versus direct
  link), and **anonymous availability** (page exists versus no public page).
  Collapsing them into one `private` checkbox would misrepresent both the safety
  posture and the user-visible consequence.

### 12.3 Privacy-by-default and consent reinforce the product boundary

- The [European Commission's data-protection-by-design guidance](https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/rules-business-and-organisations/obligations/what-does-data-protection-design-and-default-mean_en)
  says default safeguards should limit accessibility and avoid making personal
  data available to an indefinite number of people without the person's
  intervention. The [current ICO guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/accountability-and-governance/guide-to-accountability-and-governance/data-protection-by-design-and-by-default/)
  similarly requires necessary-purpose access throughout the product lifecycle.
- [ICO consent guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/lawful-basis/consent/how-should-we-obtain-record-and-manage-consent/)
  requires evidence of what a person consented to and makes withdrawal as easy
  as granting consent. **INFERRED:** Phase 22 should show the actual audience
  consequence when consent is captured and must provide an immediate
  exposure-reducing path when publishing consent or safety changes. The tenant
  controls organizational publication, but it cannot use a page setting to
  widen past Phase 10's person-owned consent or safety ceiling.

### 12.4 A generic authenticated-page switch is the wrong launch abstraction

- [Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/control-what-you-share)
  correctly distinguishes anonymous `noindex` content from access-controlled
  private content. [Cloudflare Access](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/http-apps/)
  describes authenticated application protection as an identity-aware check
  performed before each request reaches the application, while its
  [deny-by-default guidance](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/access-settings/require-access-protection/)
  exists to prevent accidental exposure when a route is deployed without a
  matching access application.
- [Cloudflare's policy documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/policies/)
  also warns that a bypass disables identity enforcement and logging. The
  [Next.js authentication guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication)
  recommends centralized authorization in a data-access layer rather than
  relying on route/UI visibility alone.
- **INFERRED:** an authenticated external ministry page would require its own
  exact viewer population, invitation/claim/revocation lifecycle, per-request
  authorization, metadata and asset access, non-public cache behavior, and
  donor UX. Phase 22 has no settled owning truth for that external audience.
  Reusing contributor access, a shared password, an expiring review URL, or a
  page-level `Authenticate` checkbox would create a second weak identity system
  and contradict Phase 10's already rejected anti-pattern.
- The permanent launch answer is therefore **no anonymous page** when content is
  not safe for public-by-link viewing. Authorized contributors and staff may
  still access the draft in their existing workspaces. A future authenticated
  supporter surface may be added only by the phase that owns its exact recipient
  and access contract; it must not be simulated by Phase 22.

### 12.5 Options for the D2 decision

#### Option A - binary Public or Not public

Every published page is listed and index-eligible; otherwise there is no public
route.

- **Advantage:** very small state space.
- **Failure:** cannot model Reliant-style direct-link giving or Phase 10's
  restricted-tier exclusion from search without one-off exceptions.
- **Risk:** teams will create external landing pages or misleading aliases to
  regain a direct-link path.

#### Option B - independent visibility switches

Expose settings such as `Public`, `Listed`, `Indexable`, `Password protected`,
`Show in sitemap`, `Allow giving`, and `Use alias` independently.

- **Advantage:** superficially flexible.
- **Failure:** contradictory combinations are inevitable, and "password" has no
  safe viewer authority behind it. This recreates the SiteStacker page-level
  authentication anti-pattern Phase 10 explicitly rejected.
- **Risk:** critical and likely; one unchecked box can become a physical-safety
  incident.

#### Option C-prime - one bounded, ceiling-resolved Publication Reach

Use one prospective, tenant-owned policy to request a reach outcome, then resolve
the exact effective result against Phase 10's current public projection,
security tier, publishing consent, hard do-not-publish rule, and review verdict.
The strictest applicable source wins. The three launch outcomes are:

1. **Listed publicly** (`discoverable_public`) - anonymously readable and
   eligible for the tenant's directory, site search, sitemap, canonical
   metadata, and search indexing. It still exposes only the Phase 10 public
   projection.
2. **Shared by link (public)** (`direct_link_public`) - anonymously readable by
   anyone with the link and explicitly reshareable; absent from the tenant
   directory, site search, public navigation, sitemap, public feeds, and
   alternate-locale discovery; emitted with `noindex` and matching non-HTML
   resource controls. It uses only an approved alias-safe projection and a
   non-identity-derived route by default. It is never labelled private,
   confidential, authenticated, or secure.
3. **Not public** (`not_public`) - no anonymous representation, metadata, media,
   OG image, JSON-LD, CTA, or discoverable route. Unauthorized requests receive
   a non-enumerating missing response. The protected working draft remains
   available only to exact D1 contributors and authorized staff.

Public alias, page reach, and Designation eligibility remain separate facts. A
`direct_link_public` page may show its exact Phase 13-approved CTA; a
`not_public` page shows none, but that outcome does not disable or redesignate
the independently owned Designation in other authorized giving flows.

### 12.6 Recommended hardening of Option C-prime

1. **No mutable page checkbox is authoritative.** Store an immutable effective
   reach on each published revision together with the requested reach, tenant
   policy version, Phase 10 projection/verdict version, consent evidence,
   subject/participant set, actor, and publication time. A newer revision or
   containment occurrence changes future behavior; history is not rewritten.
2. **Tenant flexibility is subtractive at the safety boundary.** The tenant may
   default or reduce reach by Page Family, Site, Legal Entity, and Phase 10
   security tier. It may widen reach prospectively only when the current Phase
   10 ceiling permits it, all required participant consent is present, and the
   authorized release operation succeeds. Missionaries may request wider reach;
   they cannot self-promote it.
3. **Exposure reduction is fast and easy.** An authenticated represented person
   who controls the applicable Phase 10 publishing-consent record can use one
