   clearly labelled `Stop showing me publicly` action. Mere D1
   `display_participant` status still grants no account or editorial authority.
   Phase 10 consent withdrawal or a higher safety classification automatically
   creates the same containment signal. The smallest safe scope is recomposed:
   remove one optional display participant when possible; otherwise suppress
   the exact page. Staff are informed, but a safety reduction is not delayed for
   approval.
4. **Restricted-safe alias is content, not reach.** The current Phase 10 public
   projection supplies the alias, approved derivative, and generalized region.
   A restricted/high-risk subject is never index-eligible under the already
   settled Phase 10 rule. If the safe projection is allowed and tenant policy
   permits, its maximum Phase 22 reach is direct-link public; otherwise it is not
   public. Phase 22 never falls back to a legal name or real location.
5. **URLs do not become credentials.** Listed pages may use a safe, reviewed
   human-readable slug. Direct-link pages default to a random opaque public
   route that contains no legal name, alias, location, operation, fund code, or
   sequential identifier. Entropy reduces accidental discovery but does not
   authorize the viewer. Replacing a shared link creates a new route and
   tombstones the old route without redirecting it to the new link.
6. **Every egress derives from the same effective reach.** HTML, React payloads,
   route handlers, metadata, OG/social previews, JSON-LD, sitemap, directory,
   site search, alternate locales, public APIs/feeds, media derivatives, cache
   keys, analytics, logs, and notifications must agree. A direct-link page must
   not leak through its image URL or a public CMS relationship even when the
   HTML is `noindex`.
7. **Revocation truth is local and immediate.** A safety escalation, consent
   withdrawal, page pause, or transition to `not_public` must immediately stop
   new anonymous reads at Asym's request boundary, invalidate controlled caches
   and public derivatives, and remove discovery records. Search-removal requests
   can accelerate cleanup but remain separately observed best-effort outcomes.
   The UX repeats Phase 10's honest limitation: previously shared links, copied
   content, issued messages, third-party previews, and search caches cannot be
   universally retracted.
8. **Do not make the tenant learn crawler mechanics.** The staff control should
   present only the three plain-language reach outcomes and an exact consequence
   preview. Asym derives crawler headers, sitemap/directory behavior, metadata,
   route shape, asset policy, cache posture, and invalidation. Advanced SEO
   booleans are neither editable nor visible on the common path.

### 12.7 Production-shaped proofs required by D2

1. The matrix of requested reach x Tenant x Legal Entity x Site x Page Family x
   every Phase 10 security tier x consent/do-not-publish x
   `allowed|needs_review|blocked` produces exactly one effective outcome, with
   the strictest source winning and no missing input becoming permissive.
2. A listed page appears consistently in the intended directory, site search,
   sitemap, canonical metadata, alternate-locale links, and public feed; a
   direct-link page appears in none of them and carries the intended HTML and
   media indexing controls.
3. Anyone with a copied direct-link URL can view and reshare the exact safe page;
   the UI and audit evidence never describe that URL as private or confidential.
4. A not-public page has no anonymous HTML, React payload, route-handler data,
   metadata, OG/social image, JSON-LD, media derivative, CTA, sitemap row,
   directory/search result, locale alternate, public API/feed record, cache
   residue, analytics label, log detail, or distinguishable existence response.
5. A restricted worker's legal name, real image, country, location, fund code,
   or identity-derived slug is absent from all three outcomes and from old route
   handling; no authorized contributor or staff form can override the firewall.
6. Discoverable-to-direct-link transition creates an opaque route, removes and
   tombstones the old discoverable route without redirecting to the new route,
   purges all controlled discovery surfaces, and records search-removal attempts
   without treating them as completion.
7. Direct-link rotation invalidates the old URL without changing the page,
   Designation, published content revision, attribution, or gift history.
8. Participant consent withdrawal and safety escalation during publish, cache
   regeneration, metadata rendering, media processing, CTA handoff, and
   background feed generation fail closed and contain the smallest safe scope.
9. A participant can reduce exposure from the missionary dashboard in the
   documented minimum interaction, while widening requires exact tenant release
   authority and fresh proof; concurrent opposite actions serialize safely.
10. `not_public` does not disable the source-owned Designation, and a stale or
    invalid Designation disables the page CTA without silently changing page
    reach or redirecting gifts elsewhere.

**Research recommendation:** adopt Option C-prime, hardened as one exact
effective Publication Reach with three plain-language launch outcomes. Do not
launch a generic authenticated supporter page, shared password, or arbitrary
visibility matrix. Reserve identity-gated external content for a future owning
contract with an exact authorized audience; use `not_public` until that contract
exists.

## 13. D2 UX follow-up: consequence-first Publication Reach controls

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. This section tests the staff and missionary
experience for the tenant-defaulted, Phase-10-ceiling-resolved Publication Reach
model. It uses current official documentation from a nonprofit fundraising
platform, major CMS and collaboration systems, search/video platforms, and W3C
accessibility standards. Comparator interfaces are evidence of useful patterns
and recurring mistakes; they do not supersede Asym's D1 entitlement model or
Phase 10 safety authority.

### 13.1 Comparator evidence supports three semantic outcomes, not a switch matrix

- [YouTube's current visibility documentation](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/157177)
  presents Public, Private, and Unlisted as mutually exclusive choices and
  compares the consequences for search, channel display, URL sharing, and
  resharing. It says an Unlisted item can be viewed and reshared by anyone with
  the link without signing in. Its
  [older-unlisted guidance](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9230970)
  explicitly says Unlisted is not Private and recommends treating an unlisted
  item like public content. **DOCUMENTED:** a mode name alone is insufficient;
  users need audience and discovery consequences beside it.
- [Google Drive's sharing documentation](https://support.google.com/drive/answer/2494822)
  distinguishes Restricted access from Anyone with the link and says the latter
  can be used without signing in. **DOCUMENTED:** "with the link" describes how
  anonymous public access is discovered, not who is authorized.
- [Givebutter's current Page campaign configuration](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3688273-how-to-configure-a-page-campaign)
  exposes campaign publication, accepting payments, raised-amount visibility,
  supporter-feed visibility, and unlisting as separate settings. Its
  [campaign-closing guidance](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1772204-how-to-close-or-unlist-a-campaign)
  says an unlisted campaign remains accessible to anyone with the URL, can keep
  accepting donations, and remains visible through links that were already
  shared. **DOCUMENTED:** page reach, giving availability, and individual public
  fields are independent facts. **INFERRED:** Asym should preserve those domain
  distinctions while avoiding Givebutter's potentially contradictory phrase
  "hide ... from public view" for a still-anonymous public URL.
- [Squarespace's Not linked documentation](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/360025899552-The-Not-linked-section)
  says removing a page from navigation leaves it public and potentially
  indexable. Its
  [page-settings documentation](https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/206543657-Page-settings)
  separately says hiding a page from search results leaves it public and
  directly accessible. [Wix gives the same warning](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-editor-hiding-and-unhiding-a-page-from-your-site-menu):
  hiding a page from the site menu does not remove it from search engines.
  **DOCUMENTED:** navigation, indexing, and anonymous serving are different
  technical controls. **INFERRED:** exposing them as adjacent tenant switches
  invites internally contradictory and misunderstood configurations; Asym
  should derive them from the semantic reach outcome.
- [WordPress.com's page-visibility documentation](https://wordpress.com/support/post-and-page-visibility/)
  separates Draft and Pending Review from Published, Private, and
  Password-protected states. It also warns that media on a password-protected
  page can still be indexed and accessed directly without the password.
  **DOCUMENTED:** editorial lifecycle and anonymous reach are separate, and a
  page-only protection control can leave asset egress exposed. **INFERRED:** the
  Phase 22 editor must never imply that saving a draft changes the live reach,
  or that hiding the HTML alone protects public derivatives.
- [Microsoft's current SharePoint guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/change-default-sharing-link)
  supports an organization-level sharing default with a site-level default and
  recommends a more restrictive default even when a broader link remains
  available. Microsoft's
  [sensitivity-label guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-default-sharing-link)
  applies the more restrictive scope when the site default and document label
  differ. **DOCUMENTED:** an organization-selected default plus a stricter
  item-specific ceiling is a proven enterprise pattern. **INFERRED:** Asym's
  interface should show both the requested tenant default and the Phase 10
  effective ceiling when they differ instead of silently substituting one for
  the other.

### 13.2 Staff setup should be a short guided policy, not a page-by-page chore

**RECOMMENDED setup location:** `Settings > Public ministry pages > Publication
reach`. Keep it out of general SEO settings because the decision changes human
exposure, not merely search optimization.

The common setup path should have three short stages:

1. **Choose the scope.** Show the exact Site and Page Family (`Missionary
Ministry Page` or `Project/Campaign Page`) in the heading. If a tenant has one
   Site, do not make staff select it. If it has several, show one Site at a time
   with the inherited tenant default and any existing prospective override.
2. **Choose one default reach.** Use a native radio group with three vertically
   stacked choice cards. Each card always displays its audience, discovery, and
   sharing consequence; do not hide the explanation behind an info icon or
   reveal it only after selection.
3. **Review before activation.** Show the prospective effective date or release
   boundary, the number of future/unreleased pages in scope, and counts for
   `will use this default`, `limited by safety rules`, `needs review`, and
   `unchanged`. The final action says `Save future default`, not `Publish`.

[The GOV.UK Design System radio guidance](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/radios/)
says radios are for selecting exactly one option, recommends a `fieldset` and
`legend`, advises against preselecting an answer when doing so could cause a
missed question, and warns against complex conditional content inside the
choice. **INFERRED:** the first intentional tenant setup should begin with no
radio selected even though the system remains fail-safe at `Not public`; an
existing policy should be selected when staff return to edit it. Consequence
copy should remain visible on all three cards.

The card copy should be literal and stable:

| Choice                      | Persistent consequence copy                                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Listed publicly**         | `Anyone can view and share this page. It can appear in your public directory, site search, and search engines.`                                                 |
| **Shared by link — public** | `Anyone with the link can view and reshare this page without signing in. It will not appear in Asym's directory, site search, or sitemap. This is not private.` |
| **Not public**              | `Supporters cannot open this page. Authorized staff and assigned contributors can keep working on its draft.`                                                   |

The setup must not expose `robots.txt`, `noindex`, `nofollow`, sitemap, canonical,
OG, asset-cache, directory, navigation, locale-alternate, or API-feed switches.
[Google's content-control guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/control-what-you-share)
and the CMS evidence above establish that these mechanisms have different
effects and do not constitute access control. **INFERRED:** Asym owns their
consistent derivation; asking tenant staff to compose them is both a safety
footgun and unnecessary operational work.

Changing the default affects later releases only. A separate, subordinate
`Reduce current exposure` action may apply a stricter outcome to already-live
pages after an exact affected-page preview; it can never widen them. Existing
pages must not change merely because an admin opened or saved the default form.
Widening a live page remains a D1-authorized release using current Phase 10
evidence. **RECOMMENDED:** do not combine default editing and live bulk mutation
under one Save button.

### 13.3 Staff page UX must distinguish requested, effective, and live truth

The page header should expose three quiet, separately labelled facts:

1. `Content`: Draft changes, In review, or Live revision;
2. `Public reach`: Listed publicly, Shared by link — public, or Not public; and
3. `Giving`: Accepting gifts, Giving unavailable, or another Phase 13-owned
   result.

These facts must not be compressed into one green `Published` badge. Givebutter
documents that an unlisted page may remain visible while its payment button is
disabled, and that recurring gifts can continue after a campaign is closed
([closing guidance](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1772204-how-to-close-or-unlist-a-campaign)).
**DOCUMENTED:** reach and accepting new gifts can diverge. **INFERRED:** a single
badge would give staff and missionaries false operational confidence.

When the requested default and effective reach differ, show one plain-language
resolution immediately below the reach value, for example:

> Your organization requested **Listed publicly**. Safety rules currently
> limit this page to **Shared by link — public**.

The secondary `Why?` disclosure may show the owning Phase 10 verdict, evidence
time, and who can resolve it. It must not expose restricted details to a staff
member who lacks permission. Do not label the page `Failed` when Phase 10 has
correctly reduced exposure.

Actions should be consequence-named:

- `Preview the public page` renders the exact current safe projection, never an
  unrestricted editor preview;
- `Copy public link` appears only for a currently anonymous page and repeats
  `Anyone with this link can view and reshare it` for direct-link pages;
- `Request wider reach` starts the authorized D1 review path and is absent when
  the actor cannot request it;
- `Reduce reach` opens a short impact review; and
- `View publication history` is secondary disclosure, not a prerequisite for
  ordinary work.

No reach change should occur merely by selecting a radio. W3C's
[Understanding On Input](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/on-input)
identifies automatically submitting a form or unexpectedly changing context
from a radio/select change as a failure pattern and describes a separate submit
button as a sufficient technique. **INFERRED:** selection updates an inert
consequence preview; the explicit action performs the authorized change.

Bulk administration should be exception-first. The default list shows the
effective reach and only highlights `Safety limit changed`, `Consent missing`,
`Needs review`, `Stale evidence`, or `Requested and effective reach differ`.
There should be no per-row visibility toggle. A bulk reduction requires a
selected scope, consequence summary, exact affected count, and one final
confirmation; bulk widening is not offered.

### 13.4 Missionary dashboard UX should answer one question: "What can people see?"

Each assigned page card should show:

- the Page Family and public presentation name;
- one plain-language reach label with the same consequence sentence used by
  staff;
- `View page` and, when appropriate, `Copy public link`;
- the current draft/review state separately from the live reach; and
- a calm explanation when a requested edit is awaiting staff review while the
  prior safe revision remains live.

The contributor's editor must not contain SEO or reach toggles. A contributor
may request wider reach only when the tenant allows such requests; the control
must say `Request wider reach`, not `Make public`. D1 page-edit authority does
not imply publication authority.

An exact represented person who owns the applicable publishing-consent control
receives one persistent `Stop showing me publicly` action. It opens a concise
confirmation that states the immediate Asym-controlled result and the honest
limit:

> This will stop new public access to your page now and notify your
> organization. Links, screenshots, messages, search results, or copies already
> shared outside Asym may remain.

The action must not require a reason, staff approval, support ticket, password
re-entry, or navigation into settings. After confirmation, it moves the page to
the exact safest result, announces success, and explains whether the entire page
was contained or only that participant was removed from a still-safe project
projection. Restoring exposure is a separate authorized release; it is not an
`Undo` toast.

The [ICO's current consent guidance](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/lawful-basis/consent/how-should-we-obtain-record-and-manage-consent/)
requires consent withdrawal to be as easy as giving it and requires evidence of
what was agreed. **INFERRED:** the exposure-reduction action must be easy and
immediate, while the system preserves the exact prior evidence rather than
deleting or rewriting it.

Notifications should be exception-based:

- notify the represented person when a page first becomes anonymous, widens
  from direct-link to listed, or stops being public;
- notify assigned contributors only when their action is required or their
  public representation changed;
- notify the accountable staff queue for safety containment, unresolved review,
  or failed purge work; and
- do not send routine messages every time the derived ceiling is rechecked and
  remains unchanged.

### 13.5 Accessibility and mobile requirements are part of the safety contract

- Use native HTML radios inside a `fieldset` with a visible `legend`; each
  option has a persistent visible label and description connected
  programmatically. W3C's
  [Labels or Instructions guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions)
  requires option controls to have labels that explain what is being selected,
  while the
  [WAI radio-group pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/)
  defines expected arrow-key, Space, and Tab behavior. **RECOMMENDED:** prefer
  native radio semantics over a custom three-state segmented control.
- Reach, review, and safety states must include text and an icon/shape where
  useful; green, amber, or red cannot be the only carrier. WCAG 2.2
  [Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color)
  prohibits color as the only way to convey an action or state.
- Async save, containment, copy-link, review-submission, and purge results must
  be exposed as programmatic status messages without unnecessarily stealing
  focus. WCAG 2.2
  [Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages)
  requires assistive technology to receive status changes that do not take
  focus.
- Failed saves and blocked changes must identify the exact problem in text and
  say what the user can do. WCAG 2.2
  [Error Identification](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-identification)
  says redisplaying a form without a textual explanation is insufficient.
- The consequence review provides a correctable confirmation before a
  publication widening or broad live reduction. WCAG 2.2
  [Error Prevention](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-prevention-legal-financial-data.html)
  calls for important stored-data changes to be reversible, checked, or
  confirmed. Immediate Phase 10 safety containment remains deliberately
  non-blocking because delaying it would preserve the unsafe exposure.
- Every control meets at least the WCAG 2.2
  [24 by 24 CSS-pixel target requirement](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum),
  with the WCAG
  [44-by-44 enhanced target](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced)
  as the design target for the primary card/action surfaces where practical.
  This matters especially for `Stop showing me publicly` and mobile choice
  cards, where accidental adjacent activation has a high consequence.
- The setup, page summary, consequence preview, and confirmation must reflow to
  one column without lost information or two-dimensional scrolling at a width
  equivalent to 320 CSS pixels, as required by WCAG 2.2
  [Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html). Do not use a
  desktop-only visibility matrix on mobile; stack the three choice cards and
  keep the primary action after the full consequence summary in reading order.
- Automated axe checks are necessary but insufficient. Production-shaped tests
  must include keyboard-only use, screen-reader announcements, 200% text zoom,
  400%/320-CSS-pixel reflow, high contrast, touch input, and reduced-motion
  behavior because the WAI radio example itself warns that custom ARIA examples
  can have browser and assistive-technology support gaps
  ([WAI example warning](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/radio/examples/radio/)).

### 13.6 Ruthless UX failure review and permanent prevention

| Concern                         | What could go wrong and why it matters                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Severity | Likelihood                 | Permanent prevention                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Misleading direct-link language | Staff or missionaries read `unlisted`, `hidden`, or a lock icon as private and share sensitive content. YouTube, Google Drive, Squarespace, Wix, and Givebutter all document that link-only or navigation-hidden content remains reachable. | Critical | High without explicit copy | Always label the mode **Shared by link — public** and persist `Anyone with the link can view and reshare it. This is not private.` beside every selection and copy-link action. |
| Toggle-matrix contradiction     | Independent menu, search, sitemap, indexing, CTA, asset, and API toggles disagree, exposing one egress after another is hidden. The CMS comparators document that these controls have different effects.                                    | Critical | High                       | One semantic reach radio group; derive every egress; no common-path SEO switches.                                                                                               |
| Silent ceiling substitution     | Staff choose Listed but see Shared by link later and assume Asym malfunctioned, or incorrectly report that a worker is listed.                                                                                                              | High     | High                       | Show requested default, effective reach, the stricter owning authority, evidence time, and resolution owner in plain language.                                                  |
| Editorial/reach conflation      | Saving or submitting a draft unexpectedly changes the live page, or a `Published` badge hides a stopped CTA.                                                                                                                                | High     | High                       | Separate Content, Public reach, and Giving facts in every staff and missionary summary.                                                                                         |
| Unsafe initial default          | A preselected Listed option is accepted without conscious review during first setup. GOV.UK warns preselected radios increase missed questions and wrong answers.                                                                           | Critical | Medium                     | No selection on first policy setup; fail-safe behavior remains Not public until an authorized default is saved.                                                                 |
| Live change on selection        | Merely selecting a radio publishes, widens, or suppresses a page, creating accidental exposure or outage and violating predictable-control guidance.                                                                                        | Critical | Medium                     | Selection only updates a consequence preview; an explicit, permission-checked action commits the operation.                                                                     |
| Hidden bulk blast radius        | A tenant-default edit silently changes hundreds of currently public pages.                                                                                                                                                                  | Critical | Medium                     | Defaults are prospective; any live reduction is a separately named operation with exact scope, counts, samples, and confirmation. Never bulk-widen.                             |
| Exposure-stop friction          | A represented person cannot quickly reduce exposure during a safety event because the action requires staff approval or a support ticket.                                                                                                   | Critical | Medium                     | Persistent dashboard action, one concise confirmation, immediate smallest-scope containment, append-only evidence, staff notification after containment.                        |
| False reversibility             | An `Undo` message implies externally copied content, previews, or search caches can be recalled.                                                                                                                                            | High     | High                       | Explain controlled Asym removal versus third-party persistence; restoration uses a new authorized release, not toast undo.                                                      |
| Alert fatigue                   | Routine derivation checks generate messages until users ignore the actual safety exception.                                                                                                                                                 | High     | High at scale              | Notify only on first exposure, widening, containment, action-required review, or failed controlled purge; unchanged checks remain quiet.                                        |
| Color/icon-only status          | Users with low vision, color-vision differences, or assistive technology cannot distinguish safe from public states.                                                                                                                        | High     | Medium                     | Persistent textual labels, programmatic semantics, visible focus, and non-color indicators.                                                                                     |
| Mobile truncation               | Long consequence text or a desktop matrix hides the reshare warning or final action on small screens.                                                                                                                                       | High     | High                       | Single-column card layout, full wrapping text, minimum target sizes, reflow and real-device verification.                                                                       |
| Stale confirmation              | Reach changes between opening and confirming a form, so the user approves an obsolete impact summary.                                                                                                                                       | Critical | Medium                     | Bind the review to the exact current policy/page/evidence version; re-resolve at commit and return a readable changed-since-review result instead of silently applying.         |

### 13.7 Production-shaped UX proofs added by this research

1. In moderated testing, staff correctly distinguish all three reach outcomes
   from the persistent consequence copy without opening documentation or an
   advanced panel; no participant describes direct-link public as private.
2. First-time setup has no selected radio and leaves the system fail-safe until
   an authorized save. Returning to an existing policy shows its exact current
   version and prospective scope without changing it on load.
3. Selecting an option with mouse, touch, keyboard, switch control, or screen
   reader changes only the local preview. The separate save/release action has
   the same visible and accessible name and receives the final authorization
   check.
4. When Phase 10 caps a requested Listed default at Shared by link or Not
   public, staff and affected contributors see the effective result, the
   non-sensitive reason, evidence freshness, and correct owner of the next
   action. No UI offers an override.
5. Staff can change a future default without changing any live revision. A
   separately invoked bulk reduction lists the exact affected Site, Page
   Family, current reach, resulting reach, count, exceptions, and sampled pages;
   a concurrent change invalidates the review before commit.
6. A missionary edits a draft while the previous safe revision remains live;
   both truths are apparent on a 320-CSS-pixel-wide screen without horizontal
   scrolling or hidden consequence text.
7. An eligible represented person reaches `Stop showing me publicly` directly
   from the assigned page card, understands the consequence, confirms it, and
   receives an accessible success result. The unsafe surface is contained before
   any staff approval or notification dependency.
8. A direct-link page's copy action repeats the public/reshare warning and never
   uses `private`, `secure`, `confidential`, a lock-only icon, or an identity
   claim. Rotating the link makes the old URL unusable without implying that
   already copied content disappeared.
9. Reach, content review, and Giving states can each change independently, and
   every staff/missionary view continues to label all three accurately without
   collapsing them into `Published`, `Active`, or one color.
10. Screen-reader, keyboard-only, zoom/reflow, high-contrast, touch-target, and
    failure-state tests cover setup, page-level review, bulk reduction,
    copy-link, safety containment, and async status announcements. An automated
    accessibility pass alone does not satisfy the release proof.

**UX recommendation:** retain Option C-prime, but ratify it only with one
consequence-first radio model, prospective tenant defaults, visible
requested-versus-effective resolution, independently labelled content/reach/
Giving truth, a no-hoops represented-person exposure-stop action, and exact
accessible impact review for every live or bulk change. This gives ordinary
staff a three-choice interface while keeping the large safety state space in the
policy resolver and evidence model rather than in the user's head.

## 14. D3 framing evidence: page composition and tenant customization

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. This section frames one unresolved founder
decision. It does not ratify a choice.

### 14.1 Comparable products separate an organization-owned page system from bounded participant content

- **DOCUMENTED:** Raisely models a fundraiser profile as participant data
  rendered through one dynamic profile page. The organization designs the
  profile page and chooses its fields; the logged-in fundraiser dashboard lets
  the fundraiser view and edit the resulting profile. It supports typed
  Individual, Team, and Organisation profile families rather than giving every
  participant an unrelated site builder.
  [Understanding Fundraiser Profiles](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649205175565-Understanding-Fundraiser-Profiles),
  [Managing Fundraisers](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649207914637-Managing-Fundraisers).
- **DOCUMENTED:** Givebutter lets a team member edit a bounded public-page set:
  display name, optional goal, story, photo, links, and video. The surrounding
  campaign page remains the organization's campaign surface.
  [Givebutter team-member page](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3270211-how-to-manage-your-team-member-page).
- **DOCUMENTED:** GoFundMe Pro separates organization design controls from
  participant customization. Staff can set page defaults, prevent fundraisers
  from changing headlines or goals, and control progress/comments; donation
  page settings are shared and cannot be edited by supporters.
  [GoFundMe Pro Classic peer-to-peer campaign](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288738226587-Create-a-Classic-peer-to-peer-campaign).
- **INFERRED:** The proven low-friction pattern is neither a completely fixed
  page nor an unrestricted per-participant builder. It is an organization-owned
  presentation system with an intentionally small participant-editable content
  surface.

### 14.2 Payload can implement a bounded catalog, but does not define Asym's product policy

- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload Blocks fields accept a finite block catalog, field
  access rules, validation, row limits, localization, and conditional block
  filtering. This is sufficient substrate for typed, certified page sections.
  [Payload Blocks](https://payloadcms.com/docs/fields/blocks).
- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload versions, drafts, and autosave preserve a published
  revision while newer draft revisions are edited, and support version history
  and diffs. Draft visibility still requires explicit access control.
  [Payload versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview),
  [Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts).
- **INFERRED:** Payload's ability to expose arbitrary blocks, fields, custom
  components, raw rich content, and publish actions is not evidence that those
  capabilities should be exposed to missionaries. Phase 22 must define the
  smaller product contract, and its application service must enforce that
  contract independently of the CMS admin interface.

### 14.3 The current repository is useful substrate but is not the Phase 22 contract

`apps/admin/src/cms/collections/page-builders.ts` already defines a seven-block
catalog and draft autosave. The same source also demonstrates why a direct
adoption would be unsafe:

- the layout is one freely sortable block list with no tenant profile, required
  zones, contributor-specific field authority, or release-pinned schema
  generation;
- the Hero and Call to Action blocks accept arbitrary destination URLs, while
  Phase 22 requires an exact Phase 13 Designation Binding and managed checkout
  handoff;
- `missionaryId` and `fundId` are soft text references for only one subject;
- the CMS collection has tenant-wide staff access rather than D1's exact
  page-scoped contributor contract; and
- Payload draft/published status cannot replace D2's Page Release Manifest or
  Publication Reach.

**INFERRED:** retain and evolve the shared block/configuration seam, but do not
make the current collection or Payload UI the authority seen by missionaries.

### 14.4 Decision boundary

The next decision is how much composition authority exists inside each typed
Page Family. It must preserve these already-settled boundaries:

- D1 owns explicit page-scoped contributor authority and bounded editing,
  including deliberate **Submit for review** or, in D4's tenant-configured
  automatic lane, **Publish changes**;
- D2 owns public reach and immutable release truth;
- Phase 10 owns every public-safe identity, content, and media ceiling;
- Phase 13 owns the Designation and checkout destination;
- Phase 23 owns general-purpose CMS/Web Studio breadth; and
- The Phase 29-compatible boundary owns governed media and file processing.

The decision must not reopen those owners or let contributors choose or widen
reach, manufacture publication authority, or control identity, Designation,
route, lifecycle, or arbitrary code. An authorized contributor may initiate
**Publish changes** only through D4's tenant-configured automatic lane, where
the system executes the tenant's standing authority after all current proofs.

### 14.5 Options for founder selection

#### Option A — Fixed system templates

Asym supplies one code-owned layout per Page Family. Tenants choose branding;
missionaries edit only named fields such as story, update, and approved photo.

- **Benefits:** lowest cognitive load; strongest accessibility, performance,
  and safety consistency; easiest regression testing.
- **Costs:** missions organizations and projects have legitimate presentation
  differences; each new layout need becomes an engineering request; staff may
  fall back to the general CMS or an external site.
- **Primary risk:** excessive rigidity becomes long-term product and operational
  debt.

#### Option B — Unrestricted per-page builder

Staff and contributors can add and reorder arbitrary blocks, styles, embeds,
and page-specific layouts.

- **Benefits:** maximum local expression and immediate customization.
- **Costs:** complex editing, inconsistent branding, difficult reviews,
  inaccessible or slow pages, schema/migration burden, and a blurred Phase 23
  boundary.
- **Primary risk:** contributors can remove or imitate managed financial and
  safety surfaces, introduce hostile external content, or create pages that
  cannot be reliably certified.

#### Option C-prime — Versioned tenant Presentation Profiles with bounded typed blocks — Recommended

One guided tenant default is scoped by Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, and Page
Family. An immutable prospective profile version chooses a certified shell,
allowed optional blocks, required managed blocks, permitted regions/order, and
the exact fields contributors may edit. Staff may choose among a small set of
certified variants and sparse page-specific exceptions; missionaries edit
content and may add or reorder only allowed optional blocks inside the allowed
regions.

The organization controls branding, required gift/discretion language,
validated Giving and progress surfaces, public identity placement, footer, and
other managed blocks. Those blocks are visibly read-only in the missionary
dashboard and say `Provided by your organization`. Raw HTML/CSS/JavaScript,
arbitrary React, arbitrary forms, unrestricted iframes/embeds, external scripts,
arbitrary CTA URLs, and tenant-authored query expressions are unavailable.

Each release pins the exact Presentation Profile version, block-schema
generation, locale, and content revision. A later profile change is prospective
and first shows its exact affected-page preview; it does not silently rewrite
live pages. The tenant setup uses visual previews and the plain sections
`Required`, `Available`, and `Missionaries may edit`, not a schema or workflow
designer. The missionary surface uses task language such as `Edit story`, `Add
an update`, and `Choose photo`, not CMS block terminology.

- **Benefits:** meaningful tenant flexibility and individual expression without
  turning Phase 22 into a website builder; compatible with D1 review, D2
  immutable releases, accessibility certification, and future block evolution.
- **Costs:** Asym must govern a finite block catalog, profile-version
  compatibility, migrations, and production-shaped certification.
- **Primary risks:** profile proliferation, hidden layout/content coupling, and
  override confusion. Bound them with a finite catalog, a small certified
  variant set, sparse typed overrides, exact version pins, impact preview, and
  no custom-code escape hatch.

### 14.6 Recommendation and next adversarial gate

Choose **Option C-prime**. It matches the organization-template plus bounded
participant-content pattern documented by Raisely, Givebutter, and GoFundMe Pro,
while using Payload's current block/version capabilities without exposing
Payload's full complexity or authority.

If selected, the next adversarial pass must individually test block ownership,
required-block behavior, managed CTA/progress fallbacks, contributor field
access, rich-text and embed safety, locale behavior, profile changes, per-page
exceptions, version migration, accessibility, performance, cache impact, and
the difference between staff content replacement and contributor attribution.

## 15. D3 adversarial evidence: versioned family profiles and Ministry Updates

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. The founder selected Option C-prime for
adversarial hardening and subsequently ratified the resulting C-prime-R as
Phase 22 D3. This section records the evidence and resulting guardrails.

### 15.1 Two page families require two semantic catalogs

- **DOCUMENTED:** Raisely separates Individual, Team, and Organisation profile
  types and renders each through organization-configured profile pages while
  giving fundraisers a bounded dashboard editor. Givebutter lets participants
  edit a small field set inside an organization-owned campaign. GoFundMe Pro
  similarly separates fundraiser story/details/updates from organization-owned
  campaign and donation-page controls.
  [Raisely fundraiser profiles](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649205175565-Understanding-Fundraiser-Profiles),
  [Givebutter team-member pages](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3270211-how-to-manage-your-team-member-page),
  [GoFundMe Pro fundraiser editor](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288767905179-Edit-a-fundraising-page).
- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload Blocks supplies a finite catalog, row limits,
  validation, field access, localization, and conditional availability. It does
  not supply Asym's family semantics, public authorization, activation contract,
  or D2 release truth.
  [Payload Blocks](https://payloadcms.com/docs/fields/blocks),
  [Payload access control](https://payloadcms.com/docs/access-control/overview).
- **INFERRED:** Missionary Ministry and Project/Campaign pages may share visual
  primitives and publication machinery, but one universal polymorphic layout
  would accumulate conditional fields and unsafe substitutions. Each family
  therefore needs its own code-certified semantic catalog, required managed
  blocks, optional blocks, contributor slots, shell, and compatibility tests.

The ordinary tenant receives one tested accessible built-in default per family.
Tenant configuration is intentionally bounded: a small set of certified shells,
allowed optional blocks, permitted zones/order, and exact contributor-editable
slots. There is no raw HTML, CSS, JavaScript, form/query language, arbitrary CTA
URL, iframe, or per-page schema fork.

### 15.2 Presentation Profile truth must not be a mutable Payload template

The current repository's `page-builders` collection has one freely sortable
seven-block list, arbitrary Hero/CTA URLs, soft single-subject text references,
and tenant-wide staff access. Its `page-templates` collection is a mutable draft
document whose current layout is copied into new pages. Neither collection pins
an immutable profile version, schema generation, resolved digest, exact
Tenant x Legal Entity x Site x Page Family scope, impact cohort, or D2 release.

**INFERRED:** retain Payload for bounded authoring content, drafts, and editor
machinery. Place immutable `Public Page Presentation Profile Version`,
prospective activation/binding, exact scope, sparse typed page exception,
compatibility/impact manifest, and Page Release pins behind Asym's operational
Postgres/service boundary. Resolve only:

1. an exact approved page exception;
2. the exact active family profile; or
3. the certified built-in family baseline.

Profile versions are complete documents, never fragment/deep-merge rules. A
live page pins its exact profile version, block-schema generation, resolved
layout digest, content revision, and locale. A profile change applies to new
releases prospectively. Updating existing pages first creates an exact,
CAS-guarded draft cohort and impact manifest; it never silently rewrites or
widens a live page.

Payload's Local API bypasses access control by default, so every product call
must pass an actor and `overrideAccess: false`; global block definitions may
share schema but cannot authorize a page or tenant.
[Payload Local API access](https://payloadcms.com/docs/local-api/overview),
[Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts).

### 15.3 Ministry Updates remain one canonical cross-surface concept

`CONTEXT.md` and the merged platform-surface contract already define a
**Ministry Update** as a missionary-authored post governed once and surfaced
across missionary, staff, public, donor, and communication experiences. It is
explicitly not public-page content and not a one-off email.

The current code has conflicting incomplete paths: Payload `ministry-updates`
stores one missionary relationship, the public reader returns tenant-wide
recent updates, and the missionary feed can write mutable public posts. None is
safe to infer into a page by tenant, display subject, contributor, author,
Support Assignment, or `public`/`published` flag.

The permanent page contract is therefore:

- a Presentation Profile controls only whether, where, and how many canonical
  updates the page displays;
- an immutable, exact **Ministry Update Feed Binding** selects the eligible
  canonical update source stream or source set for that page;
- the Page Release pins the feed binding, not copies or a frozen list of posts;
- each update keeps its own immutable revision, moderation/release, visibility,
  locale, Phase 10 verdict, retirement, and independently authoritative
  notification/distribution outcome;
- each served item must satisfy the strictest current page reach, update
  release/visibility, Phase 10, locale, and containment truth;
- the public preview is bounded and deterministic, ordered by
  `(released_at, opaque_id)` with a cursor-based archive; and
- an empty or temporarily unprovable feed collapses quietly on the public page,
  while the missionary dashboard presents the useful `Write your first update`
  action.

For spouses or teams, the source set is explicit; it is never inferred from
display membership. A Project/Campaign page may consume Ministry Updates only
when the canonical update owner provides an exact project/purpose binding. It
must not display a missionary's posts merely because that person contributes to
or appears on the project page. A future Project Update source may implement the
same bounded feed projection contract without redefining Ministry Update.

Givebutter and GoFundMe Pro both treat updates as separately managed posts, and
GoFundMe Pro separates a page's Updates workspace from its story/details.
Givebutter also treats public posting and supporter email distribution as
separate choices, supporting Asym's independent publication and notification
truths.
[Givebutter campaign updates](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/5497893-how-to-use-campaign-updates),
[GoFundMe Pro fundraiser editor](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288767905179-Edit-a-fundraising-page).

### 15.4 Security, accessibility, performance, and dependency findings

- Rich content uses an allowlisted AST and server-side validation/sanitization;
  URLs use protocol/domain allowlists; governed Phase 29-compatible media is transformed,
  metadata-scrubbed, dimensioned, and alt-text checked. CSP is defense in depth,
  not the sanitizer. Raw embeds are unavailable.
  [OWASP XSS Prevention](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html),
  [OWASP File Upload](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html).
- The authoring experience must itself be accessible and help authors produce
  accessible output. Reordering needs keyboard/button alternatives rather than
  drag-only controls; validation, save, conflict, review, and release states
  need programmatic announcements.
  [W3C ATAG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/atag/),
  [W3C forms](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/forms/).
- Compile a privacy-minimized render plan at D2 release rather than joining the
  entire CMS/profile/operational graph on each public request. Cache identity
  includes exact tenant, site, page, locale, release, profile version, and
  safety generation; invalidation is targeted by page/profile/feed rather than
  a tenant-global purge. The feed is bounded and indexed, media has budgets,
  and editor JavaScript is absent from the public render.
- The repository pins an internal Payload 4 prerelease. Official Payload docs
  are directionally useful, but activation requires adapter/contract tests
  against the installed build, documented APIs only, and a retained legacy
  renderer for every still-referenced schema generation.

### 15.5 Production proof and migration requirements

Before activation, production-shaped tests must prove family separation,
required managed blocks, contributor field allowlists, exact tenant/site/legal
entity scope, profile immutability and single-active resolution, CAS conflict
behavior, old-release stability, unknown-generation fail-closed behavior,
preview/live renderer parity, exact page/feed binding, deterministic pagination,
no tenant-wide update leak, Phase 10 enforcement at every egress, safe URL/rich
text/media handling, targeted cache invalidation, keyboard/mobile accessibility,
and performance for every certified variant.

Legacy pages and both incomplete update stores require a manifest-driven
classification and shadow compile. Each record is adopted, mapped, quarantined,
retained under a legacy renderer, or retired with evidence. No old
`missionaryId`, `fundId`, copied identity field, generic block, `_status`, or
`visibility = public` value is treated as proof of a D1 binding, D2 release, D3
profile, or Phase 10 public-safe projection.

### 15.6 Adversarial verdict

Option C-prime is the correct direction only as two family-specific,
immutable, code-certified Presentation Profile systems under one shared
contract. The Ministry Updates section is a managed projection over exact
canonical source bindings, not an editable layout container or duplicate post
store. Strong defaults and prospective, impact-reviewed activation preserve the
tenant flexibility the founder wants without creating a general website builder,
silent live rewrites, or a second update domain.

**Ratification:** the founder ratified the hardened formulation as Phase 22 D3
on 2026-08-03. The binding decision and source-of-truth boundaries are recorded
in the Phase 22 decision log and ADR-0120.

## 16. D4 framing evidence: review and release policy

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. This section frames one unresolved founder
decision. It does not ratify a choice or reopen D1-D3.

### 16.1 The merged contract requires both moderation and tenant-authorized automatic release

The merged `platform-boundaries` OpenSpec requires missionary-managed public
content to follow tenant-configured approval and moderation rules. It also
requires Asym to respect a tenant's choice to allow automatic publishing for an
allowed content path rather than inventing a universal manual gate.

D1 already separates contributor access from Page Release Authority. D2
requires immutable Page Release Manifests and current safety reproof. D3
separates page revisions, managed projections, Presentation Profile Versions,
and independently released Ministry Updates. None yet decides which exact
submitted revisions require a human review or may execute standing tenant release
policy automatically.

### 16.2 Existing CMS state is insufficient release evidence

- The current tenant access helpers grant broad tenant-staff collection access;
  they do not express exact submission, reviewer, semantic-diff, or release
  authority.
- The current audit hook records that Payload `_status` changed, not an exact
  submitted revision, current policy, reviewer decision, Phase 10 evidence, or
  D2 release activation.
- The public reader correctly requests only published CMS documents, but
  `_status = published` is content availability, not Asym's moderation,
  safety, reach, or release proof.
- Payload drafts and versions are useful editing substrate and can restrict who
  sets `_status = published`; they do not establish Phase 22's tenant policy or
  immutable business approval contract.
  [Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts),
  [Payload versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview).

### 16.3 Comparator evidence supports tenant moderation but exposes the all-or-nothing problem

- **DOCUMENTED:** Blackbaud TeamRaiser can place new or modified participant
  personal pages in a pending state until an administrator approves them. Its
  event setting can also disable that approval requirement.
  [TeamRaiser participant pages](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_participants_personalpages.html),
  [TeamRaiser advanced options](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_configuring_blueprints_03cselectingadvancedeventoptions.html).
- **DOCUMENTED:** CiviCRM can require administrator approval before a Personal
  Campaign Page becomes active.
  [CiviCRM Personal Campaign Pages](https://beta.docs.civicrm.org/user/contributions/personal-campaign-pages/).
- **INFERRED:** a single mandatory-review setting is proven and understandable,
  but treats punctuation, a new family photograph, a location disclosure, and
  a Giving-destination change as equivalent. A blanket automatic/manual switch
  instead forces the tenant to choose between speed and safety for the entire
  Page Family. Neither is sufficient for Asym's restricted-worker and managed
  financial surfaces.

### 16.4 Concrete scenario

Harbor Missions gives Daniel and Ruth separate contributor access to their
shared Missionary Ministry Page. Ruth corrects punctuation in already approved
copy. Daniel uploads a new family photograph and changes a generalized region
to a city. Staff changes the Giving destination and progress source. A
restricted missionary submits a new Ministry Update. Harbor wants routine safe
corrections to move quickly, but never wants identity, location, media, reach,
Giving, progress, or restricted-worker changes to bypass qualified review.

Phase 22 needs one policy that distinguishes these submissions without asking
staff to build a workflow graph or letting an author label their own change
safe.

### 16.5 Options for founder selection

#### Option A — Human review for every submitted revision

Every page or Ministry Update submission waits for an authorized staff member
to release that exact revision.

- **Benefits:** simplest conservative mental model; direct approval evidence;
  close to Blackbaud and CiviCRM's moderation modes.
- **Costs:** every typo competes with new media and sensitive-location changes;
  creates queue fatigue, stale public content, and eventual rubber-stamping;
  imposes an unwanted manual gate on tenants that intentionally permit
  automatic publication.
- **Primary risk:** operational burden weakens the quality of the review that
  actually matters.

#### Option B — Tenant-wide automatic/manual switch

For each Site and Page Family, the tenant chooses either `Staff reviews every
change` or `Publish automatically`; every valid submission follows that choice.

- **Benefits:** extremely simple setup and implementation.
- **Costs:** one mistaken setting has a large blast radius; ordinary text,
  location, media, metadata, locale, profile, progress, and Giving changes share
  one policy; page exceptions quickly become a flag matrix.
- **Primary risk:** apparent simplicity hides materially different safety and
  financial consequences.

#### Option C-prime — Versioned semantic Review & Release Profiles — Recommended

One prospective immutable profile is scoped by Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, and
publication path: Missionary Ministry Page, Project/Campaign Page, or Ministry
Update. Staff choose only:

1. **Review every submitted revision** — the safe default; or
2. **Publish routine changes automatically** — only a closed, code-certified
   catalog of low-risk semantic changes may qualify.

Asym computes the complete semantic diff and re-proves the entire resulting
revision. The tenant does not design rules or declare a change safe. Unknown or
unclassified change always requires review.

Non-waivable human-review floors include first public release, reach widening,
subject/display identity or consent changes, new location disclosure, media or
media-metadata changes, routes/slugs/locales/fallbacks, Presentation Profile or
feed-binding changes, Designation/Giving/legal-language/progress changes,
restricted/high-risk subjects, and any stale, missing, contradictory,
`needs_review`, or blocked Phase 10 evidence.

A routine editorial submission may release automatically only when every change
belongs to the closed low-risk catalog, remains inside D3 contributor-editable
slots, the full resulting revision passes current Phase 10 and content safety,
the exact contributor assignment and tenant policy are current, and D2's sole
release command succeeds. This is system execution of tenant-owned Page Release
Authority—not publication authority granted to the contributor.

- **Benefits:** preserves tenant choice without a workflow DSL; keeps small-team
  content current; reserves human attention for consequential changes; supplies
  one coherent contract for pages and independent Ministry Updates.
- **Costs:** the semantic classifier and low-risk catalog require versioning,
  exhaustive hidden-egress coverage, and maintenance whenever D3 adds a field
  or block.
- **Primary risk:** unsafe misclassification. Permanently contain it by making
  the catalog closed, full-revision proof mandatory, and every unknown manual.

### 16.6 Recommended UX and next adversarial gate

Staff configure one plain-language choice in **Settings → Public ministry pages
→ Review policy**, with separate cards only for the publication paths they use.
`Publish routine changes automatically` expands a short, code-owned explanation
of what always stops for review. It is not a field or workflow matrix.

Contributors see `Draft saved`, `Submitted`, `Publishing after checks`, `Needs
staff review`, `Changes requested`, or `Live`. Staff receive one
exception-first queue showing the exact visual/text/media/metadata diff, plain
`Why this needs review` reasons, and `Publish this revision` or `Request
changes`. Healthy automatic releases remain quiet.

Choose **Option C-prime**. If selected, the adversarial pass must test rich-text
smuggling, hidden metadata/OG/JSON-LD/locale/media changes, policy or safety
changes after approval, automatic-release races with containment, every Payload
and scheduled-publish bypass, stale restore, notification overload,
segregation-of-duties loops for one-person tenants, and the separation of page
release, Ministry Update release, public reach, Giving, cache propagation, and
communication delivery.

## 17. D4 adversarial evidence: tenant-chosen review or publish-after-checks

**Research date:** 2026-08-03. The founder selected Versioned semantic Review &
Release Profiles and clarified that the tenant, not Asym, decides whether an
authorized missionary submission waits for staff review or can go live without
staff review. This section pressure-tests and hardens that direction. It records
research and a proposed formulation only; D4 is not ratified here.

### 17.1 The choice corrects an overreach in the initial framing

The initial C-prime framing made automatic release available only to a
platform-defined catalog of "routine" changes and imposed broad human-review
floors for media, geography, first release, and other semantic categories. That
would quietly reinsert Asym's review preference after the tenant chose automatic
publishing, contrary to the merged `platform-boundaries` contract.

The hardened distinction is narrower and more honest:

- **Review before publishing:** an authorized staff member must review the exact
  submitted revision before release.
- **Publish after checks:** the contributor deliberately chooses `Publish
changes`; Asym releases that exact revision without staff review when every
  current owning-phase, authority, structural, privacy, safety, media, link,
  accessibility, and reference proof succeeds.
- Autosave is private in both modes. It never creates release intent.
- Phase 10 remains an independently authoritative ceiling. `allowed` may use the
  tenant's automatic lane, `needs_review` follows Phase 10's authorized human
  review path, and `blocked` cannot release. A missing, stale, contradictory, or
  unavailable non-substitutable proof remains a cause-owned `Needs attention`
  exception until the owning proof is restored; a reviewer cannot click around
  it. This is not a discretionary Asym editorial gate.
- Contributor-editable D3 slots may include text and media. An allowed media or
  location change is not forced to human review solely because of its semantic
  type when the tenant chose `Publish after checks`.
- D1/D3 managed identity, Giving, route, reach, Presentation Profile, feed, and
  financial facts remain non-contributor-editable. They follow their owning
  staff and release contracts rather than masquerading as missionary content.

"Semantic" therefore means a deterministic, exhaustive understanding of the
candidate's complete public consequences and required proof plan. It does not
mean an AI risk score, author-selected risk, or a hidden platform rule that
overrides an otherwise allowed tenant automatic lane.

### 17.2 Current product evidence supports both tenant postures

- **DOCUMENTED:** Blackbaud TeamRaiser can hold new or modified participant
  pages pending administrator approval while the prior/default page remains
  public. CiviCRM exposes an `Approval Required` option for Personal Campaign
  Pages. These establish review-before-live as familiar nonprofit behavior.
  [Blackbaud participant pages](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/lo/content/teamraiser_participants_personalpages.html),
  [CiviCRM Personal Campaign Pages](https://docs.civicrm.org/user/en/latest/contributions/personal-campaign-pages/).
- **DOCUMENTED:** Givebutter lets a team member edit bounded public-page fields
  and states that those changes appear on the public page. This establishes that
  a no-staff-review posture is also a reasonable fundraising-platform choice.
  [Givebutter team-member page](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3270211-how-to-manage-your-team-member-page).
- **DOCUMENTED:** GoFundMe Pro separates `Save` from `Publish/Update`; saved work
  does not affect the live campaign. This is the correct interaction model even
  when the tenant chooses no staff review.
  [GoFundMe Pro Studio](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288737506331-Create-a-Studio-donation-page).
- **DOCUMENTED:** HubSpot configures approvals by content type and supports
  approve/request-changes and mobile review. Its super-admin and per-user bypass
  lists are not appropriate Asym defaults because they make exact release
  authority harder to reason about.
  [HubSpot content approvals](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/website-and-landing-pages/approve-hubspot-content).
- **DOCUMENTED:** Sanity Content Releases preserve an exact version, preview,
  validation, and deliberate release. Contentful snapshots published versions
  and exposes comparisons. These support immutable release candidates and exact
  review evidence, not approval of a moving draft.
  [Sanity Content Releases](https://www.sanity.io/docs/studio/content-releases),
  [Contentful versioning](https://www.contentful.com/help/faq/versioning/).
- **DOCUMENTED:** Payload drafts and autosave separate saved work from published
  work, but setting `_status = published` can update the main collection even
  with `draft: true`; restore and schedule operations also exist. Payload is
  therefore authoring substrate, not Asym's product release authority.
  [Payload drafts](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/drafts),
  [Payload autosave](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/autosave),
  [Payload versions](https://payloadcms.com/docs/versions/overview).

### 17.3 Exact hardened contract

#### One prospective profile and one winning resolution

An immutable `Public Content Review & Release Profile Version` is scoped to the
exact Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, Page Family, environment, and publication path
(`page_revision` or `ministry_update`). The setup begins with one organization
preset and exposes only the paths the tenant uses under `Customize`. There is no
per-field matrix, workflow graph, risk-score configuration, or author bypass.

Until the tenant deliberately activates a profile, the UI truthfully identifies
Asym's safe fallback as `Review before publishing`; it must not pretend the
tenant selected it. Activation previews the exact affected paths and is
prospective:

- tightening from automatic to review stops queued automatic execution at its
  next current-policy reproof;
- loosening from review to automatic never drains or reinterprets an existing
  review backlog; staff may decide it or the contributor may create a new
  submission under the new profile;
- the submission preserves the profile version used to explain the author's
  action, while release also applies the current active policy and every current
  owning-phase proof. The stricter applicable result wins.

#### Immutable release candidate and complete semantic diff

Autosaves may remain Payload draft versions, but one deliberate `Submit for
review` or `Publish changes` action freezes an immutable candidate with:

- exact normalized content snapshot and digest;
- exact live base release and pointer generation;
- Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, Page Family, page/update identity, locale, and
  environment;
- actor and D1 contributor-assignment version;
- D3 Presentation Profile, semantic catalog, renderer, media, and feed-binding
  generations;
- active Review & Release Profile Version;
- complete canonical semantic diff and public-egress manifest;
- exact current Phase 10 and other required dependency evidence.

The semantic diff covers visible text, rich-text AST, links, added/removed or
reordered blocks, alt text, captions, media identity and derivatives, locale and
fallback output, metadata, canonical/OG/JSON-LD output, feed consequences, and
all other public renderer egress. A raw JSON patch or raw HTML comparison is not
sufficient. Every D3 field and block has an exhaustive code-owned
classification and proof plan. An unknown schema node or public egress
quarantines that release generation until engineering certifies it; ordinary
staff review cannot substitute for a proof the system cannot construct. AI may
suggest or flag content but never supplies release authority or a safety
verdict.

#### One manual/automatic release kernel

Manual and automatic modes execute the same sole idempotent release command.
Immediately before its compare-and-swap activation, it re-proves:

- the current actor/system principal and exact authority;
- the contributor assignment and reviewer/releaser capability where applicable;
- the immutable candidate, digest, base release, and current target head;
- current Review & Release Profile and semantic/renderer compatibility;
- current Phase 10 publication safety, consent, containment, and requested/effective
  D2 reach;
- current D3 profile/feed, media, locale, links, managed references, and all
  owning-domain dependencies.

Automatic release is system execution of the tenant's standing Page Release
Authority. It does not grant the contributor a generic publish capability. A
successful transaction writes the immutable D2 Page Release Manifest, advances
the exact current-release pointer with CAS, and records an outbox event. Manual
approval is an append-only decision bound to the exact candidate and is not
itself publication.

Payload Admin, `_status`, REST, GraphQL, Local API, service-role scripts, bulk
operations, restore, and native scheduled publishing cannot create D2 release
truth. Restore creates a new draft and candidate. A schedule pins one exact
candidate and merely wakes the same command, which fully re-proves at execution
time. Ambiguous outcomes are inspected by idempotency key before retry; only
uncompleted downstream effects retry.

#### Truth separation and failure posture

Draft saved, submitted, human-approved, automatically eligible, release
committed, publicly reachable, cache propagated, Giving ready, Ministry Update
released, supporter notification requested/delivered, search-indexed, and
externally discovered remain independently authoritative facts. The prior
certified release remains live until the replacement release commits. Cache,
search, sitemap, or notification failure does not rewrite release truth; an
idempotent outbox owns residual recovery. Current Phase 10 containment always
wins over a warm cache.

### 17.4 Quiet, mode-honest UX

#### Tenant setup

Use **Settings -> Public ministry pages -> Review and publishing**. The primary
screen contains one default choice and only the used content paths:

1. **Review before publishing**
   `A staff member reviews each missionary submission before it goes live.`
2. **Publish after checks**
   `Missionaries choose when to publish. Changes go live without staff review
after required privacy, safety, media, link, accessibility, and reference
checks pass. Anything needing judgment goes to staff review.`

`Customize` reveals at most Missionary Ministry Page revisions,
Project/Campaign Page revisions, and Ministry Updates. Before activation, show
the affected Site/Page Family paths, current pending-review count, and the
prospective rule. Do not auto-release the existing count. Keep optional
different-person review out of the default flow; it may be activated only when
an owning-phase or tenant policy needs it and eligible reviewer capacity plus an
escalation path are proved. A one-person tenant must not be trapped in fictional
dual control.

#### Missionary experience

- The editor always autosaves privately and says `Draft saved - your live page
has not changed.`
- In review mode the primary action is `Submit for review`; the persistent
  explanation is `Your organization reviews changes before they go live.`
- In automatic mode the primary action is `Publish changes`; the explanation is
  `Your changes go live after required checks.`
- The final consequence view uses the production renderer and summarizes the
  exact public page, locale, media, and update/notification consequences.
- After action, use mode-honest states: `Checking your changes`, `In review`,
  `Changes requested`, `Publishing`, `Live`, `Needs attention`, `Superseded`, or
  `The live page changed - review and resubmit`. Never use `Approved`, `Done`,
  or `Published` before that exact fact is true.
- If a mandatory proof is uncertain, preserve the private work and say plainly
  that the current live page is unchanged and staff review is needed. Do not
  present exception routing as lost work.
- Editing after submit creates a new working draft. It never mutates the
  submitted candidate.

Publishing a Ministry Update and notifying eligible supporters are separate
choices and outcomes. `Notify supporters` appears only when the tenant and
owning communication phase allow it and names the audience; a delivery failure
cannot undo a successful update release.

#### Staff review

Use one exception-first **Public page reviews** workspace. A row identifies the
page/update, author, exact Site and locale, age, change types, safe reason codes,
assigned reviewer, and one next action. Opening it provides:

- plain-language reason and change summary;
- exact semantic diff against the pinned live base;
- mobile-first public preview with desktop available;
- field-anchored comments;
- `Publish this revision` and `Request changes` actions;
- `Schedule publication` only as a secondary action.

Staff corrections create a new attributable candidate; they never mutate the
missionary's submission. Approval comments are optional; requesting changes
requires a concise actionable reason. Healthy automatic releases never appear
in the queue and do not notify staff.

The diff must not rely on red/green alone; it labels `Added`, `Removed`, and
`Changed`, reflows at 320 CSS pixels, has logical keyboard/focus order, retains
visible focus, announces concise save/check/release status without moving focus,
provides text errors and suggestions, supports non-drag alternatives and
adequate touch targets, and makes the authoring tool help produce accessible
content. These requirements follow WCAG 2.2 and ATAG's two-part authoring-tool
model.
[WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/),
[ATAG overview](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/atag/).

Every requested category has a concern. `Possible` means realistic in normal
product operation; it does not mean acceptable.
