| Other development hazards         | **Yes** | TOCTOU races, partial deployments, duplicate workers, clock/time-zone errors, revocation after checks, or impossible universal maker-checker rules create unsafe release or deadlock.                                    | Critical | Possible   | Re-prove inside target CAS transaction; pin compatible code/schema generations; UTC schedule plus site-zone display; idempotent workers/outbox; bounded kill switch/containment; maker-checker only when actually configured and capacity-proved; property, concurrency, RLS, bypass, accessibility, and production-shaped tests.                    |

### 17.6 Ruthless synthesis and ship order

1. **Make D2 the only public authority.** Public runtime resolves an immutable
   release snapshot and current D2 pointer, never current Payload `_status`.
2. **Define the exact candidate and semantic compiler.** Freeze the submitted
   content, base, scope, profile, complete egress, and proof generations; prove
   exhaustive D3 field/block coverage and unknown-generation quarantine.
3. **Build one release kernel.** Manual and automatic paths share current
   authority/safety/dependency reproof, target CAS, immutable manifest,
   idempotency, and transactional outbox.
4. **Close every alternate path.** Reject governed raw publish; make restore a
   draft; disable native schedule authority; test REST, GraphQL, Local API,
   Admin, bulk, job, service-role, stale preview, and direct-database paths.
5. **Deliver the two-choice UX.** Guided setup, explicit submit/publish intent,
   exact accessible preview/diff, honest one-person behavior, and one quiet
   exception-first queue.
6. **Migrate without reinterpretation.** Census and shadow-compile legacy live
   content, seed D2 manifests, switch the reader once, and never auto-publish old
   drafts or pending reviews.
7. **Certify production-shaped behavior before shipping.** The gate covers
   manual/automatic x Page Family/update x first/subsequent release x locale x
   media x unrestricted/restricted x Phase 10 `allowed`/`needs_review`/`blocked`;
   every D3 field and hidden egress; rich-text/URL/metadata fuzzing; concurrent
   contributors; assignment/policy/safety/reach revocation races; one-person
   tenants; scheduling/restore/bypass; tenant RLS; cache/notification failure;
   keyboard, screen reader, 320px reflow, status announcements, and mobile
   review. Ship only when every route proves one exact release or a visible,
   recoverable non-release.

### 17.7 Ratified hardened formulation

**C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) - one prospective, immutable,
tenant-owned Public Content Review & Release Profile Version scoped exactly by
Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, Page Family, environment, and publication path,
giving the tenant one honest choice between `Review before publishing` and
`Publish after checks` for Missionary Ministry Page revisions,
Project/Campaign Page revisions, and Ministry Updates through progressive
customization; with a disclosed manual-review fallback until deliberate tenant
activation, private autosave, explicit contributor release intent, and one
immutable Release Candidate pinned to the exact live base, normalized content,
complete canonical semantic diff and public-egress manifest, locale, actor and
contributor assignment, profile/catalog/renderer generations, media, feed,
safety, reach, and managed-reference facts. In review mode an authorized staff
member decides that exact candidate; in automatic mode every contributor-editable
candidate that passes all current owning-phase and structural proofs releases
without an invented human gate - including an initial content release when the
tenant's managed page, route, reach, and safety setup is already valid. Phase 10
`needs_review` follows its authorized human-review path and `blocked` cannot
release, while unknown public egress or missing, stale, contradictory, or
unavailable non-substitutable proof preserves the saved candidate in a
cause-owned exception that no ordinary review click can override. Both modes use D2's sole
idempotent CAS-guarded release command with current actor, assignment, profile,
safety, reach, dependency, and generation reproof, immutable decision/release
evidence, exact current-head activation, and transactional outbox; automatic
release is system execution of standing tenant-owned release authority, never
generic contributor authority or an AI judgment. Profile changes are
prospective, tightening stops queued automation, loosening never releases an old
backlog, restore creates a new draft, and scheduling only wakes the same
current-proofed command. Draft saved, submitted, human-approved, automatically
eligible, released, publicly reachable, cache-propagated, Giving-ready,
Ministry-Update-released, supporter-notification-requested/delivered,
search-indexed, and externally discovered remain independently authoritative;
one accessible mode-honest missionary editor and quiet exception-first staff
workspace expose exact previews, semantic diffs, causes, and next actions -
without workflow DSLs, per-field matrices, broad human-review floors that
contradict the tenant's automatic choice, author-declared risk, AI release
authority, autosave-to-live, moving-target approval, fictional dual control,
email-click approval, mutable restore, blind retry, stale approval, automatic
backlog publication, or Payload `_status`, Admin, Local API, scheduler, bulk,
service-role, cache, or notification authority over public truth.**

**Ratification:** the founder ratified this formulation as Phase 22 D4 on
2026-08-03. It is recorded in the Phase 22 decision log and ADR-0121.

## 18. D5 framing - represented-person and public-asset authorization coverage

**Status:** resolved by the founder and ratified as Phase 22 D5 on 2026-08-03.
Sections 18.4-18.5 preserve the rejected preliminary direction; section 18.6
is the binding simplified conclusion.

### 18.1 Why this is the next load-bearing seam

D1 permits one page to represent several people while contributor access stays
separate. D3 permits stories, quotations, relationship references, media, and
Ministry Updates. D4 permits a tenant to select a genuine `Publish after checks`
lane. Those decisions require an exact answer to a narrower question that Phase
10 intentionally leaves for the consuming public-page product: what current
authorization covers each represented person and public asset in one exact
release?

Phase 10 already owns the strictest-wins publication firewall, per-person
permission to publish name/photo/story, do-not-publish, and the
`allowed|needs_review|blocked` verdict. D5 must consume that authority rather
than create a second consent system. It must make the release-time coverage
complete enough for spouses, teammates, children, local partners, group media,
quotations, captions, alt text, metadata, locales, Ministry Updates, search,
social previews, and later withdrawal.

The shipped runtime does not yet provide that proof. The current public worker
route renders mock identity, location, photos, and updates, while the CMS public
reader explicitly reserves restricted-person and consent predicates. Existing
route tests prove tenant and publication filters, not represented-person or
asset coverage.

### 18.2 Concrete scenario

Daniel and Ruth use separate accounts and share one Missionary Ministry Page.
Daniel is its Page Subject and a contributor; Ruth is a Display Participant.
The hero photo includes both adults and their daughter. A Ministry Update quotes
a local partner and shows a recognizable school exterior. The tenant selected
D4 automatic release. Ruth permits her alias and story but not her photograph;
the child's prior guardian evidence is no longer current; and the local
partner's quotation has no recorded authority.

Marriage, household or team membership, authorship, contributor assignment,
staff employment, a prior publication, and D4 automatic release must not be
treated as authorization. The product needs a deterministic, low-friction way
to release what is covered, contain what is not, and explain the smallest next
action.

### 18.3 Current evidence and comparator lessons

- Phase 10 requires explicit per-person permission for name, photo, and story,
  hard do-not-publish enforcement, strictest-wins public projection, and
  controlled-surface invalidation. It does not define release-specific
  multi-person or asset coverage.
- GoFundMe requires an organizer who posts another person's name, image, or
  likeness to have that person's permission and be able to provide evidence;
  an authorized representative may act for a person who cannot act for
  themselves. This is comparator evidence for evidence-backed representation,
  not a rule that Asym should copy wholesale.
  [GoFundMe Terms](https://www.gofundme.com/c/terms).
- The UK ICO describes consent as an ongoing relationship rather than a one-off
  checkbox, recommends preference-management tools, says changed purposes may
  require refreshed consent, and says withdrawal should be as easy as giving
  consent. Asym must not claim consent is the only lawful basis in every
  jurisdiction; the durable product lesson is versioned, reviewable authority
  with easy narrowing and honest provenance.
  [ICO consent management](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/lawful-basis/consent/how-should-we-obtain-record-and-manage-consent/).
- Current FCDO child-safeguarding guidance requires informed child/caregiver
  permission for images and stories, purpose/use disclosure, withdrawal, and a
  separate contextual risk assessment even when permission exists. It also
  calls out captions, background details, recognizable buildings, and geotags
  as exposure paths.
  [FCDO child-safeguarding guidance](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/dfid-enhanced-due-diligence-safeguarding-for-external-partners/child-safeguarding-due-diligence-for-external-partners).
- Phase 10 and D2 already establish the decisive architecture: authorization
  evidence remains private, the public projection receives only the minimum
  derived result, and current narrowing reaches every controlled egress rather
  than only the visible body.

### 18.4 Options for D5

#### Option A - one blanket person-level public-presentation switch

Each represented person is either permitted or not permitted to appear.

This is easy to explain and query, but it cannot distinguish alias, story,
quotation, photograph, relationship reference, Ministry Update, page family,
site, reach, or asset. Withdrawal either removes too much or leaves something
exposed. It is too coarse for multi-person pages and group media.

#### Option B - approve every field and asset on every release

Every revision, locale, field, media item, quotation, and egress receives a
separate approval.

This is theoretically precise, but turns ordinary editing into a matrix,
defeats D4 automation, couples authority to incidental renderer changes, and
creates approval fatigue. It is operationally brittle and unsafe in practice.

#### Option C-prime - versioned, participant-scoped Public Presentation Authorization Coverage - recommended

Phase 10 remains authoritative for a current versioned standing Public
Presentation Authorization for each represented person, bounded by meaningful
semantic uses such as public identity, story/quotation, likeness/media,
relationship/family reference, and Ministry Updates. The authority is scoped
to the exact Tenant, Legal Entity, represented person, authorized actor,
purpose, applicable Page Family/site set, reach ceiling, effective interval,
statement/policy version, capture method, evidence reference/digest, and any
proved representative authority. There is no invented universal annual expiry;
an owning policy or evidence source may require one.

Each immutable D4 release candidate receives one Public Presentation
Authorization Coverage Manifest enumerating every represented person, content
and asset representation, locale, metadata, search/social output, and exact
authority version. Missing, stale, contradictory, or narrower coverage feeds
Phase 10's `needs_review` or `blocked` verdict. An authorized review may resolve
only what the owning Phase 10 contract permits a human to resolve; it cannot
fabricate non-substitutable permission or override do-not-publish.

Routine revisions within unchanged semantic coverage remain eligible for D4
automatic release. A new person, use, reach, or content class requires new
coverage. Withdrawal narrows every affected future and controlled live egress
at the smallest safe scope: remove a representation or asset when separable;
contain the page when its essential subject or the current Phase 10 state makes
safe partial rendering impossible. Historical evidence remains private and
append-only. External caches and copies receive honest propagation status, not
a false recall guarantee.

The missionary-facing UX is one calm **How I appear publicly** preview with a
few plain-language choices and easy narrowing. Staff see only cause-owned
exceptions such as **Ruth has not authorized this photo**, with direct actions
to request authority, replace or crop the asset, or record independently
obtained evidence with provenance. It is not a legal-basis adjudicator or a
permissions grid.

### 18.5 Preliminary adversarial conclusion

Option C-prime best preserves the prior decisions. Its major risks are consent
laundering from relationships, ambiguous group media, guardian/age transitions,
withdrawal leakage through metadata and derivatives, release-time races,
cross-tenant evidence reuse, private-evidence exposure, service-role bypass,
and prompting fatigue. The permanent controls are exact represented-person
scope, asset-participant coverage, verified representative evidence where
applicable, one all-egress dependency graph, current-version reproof inside
D2's release CAS, composite same-scope keys plus RLS and domain authorization,
private evidence with opaque public references, and just-in-time prompts only
when semantic coverage changes.

### 18.6 Founder clarification - simplify D5 and do not duplicate D4

The founder clarified that the intended product is much simpler than the
staff-facing authorization model above. A tenant chooses whether changes to a
Missionary Ministry Page, Project/Campaign Page, or Ministry Update require
staff review. When review is enabled, staff use their judgment on the exact
candidate and approve it or return it for changes. When review is disabled,
the candidate may publish after the already-required hard checks. This is the
D4 Review & Release Profile; D5 must not create another approval product.

The earlier C-prime framing remains useful only as adversarial evidence for
release-time safety plumbing. Its per-use authorization matrix, recurring
evidence prompts, separate exception queue, and routine asset-by-asset staff
configuration would be needless operational complexity for the ordinary
tenant. Current service-design guidance supports removing questions and data
collection that are not needed, using short closed choices, and revealing
special-case help only where it is relevant. Modern CMS release practice also
supports rendering and validating the exact candidate before one explicit
publish action; it does not require a second parallel approval ontology.

The corrected recommendation is therefore:

**Option C-prime-amended-and-simplified - one tenant-controlled Review &
Release Profile with a quiet Phase 10 Public Eligibility check.** D4 alone
controls whether submitted page or update changes require staff review. In
review mode, an authorized staff member sees the rendered candidate and a
concise semantic diff, then chooses **Approve & publish** or **Request changes**
with a short reason. A terminal **Reject** action is reserved for content that
must not continue through the workflow, so an ordinary fixable edit is not
presented as a dead end. In automatic mode, no healthy item enters a staff
queue; the candidate publishes after the same hard validation and safety
checks.

Phase 10 remains the sole non-overridable safety ceiling for current
do-not-publish, restricted-person, and safe-projection rules. D1's exact
Display Participant membership is required for a represented spouse, teammate,
or leader, but neither that relationship nor staff editorial approval may
override Phase 10. The release command quietly pins and reproves the applicable
Phase 10 verdict/version inside D2's sole CAS operation. An exceptional hard
block produces one plain-language cause and next action; it never exposes a
general permissions matrix or an **Approve anyway** escape hatch.

The normal missionary statuses are only **Draft**, **Waiting for review**,
**Changes requested**, and **Published**. Staff receive one quiet review queue
containing review-mode submissions plus safety exceptions, with the latter
visually distinguished because they cannot be approved away. Tenant setup uses
two plain choices - **Review before publishing** and **Publish after checks** -
and may reveal separate choices for Missionary pages, Project pages, and
Ministry Updates only when the tenant selects **Customize**. No second consent
workflow, evidence-upload requirement, field-level approval grid, or parallel
publication state is introduced.

This clarification supersedes the preliminary recommendation in 18.4-18.5 for
the founder decision. It does not weaken D1-D4 or Phase 10.

Supporting UX evidence:

- GOV.UK service guidance recommends removing questions and personal data that
  are not needed, using understandable closed questions, and placing concise
  help at the point of need rather than explaining an over-complex interface.
  [Collecting personal information](https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/design/collecting-personal-information-from-users)
  and
  [Designing good questions](https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/design/designing-good-questions).
- Sanity's current release model keeps a versioned candidate separate, supports
  preview and validation, and then uses one explicit publish action. That is
  comparator evidence for candidate preview and atomic release, not a reason
  to import an enterprise release-management surface into the missionary UX.
  [Sanity Content Releases](https://www.sanity.io/docs/studio/content-releases).

**Ratification:** the founder ratified the amended-and-simplified formulation
as Phase 22 D5 on 2026-08-03. It is recorded in the Phase 22 decision log and
ADR-0122.

## 19. D6 framing - source-authoritative public support progress

**Status:** resolved by the founder and ratified as Phase 22 D6 on 2026-08-03.

### 19.1 Why this is the next load-bearing seam

The roadmap promises public support progress, but no Page Family makes progress
mandatory or proves what it should mean. A Project/Campaign Page often compares
corrected received gifts with one finite campaign goal, but an ongoing project
may instead use an exact recurring-period measure or intentionally publish no
progress. A Missionary Ministry Page often compares active monthly commitments
with a support-raising goal, but it may compare received support for an exact
period or intentionally show no public progress. Page Family may guide the
recommended presets and constrain incompatible sources; it cannot silently
choose visibility, measurement semantics, or a goal for an individual page.
Commitments, received gifts, processor settlement, Field Account balance,
assessment, available funds, compensation, accounting, and payment are
independently authoritative facts and must never become one percentage.

The current runtime is explicitly unsafe as the permanent seam. The public
projection reads mutable `missionaries.current_funding` and `funding_goal`,
assumes cents divide by 100, loses exact over-goal truth by clamping percentage
to 100, and has no source cursor, ISO currency, period, through-date, correction
coverage, or Phase 13/16 provenance. The database also retains writable
`funds.current_amount`, duplicate goal columns, and broad anonymous read paths.
Phase 13 D17 already rules that public progress is derived from the canonical
posted-effective fold, per currency, corrected through append-only entries,
privacy-filtered before aggregation, and never stored as a mutable counter.
Phase 16 separately owns received-period and cadence-normalized commitment
truth; Phase 28 owns missionary Support-Raising Goal Versions; Phase 21 Field
Account truth is prohibited from public fundraising progress.

### 19.2 Current comparator and accessibility evidence

- Givebutter makes goals optional, lets organizations hide the amount raised,
  includes configured offline/imported sources, deducts refunds from the goal
  total, and does not close giving merely because the goal is met. These are
  useful presentation precedents; its broad source inclusion is not authority
  for Asym to count unposted evidence.
  [Campaign goals](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1761125-how-to-update-a-campaign-goal)
  and
  [refund behavior](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/7109570-how-to-issue-a-refund).
- Donorbox configures a goal per campaign and permits the goal meter to be
  hidden without deleting the campaign's internal goal. Its meter is limited to
  gross donations received. That is strong evidence for separating internal
  goal truth, public visibility, and progress meaning rather than deriving one
  from another.
  [Donorbox goal meter](https://donorbox.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/360020293632-How-to-add-a-donation-progress-meter-to-my-campaign).
- GoFundMe Pro's current progress metric uses the intended donation amount and
  excludes fees, while its multi-currency goal conversion may fluctuate daily.
  This supports gross designated-gift presentation and is direct evidence
  against an unlabeled floating-FX public total.
  [Progress metrics](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288737740187-Progress-metrics)
  and
  [multi-currency support](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288800980123-Multi-currency-support).
- MPDX separately labels goal, gifts started/received, commitments, below-goal,
  and account balance. It demonstrates the missionary-domain need for distinct
  measures rather than proving a public-page formula.
  [MPDX dashboard](https://help.mpdx.org/article/1201-mpdx-quick-reference-guide-the-dashboard).
- Sola explicitly supports monthly or one-time goals and tracks one-time and
  recurring gifts for long- and short-term ministry contexts. Sowfund describes
  a long-term missionary profile separately from finite trip/project
  fundraisers with goal bars. Together they support guided fundraising-shape
  presets, but their respective product choices do not justify hard-coding
  every missionary page as monthly or every project page as finite.
  [Sola](https://www.trustsola.com/) and
  [Sowfund](https://sowfund.org/blogs/what-is-sowfund).
- Bloomerang supplies typed, optional goal displays and permits over-100%
  presentation, but can be configured to include unverified offline and
  unfulfilled matching amounts. Blackbaud documents a goal meter whose refunds
  are not reflected and whose manual offline aggregate may lack underlying
  gift rows. Those are useful warnings: tenant flexibility must select typed
  source contracts, not authorize manual public totals.
  [Bloomerang goals and thermometers](https://help.bloomerang.com/en/articles/13382483-goals-and-thermometers)
  and
  [Blackbaud Goal Meter Designer](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/rex/content/web-components-designer-rc.html).
- WAI defines a meter as a numeric value within a known range and requires an
  accessible name and understandable value text. For an over-goal result, Asym
  should cap only the visual/semantic fill while retaining exact visible text;
  color or animation cannot be the only communication.
  [WAI meter pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/meter/).

### 19.3 Concrete scenario

Grace and Daniel Kim share one Missionary Ministry Page and are Display
Participants on a separate Village Water Project page. Their organization uses
active commitments for missionary support but does not publish Field Account
balances. It accepts USD and CAD. Current source facts include USD 4,300 of
active monthly commitments against a USD 5,000 Phase 28 goal; a newly recorded
USD 100 commitment whose first payment has not occurred; a USD 500 offline
check that has not yet posted; one posted USD 250 gift later refunded; separate
CAD support; and USD 12,500 of corrected posted project gifts against a USD
10,000 campaign goal.

A truthful missionary display may say **USD 4,300 committed monthly of USD
5,000**. It cannot call the USD 4,300 received or add a separate received
amount into that numerator. The unposted check does not count. CAD remains a
separate fact or is omitted. The project page may say **USD 12,500 received of
USD 10,000 - 125%** while the visual meter is full. The refund has already
reduced the applicable received total, and reaching the goal does not itself
remove the Give action.

### 19.4 Options for D6

#### Option A - one universal received-toward-goal meter

Every page compares posted gross gifts with one monetary goal.

- **Benefits:** one setting, one donor mental model, and a strong fit for a
  conventional project campaign.
- **Costs:** misrepresents missionary organizations that manage active monthly
  commitments, recurring support, a different reporting period, or no public
  goal; tenants will ask for manual offsets or relabel the same number.
- **Downstream risk:** the apparently simple universal field becomes a hidden
  formula and duplicated source truth.

#### Option B - tenant-built formulas and progress widgets

Tenants may combine gifts, commitments, matches, offline numbers, balances,
fees, adjustments, and custom periods.

- **Benefits:** maximum surface flexibility.
- **Costs:** creates a financial formula builder inside Phase 22, duplicates
  accounting/reporting logic, and cannot remain intelligible or testable.
- **Downstream risk:** promises look received, currencies and designations
  double count, manual totals drift, and Phase 21 internal balance leaks into a
  donor-facing claim.

#### Option C-prime - typed Public Support Progress Profile Versions - recommended

Every individual page resolves one explicit, immutable, prospective posture:
`Do not show public progress` or `Show one compatible public progress metric`.
When shown, the page selects at most one primary metric from a small code-owned,
source-certified catalog:

- **Missionary Ministry Page:** `No public progress`, `Active monthly
commitments toward support goal`, or `Gross support received for an exact
period toward support goal`.
- **Project/Campaign Page:** `No public progress`, `Cumulative gross gifts
received toward campaign goal`, `Gross gifts received during an exact
recurring or fixed period toward a compatible goal`, or one compatible Phase
  13 typed `supporter count`, `gift count`, or `recurring supporter count` goal.

These Page-Family lists are compatibility boundaries and recommended starting
points, not assumptions that all missionary work is recurring or all projects
are finite. A metric requiring an owning source contract that does not yet
exist remains unavailable with a clear explanation; Phase 22 does not fabricate
it. New page-family tenant defaults may seed a draft, but each page materializes
its own choice. A later default change cannot mutate, republish, or change the
meaning of any existing page. Missing page configuration resolves to `Do not
show public progress`, never to runtime inheritance.

The page-resolved profile binds one exact Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, page,
Page Family,
subject/Designation or campaign coverage, metric kind, period and governing
timezone, source-owned goal identity/version, evaluator generation, and public
presentation choice, plus exact ISO currency and exponent for monetary
metrics. The tenant chooses a named preset and previews the real result; there
is no formula editor. Changing metric, goal, currency, period, or coverage
creates a prospective successor profile rather than rewriting the meaning of
the existing release.

The primary numerator is Phase 13 corrected posted-effective gross designated
gift truth, one Phase 13 canonical distinct-set count, or the exact public-safe
Phase 16 commitment projection. These metrics are never added. Offline gifts
join only after Phase 15 has produced a Phase 13 posted-effective fact. Gross
progress excludes a separate donor fee-cover amount and is not reduced by
processor cost, assessment, or a designation-borne internal support-credit
policy; refunds, chargebacks, returns, NSF, and redesignations change monetary
and count projections through the owning append-only fold. Phase 20
settlement/accounting and every Phase 21 Field Account, availability, expense,
compensation, reimbursement, payroll, and payment fact are structurally
ineligible.

The changing result is a disposable, rebuildable, source-watermarked public
projection rather than a CMS field or mutable counter. It carries exact source
cursors/versions, currency, period, through-time, numerator, denominator,
coverage, evaluator version, freshness, and a typed absent/updating/suppressed
outcome. Anonymous requests receive only the minimal Phase 10-safe result
through the Phase 5/D2 reader; they never query or aggregate ledger,
commitment, goal, binding, or internal projection tables.

The staff editor presents one quiet `Support progress` card. Its first choice is
`Don't show progress on this page` or `Show progress on this page`. When shown,
staff see only compatible plain-language definitions, an exact source/currency/
period explanation, and the literal visitor preview. A bounded disclosure
choice may show amounts plus percentage or percentage only; D3 owns visual
placement and treatment but cannot select the financial meaning or force the
block onto a page. The page states `This page only`; there is no formula editor,
rules matrix, inherited-policy badge, or source-field picker. D1 contributors
may see the current choice and preview, but progress remains a protected tenant
control.

The donor sees one strong sentence plus one quiet visual meter, not financial
provenance controls. Exact text remains visible; the fill caps at 100% while an
over-goal amount and percentage remain exact. A goal reached state does not
close Giving. Missing or incompatible goals, stale or incomplete source
coverage, suppression, absence, and authoritative zero remain different and
never silently display `0%`. When the source is not safely computable, omit only
the optional progress block and raise one cause-owned staff exception; keep the
page and independently eligible Give action healthy. Hiding is enforced in the
server projection and cache path, not CSS, markup, metadata, or a client toggle.

### 19.5 Final adversarial conclusion

Option C-prime provides the needed per-page tenant flexibility without a formula
builder. Its main hazards are live tenant-default inheritance, Page-Family
assumptions, mutable-denominator manipulation,
commitment/receipt conflation, unposted offline inflation, refund lag,
cross-currency aggregation, internal-finance leakage, double counting, stale
cache, rounded false goal completion, small-cell inference, hidden-data egress,
and configuration burden. The permanent controls are explicit page-resolved
postures, draft-only defaults, immutable prospective profiles, exact
source-owned goal references, mutually exclusive metric kinds, Phase 13/16
source cursors, privacy-before-aggregation, canonical set-union rollups,
integer/rational arithmetic, one ISO currency per meter, typed freshness and
suppression, exact through-dates, guided compatible presets, one visitor preview,
and exhaustive isolation, correction, concurrency, accessibility, anonymous-
egress, cache, and production-volume proof. Existing pages and pages whose
sources cannot be proved migrate as hidden; mutable legacy `current_funding`,
`funding_goal`, and `current_amount` fields are never migration authority.

**Ratified formulation:** **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) - one
explicit, prospective, immutable, page-resolved tenant-owned Public Support
Progress Profile Version for every released page, selecting `Do not show public
progress` or exactly one primary source-authoritative compatible metric for each
individual Missionary Ministry Page and Project/Campaign Page; with
Page-Family-guided but
not Page-Family-determined presets for Phase 13 corrected gross-received,
exact-period, and typed-count projections or a compatible Phase 16
active-commitment projection against one exact Phase 13 campaign goal or Phase
28 Support-Raising Goal Version; tenant/page-family defaults that seed new
drafts only and never govern existing pages at runtime; exact Tenant, Legal
Entity, Site, page, subject/Designation or campaign coverage, metric, period,
timezone, goal, evaluator, and source-watermark scope plus one ISO currency for
monetary metrics; one bounded public disclosure choice, an exact visitor
preview, and a clear source/period/through-date explanation; disposable
correction-aware public projections; proof-gated offline inclusion;
privacy-before-aggregation and small-cell suppression; server-enforced hidden
state; accessible over-goal truth; smallest-scope widget omission and
cause-owned staff exception when truth is not safely computable; and
independently controlled Giving - without mandatory or tenant-global progress,
live default inheritance, page-family fundraising assumptions, arbitrary
formulas, commitment-and-receipt blending, unverified manual totals, writable
counters, floating-FX aggregation, Field Account or available-funds claims,
retroactive goal rewriting, automatic metric fallback, stale zeroes, hidden
data egress, double counting, stale `Live` claims, or public access to source
tables.**

The binding interpretation is recorded in
[Phase 22 D6](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d6---page-resolved-source-authoritative-public-support-progress)
and
[ADR-0123](../../adr/0123-page-resolved-source-authoritative-public-support-progress.md).

### 19.6 Current-repository implementation hazards found during ratification

- `supabase/migrations/20260625002117_canonical_tanstack_db_realtime_rls.sql`
  currently grants anonymous/browser reads over raw `missionaries` and `funds`,
  and publishes `funds` through Supabase Realtime. Phase 22 must replace that
  path with server-only public-safe projections and a forward migration that
  revokes the obsolete grants, policies, and publication membership. Because an
  earlier demo migration also grants broad reads, certification applies the full
  migration chain and asserts final privileges rather than inspecting only the
  new migration.
- `packages/api/src/public-giving/{columns,types,projection}.ts` and
  `packages/api/src/donate/index.ts` currently read mutable
  `missionaries.current_funding`/`funding_goal` and
  `funds.current_amount`/`target_amount`, assume 100 minor units, round to whole
  units, and clamp public percentages at 100. These are explicit replacement
  targets, along with tests that currently freeze the legacy behavior. D6 uses
  exact ISO exponents, source versions/watermarks, and visible plus assistive
  over-goal truth.
- The current Phase 5 cache implementation is keyed/tagged too coarsely and uses
  stale-while-revalidate for every change. D6 requires exact Tenant, Site, page,
  locale, release, profile, projection, currency, and safety scope. Ordinary
  positive refresh may use bounded stale-while-revalidate; hiding, adverse
  correction, retirement, containment, or Phase 10 narrowing expires the
  affected scope immediately while request-time safety remains authoritative.
- These are migration and certification findings, not permission to add a
  parallel public API, duplicate ledger, mutable snapshot, or second release
  head. The same Phase 5 server choke point and D2 Page Release head remain the
  only public-serving and active-configuration boundaries.

## 20. D7 framing - page-scoped Giving offers and donor-intent continuity

**Status:** resolved by the founder and ratified as Phase 22 D7 on 2026-08-04.

### 20.1 Why this is the next load-bearing seam

D1 protects Designation and checkout controls, D2 keeps Giving readiness
independent from public reach, and D3 permits several CTA placements. None yet
defines whether a page may offer one Designation or a bounded set, what cached
CTA state may authorize, or what happens when the selected destination becomes
ineligible between page render and checkout.

This decision must preserve two accepted predecessor contracts:

- Phase 5 A8 uses plain handoff parameters plus server-side re-resolution. It
  rejected a signed token as redundant because no parameter is authority.
- Phase 13 D15 owns the multi-designation cart, revalidates every cart line, and
  lets a donor deliberately add another Designation. Phase 13 D13 also reserved
  campaign `expected designations` as a future public-choice seam. D7 must decide
  whether that seam enters the MVP or remains non-public intent data.

### 20.2 Current evidence

- [ABWE's worker page](https://give.abwe.org/worker/652) keeps the worker-support
  purpose in context, offers bounded amounts, and lets the donor add that exact
  purpose to a basket rather than starting with a generic organization search.
- [MTW's project page](https://mtw.org/projects/details/ambassadors-program/)
  preserves one visible project number while presenting amount and recurring
  intent beside the Give action.
- [Givebutter's current parameter contract](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/4868782-how-to-leverage-url-and-html-parameters)
  allows amount, frequency, and fund preselection only for options already
  configured on the campaign; parameters cannot create a fund or cadence.
- [Blackbaud Online Express Magic Links](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/online-express/content/donations-magic-links.html)
  can preselect or limit a donation form to one Designation and suggested amount.
  This validates the low-friction direct pattern, but URL parameters remain an
  older transport convenience rather than financial authority.
- [Stripe's Checkout Sessions documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout-sessions)
  creates the Session server-side and recommends application identifiers for
  reconciliation. The provider session is execution state, not Page Giving
  authority.
- [OWASP Authorization guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html)
  requires deny-by-default and permission validation on every request; its
  [Business Logic Security guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Business_Logic_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html)
  specifically says to re-derive security-relevant ownership/value inputs on
  the server. A cached page or tampered parameter therefore cannot authorize a
  current financial destination.

### 20.3 Concrete scenario

Harbor Missions publishes Grace and Daniel Kim's Missionary Ministry Page. A
donor arrives from the August prayer email with `?sc=aug-prayer`, views the page
in French, and chooses **Give monthly**. Between page render and checkout,
finance pauses the Designation or its Settlement Account Binding; the donor may
also alter Designation, currency, locale, or source-code parameters.

For a separate Kenya Water Project, staff may track three expected Designations
for wells, training, and where needed most. The founder's MVP ruling makes the
public page select exactly one of them; the remaining Phase 13 intent data stays
intact without becoming a public directory or dormant Phase 22 picker.

### 20.4 Options for D7

#### Option A - always open the universal giving chooser

The page passes attribution and perhaps a suggested destination, then the donor
selects from every currently eligible Designation.

This maximizes choice but repeats a decision the donor already made, weakens
page-to-gift intent, risks exposing unrelated or sensitive destinations, and
turns every ministry page into an indirect fund directory. A separately labelled
**Explore other ways to give** action may start a new donor choice, but it cannot
pretend to continue the page's purpose. **Reject as the primary action.**

#### Option B - exactly one Designation on every page - selected for the MVP

Every page binds one exact Designation; all CTA placements add only that line to
the Phase 13 cart. A stale or ineligible binding fails closed with no fallback.

This is the simplest safe direct-giving contract and fits ordinary missionary
and single-purpose project pages. The founder selected that deliberate MVP
boundary. Phase 13's `expected designations` remains staff intent and a future
product seam, not a public picker in Phase 22. The MVP implements the singular
contract directly rather than hiding a dormant multi-choice engine behind it.

#### Option C-prime - one immutable page-scoped Public Giving Offer Version - not selected for the MVP

This broader option would have let every released page pin exactly one posture:

1. **No Giving on this page**;
2. **Give directly** to one exact eligible Phase 13 Designation; or
3. for a compatible Project/Campaign Page only, **Choose what to support** from
   one bounded, explicitly ordered set of exact campaign-approved Designations
   under the same Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, and currency lane.

Direct is the quiet default. The bounded chooser appears only when staff
explicitly configures more than one compatible project option and production-
shaped proof passes. It is not the tenant's universal Designation list. Every
CTA placement points to the same active offer; placement-specific copy,
registered source code, and bounded amount/frequency suggestion may vary but
cannot select another destination.

The donor's explicit selection becomes one Phase 13 cart line. Phase 13 may
still offer its quiet **Add another designation** action afterward; that begins
a separate donor choice and does not rewrite the page-origin line. Source code,
UTM, locale, entry method, amount, and cadence are untrusted context or
suggestions—not destination, charge, issuer, or eligibility authority.

Phase 5 carries the already-ratified plain-parameter handoff. The server
re-resolves the current Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, D2 release, Phase 10-safe
label and public eligibility, offer version, selected Designation, Phase 13
public-giving eligibility, current Settlement Account Binding, currency,
cadence capability, registered attribution, and internal return path at cart
mutation/checkout entry and again immediately before provider execution. A
stale, forged, cross-scope, or revoked option fails closed; another Designation
is never substituted automatically.

If one bounded project option becomes unavailable, that option is calmly marked
unavailable and the donor must explicitly choose another. If the direct option
or every bounded option is unavailable, the safe page may remain public while
the Giving block becomes **Giving is temporarily unavailable** with a separate
**Explore other ways to give** path if the tenant provides one. The latter starts
a fresh choice with no inherited destination. Changing offer posture, scope, or
membership is prospective staff-controlled configuration released through D2;
current eligibility changes contain the stale action immediately without
rewriting release history.

The ordinary staff UI is one **Giving** card:

- **On this page:** Give directly / Choose what to support / No Giving;
- **Destination or choices:** Phase 10-safe donor-visible labels;
- **Organization receiving the gift:** exact Legal Entity;
- **Currency and gift options:** current certified capabilities; and
- **Status:** Ready, Giving unavailable, or Staff action needed.

Missionary contributors see a read-only public preview and status. They cannot
change Designations, issuer, currency, cadence, attribution authority, or
fallback behavior.

### 20.5 Final adversarial conclusion and founder ruling

| Concern                        | What could go wrong                                                          | Severity | Likelihood without control | Permanent prevention                                                                    |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Stale-cache TOCTOU             | Page rendered while valid, then destination paused before checkout           | Critical | Medium                     | Re-resolve at cart/checkout and provider boundary; immediate affected-scope CTA expiry  |
| Parameter tampering            | Donor changes Tenant, Designation, currency, locale, source, or return path  | Critical | High                       | Treat all parameters as untrusted; same-scope lookup plus internal-path allowlist       |
| Silent fallback                | Intended gift reaches a general fund or another project option               | Critical | Medium                     | No substitution; require an explicit new donor choice                                   |
| Universal-picker friction/leak | Primary CTA exposes unrelated or restricted choices                          | High     | Medium                     | No Phase 22 MVP picker; one exact page binding; Phase 10 before any public label        |
| Singular-MVP scope pressure    | A multi-purpose project expects several choices on one page                  | Medium   | Medium                     | Make the limitation explicit; retain Phase 13 intent data without dormant picker logic  |
| CTA placement drift            | Hero, body, mobile, and update actions route differently                     | Critical | Medium                     | All placements reference one released Page Giving Binding                               |
| Attribution-as-routing         | Source code or UTM selects the money destination                             | Critical | Medium                     | Separate typed attribution from exact Designation authority                             |
| Restricted identity leakage    | Checkout, descriptors, errors, logs, or alternatives reveal a protected name | Critical | Medium                     | Same Phase 10-safe label projection across every money and observability egress         |
| Currency/issuer ambiguity      | Donor thinks one entity/currency receives the gift but another does          | Critical | Medium                     | One Legal Entity/currency lane per binding and explicit issuer before confirmation      |
| Stale amount/cadence           | Preset becomes charge truth or enables an unsupported frequency              | High     | Medium                     | Bounded suggestions revalidated against current Phase 13/16 capability                  |
| Replay/duplicate line          | Repeated taps or retries create duplicate intent                             | High     | Medium                     | Phase 13 cart-line semantic dedupe and idempotency; click creates no contribution       |
| Provider/outage coupling       | Checkout outage takes down an otherwise safe public story                    | Medium   | Medium                     | Independent page/Giving states and smallest-scope unavailable presentation              |
| Accessibility                  | Disabled button gives keyboard/screen-reader users no explanation            | High     | Medium                     | Replace dead controls with named status and a clearly separate alternative action       |
| Tenant isolation               | Forged option crosses Site, Legal Entity, page, or tenant                    | Critical | Medium                     | Composite same-scope constraints, indexed RLS, server-only commands, negative tests     |
| Migration                      | Mock IDs and handcrafted URLs are mistaken for valid authority               | Critical | High                       | Existing pages remain Not public until exact binding proof and deliberate D2 release    |
| Observability/privacy          | Broken CTAs go unseen or logs leak donor/restricted data                     | High     | Medium                     | Cause-coded, privacy-safe telemetry and one page-scoped staff exception                 |
| Over-engineering               | Future choice machinery becomes a dormant MVP workflow or financial DSL      | High     | Medium                     | Implement one singular binding directly; no hidden picker, offer DSL, or fallback graph |

**Ratified formulation:** **B-prime-amended-and-hardened (B-prime-R) - Phase
22 MVP requires every released Missionary Ministry Page and Project/Campaign
Page to pin one immutable, released-page-owned Page Giving Binding to exactly
one Phase 13 Designation under the exact Tenant, Legal Entity, Site,
environment, and currency lane; carried through Phase 5's server-resolved plain-
parameter handoff and revalidated at cart/checkout entry and immediately before
provider execution against the current D2 release, Phase 10-safe public
eligibility and donor-visible labels, exact binding and Designation eligibility,
Settlement Account Binding, issuer, currency, supported cadence, registered
attribution, and allowlisted internal return path. Every CTA placement shares
that one destination while source code, copy, suggested amount, and suggested
frequency may vary only as independently validated context or bounded
suggestions; destination replacement is prospective, staff-controlled,
consequence-previewed, and released through D2's sole path. A stale, forged,
cross-scope, paused, or otherwise ineligible binding receives immediate
affected-CTA containment with a calm page-visible/Giving-unavailable state and,
when the tenant supplies it, one separately labelled fresh general-giving path
that carries no inherited destination - without a Phase 22 MVP fund picker,
contributor-controlled destination, mutable CMS checkout URL, source-code or UTM
routing authority, stale-cache authority, cross-tenant or cross-entity
selection, automatic fallback, adjacent-purpose substitution, or any claim that
a page, CTA click, cart line, Checkout Session, provider acceptance, or
attribution fact proves a contribution.**

The binding decision is recorded in
[Phase 22 D7](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d7--one-exact-page-giving-binding-per-released-page-for-the-mvp)
and
[ADR-0124](../../adr/0124-one-exact-page-giving-binding-for-phase22-mvp.md).

## 21. D8 framing — source-qualified public route and lifecycle dispositions

**Status:** resolved by the founder and ratified as Phase 22 D8 on 2026-08-04.

### 21.1 Why this is the next load-bearing seam

D2 already fixes immutable route generations, permanent tombstones, opaque
restricted/shared-link routes, and the rule that an old direct-link route never
redirects to its replacement. D7 fixes one exact Giving destination and forbids
silent destination fallback. The remaining question is narrower but still
load-bearing: what a supporter should receive at an existing Listed-public
address when its page moves or its worker/project enters a terminal transition.

That cannot be inferred from one `departed`, `retired`, `unpublished`, or
`designation closed` flag. Public presentation, new-Giving eligibility,
existing recurring support, source-purpose succession, and external search
cleanup remain independently authoritative facts.

### 21.2 Current repository and documentation evidence

- The current donor route
  `apps/donor/app/(public)/(solid)/workers/[id]/page.tsx` is a mock-data route
  keyed by a path value called `id`, while
  `apps/missionary/app/profile/use-profile-page-view.ts` constructs a different
  name-derived `/workers/{first}-{last}` address. Those paths disagree and the
  latter is unsafe for a restricted identity.
- The current missionary CMS reader is operational-ID-oriented, while the
  project reader is slug-oriented. The shared page-builder fields expose one
  mutable `slug`, and the current collection posture permits destructive
  deletion. None of those legacy facts is a safe route-lifecycle authority.
- Phase 5 A12 says the general CMS/Web Studio layer owns ordinary slugs and
  redirects, but D2's later, more specific contract makes Phase 22's immutable
  Page Route Binding and current release authoritative for these two public
  ministry page families. Phase 23 may provide a generic redirect-management
  surface; it cannot decide that one worker/project is the charitable-purpose
  successor of another.
- The installed Next.js 16.2 documentation confirms that dynamic route params
  are untrusted strings requiring runtime validation, permanent redirects are
  for a real new canonical URI, and missing content must return a real HTTP
  result rather than a misleading success page. Large data-driven route maps
  belong behind indexed runtime resolution rather than an ever-growing static
  Next configuration.
- [Google's current URL guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/url-structure)
  recommends simple, intelligible, descriptive URLs when safe. Its
  [site-move guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)
  recommends direct permanent redirects for genuine replacements and real
  `404`/`410` responses when no replacement exists; irrelevant mass redirects
  are specifically discouraged.
- [Payload's redirects plugin](https://payloadcms.com/docs/plugins/redirects)
  stores `from`/`to` records but explicitly leaves request-time redirect
  execution to the frontend. It does not prove tenant scope, identity safety,
  charitable-purpose continuity, current reach, or Giving eligibility.
- [Givebutter](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1772204-how-to-close-or-unlist-a-campaign)
  and [GoFundMe Pro](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288802138651-Campaign-status-definitions)
  both document that closing/unpublishing a campaign does not itself stop
  existing recurring gifts. The page lifecycle and recurring-gift lifecycle
  are separate facts.
- [Antioch Ministries' current giving FAQ](https://antioch.org/give) says a
  departing missionary's account ordinarily remains open for one to three
  months before recurring gifts stop. That is direct comparator evidence
  against automatically equating worker departure, page removal, Designation
  closure, and recurring termination.

### 21.3 Concrete scenario

Hope Mission's Smith family leaves on September 30. Their organization keeps
the support Designation open for a documented transition; printed prayer cards
and church websites still point to the current public page; existing monthly
gifts remain governed by Phase 16; and one spouse later receives a narrower
Phase 10 publication ceiling. A related team page exists, but similarity of
people, labels, region, or ministry is not proof that it is the same charitable
purpose.

Phase 22 must decide what the old address shows without deciding where money or
recurring support goes.

### 21.4 Fixed constraints from ratified decisions

- A lifecycle source event may open work but cannot itself choose the public
  disposition.
- D2 remains the sole Publication Reach/release authority. Immediate safety
  narrowing always wins.
- Shared-by-link and restricted/direct-link rotations keep D2's permanent,
  non-redirecting tombstone. An old link cannot reveal its replacement.
- D7's exact Page Giving Binding remains independent. A page move, retirement,
  or redirect never changes a Designation, reroutes a gift, or supplies a
  fallback destination.
- Phase 13 alone owns Designation and accepted source-purpose succession;
  Phase 16 alone owns recurring-support stop/successor facts. Phase 22 consumes
  their proofs and never recreates them.
- Search, CDN, social-preview, copied-link, and crawler cleanup are observed
  best-effort external outcomes, not proof of local withdrawal.

### 21.5 Options for D8

#### Option A — terminal pages always disappear

Every terminal transition permanently tombstones the route and returns a true
privacy-safe `404` or `410`. No successor redirect or informational continuity
is possible.

This is small and safe, but it unnecessarily breaks printed links when the same
Listed page only receives a new safe canonical address or an exact same-purpose
successor presentation has already been proved. **Safe but too destructive.**

#### Option B — tenant-managed CMS lifecycle and arbitrary redirects

Staff may keep, archive, delete, or redirect a page to any entered URL.

This looks flexible but turns a presentation control into a cross-tenant,
privacy, and financial-intent footgun. It permits redirect loops, unrelated
general-fund destinations, external URLs, name leakage, and a second mutable
route state machine in Payload. **Reject.**

#### Option C-prime — source-qualified route and lifecycle dispositions — recommended

One quiet, cause-owned staff case offers only the outcomes currently proved to
be safe:

1. **Keep the current page** while D2/Phase 10 permit it; Giving may remain
   independently available or unavailable under D7.
2. **Publish a truthful transition page** at the current address as soon as D2
   and Phase 10 permit it. Its claims are independently proof-gated and
   through-dated, so open Phase 13 or Phase 16 transition work is presented as
   open rather than guessed complete. It retains D7's current exact binding and
   Giving state; D8 supplies no no-Giving switch.
3. **Move permanently** only when the same immutable Page identity has an
   already released, currently eligible new Listed-public canonical route. A
   different proved successor presentation may appear only as a separately
   labelled fresh link from a transition page; it is never an automatic move.
4. **Remove permanently** through the same tenant-branded real `404` plus
   `noindex` used for an unknown page. The exact internal reason remains
   append-only evidence, not a public existence/history oracle.

Staff never type a raw redirect URL. The server derives a permanent-move target
only from the same immutable Page's exact newly released route. A distinct
successor presentation may be selected only for a separately labelled fresh
link from exact same-Tenant, same-Legal-Entity, same-Site, same-locale eligible
pages returned by the server. Missionary contributors see a read-only transition
summary and visitor preview; they cannot choose a route, successor, financial
outcome, or recurring disposition. Healthy pages create no lifecycle task.

### 21.6 Adversarial review of C-prime

| Category                | Concern? | What could go wrong                                                                                   | Severity | Likelihood without control | Permanent prevention                                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Brittleness             | Yes      | Departure automatically removes a page while its authorized transition remains open.                  | Critical | High                       | Source events open a case; they never infer the outcome.                                                |
| Technical debt          | Yes      | Mutable CMS slugs and redirect rows become a second live state machine.                               | High     | High                       | One append-only operational route/disposition model under D2.                                           |
| Edge cases              | Yes      | Couples, teams, alias changes, locale routes, delayed account closure, and safety narrowing conflict. | Critical | High                       | Exact participant, locale, source-version, purpose, reach, and safety proof.                            |
| Footguns                | Yes      | Staff redirects to a general fund, another worker, or an external URL.                                | Critical | Medium                     | No raw URL field; only currently qualified internal targets.                                            |
| Tenant safety           | Yes      | A collision or lookup crosses Tenant, Site, Legal Entity, or locale.                                  | Critical | Medium                     | Composite same-scope constraints, indexed RLS, and server-owned commands.                               |
| Over-engineering        | Yes      | A lifecycle rules DSL creates contradictory combinations.                                             | High     | Medium                     | Four bounded outcomes; no arbitrary workflow/redirect matrix.                                           |
| UX/UI friction          | Yes      | Staff must mentally combine publication, Giving, recurring, safety, and SEO.                          | High     | High                       | One consequence-first case with a literal visitor preview and plain-language non-effects.               |
| Hidden coupling         | Yes      | Page retirement silently closes a Designation or changes recurring gifts.                             | Critical | High                       | Phase 13 and Phase 16 remain independently authoritative.                                               |
| Failure modes           | Yes      | Old and new routes are both current, or stale output survives a safety change.                        | Critical | Medium                     | D2 CAS activation, request-time gates, exact invalidation, and append-only recovery.                    |
| Data integrity          | Yes      | A tombstoned path is reused for an unrelated future ministry.                                         | Critical | Medium                     | Never reuse route identities; immutable generations and tombstones.                                     |
| Security/privacy        | Yes      | A legal name leaks in a slug or an old direct link reveals a replacement.                             | Critical | Medium                     | Phase 10-safe route class; opaque non-redirecting direct links; privacy-safe `404`.                     |
| Scalability/performance | Yes      | Every request scans CMS redirect documents or a static config grows without bound.                    | High     | Medium                     | Indexed exact route projection and one-hop server resolution.                                           |
| Operational burden      | Yes      | Staff repeatedly certify healthy pages or chase external crawlers manually.                           | Medium   | High                       | Cause-owned exceptions only; automated cleanup observation.                                             |
| Observability gaps      | Yes      | Local withdrawal succeeds while sitemap, CDN, social, or search remains stale.                        | High     | Medium                     | Separate local authority from privacy-safe external-cleanup telemetry.                                  |
| Dependency/integration  | Yes      | Payload or a crawler is mistaken for semantic route authority.                                        | High     | High                       | Phase 22 owns disposition; Phase 5 serves it; external systems report outcomes only.                    |
| Migration/upgrade       | Yes      | Mock IDs, name-derived URLs, and mutable slugs are treated as proven history.                         | High     | High                       | Route census plus shadow resolution; no inferred public activation or redirect.                         |
| Other hazards           | Yes      | Concurrent release/retirement, redirect cycles, replay, or successor retirement causes split truth.   | Critical | Medium                     | Shared D2 authority-head locking, cycle validation, semantic idempotency, and append-only supersession. |

### 21.7 Ratified C-prime-R formulation

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — one source- and
> cause-qualified, append-only Public Page Route Disposition Case for every
> canonical-route change or terminal Missionary Ministry Page or
> Project/Campaign Page transition, preserving D2 Publication Reach, D7's one
> exact Page Giving Binding, Phase 10 safety and concealment, Phase 13
> Designation and source-purpose-succession truth, and Phase 16 recurring-
> support truth as independently authoritative. Each case binds the exact
> Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, locale, Page Family, immutable Page identity,
> origin Route Generation, source family and version, cause, actor, effective
> time, release heads, and effect manifest, and offers only currently proved
> outcomes: continue the current release; publish a substantive, coverage-aware
> Transition Notice Release whose every claim is through-dated and proof-gated;
> permanently move an eligible Listed-public address only to the same immutable
> Page's already released, currently eligible new canonical Route Generation;
> or remove it through the same privacy-safe real `404` and `noindex` response as
> an unknown page. A different eligible, proved same-purpose successor
> presentation may appear only as a separately labelled fresh link from a
> transition notice, with no inherited Designation, amount, cadence, source code,
> query, return path, or recurring-support action; it is never an automatic
> redirect. Shared-by-link and restricted/direct-link rotations retain D2's
> non-redirecting tombstones, and unknown, ambiguous, stale, or unavailable
> resolution never becomes a cached move or removal. Supabase keeps normalized,
> never-reused immutable route and disposition facts in a non-browser operational
> boundary with explicit grants, indexed defense-in-depth RLS, externally unique
> Site × locale × canonical-path identity, composite same-scope foreign keys,
> deterministic locking, semantic idempotency, and D2-head CAS activation; Phase
> 5 performs indexed one-hop request-time resolution, rechecks target eligibility,
> and returns the exact `200`, `308`, `404`, or transient no-store `503` result.
> One accessible, mobile-ready staff page asks what supporters should see,
> previews the literal visitor result and independent Page, new-Giving,
> recurring-gift, discovery, and external-cache consequences, and requires only
> one final confirmation for permanent move or removal. Effects use an idempotent
> outbox and immutable manifest for origin response, scoped cache invalidation,
> internal links, canonical and structured metadata, social metadata, and
> sitemap membership; external cleanup remains observed best effort — without
> automatic departure-to-retirement inference, a separate `410` behavior,
> redirect chains, raw or external URLs, cross-scope targets, destructive
> deletion or rollback, path reuse, mutable CMS route authority, contributor-
> controlled lifecycle, general-fund or adjacent-ministry fallback, untrusted
> parameter forwarding, silent recurring changes, or any claim that worker
> departure, page transition, route movement, Designation closure, recurring
> termination, cache purge, search removal, and donor transition are the same
> fact.**

### 21.8 Additional adversarial comparator and UX evidence

This pass found one substantive correction to the initial C-prime framing and
several implementation constraints that should be binding if C-prime is
ratified.

#### Current comparator and standards evidence

- [Givebutter's current close/unlist documentation](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/1772204-how-to-close-or-unlist-a-campaign)
  separates at least four facts: whether a page is listed, whether the direct
  link still works, whether new payments are accepted, and whether existing
  recurring donations continue. A Page/Event campaign can remain visible with
  its payment button disabled; an unlisted campaign remains available to
  anyone holding its link; and closing does not cancel recurring donations.
  This is strong evidence against one overloaded `archived` or `departed`
  status.
- [GoFundMe Pro's current campaign statuses](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288802138651-Campaign-status-definitions)
  likewise say an unpublished page is no longer public while its recurring
  donations continue. Its
  [fundraising-page management documentation](https://prosupport.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/37288766899867-Manage-fundraisers-and-teams)
  shows an additional useful distinction: an archived page can disappear from
  discovery and leaderboards while remaining directly accessible in an
  archived state. That same document also shows the danger of hidden coupling:
  archiving some pages automatically cancels an attached fundraising
  commitment. Asym must preserve the useful reach separation and reject the
  implicit financial side effect.
- [Cru's current donor FAQ](https://give.cru.org/frequently-asked-questions.html)
  documents a three-month missionary transition during which the account and
  recurring gift remain active, followed by a separately communicated donor
  transition. Whatever a tenant's Phase 16 policy ultimately is, this proves
  that a useful public transition notice may be needed **before** recurring
  disposition is complete. The original C-prime phrase allowing an
  informational page only after complete transition coverage is therefore too
  restrictive and could leave a stale, misleading ministry story public during
  the most important donor-communication window.
- Google's current
  [crawl-error guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors)
  says to use a permanent redirect only when content has moved to a clear
  replacement and to return a true `404` or `410` when it has not. Its current
  [site-move guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/site-move-with-url-changes)
  warns against irrelevant redirects, requires canonical and sitemap updates,
  recommends directing the old route straight to the final target, and notes
  that external search changes take time. Asym must not claim that `410` is
  faster or stronger than `404`, that a local cutover proves search removal, or
  that an adjacent ministry is a replacement.
- [Shopify's current redirect documentation](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/menus-and-links/url-redirect)
  permits raw relative or external destinations, notes that permanent
  redirects can remain cached after deletion, and describes market/locale
  subfolder effects. Those are acceptable generic-commerce capabilities but
  are precisely the Phase 22 footguns to exclude: staff must not type a URL,
  choose an external destination, or accidentally apply one disposition across
  locales.
- W3C's current
  [irreversible-action confirmation technique](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/general/G168)
  requires users to see the consequences and be able to confirm or cancel.
  WAI-ARIA's
  [modal-dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/)
  recommends initial focus on the least destructive action for a hard-to-undo
  final step. WCAG's
  [status-message guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
  and
  [minimum target-size guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
  require nonvisual action feedback and operable touch targets. D8 therefore
  needs an accessible consequence review, but not a long wizard or repeated
  confirmation ritual.

#### Correction to the four outcomes

Outcome 2 should be **Keep a truthful informational or transition page**, not
"informational page only after applicable transition coverage is complete."
The page may be released while Phase 13 or Phase 16 transition work remains
open, but it may state only proved, through-dated facts. Before completion, its
plain-language default is equivalent to:

> This ministry is in transition. New Giving and existing recurring gifts are
> managed separately; see their current status below or contact the organization
> with questions.

The exact Giving state, donor self-service, and contact links appear only when
their owning phase and tenant configuration authorize them. The page never says
new Giving is unavailable unless Phase 13/D7 proves that result, and never says
an existing gift stopped, moved, or will support another purpose without the
corresponding Phase 16/13 proof. After complete coverage, the same page may
present the exact final proved outcome. A retained informational page is a
substantive, current `200` document with self-canonical metadata; it is not a
`200` error surrogate or soft `404`. If the tenant has no honest substantive
information to retain, the permanent-removal outcome is the correct choice.

#### Complete adversarial delta

| Category                          | Concern? | What could go wrong and why it matters                                                                                                                                                     | Severity | Likelihood | Binding permanent prevention                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

| Technical debt                    | Yes      | CMS status, redirect rows, UI labels, and route middleware each grow their own meaning for `archive`, `close`, or `move`.                                                                  | High     | High       | One typed append-only disposition command and one derived current visitor-result projection; CMS stores approved presentation content only.                                                                                                                                     |

Show current versus after, exact page/Giving/recurring/discovery non-effects, and literal action verbs. Confirm only permanent move/removal once; never require typing a slug to confirm.                                |

It references their exact outcomes and says "managed separately" while they remain unresolved.                                                                                                                                                |

If the target becomes ineligible, quarantine the old route to the uniform privacy-safe `404` and open one cause-owned exception. |
