| [Epistle pricing](https://www.epistle.org/pricing/) and [pricing update](https://www.epistle.org/pricing-update/) | Current direct page displays `$14/month`; update says price changes from `$12` to `$14` on September 15 and adds sales tax                                                                                                  | The update does not state the year. Its “soon” audit/certification language is not evidence that a certification currently exists                                                                                            |
| [Epistle iOS listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/epistle/id6498960558)                                         | Partner feed/read/respond behavior and dated version-history evidence for login/deep-link improvements, in-feed media, and partner segments                                                                                 | Developer declarations are not independently verified by Apple. “Accessibility features not indicated” means unreported, not necessarily absent                                                                              |
| [Epistle Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.epistle.app.prod)                 | Current Android product description and developer data-safety declarations                                                                                                                                                  | Listing was updated 2026-07-26. Data-safety answers are developer-reported; its “Data can’t be deleted” declaration conflicts with the website privacy policy's deletion-by-email statement                                  |
| [Live sample ministry site](https://orourkes-mexico.epistle.org/)                                                 | One currently served public-page/feed implementation, update permalink, external Give link, Subscribe form, and Login path                                                                                                  | One sample is not the universal Epistle tenant contract. Its visible updates are largely from 2022–2023, so its content and configuration can be old even though the application was live when inspected                     |
| [Epistle sitemap](https://www.epistle.org/sitemap.xml)                                                            | Discoverable first-party page inventory and `lastmod` metadata                                                                                                                                                              | `lastmod` does not establish substantive review, and `robots.txt` returned 404 during this pass                                                                                                                              |

Epistle also states that it has delivered more than 20 million email updates.
That is useful scale context but remains an unaudited vendor assertion. The
[Giving Impact page](https://www.epistle.org/giving-impact/) reports a `$5,178`
annual giving result and associates weekly posting with better outcomes, but it
does not publish a sample, method, confidence interval, or controls. It is not
reliable evidence for a product requirement, recommended cadence, or causal
fundraising claim. The [testimonial page](https://www.epistle.org/testimonials/)
is likewise anecdotal evidence rather than a feature contract.

### 24.2 What Epistle's documented product loop actually does

The following are **documented facts**, not an inferred Epistle data model:

1. **Create an update.** A missionary can create an update with text,
   photographs, and video. Epistle advertises drafts, image captions, and the
   ability to restore previous versions. Its training summary advises one clear
   topic and call to action and describes publishing an update.
   [Home](https://www.epistle.org/),
   [tour](https://www.epistle.org/tour/),
   [training](https://www.epistle.org/training/).
2. **Reuse updates for email.** Epistle says it can combine one or more updates
   into a single email rather than requiring an author to recreate the same
   content in a separate newsletter composer.
   [Home](https://www.epistle.org/),
   [tour](https://www.epistle.org/tour/).
3. **Let partners choose cadence.** Epistle says ministry partners can choose
   daily, weekly, or monthly delivery and that Epistle groups and schedules the
   applicable updates. This is evidence for recipient-controlled cadence, but
   the public documentation does not define cutoff time, timezone, batching,
   duplicate suppression, retry, correction, or segment-intersection rules.
   [Tour](https://www.epistle.org/tour/).
4. **Use bounded audiences.** The iOS version history says version `1.0.29`,
   dated 2025-02-17, added partner segments so updates can be sent to particular
   groups. The public sources do not disclose the segment rule model, overlapping
   membership behavior, or whether segment selection separately governs web,
   email, mobile feed, and notifications.
   [iOS listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/epistle/id6498960558).
5. **Render a ministry website/feed.** Epistle describes a personal ministry
   website containing ministry updates. The live sample confirms an integrated
   “Latest Updates” feed rather than a newsletter archive detached from the
   giving page.
   [MPD page](https://www.epistle.org/mpd/),
   [live sample](https://orourkes-mexico.epistle.org/).
6. **Collect partner responses.** Epistle advertises likes, prayer responses,
   comments, and giving responses, plus reports showing opens and engagement.
   The mobile listing says partners can read and respond in their feed. Public
   documentation does not establish moderation, abuse handling, response
   visibility, or whether every response type is available for every audience.
   [Home](https://www.epistle.org/),
   [iOS listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/epistle/id6498960558).
7. **Join communications to relationship management.** The MPD page documents
   partner/contact profiles, commitments, giving information, tasks, activity,
   direct messages, physical-mail export, and claimed Partner Essentials and
   DonorHub synchronization. The training page describes Integrated,
   Communication, and MPD modes and exposes create-update, invite-partner,
   add-contact, add-commitment, task, activity, and giving-link actions. This is
   evidence that Epistle treats updates as part of a broader supporter workflow;
   it does not prove that update, CRM, financial, and delivery truth share one
   underlying record or authority boundary.
   [MPD page](https://www.epistle.org/mpd/),
   [training](https://www.epistle.org/training/).

Epistle's strongest observable pattern is therefore **author once, project to a
ministry-site feed, and distribute to opted-in partners on their cadence**. Its
public material does **not** say that it implements one immutable canonical
update, version-pinned audience projections, append-only correction events, or
independently authoritative release and delivery facts. Those are proposed
Asym hardening concepts, not facts that may be attributed to Epistle.

### 24.3 Current live-sample UX observation

The live sample at
[orourkes-mexico.epistle.org](https://orourkes-mexico.epistle.org/) was inspected
without authenticating or submitting a form:

- Its top-level experience was a ministry profile with hero content, an
  external **Give** action, **Subscribe**, **About**, **Login**, and a “Latest
  Updates” stream. The Give action led to Pushpay. This proves that at least one
  Epistle site can place updates and giving in one ministry-page experience; it
  does not make Epistle the donation or financial system of record.
- The feed used scannable cards with dates, titles, excerpts, media previews,
  media counts, and tag filters such as `#churchplant`, `#ukraine`, and
  `#epistle`. Selecting a card opened a stable-looking update permalink with
  the full story, media, date, and a share-link control.
- Anonymous visitors could view the sample page and update permalink. The
  responses included `X-Robots-Tag: noindex,nofollow`, a matching robots meta
  directive, `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store`, HSTS,
  `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. This is a
  useful example of **public/link-accessible but search-discouraged**, not an
  authenticated-private audience. It must not be generalized to all Epistle
  sites or treated as a confidentiality control.
- Anonymous rendering did not expose like, prayer, or comment controls during
  this inspection. That does not prove the features are absent; Epistle's app
  listing associates response behavior with ministry partners.
- The sample [Subscribe page](https://orourkes-mexico.epistle.org/subscribe)
  asked only for first name, last name, and email, followed by **Subscribe**.
  Before submission it showed no visible cadence, update scope, permission
  reminder, privacy link, or confirmation explanation. A DOM/accessibility
  snapshot of this one page also did not expose names for its generic textboxes.
  This was not a complete accessibility audit and does not establish all
  Epistle templates. No submission was performed, so confirmation, double
  opt-in, default cadence, unsubscribe, and preference-management behavior
  remain unknown.
- The sample [Login page](https://orourkes-mexico.epistle.org/login) said users
  could enter their Epistle account email or the address where Epistle sends
  updates, then select **Continue**. The next step was not exercised; no
  passwordless-link, code, or identity-linking behavior should be inferred.

This live UX supports the founder's description of an Epistle-like feed
integrated into a giving page. It also exposes a critical vocabulary boundary:
`noindex`, a hidden navigation link, or a stable permalink can reduce discovery
without making released content private.

### 24.4 Security and privacy behavior Epistle documents

Epistle's [security page](https://www.epistle.org/security/) documents three
distinct presentation/delivery controls:

- **Private posts:** described as visible only to ministry partners.
- **Invisible mode:** the missionary site is described as visible only to
  partners, with login required for everyone else.
- **Secure emails:** email bodies omit the protected content and notify the
  partner to log in to view it.

That separation is material: a private web post and a content-bearing email are
different disclosure surfaces. Epistle also recommends working with the sending
organization's security team, using a VPN, and using pseudonyms where needed.
Most importantly, it explicitly warns that Epistle should not be used for
information whose disclosure could harm people and that some contexts should
not use the product at all. That is a stronger and more honest safety boundary
than treating login, encrypted transport, or `noindex` as a guarantee against
copying, screenshots, compromised recipients, or account takeover.

The same page asserts US hosting, a private network, encryption in transit and
at rest, TLS-protected email transport, DKIM/SPF/DMARC, employee-access logging
“where possible,” and MFA/IP allowlisting for services “where possible.” These
are vendor security statements, not evidence of a current SOC 2 report,
penetration test, audit scope, incident SLA, or certification. The pricing-update
page's statement that audit/certification work is coming “soon” must likewise
not be converted into a current compliance badge.

The 2018 [privacy policy](https://www.epistle.org/privacy-policy/) says Epistle
collects account identity/contact information, billing information, user text,
images, audio, video, files, partner-provided messages, IP/browser/device data,
activity logs, and cookies. It also says a user may request account termination
and deletion by email. The current Google Play developer declaration says
“Data can't be deleted.” The public sources do not reconcile whether this is a
platform-form error, an app-specific distinction, or a real policy change. This
is a documented contradiction, not a choice reviewers should silently resolve.

No reviewed first-party source supplied a current subprocessor list, field-level
retention schedule, backup-deletion interval, data-residency option, DPA, breach
notification term, organization-admin export contract, audit-event schema, or
role/revocation latency guarantee.

### 24.5 Comparative calibration from current first-party documentation

These comparators show that **web release** and **email delivery** are not one
industry-invariant action:

| Product and primary source                                                                                                                                                             | Documented behavior                                                                                                                                                                               | Evidence boundary                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Givebutter campaign updates](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/5497893-how-to-use-campaign-updates), updated 2026-06-22                                                         | An admin can create a public campaign update in the supporter feed and separately choose to email it to campaign followers when the required Engage capability is present; recipients can opt out | Strong evidence for separate page-post and email-send choices, not for Asym's data model        |
| [GoFundMe updates](https://support.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/12553895153563-Keep-your-supporters-updated), updated 2026-06-29                                                     | An update is visible to current and potential supporters and is automatically emailed to subscribed supporters; it can also be shared socially                                                    | Evidence that some products intentionally couple public update publication and subscriber email |
| [Substack imported-post behavior](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/360041912391-If-I-import-a-post-from-elsewhere-will-it-be-emailed-out-to-my-list), updated 2024-12-09 | An imported post can exist on the web without being emailed; email delivery is a separate selected action                                                                                         | Narrow but clear evidence that web existence need not imply dispatch                            |
| [Mailchimp subscriber groups/preferences](https://mailchimp.com/help/how-to-use-groups-to-add-or-update-subscriber-preferences/)                                                       | Subscriber-facing groups can collect daily/weekly/monthly preferences and support preference updates; segments can then select recipients                                                         | Evidence for recipient-visible preferences distinct from internal operator-only tags            |

Givebutter's separation resembles Epistle's authoring/reuse concept, while
GoFundMe demonstrates a simpler coupled release model. Neither is “the” modern
standard. The evidence instead requires any Phase 22 design to state plainly
whether a single action changes page visibility, queues email, changes a mobile
feed, notifies subscribers, or only prepares content—and to record the actual
outcome of each surface independently.

### 24.6 Repository continuity: “My Feed” intent versus current incomplete code

The repository history independently confirms the founder's statement that
earlier Asym called the experience **My Feed**. The initial prototype README at
commit `ce041d682` described My Feed as rich-text and multi-media missionary
storytelling with drafts, Public-versus-Partners-Only visibility, follower
requests, reactions, prayers, and comments; it also described automatic donor
feed integration after a gift or Follow. The useful authoring and engagement
intent survives, but donation/follow inference and overloaded visibility do
not. Current code uses **Ministry Updates** while retaining `/feed` as an
implementation route/module:

- `apps/missionary/app/ministry-updates/page.tsx` re-exports the current feed
  client and describes the page as publishing ministry updates to supporters.
- `apps/missionary/app/feed/worker-feed-page-client.tsx` labels the experience
  **Ministry Updates**, includes Published/Drafts UI, and describes sharing with
  supporters.
- `apps/missionary/app/feed/feed-model.ts` still contains mutable
  `published | draft` post state and a “Public feed visible on your giving page”
  reach description.

Those files prove the current naming and an existing UI seam. They do not prove
that the current mutable feed model has D1 assignment authority, D2 reach,
D4/D5 release governance, D9 media safety, exact audience release, Phase 6
dispatch truth, or the canonical cross-surface semantics already described in
section 15.3. Historic naming should be migrated as vocabulary, not treated as
authority to preserve unsafe storage or publication behavior.

### 24.7 Claims the public Epistle evidence does not establish

Every item below remains **unknown or ambiguous**, not a negative finding about
Epistle:

1. Whether there is one canonical stored update or copied web/email/mobile
   content; whether revisions are immutable; and what a restore operation does
   to already released or emailed versions.
2. Whether organization staff can require review, approve, reject, override,
   withdraw, correct, or restore missionary-authored updates; who can coauthor;
   and whether husband-and-wife or project teams share one authoring stream.
3. Whether web reach, segment membership, email inclusion, mobile-feed reach,
   push notification, and interaction permission are separate audience facts or
   one overloaded visibility field.
4. Exact segment evaluation time, schedule cutoff, timezone, recipient dedupe,
   overlapping-segment behavior, retry, suppression, unsubscribe, complaint,
   bounce, resend, or post-send correction handling.
5. Whether private-post access is rechecked on every request; how quickly
   membership revocation takes effect; whether media URLs remain valid; and how
   caches, forwarded email, screenshots, downloads, or quoted replies behave.
6. Comment/prayer/like visibility, moderation, deletion, abuse reporting,
   notification, export, retention, and author-blocking behavior.
7. Full-fidelity export of update revisions, media, captions, comments,
   reactions, partner preferences, consent evidence, schedules, and delivery
   events. The MPD/training pages verify a CSV/physical-mail workflow, not a
   complete custody/export contract for all update data.
8. API or webhook availability, localization, right-to-left support, media
   size/type limits, video-transcoding behavior, accessibility conformance,
   keyboard/mobile authoring parity, public-page performance limits, or service
   recovery objectives.
9. Tenant/legal-entity isolation, database RLS posture, staff auditability,
   service-role boundaries, role taxonomy, break-glass access, or exact
   environment separation.
10. Whether a Give response is only an external link, an attributed referral,
    or a native integration for every site. The live sample's Pushpay link and
    Epistle's integration marketing do not grant Epistle financial authority.

The [Epistle status page](https://status.epistle.org/) returned a fetch error
during this pass and exposed no trustworthy current incident/uptime record, so
it was not used as reliability evidence.

### 24.8 Evidence boundary for D11's adversarial review

Epistle supplies strong primary-source evidence for the human workflow the
founder wants: write a ministry update once, show it in an integrated ministry
site/feed, reuse it in email, let partners choose cadence, target bounded partner
segments, and preserve lightweight relationship/engagement context. Its
security guidance also correctly distinguishes authenticated content from
search-discouraged public content and refuses to promise that sensitive content
can be made harmless merely by putting it behind a login.

Epistle does **not** publicly prove the harder contract named in the D11 option:
one canonical versioned object, exact audience-scoped immutable releases,
separate current authorization and historical delivery truth, correction and
tombstone semantics, cross-tenant enforcement, organization review authority,
complete export, or accessibility and operational certification. Those claims
must be specified and production-tested from Asym's own owner-domain contracts;
they cannot be justified by competitor analogy or by Epistle marketing copy.

## 25. D11 adversarial review — canonical Ministry Update and audience projections

**Status:** Ratified by the founder as Phase 22 D11 on 2026-08-06. The exact
decision is recorded in the Phase 22 decision log and ADR-0128.

### 25.1 Verdict

The product direction is correct, but a naive implementation is unsafe. The
permanent shape is not one `visibility` value and not a copied post for every
surface. It is:

1. one stable Ministry Update identity;
2. immutable Update Revisions, with a mutable autosaved working draft only
   before submission;
3. one immutable Audience Release Manifest expressing the exact requested
   public and/or supporter consequences;
4. independently authoritative and independently recoverable Public Page and
   authenticated purpose-authorized Supporter projections; and
5. a separate, deliberate supporter-notification occurrence whose recipients,
   consent, suppression, cadence, dispatch, and provider outcomes remain owned
   outside Phase 22.

This keeps Epistle's useful **write once, stay connected with little overhead**
experience while preserving the authority boundaries already ratified in
Phase 22 D1–D10. The current Supabase `posts` table, Payload
`ministry-updates`, `/feed` UI, follower requests, feed preferences, browser
collections, and engagement rows are migration inputs, not authority.

### 25.2 What Asym should copy, improve, and refuse

**Copy the proven human workflow:** a fast mobile composer; small updates rather
than newsletter-scale production; drafts and version recovery; safe still
images with captions and alt text; a ministry-page feed; authenticated deep
links; recipient-controlled cadence; lightweight love/prayer/comment response;
and one place for the author to understand what happened.

**Improve the contract:** one candidate may request both audiences, but each
projection has its own exact outcome. A notification can be requested in the
same final review without becoming the release itself. Current supporter access
is re-proved on every protected read; only dispatch freezes exact recipients.
Corrections, withdrawals, safety containment, and privacy-safe tombstones are
append-only and projection-specific. Delivery analytics are advisory and never
proof of reading or relationship quality.

**Refuse unsafe inheritance:** no `high | medium | low` security presets; no
`publicMirror`; no generic `partners` flag; no automatic follower approval; no
gift, follow, spouse, teammate, subject, author, project, page, or Support
Assignment inference; no raw tenant-wide feed; no implicit email caused by
publication; no raw Payload or provider status as release truth; and no public
video until D9/Phase 29 separately certifies an exact video family.

Givebutter's current campaign-update flow and Ghost's current publishing flow
both present web publication and email as separate choices with a consequence
summary. Gmail requires opt-in discipline and one-click unsubscribe for
subscription messages. Mailchimp supports recipient-facing topic/cadence
preferences rather than treating internal tags as consent. Those patterns are
safer for Asym than GoFundMe's documented auto-email-on-update coupling. The
Epistle-style daily/weekly/monthly experience remains available, but only after
the owning communication phases prove the exact recipient and preference.

### 25.3 Exact ownership and data contract

- **Phase 22 owns:** canonical Update identity; exact source/purpose binding;
  immutable revision; typed common body and optional explicitly authored
  public-safe variant; requested audience manifest; Public Page and Supporter
  projection occurrences/current heads; projection-specific correction,
  withdrawal, containment, and privacy-safe tombstone; deterministic feed
  ordering/cursor; and the source occurrence requesting a supporter
  notification.
- **D1 owns** contributor authority. Authorship never grants view, review,
  release, notification, or page-inclusion authority.
- **D3 owns** the exact page-scoped Feed Binding. A Public Page projection may
  render only where that binding selects its canonical source/purpose. A page
  pins the feed contract, not a copied list of updates.
- **D4/D5 own** the only review-and-release lane. One candidate and one staff
  review may cover both audience previews; there are not duplicate reviews per
  surface.
- **D2 and Phase 10 own** current public reach and every public/protected egress
  ceiling. Phase 10 may narrow or block an audience or the whole capability and
  can require notification-only email; it cannot be overridden by an author or
  tenant preset.
- **Phase 12 owns** current principal/capability authorization. Authentication,
  role, a copied link, or a prior successful read grants nothing by itself.
- **Phase 9/28 own** supporter relationships, audience purpose, contactability,
  and any governed saved supporter group. Phase 22 stores an exact owner
  reference and never builds a second follower network or segment DSL.
- **Phase 24 owns** locale truth. No public or supporter projection uses an
  unsafe locale fallback.
- **Phase 25 owns** supporter preference-center UX. **Phase 17** owns governed
  notification presentation, sender/profile, and digest rendering. **Phase 6**
  owns consent, suppression, recipient dispatch, dedupe, provider outcome, and
  communication history. **Phase 32** is only the external Mailchimp bridge.
- **D9/Phase 29 own** media admission, sanitized bytes, derivative delivery,
  retention, and disposal. **D7/Phase 13 own** the page's Give action and money
  truth; a reaction or update never creates a financial relationship.

Each released projection repeats or references with enforced same-scope keys
the exact Tenant, Legal Entity, environment, canonical source kind/id and
purpose, Update and Revision, audience kind, audience-contract version, locale,
release candidate/occurrence, current authorization and safety epochs,
renderer/profile generation, and D9 media manifest. A Public Page projection
also carries exact Site, Page, Page Family, Feed Binding, and D2 reach
coordinates. Cache keys, cursors, jobs, engagement queries, diagnostics, and
communication correlations carry the same complete scope.

The Supporter projection pins a governed **audience rule**, not a permanent
recipient list. Current access is re-evaluated on every read, including whether
a later supporter may see earlier updates under the Phase 28-owned history
rule. A notification request separately resolves and freezes the exact eligible
recipient/channel set at dispatch, after current consent and suppression
reproof. Overlapping groups dedupe there, not in Phase 22.

### 25.4 Quiet, explicit UX

#### Missionary author

The canonical navigation label is **Ministry updates**. The legacy `/feed`
route may redirect and search/help may recognize **My Feed**, but the product
must never expose two concepts or stores.

The ordinary mobile-first flow is:

1. **Write** in one autosaving editor. Show `Saving…`, `Saved`, offline, and
   conflict states; restoration creates a new working revision rather than
   rewriting released history.
2. **Add images** through D9, with crop/focal preview, caption, alt-text help,
   processing/error state, and no source filename or raw provider URL.
3. **Choose who can read this:** `Supporters`, `Public page`, or `Public page
and supporters`. Show only currently supported choices and seed the tenant's
   default. `Save draft` is a separate action, not a fictional private release.
4. **Preview consequences** in `Supporters` and/or `Public page` tabs. If both
   audiences use one body, no duplicate editing appears. A collapsed
   **Customize public summary** control permits an explicitly authored and
   reviewed public-safe variant; Asym never auto-truncates or AI-redacts a
   protected body into public content.
5. **Release deliberately.** The final sheet states the exact pages/audiences
   and offers `Publish` plus, only when the supporter and communication owners
   are ready, `Publish & notify supporters`. Under review mode this exact intent
   travels in the one D4/D5 candidate. Recipient cadence remains their choice.

The completion view never says only **Published**. It reports independent facts
such as:

- `Visible on 1 public ministry page`;
- `Visible to authorized supporters`;
- `Notification not requested`;
- `Queued for 63 eligible supporters according to their preferences`; or
- `Public page visible · supporter release needs attention`.

Healthy results stay compact; detail opens only on request. An exact problem has
one owner, plain-language effect, and safe retry or correction action.

#### Staff reviewer

Staff receive one review item with a semantic diff, exact author/source/purpose,
affected page(s), `Public page` and `Supporters` previews, media/alt-text status,
Phase 10 warnings, and notification consequence. The normal choices remain D5's
`Approve & publish` and `Request changes`; D11 adds no second approval system.
Automatic-release tenants receive no routine queue noise.

#### Public visitor and authenticated supporter

Public pages show only current D3-bound Public Page projections in a bounded,
deterministically ordered **Latest updates** section. The section collapses
quietly when disabled or empty. Give remains the page's D7 action, not an
update-owned designation.

Authorized supporters see **Updates** in the donor experience and may follow an
email/app deep link through ordinary sign-in continuation. Every content,
media, comment, reaction, refresh, and pagination request reauthorizes the
exact projection. Unauthorized viewers receive a uniform non-enumerating
response; title, author, excerpt, media, counts, comments, metadata, cache, and
timing do not reveal protected existence.

The authoring tool and output must satisfy WCAG 2.2 AA and the applicable W3C
ATAG principles: keyboard operation, 320 CSS-pixel reflow, visible focus,
adequate targets/contrast, semantic headings, accessible editor controls,
status announcements, error recovery, alt-text prompting, reduced motion, and
previews that help authors produce accessible output.

### 25.5 Edge and failure semantics

- **One projection succeeds and the other fails:** preserve the successful
  result, preserve the prior-good head for the failed audience, show the exact
  residual work, and retry only that idempotent occurrence.
- **Supporter access is revoked:** the next protected request denies access.
  Historical release and communication evidence remain; a sent email or
  screenshot cannot be recalled.
- **A notification is queued when a correction/withdrawal occurs:** the
  notification remains pinned to its exact revision and is suppressed if still
  cancellable under Phase 6. If already sent, the UI never claims recall; an
  explicit corrective notification may be authorized as a new occurrence.
- **Phase 10 narrows:** affected current serving, previews, metadata, media, and
  engagement fail closed at the smallest scope. Unaffected audience projections
  and immutable history remain intact.
- **A public page is retired:** public serving follows D8. The Supporter
  projection is not silently retired. Conversely, a supporter-audience change
  does not mutate the public release.
- **A source, purpose, locale, or media binding is wrong:** do not edit the
  released revision in place. Withdraw/supersede the exact affected projection
  and release a corrected revision after current proof.
- **A spouse, teammate, or staff contributor authors:** D1 proves the action and
  records the actor; contributor relationship never selects the source,
  audience, page, supporter cohort, or notification recipients.
- **No eligible supporters exist:** supporter release may still succeed only if
  its governing history rule permits future eligible readers. Notification
  truth reports zero eligible recipients; it never reports sent.
- **A provider, Payload, Phase 28, or Phase 6 dependency is unavailable:** block
  only the new affected positive action, keep prior safe projections readable,
  retain the draft, and expose a cause-owned exception. Never fall back to a
  broader audience, raw CMS data, or blind send.

### 25.6 Ruthless adversarial matrix

| Category                          | Concern? | What could go wrong and why it matters                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Severity | Likelihood      | Best permanent fix or prevention                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Brittleness                       | **Yes**  | One mutable `public/partners/private` field or an atomic “Both” action collapses content, public serving, supporter access, and email. A partial outage then produces ambiguous or silently inconsistent truth.                                                                                              | Critical | Likely          | Immutable revisions and one requested-audience manifest; separate current heads/outcomes per projection; request-time safety/access reproof; residual-only recovery.                                                                                                        |
| Technical debt                    | **Yes**  | Payload `publishedAt`, Supabase `posts`, `/feed` security levels, tenant-wide public readers, interaction APIs, and notification preferences form incompatible authorities and serializers. Wrapping all of them would institutionalize drift.                                                               | Critical | Likely          | One canonical operational contract behind narrow server commands; Payload is authoring substrate only; complete census and one authority cutover; retire legacy flags/readers instead of maintaining translators forever.                                                   |
| Edge cases                        | **Yes**  | Coauthors, project-only updates, multiple page bindings, later supporters, revoked supporters, page retirement, locale gaps, withdrawn media, overlapping groups, corrections after send, and mixed projection outcomes can expose the wrong content or lose history.                                        | Critical | Likely          | Exact source/purpose and audience-contract references; immutable per-audience occurrences; explicit history rule; no locale fallback; append-only correction/withdrawal; a tested transition matrix.                                                                        |
| Footguns                          | **Yes**  | `Public Mirror`, `Partners only`, auto-approved donors, copied protected links, arbitrary segments, in-place edits/deletes, or a preselected hidden email send make disclosure and spam easy.                                                                                                                | Critical | Likely          | Plain-language audience choices; Save draft outside release; visible consequence review; deliberate `Publish & notify`; governed audiences only; immutable release and inert unauthorized links.                                                                            |
| Tenant safety                     | **Yes**  | A missing Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, source, purpose, audience, locale, or environment condition in a row, join, RLS policy, cursor, cache, media read, engagement call, or job can mix organizations. Service roles and definer views can bypass RLS.                                                      | Critical | Possible        | Complete structural scope; same-scope composite constraints; indexed restrictive and forced RLS; security-invoker views or revoked raw access; narrow service commands; scope-poison and cross-tenant tests.                                                                |
| Over-engineering                  | **Yes**  | An arbitrary ACL/segment language, frozen follower social graph, per-surface post copies, D11-owned digest scheduler, or per-block permissions would make a simple update unusable and duplicate later phases.                                                                                               | High     | Likely          | Three release choices, one tenant default, rare progressive disclosure, code-owned audience kinds, owner-domain references, and no Phase 22 follower, consent, sender, or scheduler product.                                                                                |
| UX/UI and user friction           | **Yes**  | Authors and staff cannot tell who can read an update, whether it is live, whether review is pending, or whether anyone was emailed; duplicate reviews and dense security jargon will suppress use.                                                                                                           | High     | Likely          | One mobile composer, one review candidate, audience preview tabs, exact consequence sheet, independent calm status lines, tenant defaults, healthy-state compression, and accessible recovery.                                                                              |
| Hidden coupling                   | **Yes**  | Public release, supporter access, page lifecycle, notification, delivery, comments, and giving could trigger or undo one another. A retry could duplicate email or a page withdrawal could erase protected history.                                                                                          | Critical | Likely          | Stable IDs plus separate idempotent occurrences/current heads connected by an outbox; each owner retries only residual work; no downstream side-effect replay.                                                                                                              |
| Failure modes                     | **Yes**  | Projection release can time out after commit; cache invalidation can fail; a queued digest can race a correction; Phase 28/6 can be unavailable; media can later be contained. Blind retry or fallback can leak or duplicate.                                                                                | Critical | Possible        | CAS and idempotency keys; inspect-before-retry; previous-good head; exact revision fences; scoped cache invalidation/backstop; smallest-scope fail-closed containment; cause-owned recovery.                                                                                |
| Data integrity risks              | **Yes**  | Mutable content/status, duplicate release, nondeterministic ordering, inferred audiences, destructive deletion, or engagement attached only to a mutable post rewrites what people saw and breaks audit or pagination.                                                                                       | Critical | Likely          | Stable Update ID; immutable revisions and release coordinates; unique idempotency constraints; keyset cursor `(released_at, projection_id)`; append-only successor/tombstone; exact engagement projection/version references.                                               |
| Security and privacy risks        | **Yes**  | Protected content can leak through subject/preheader, email body, Open Graph metadata, search, caches, raw media/file names, comments, reaction identities, logs, timing, or an IDOR. Login alone does not prove supporter access.                                                                           | Critical | Possible        | Phase 10 per-egress proof; notification-only secure mode; D9 derivatives; sanitized closed renderer; no protected metadata; uniform denial; current object-level authorization on every resource; privacy-safe projection-separated engagement.                             |
| Scalability and performance risks | **Yes**  | Tenant-wide/offset scans, nested unindexed RLS joins, fan-out during publish, global cache purges, and synchronous media/email work will degrade with tenants, posts, supporters, and engagement.                                                                                                            | High     | Likely          | Indexed exact-scope read projections; bounded keyset feeds; authorization-bound cache keys/tags; asynchronous durable Phase 6 fan-out; tenant-fair queues/rate limits; measured SLOs and load tests.                                                                        |
| Operational burden                | **Yes**  | Too many audience profiles, repeated staff certification, manual follower approval, separate public/private copies, and opaque denied access create constant support work and tribal knowledge.                                                                                                              | High     | Likely          | One seeded default plus rare Customize; D4/D5 automatic lane where chosen; machine-prepared consequence/exception summaries; one explain-access surface; no healthy-state queue noise.                                                                                      |
| Observability gaps                | **Yes**  | A single `published` badge hides public serving, protected serving, notification creation, recipient suppression, provider delivery, stale cache, or safety containment. Teams cannot repair the correct cause.                                                                                              | Critical | Likely          | Correlation across revision/projection/notification without collapsing status; coverage watermarks; privacy-redacted reason taxonomy; expected-versus-current counts; owner-specific alerts and diagnostics.                                                                |
| Dependency and integration risks  | **Yes**  | Payload status, Supabase JWT metadata, browser grants, Resend topics, Mailchimp segments, CDN URLs, or provider open/click analytics can become accidental authority or change semantics on upgrade.                                                                                                         | High     | Possible        | Provider-neutral internal contracts; exact adapter capabilities/versions; Payload as authoring only; providers as transport/evidence only; no user-editable JWT authorization; kill switches and recertification on dependency change.                                      |
| Migration and upgrade risks       | **Yes**  | Legacy My Feed rows, `publicMirror`, `partners`/`partners_only`, follower requests, hard-coded/coarse preferences, mutable Payload documents, raw HTML/media, and historic sends lack exact modern evidence. Auto-adoption could publish or email the wrong people; dual write creates permanent divergence. | Critical | Likely          | Complete migration manifest with canonical/adapted/quarantined/historical-only/retired disposition; absence of proof maps private; D9 reprocessing; one cutover; preserve historic send evidence without inferring audience; no dual write/read authority.                  |
| Other development hazards         | **Yes**  | Concurrent edits/releases, TOCTOU authorization, stale epochs, reaction/comment abuse, timezone cutoff errors, duplicate segment recipients, hydration leaks, unsafe rollback, and open-rate overclaim can remain after a plausible implementation.                                                          | Critical | Possible–Likely | Optimistic concurrency and CAS; transactional outbox; dispatch-time proof/dedupe; moderation/rate limits; recipient-local cadence owner; server authorization; append-only successor rollback; property/concurrency/abuse/deployment-skew tests; advisory analytics labels. |

Every requested category therefore contains a real concern in the unhardened
option. None requires abandoning C-prime; each is addressed by separating
authority while keeping the interaction quiet.

### 25.7 Best path forward and certification order

1. **Ratify vocabulary and ownership first.** Keep **Ministry Update** canonical;
   mark **My Feed** as a legacy alias; define Revision, Audience Release
   Manifest, Public Page Projection, Supporter Projection, and Notification
   occurrence without giving later phases' authority to D11.
2. **Lock the simple UX contract.** Prototype and test the three audience
   choices, separate Save draft, dual preview, optional public-safe variant,
   one consequence sheet, and independent outcome copy with missionaries,
   communications staff, reviewers, restricted-worker security staff, donors,
   keyboard users, and screen-reader users before schema/API implementation.
3. **Build the canonical immutable spine and isolation first.** Add exact scope,
   same-scope constraints, indexed RLS, narrow commands, revisions, manifests,
   projection heads, outbox, correction/withdrawal, and deterministic cursor.
   Raw `posts`, `follows`, comments, and Payload collections cannot remain a
   parallel browser authority.
4. **Connect public serving.** Consume D3 Feed Binding, D4/D5 release, D2 reach,
   Phase 10, locale, D9 media, and Phase 5 rendering. Certify public metadata,
   caching, containment, and retired-page behavior before anonymous launch.
5. **Connect protected serving.** Consume the ratified Phase 9/28 purpose-owned
   supporter contract and Phase 12 current authorization. Apply the same exact
   resolver to content, media, pagination, comments, reactions, counts, and
   deep links.
6. **Connect notification last as a separate occurrence.** Resolve the exact
   revision and released Supporter projection; then let Phases 28/17/6 own
   recipients, preference/cadence, consent, suppression, rendering, dedupe,
   dispatch, and provider outcome. Notification failure never rolls back a
   release; a release retry never sends again.
7. **Migrate once, conservatively.** Shadow-classify every legacy Supabase,
   Payload, follower, preference, engagement, and send row. Treat public or
   supporter visibility as unproved unless exact evidence exists. Reprocess
   media, compare counts/digests, cut over one authority, and monitor overlap,
   gaps, and unauthorized reads.
8. **Certify production-shaped behavior.** Required suites cover cross-Tenant/
   Legal-Entity/Site/source/audience/locale substitution; restricted-worker and
   current-safety narrowing; contributor/coauthor/reviewer matrices; later and
   revoked supporters; mixed projection outcomes; correction-versus-send;
   retries/concurrency; cache/search/social metadata; media containment; XSS
   and link safety; engagement abuse/privacy; consent/unsubscribe/bounce;
   cursor stability; accessibility; mobile/offline authoring; load, tenant
   fairness, dependency outage, deployment skew, and append-only rollback.

### 25.8 Ratified wording

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — one canonical,
> source-scoped, independently and immutably versioned Ministry Update with one
> exact Audience Release Manifest and independently authoritative Public Page
> and authenticated purpose-authorized Supporter Release Projections; composed
> through D1 contributor authority, D3's exact Ministry Update Feed Binding,
> D4/D5's sole Review & Release lane, D2's current Publication Reach, Phase
> 10's per-egress safety ceiling, Phase 12's current authorization, Phase 24
> locale truth, and D9/Phase 29-certified media; using one quiet accessible
> Ministry updates experience—formerly My Feed only as a migration/search/help
> alias—with autosave and version recovery, separate Save draft, a
> tenant-seeded `Supporters`, `Public page`, or `Public page and supporters`
> choice, exact audience previews, an optional explicitly authored public-safe
> variant, one consequence review, and independently truthful outcomes. Every

> source/purpose, Update Revision, audience contract, locale, safety and
> authorization epochs, release occurrence, renderer/profile generation, and

**Architectural record:**

## 26. D12 research — bounded Ministry Update engagement

> **Status:** Historical research and options that preceded D12's ratification
> on 2026-08-06. The ratified hardened decision is recorded in §27 and
> [ADR-0129](../../adr/0129-bounded-supporter-response-profiles.md). D11 remains
> authoritative for the canonical Ministry Update, audience-scoped release
> projections, current-access reproof, and the separation of engagement,
> notification, and Giving truth.

### 26.1 Decision seam

D11 establishes where a Ministry Update exists and who may read each exact
release projection. It deliberately does not decide the interaction product
inside that audience. The next bounded decision is:

> **What responses may a viewer make to a released Ministry Update, who may
> read each response or aggregate, and what moderation, notification, privacy,
> retention, and accessibility contract applies?**

The founder's Epistle reference is valuable for the human loop, but it is not a
safe database or authorization specification. This research therefore keeps
the useful **read → like/pray/comment → creator learns that supporters engaged**
loop while checking every undocumented behavior before recommending it.

### 26.2 What Epistle documents — and what it does not

The current [Epistle tour](https://www.epistle.org/tour/) says ministry partners
can respond to updates with **likes, prayers, comments, and/or giving**, and
that the missionary receives detailed insight into who opens, likes, prays,
and comments. The [iOS listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/epistle/id6498960558)
also describes likes, prayers, and comments as partner responses. Epistle's
[security page](https://www.epistle.org/security/) separately says private
posts are limited to ministry partners and offers an invisible-site and
secure-email mode. Together, those sources establish the intended relationship
loop; they do not establish the implementation contract below.

| Behavior                                                                             | Publicly documented by Epistle? | Evidence boundary for Asym                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Like, prayer, comment, and giving response categories                                | **Yes**                         | These are product categories, not proof that they share one transaction, authorization rule, or database row. Giving remains D7/Phase 13-owned.                                                                                   |
| Missionary insight into opens, likes, prayers, and comments                          | **Yes**                         | Epistle does not document count consistency, identity visibility, privacy controls, or whether analytics are exact versus advisory.                                                                                               |
| Ministry-partner response in the app                                                 | **Yes**                         | The public sources do not prove that anonymous visitors may respond. The live public sample inspected for §24 showed no anonymous response controls.                                                                              |
| Notifications for reactions/comments                                                 | **Partly**                      | Testimonials mention prayer/comment notifications and supporter-activity email, but testimonials are anecdotes, not a stable delivery or preference contract.                                                                     |
| Public versus private response visibility                                            | **No**                          | Epistle does not state whether counts, identities, comments, or replies inherit the update audience or cross between public/private views.                                                                                        |
| Replies, nesting depth, edits, self-deletion, and locking                            | **No**                          | No current first-party product contract was found for these behaviors.                                                                                                                                                            |
| Moderator roles, reports, hide/restore, blocking, appeals, or audit history          | **No**                          | The [terms](https://www.epistle.org/terms-of-use/) prohibit harmful or offensive use and reserve suspension/termination rights, but do not describe tenant moderation tools.                                                      |
| Spam controls, rate limits, duplicate detection, link policy, or automated screening | **No**                          | These cannot be inferred from a working comment box.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Engagement export and retention                                                      | **No**                          | The 2018 [privacy policy](https://www.epistle.org/privacy-policy/) mentions deletion by email, while the current Google Play developer declaration says data cannot be deleted. That conflict is not a usable retention contract. |
| Accessibility semantics and keyboard/screen-reader behavior                          | **No**                          | The app listings and public marketing do not publish an interaction accessibility conformance contract.                                                                                                                           |

The safe conclusion is narrow: Epistle validates that supporters value a
low-effort response loop. It does **not** justify anonymous comments, public
identity exposure, cross-audience counts, arbitrary reactions, unbounded reply
trees, unconfigurable email, destructive moderation, or coupling a response to
a donation.

### 26.3 Comparable-product findings

Current first-party documentation shows several useful patterns and several
anti-patterns:

- [Givebutter campaign updates](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/5497893-how-to-use-campaign-updates)
  place public updates in the supporter feed beneath the donation action, while
  email is a separate choice. This supports visual adjacency without making
  content release, notification, and Giving one fact.
- [Givebutter supporter-feed moderation](https://help.givebutter.com/en/articles/3586667-how-to-hide-messages-in-the-supporter-feed)
  lets an admin hide a message or the whole feed. Its warning that a billing
  name may remain public under one toggle combination demonstrates why public
  identity must be projected deliberately, not inherited from a transaction or
  profile. Requiring vendor support to restore or anonymize a post is an
  operational anti-pattern for Asym.
- [GoFundMe comments](https://support.gofundme.com/hc/en-us/articles/204191158-Adding-and-editing-words-of-support-or-comments)
  require both a signed-in account and a donation, support replies, let an
  author delete a comment, and bound edits to “words of support.” This supports
  authenticated relationship-gated writing, but Asym must not infer a durable
  supporter relationship from one gift.
- [Patreon comment settings](https://support.patreon.com/hc/en-us/articles/19789361628045-Comment-settings)
  use a saved default plus a per-post setting, permit comments to be disabled,
  retain hidden comments for the creator, apply rate controls, and expose
  auto-moderation mistakes for restoration. This supports a bounded tenant
  default and per-update narrowing. Patreon's early-access media comments and
  audience matrix also show how quickly a simple response surface can become a
  second social network.
- [Patreon blocking](https://support.patreon.com/hc/en-us/articles/207982093-Everything-you-need-to-know-about-blocking-another-user)
  demonstrates that harassment controls must address both future interaction
  and existing comments. Its platform-global blocking consequences are too
  broad for a multi-tenant CRM; Asym needs tenant- and source-bounded
  restriction.
- [Substack comment moderation](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/5780832770452-Can-I-moderate-comments-on-my-Substack-posts)
  uses reader reports, a reported queue, reasons, and approve/remove outcomes.
  Its daily notification cadence is materially quieter than one email per
  report.
- [Substack Reply Rules](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/49712271829012-What-are-Reply-Rules-on-Substack)
  hide rather than immediately delete suspected comments and allow review and
  restoration. Exempting paid subscribers, followed accounts, and contributors
  from screening is an unsafe trust bypass that Asym must not copy.
- [Substack notification controls](https://support.substack.com/hc/en-us/articles/14740062438932-How-do-I-disable-Substack-Notes-notifications)
  separate reply and like preferences across email and push. The useful lesson
  is per-type muting; Phase 22 must still leave channel, consent, suppression,
  cadence, and delivery to Phases 17/6.

The convergent modern pattern is a verified writer, a clear audience, a saved
default with per-item narrowing, reversible moderation, reporting, rate limits,
quiet preference-aware notifications, and a visible way for a contributor to
remove their own content. The products diverge sharply on public identity,
restore behavior, automation, and global blocking, so none should be copied
whole.

### 26.4 Repository truth and migration hazards

The repository contains useful prototype seams, but none is safe to promote as
D12 authority without replacement or hardening:

- `packages/ui/components/ministry-update/reaction-bar.tsx` centralizes the
  reaction UI, uses native buttons with `aria-pressed`, honors reduced motion,
  and supports quiet/static presentations. That is a valuable presentation and
  testing seam.
- `packages/ui/components/ministry-update/normalize.ts` carries three legacy
  reaction dialects and canonicalizes `love`, `prayer`, and `fire`, defaulting
  missing counts to zero. The `fire` reaction is not documented Epistle parity,
  is semantically unclear in this context, and a missing authoritative count
  must not silently become a certified zero.
- `packages/ui/components/ministry-update/comments-dialog.tsx` renders one flat
  client list and retains an optimistic comment when the transport reports
  `persisted: false`. `packages/api/src/posts/comments.ts` confirms that POST is
  a read-only demo no-op. A user can therefore see a comment that was never
  saved; that behavior must be removed rather than migrated.
- The same comment GET proves only authentication, queries by `post_id`, and
  returns raw profile first name, last name, and avatar. It does not prove the
  D11 audience projection or use an audience-safe display identity.
- `packages/api/src/posts/reaction-route-utils.ts` proves the viewer and post
  have the same tenant before a service-role RPC. It does not prove current
  exact release/audience authorization. Service-role execution makes that
  missing check a critical authorization gap, not a harmless RLS fallback.
- `supabase/migrations/20260625002117_canonical_tanstack_db_realtime_rls.sql`
  grants anonymous and authenticated browser reads to comments and reaction
  rows whenever the legacy parent post is published/public. The interaction
  rows carry no D11 release-projection, audience, Legal Entity, purpose,
  environment, or privacy-display coordinate, so this policy cannot safely
  represent D12.
- `supabase/schema.sql` permits recursive `post_comments.parent_id`. The atomic
  add RPC checks that a parent belongs to the post, but does not bound reply
  depth. The delete RPC removes only a comment and direct children, so deeper
  descendants can create integrity or deletion failures.
- `packages/api/src/admin/comments/comment.ts` allows staff to rewrite comment
  bodies in place and delete a thread. D12 needs immutable self-edit revisions
  and explicit hide/redact/tombstone moderation outcomes; staff must not
  silently impersonate a commenter by rewriting their words.
- Reaction and comment counts are mutable scalars on `posts`. Interaction rows
  are also placed in the Realtime publication. Neither design supplies
  audience-separated counts, version fences, privacy-safe realtime
  authorization, or correction evidence.
- Existing unit tests around reactions, interaction storage, comment auth, and
  admin tenant scoping provide reusable public seams. They do not yet certify
  exact audience substitution, cross-tenant/Legal-Entity isolation, comment
  lifecycle, abuse limits, notification dedupe, privacy erasure/export, or the
  accessible failure path.

Nia was queried with the required `Asymmetric-al/core` scope and task/stack
preamble, but its indexed paths and test inventory were stale during this
pass. The findings above come from direct current-worktree reads and exact
`rg` searches; indexed snippets were not treated as current authority.

### 26.5 Product options

#### Option A-prime — Acknowledgements only

Authenticated, currently purpose-authorized supporters may select **Like** or
**I prayed** on the exact Supporter projection. Viewers see audience-local
aggregates; authorized contributors and staff may inspect privacy-projected
responders. There are no comments or replies.

- **Strengths:** smallest attack surface, almost no moderation workload, very
  fast mobile interaction, and much safer for restricted workers.
- **Weaknesses:** loses the conversational part of the Epistle loop and pushes
  meaningful replies into disconnected email or messaging.
- **Best fit:** tenants that primarily need prayer acknowledgement and cannot
  staff moderation.

#### Option B-prime — Fixed Epistle-style supporter responses

Every authenticated, currently purpose-authorized supporter receives **Like**,
**I prayed**, and one flat comment box on every Supporter projection. Public
pages remain read-only and Giving remains the existing page CTA.

- **Strengths:** clear, recognizable, and close to the behavior Epistle
  actually documents; fewer settings than C-prime.
- **Weaknesses:** forces a comment/moderation workload on every tenant and every
  update, provides no quiet acknowledgement-only mode, and cannot safely serve
  restricted or low-capacity organizations without one-off exceptions.
- **Best fit:** a homogeneous product where every tenant commits to active
  community moderation.

#### Option C-prime — Bounded Supporter Response Profiles — Recommended

One versioned tenant default chooses among three code-owned modes:
**Responses off**, **Like + I prayed**, or **Like + I prayed + comments**. An
optional project-page-family default is exposed only when the tenant uses
project updates. On an individual update, an authorized author or staff member
may keep the default or **narrow** it—for example, close comments—but may not
broaden beyond the tenant ceiling. No arbitrary reaction picker, ACL builder,
or moderation workflow designer is introduced.

All writes require a verified authenticated identity and current access to the
exact D11 Supporter projection. Anonymous public-page visitors may read a
public release but cannot react or comment. When the same update has a
Supporter projection, the public page may show a quiet **Supporter? Sign in to
respond** link into that protected experience; it never embeds protected
counts, identities, or comments in the anonymously cached page.

- **Strengths:** preserves the Epistle connection loop, lets tenants avoid a
  feature they cannot moderate, keeps restricted/public surfaces safe, and
  remains understandable because it exposes three named modes rather than a
  rule matrix.
- **Weaknesses:** requires a real engagement-space model, moderation queue,
  privacy projection, notification preferences, and migration from the demo
  tables. Those are necessary complexity once comments are enabled.
- **Why recommended:** it gives the tenant meaningful control without turning
  Phase 22 into a social-network platform or pretending all tenants have the
  same risk and staffing profile.

### 26.6 Recommended C-prime contract if selected

#### Exact authority and data shape

1. A **Supporter Response Profile Version** is prospective and immutable. D11's
   Supporter Release occurrence pins its exact version. A later default change
   does not silently open, close, or relabel existing discussion.
2. Every **Engagement Space** carries the complete Tenant, Legal Entity,
   environment, canonical source/purpose, Update ID and Revision, Supporter
   Release Projection and version, audience contract, safety/authorization
   epoch, and Response Profile version. Same-scope constraints prevent a
   comment or reaction from attaching across any coordinate.
3. Current audience access is re-proved on every list, count, react, unreact,
   comment, reply, edit, delete, report, moderate, export, stream, and
   notification-deep-link request. Authentication alone and tenant equality
   are insufficient. Narrow service commands validate authorization before any
   elevated database operation; raw interaction tables are not browser APIs.
4. **Like** and **I prayed** are fixed typed acknowledgements. `I prayed` is an
   actor's acknowledgement, not proof, an endorsement, or a financial event.
   The existing `fire` value is historical/migration input only unless a later
   decision explicitly adopts it.
5. One actor has at most one current acknowledgement of each kind per exact
   Engagement Space. Add/remove uses idempotency keys and append-only
   occurrences; audience-local current counts are derived or transactionally
   projected from those occurrences, never copied into the canonical update.
   No cross-audience grand total exists.
6. Comments are plain text with bounded length and sanitized `http`/`https`
   links only; no HTML, embeds, attachments, mentions, direct messages, polls,
   or arbitrary emoji reactions. Replies are limited to one level and must
   share the exact Engagement Space. Pagination is bounded and keyset-based.
7. A commenter may edit their own comment through immutable revisions and sees
   an **Edited** label. Self-removal hides the body immediately and leaves a
   neutral tombstone only when necessary to preserve replies. Staff may
   hide/restore, redact for a documented privacy/safety reason, lock an update,
   or restrict an actor at the smallest tenant/source scope; staff never
   rewrite the comment as though the commenter authored the new words.
8. Reactions expose aggregates to the exact supporter audience; responder
   identities are limited to authorized update contributors and tenant staff.
   Comments use a purpose-authorized display-identity projection—not raw
   profile joins—and the composer previews exactly what name/avatar, if any,
   other supporters will see.

#### Quiet UX for supporters, missionaries, and staff

- The supporter feed shows two labelled toggle buttons, **Like** and **I
  prayed**, then **Comments** only when enabled. A successful toggle responds
  immediately, can be undone, and never implies that money moved or that the
  missionary was notified.
- The comment composer states **Visible to supporters who can read this
  update**, previews the display identity, preserves text across transient
  failures, prevents double submission, and distinguishes `Sending`, `Posted`,
  `Not posted—retry`, and `Comments closed`. Optimistic content is never left
  looking persisted after a rejected/no-op write.
- Comments open as a bounded inline section or sheet with **Load more**, one
  visible reply level, and clear `Reply`, `Edit`, `Remove`, and `Report` actions
  based on current authority. It is not an infinitely nested social feed.
- The author sees one compact response summary—likes, prayer
  acknowledgements, and unread comments—plus a batched activity view. Reaction
  identities and comment details are progressive disclosure, not dashboard
  noise.
- An assigned missionary/contributor may immediately hide a harmful comment or
  close comments on their authorized source. Tenant moderation staff retain the
  final restore/restrict decision. Healthy tenants see no moderation queue;
  only reported, automatically held, or author-hidden items appear.
- Setup asks one plain-language question with a live preview: **How can
  supporters respond to ministry updates?** The three fixed choices explain
  workload and visibility. The project-family override and abuse settings stay
  collapsed until relevant.
- A page-level Give action may appear after an update or response section using
  D7's current route, designation, locale, currency, and attribution. It is
  visually separated and labelled **Give**, never presented as a fourth
  reaction. Clicking, reacting, commenting, starting checkout, completing a
  gift, and settled donation truth remain independent occurrences.

#### Moderation, abuse, and failure handling

- Every comment has **Report** with bounded reasons and optional detail.
  Duplicate reports coalesce; reports enter one tenant/source-scoped queue.
  Hide is reversible, delete/redaction is exceptional, and every action records
  actor, reason, prior state, exact comment revision, and timestamp.
- Apply body/link/count limits, duplicate and burst detection, per-identity and
  tenant-fair rate limits, abuse IP/device signals with privacy controls, and
  step-up verification for suspicious activity. Automated spam/safety
  screening may hold content for review but never creates an unreviewable
  permanent deletion or exempts donors, staff, contributors, or “trusted”
  accounts from baseline controls.
- A contained, withdrawn, or inaccessible Update projection stops new reads
  and writes at that exact scope. Existing response evidence remains available
  only to authorized custody/audit surfaces. A failed notification, report
  classifier, realtime channel, or count projection does not widen access or
  roll back a valid comment; the UI shows the exact degraded capability.
- Reaction storms do not generate one email each. Phase 22 emits typed,
  deduplicable response occurrences. Phases 17/6 own channel, cadence, consent,
  suppression, batching, dispatch, and provider outcome. Recipients can mute
  reaction summaries, comment/reply notices, or one conversation without
  changing content access.
- Tenant custody export includes authorized comments, comment revisions,
  acknowledgements, visibility/moderation outcomes, and stable references in a
  documented portable format. A person can export their own contributions.
  Erasure requests remove display PII/content where required while preserving
  the minimum non-identifying integrity, security, or legal-hold evidence; an
  indefinite immutable copy of personal comment text is not the default.

These controls follow OWASP's guidance to enforce least privilege, deny by
default, validate authorization on every request, protect static resources,
and test authorization; its XSS guidance to encode or sanitize untrusted
content; and the OWASP API Security guidance to bound resource consumption.
They are security engineering requirements, not claims that automated
screening or RLS alone makes comments safe.

#### Accessibility contract

The interaction must meet WCAG 2.2 AA. In particular:

- use native buttons with stable visible labels and `aria-pressed` for Like and
  I prayed; support Enter/Space, a visible focus indicator, and at least WCAG's
  24-by-24 CSS-pixel minimum target (larger touch targets are preferred);
- announce posted, removed, held, failed, and retry results as programmatic
  status messages without moving focus, while keeping error text adjacent to
  and associated with the composer;
- preserve typed text and expose deterministic recovery after network,
  authorization, moderation, or conflict failure;
- render updates and comments as semantic articles/lists with meaningful
  author, time, and action labels. Prefer **Load more** to an automatically
  loading nested ARIA feed; W3C notes that nested feeds add keyboard and
  assistive-technology navigation cost;
- never encode reaction kind, mine/not-mine state, moderation state, or unread
  status by icon, color, animation, or count alone; and
- honor reduced motion and avoid celebratory particles for `I prayed` when
  reduced motion is requested.

The W3C [button pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/),
[feed pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/feed/), and WCAG
[status-message guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
inform these requirements. ARIA Authoring Practices examples are informative
patterns, not production components to copy without testing.

### 26.7 Highest-risk adversarial findings to carry into the D12 grill

| Risk                                                                                                            | Severity | Likelihood                           | Permanent prevention                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Protected comments, counts, identities, or realtime events leak into a public cache or another audience         | Critical | Possible–Likely                      | Exact Engagement Space scope, current request authorization, audience-bound caches/cursors/streams, no anonymous raw-table reads, and cross-scope poison tests       |
| A no-op, timeout, or blind retry makes a comment appear posted or creates duplicates                            | High     | Likely without change                | Idempotent commands, commit/readback truth, optimistic rollback or explicit pending state, inspect-before-retry, and no `persisted:false` success presentation       |
| Tenant staff become unpaid full-time moderators                                                                 | High     | Likely for public/unbounded comments | Supporter-only verified writers, responses-off/acknowledgement modes, one-level plain-text discussion, quiet exception queue, rate limits, and batched notifications |
| A staff edit changes a supporter's words without evidence                                                       | Critical | Possible                             | Immutable self-edit revisions; staff hide/restore/redact with reason; never mutate content in place as the author                                                    |
| Raw donor/profile names or avatars become visible outside intended relationship context                         | Critical | Possible                             | Separate audience-safe display-identity projection, previewed at compose time; reactions reveal no viewer identities; no transaction/profile fallthrough             |
| Prayer/like/comment is interpreted as relationship, notification, or giving truth                               | High     | Likely                               | Typed independent occurrences and plain copy; no `Give` reaction; D7 CTA visually separated; independent status/analytics                                            |
| Recursive replies, attachments, mentions, DMs, arbitrary reactions, and realtime become a hidden social network | High     | Likely if inherited from prototypes  | Fixed two acknowledgements, one reply level, plain text, bounded pagination, no media/mentions/DMs, and polling or authorized scoped streams only                    |
| Moderation or deletion destroys custody evidence or retains personal content forever                            | High     | Possible                             | Reversible hide, explicit redaction/tombstone, bounded retention/legal hold, self and tenant export, and privacy-safe minimal audit evidence                         |
| Icon-only reactions, dynamic counts, nested feeds, or failed optimistic writes exclude or mislead users         | High     | Likely                               | Visible labels, toggle semantics, status announcements, preserved input, Load more, keyboard/screen-reader/mobile testing, and reduced-motion behavior               |

### 26.8 Required certification seams if C-prime proceeds

Before release, tests must prove:

1. cross-Tenant, Legal-Entity, environment, source, purpose, Update Revision,
   audience, release-version, safety-epoch, and Response-Profile substitution
   fails without revealing existence;
2. anonymous public readers cannot infer protected counts, identities,
   comments, moderation state, cache keys, cursors, or realtime events;
3. revoked supporters lose the next read/write while prior valid response
   evidence remains correctly scoped;
4. acknowledgement add/remove and comment submit are idempotent under duplicate,
