  never says why records might be absent. An all-empty tenant uses one generic
  tenant-authored state.
- Default browse order is eligible featured cards, then locale-appropriate
  public title and an opaque identifier tie-breaker. Query order is code-owned
  textual relevance over admitted fields, exact public title/alias first, then
  the same stable tie-break. Donation amount, donor count, support progress,
  urgency, recency, popularity, internal priority, exact geography, and random
  order never rank results.

### 29.5 Data, search, activation, and failure contract

1. **One complete projection.** Each current eligible listed release has
   exactly one typed row in one current generation. Every other release has no
   public row. A private exclusion ledger records the source-owned reason for
   staff diagnostics without becoming a public placeholder or count.
2. **Structural scope.** Non-null Tenant, Legal Entity, environment, Site,
   locale, Page Family, Page, Release, reach/safety/route/profile generations,
   and projection generation participate in same-scope constraints and indexes.
   An opaque public ID is not a tenant boundary.
3. **Minimal public fields.** The row contains only the approved route, public
   title/alias, safe summary, Page Family, D9 derivative reference, optional
   D6/D7 presentation capabilities, allowlisted public labels, stable sort
   keys, and as-of facts. Legal names, Party/worker/fund/Designation IDs, notes,
   exact location, employment/support state, donor data, and raw CMS documents
   never enter the public search document.
4. **Narrow server query.** Internal tables stay in an unexposed schema. One
   bounded server command validates host scope and allowlisted topology/family,
   query, filter, limit, and cursor inputs, then reads a deliberately narrow
   projection with explicit grants and defense-in-depth indexed RLS. No browser
   table, service key, or Realtime stream is the public contract.
5. **Locale-correct search.** A locale pins an explicit PostgreSQL text-search
   configuration or a declared literal-token mode. The generated vector and GIN
   index use the same configuration. Unsupported locale or missing translation
   produces a declared safe state, never a hidden source-language, legal-name,
   or cross-locale fallback. Search input is Unicode-normalized, length- and
   complexity-bounded, parsed as plain text, and never interpolated as SQL or a
   raw `tsquery`.
6. **Snapshot-consistent pagination.** Count, cards, and next cursor come from
   one generation. An opaque signed keyset cursor binds Tenant, Legal Entity,
   Site, locale, topology, family, normalized query/filter digest, sort
   contract, profile generation, reach/safety generations, and projection
   generation. A stale, malformed, or substituted cursor cannot broaden scope;
   the UI restarts calmly against the current generation.
7. **Safe activation.** A next generation is built in non-authoritative shadow
   from a complete current-release census, reconciled for one-and-only-one
   eligible membership and zero ineligible membership, then activated by one
   idempotent CAS head change. Topology activation also proves route collisions,
   locale, canonical/sitemap behavior, current profile, and current safety and
   reach evidence.
8. **Adverse continuity.** Phase 10 or D2 narrowing, containment, withdrawal,
   or route invalidation removes the affected positive row before or atomically
   with any wider rebuild and invalidates every matching cache generation. A
   failed rebuild preserves proved absence and never restores an older positive
   through a stale cache, mock, Payload, Party, Designation, or `locations`
   fallback.
9. **Bounded failure.** If search fails while a current authorized browse
   projection remains provable, show that browse view plus `Search is
temporarily unavailable`. If current projection authority is uncertain,
   return a safe no-store unavailable state. Missing progress removes progress;
   missing Giving removes Give; neither makes a safe page disappear. Metrics
   record scoped lag, mismatches, removals, cursor rejections, query latency,
   timeouts, and failures without raw queries, legal names, locations, or hidden
   identifiers.
10. **One crawl surface.** Exactly one topology is active. Combined and separate
    full catalogs never remain concurrently indexable. Canonical URLs, sitemap,
    internal navigation, structured metadata, and query/filter crawl policy are
    generated from the same route manifest. Phase 5 performs request-time
    resolution; external index/cache cleanup remains independently observed.

| **Migration and upgrade risks**       | **Yes**  | Current mock/static `/workers`, `public.locations`, exact-coordinate map, old links, and separate topology routes can be dual-read or indexed during cutover.                                                                       | Hidden records, duplicate SEO surfaces, broken donor links, and irreversible cached routes can survive an otherwise correct launch. | High     | Likely                                    | Build from canonical D2 releases in shadow, reconcile the full cohort, prove routes/caches/sitemaps, cut over one Site/locale generation, revoke raw `locations`/Realtime exposure before launch, remove dual reads, and use the proved route-disposition contract. |
| **Other development hazards**         | **Yes**  | Races among release, safety, route, profile, rebuild, and cache activation; blind retries; unsigned cursors; mutable feature flags; weak negative tests; or destructive rollback can reintroduce stale positives.                   | Rare concurrency bugs on a public safety boundary have outsized impact and are difficult to reproduce.                              | Critical | Possible                                  | Transactional locking and CAS, semantic idempotency, signed generation-bound cursors, immutable versions, append-only recovery, affected-scope containment, deployment kill switches, and mandatory race/negative/fault-injection tests.                            |

### 29.7 Production-shaped proof required before shipping

1. **Authority matrix:** anonymous, authenticated, contributor, reviewer, staff,
   service, wrong Tenant, wrong Legal Entity, wrong Site, wrong locale, wrong
   family, stale grant, and revoked/safety-contained cases at the public command
   and database boundary.
2. **Complete coverage:** for representative cohorts, prove exactly one row for
   every current listed/safe release and zero rows for public-by-link,
   not-public, missing-locale, withdrawn, retired, ambiguous, or contained
   releases in both topologies.
3. **Race and cache proof:** interleave release activation, Phase 10 narrowing,
   D8 route change, profile switch, rebuild, query, cursor continuation, cache
   hit, and purge. No stale positive may survive and no retry may duplicate a
   row or widen scope.
4. **Query abuse and locale fixtures:** apostrophes, accents, combining marks,
   CJK and right-to-left text, aliases, punctuation, emoji, empty/all-stopword,
   extremely long, SQL-like, wildcard-like, and malformed cursor input; stable
   order and no duplicate/omitted pagination rows.
5. **Privacy egress:** assert that rendered HTML, RSC/JSON, metadata, structured
   data, sitemaps, cache keys, logs, traces, metrics, errors, response timing,
   accessible names, images, and downloaded assets contain no hidden source
   value or exact location.
6. **UX/accessibility:** Together and Separate, empty family, all-empty,
   no-match, search failure, D6/D7 degradation, no JavaScript, slow network,
   keyboard, screen reader, focus, 320px reflow, 200% text spacing, zoom,
   images disabled, reduced motion, and mobile touch targets.
7. **SEO and route proof:** one active canonical topology, no conflicting
   combined/separate catalogs, bounded query/filter crawl behavior, correct
   sitemap generation, D8-compatible old-route outcome, and honest observation
   that local removal is not external de-indexing.
8. **Scale and recovery:** large and highly skewed tenant catalogs, abusive
   traffic, rebuild under load, tenant fairness, current-generation loss,
   partial build, timeout, and operator containment/recovery with observable
   evidence.

### 29.8 Ruthless synthesis and ordered path

1. Name one **Public Ministry Discovery Profile**, one **Public Ministry
   Directory Projection**, and one query/card contract. Do not permit “separate”
   to mean duplicate authority.
2. Preserve D2 and Phase 10 as the sole membership and safety inputs. Remove the
   current mock, `locations`, client filtering, exact map, and Realtime paths
   from launch authority.
3. Make **Together** the quiet built-in default and expose only one optional
   tenant change: **Separate pages**. Bind the choice immutably to exact Site and
   locale scope and preview the actual routes and consequences.
4. Build one minimal private projection with complete structural coordinates,
   approved public fields, complete coverage, atomic generation activation, and
   affected-positive-first removal.
5. Build one locale-pinned PostgreSQL search command with a GIN-backed document,
   stable relevance/order, allowlisted optional filters, tenant-fair limits,
   signed keyset cursors, and generation-complete caching.
6. Render ordinary URL-backed, semantic, accessible directory views with exact
   family labels and independently degrading D6/D7 content. Keep advanced
   discovery, predictive autocomplete, maps, fuzzy matching, external search,
   and arbitrary taxonomy out until evidence proves a need and safety contract.
7. Activate only after complete authority, privacy, race, accessibility, SEO,
   scale, failure, and migration proof. A topology change is a route/presentation
   change, never a privacy or Giving change.

### 29.9 Ratification outcome

The founder ratified the exact **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R)**
formulation in §29.3 as **Phase 22 D13** on 2026-08-06. The binding decision,
interpretation, ownership boundaries, and consequences are recorded in the
[Phase 22 decision log](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md) and
[ADR-0130](../../adr/0130-scoped-public-ministry-discovery-with-tenant-chosen-topology.md).

## 30. D14 option research — release-bound public search presentation

> **Status:** historical option record. The founder later selected, hardened,
> and ratified the expanded search-and-sharing C-prime-R formulation in §32.8
> as Phase 22 D14. This section preserves the earlier decision input and does
> not alter D1–D13.

### 30.1 Why this is the next dependency-ordered seam

D2 now decides publication reach, D3 binds the typed page presentation, D4/D5
own the one review/release path, D8 owns canonical route disposition, D9 owns
safe released media, and D13 owns the on-site directory/search topology. The
remaining public identity surface is search-engine presentation: page title and
description, canonical URL, crawler directives, sitemap membership, locale
alternates, and structured data.

Those outputs are not cosmetic. They can expose an identity or location outside
the visible page, advertise a Shared-by-link page, keep a withdrawn route
discoverable, create cross-Site canonicals, or tell crawlers that an unavailable
locale exists. D14 must define one release-bound projection of existing truth,
not a second visibility, routing, safety, or publication authority.

Open Graph and social-card presentation remain a separate next seam. Search
metadata may supply safe default copy later, but D14 does not authorize a social
image, social audience, crawler preview, or share-card release.

### 30.2 Concrete founder scenario

Hope Mission has:

- one English Listed-public Missionary Ministry Page released as **The River
  Team**, using an approved alias and the generalized public region **Southeast
  Asia**;
- a Spanish draft with no approved Spanish Page Release;
- one Project/Campaign Page that is **Shared by link**; and
- one Listed-public project whose canonical route has changed through D8.

The missionary wants a clear search result, and staff want low maintenance. The
system must not leak a legal name or exact location, advertise the link-only
project in search, emit an alternate for the unreleased Spanish draft, preserve
the old project route as another canonical page, or leave stale positive
sitemap output after a safety takedown.

### 30.3 Current repository evidence and hazards

The current implementation is useful migration evidence, not D14 authority:

1. `packages/lib/seo/metadata.ts` builds worker search copy as
   `Support ${name} - Missionary in ${location}` and creates a URL from one
   process-wide `SITE_URL` plus a raw worker id. That can leak a legal name or
   over-precise location and cannot prove Tenant, Legal Entity, Site, locale,
   D2 reach, D8 route, or Phase 10 safety.
2. `packages/lib/seo/json-ld.tsx` emits a `Person` with raw route id,
   `jobTitle`, and `workLocation`; it also emits a site-wide `SearchAction`.
   A Missionary Ministry Page may represent an alias, couple, family, or team,
   so `Person` is not a safe family-wide default. Google retired the sitelinks
   search box result globally in November 2024, making `SearchAction` obsolete
   for the behavior it was intended to request.
3. `apps/donor/app/layout.tsx` supplies one static metadata base, locale,
   canonical, Open Graph object, and descendant `index, follow` default. A
   route that fails to replace every inherited field can silently claim the
   wrong host, locale, canonical, or indexing posture.
4. `apps/donor/app/(public)/(solid)/workers/[id]/page.tsx` generates metadata
   and JSON-LD from mock worker records. It has no D2/D8/D10 release proof and
   no typed Missionary-versus-Project subject rule.
5. `apps/donor/next.config.ts` assigns long shared cache headers to
   `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`. No Phase 22 generation-bound metadata route
   was found. A later implementation could therefore leave a stale positive
   after an adverse reach or safety change unless the search artifact is bound
   to the same release/effect generation.
6. Existing tests do not prove wrong-Tenant, wrong-Site, wrong-locale,
   Shared-by-link, missing locale, stale release, safety containment, route
   replacement, sitemap removal, reciprocal alternate, structured-data egress,
   or query-URL crawl behavior.

### 30.4 Current primary-source findings

- The installed Next.js 16 metadata guidance supports route-owned generated
  metadata, `robots.ts`, and `sitemap.ts`; JSON-LD must be safely serialized
  rather than interpolated as untrusted HTML. D14 should use those installed
  seams instead of inventing a parallel head manager.
- [Google's sitemap guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap)
  says to include canonical URLs intended for search, treats sitemap submission
  as a hint rather than a guarantee, ignores `priority` and `changefreq`, and
  uses `lastmod` only when it accurately represents a significant page change.
- [Google's robots-meta guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag)
  says a crawler must be allowed to access a page to observe `noindex`.
  Therefore a Shared-by-link page must not be disallowed in `robots.txt`; doing
  so can both prevent `noindex` observation and turn a crawler-control file into
  a list of sensitive-looking paths.
- [Google's canonical guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls)
  and [localized-version guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions)
  support exact canonical and reciprocal locale-alternate relationships. A
  draft, unsafe, Shared-by-link, or absent locale cannot be advertised as an
  alternate release.
- [Google's structured-data policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies)
  require markup to describe visible page content accurately. Its
  [ProfilePage guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/profile-page)
  does not justify calling every ministry, couple, team, or project one Person.
- Google has [retired the sitelinks search box](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/10/sitelinks-search-box),
  so the present `SearchAction` is not a modern launch requirement.
- [Google's snippet guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet)
  and [title-link guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link)
  make clear that search engines may choose or rewrite displayed copy. The UI
  must call its rendering a preview or influence, never an exact promise.
- The [Payload SEO plugin](https://payloadcms.com/docs/plugins/seo) demonstrates
  the useful low-friction editor pattern: generated title/description defaults,
  optional edits, live preview, and soft length guidance. Its extensible
  arbitrary JSON-LD seam is deliberately not adopted for this safety-sensitive
  surface.

### 30.5 Options

#### Option A-prime — Fully automatic safe search presentation

Generate title, description, canonical, crawler directives, sitemap membership,
locale alternates, and typed structured data entirely from the current safe Page
Release. Contributors and staff receive a read-only preview.

**Benefits:** smallest authority surface, almost no admin work, deterministic
output, and a strong privacy posture.

**Costs:** safe generated wording may be bland or poorly fit a tenant's voice,
project campaign, or local-language search intent. Staff have no bounded way to
improve it without changing visible page copy.

#### Option B-prime — Full tenant SEO studio

Let contributors or staff configure search title, description, canonical,
robots, sitemap inclusion, locale alternates, keywords, structured-data types,
and JSON-LD.

**Benefits:** maximum theoretical marketing control.

**Costs:** creates a second reach and routing console, invites cross-Site
canonicals and false locale alternates, makes hidden text/JSON-LD an identity
leak, and imposes specialist work on small nonprofit teams. It is inconsistent
with D2, D8, D10, and D13 and is rejected as the launch recommendation.

#### Option C-prime — One release-bound Public Search Presentation with bounded editorial copy — Recommended

Keep title and description the only optional editorial inputs. They are
locale-specific fields inside the ordinary D3 page draft and therefore follow
the exact D4/D5 review and release behavior already selected by the tenant.
Safe generated defaults mean nobody must configure them. Canonicals, crawler
directives, sitemap membership, locale alternates, and structured-data types and
properties remain code-owned derivations of current D2, D8, Phase 10, Site,
locale, and Page Release truth.

The staff and missionary experience is one collapsed **Search preview** section:

- show the current Site, locale, resolved public URL, reach outcome, generated
  title, and generated description;
- allow optional **Search title** and **Search description** edits only when the
  contributor already has D1/D3 authority to edit that page and locale;
- provide plain-language examples, soft character guidance, an accessible live
  preview, and **Reset to generated**;
- state that search engines may display different wording and that
  `Listed publicly` makes a page eligible, not guaranteed, to appear in search;
- show Shared-by-link as **Not eligible for search listings** without presenting
  an editable indexing toggle; and
- keep advanced details collapsed and provide a cause-owned staff explanation
  when a page is omitted due to reach, safety, locale, route, or stale proof.

The binding shape proposed for hardening after founder selection is:

1. A current Listed-public, Phase-10-safe release is self-canonical and eligible
   for the exact Site/locale sitemap. Eligibility is not a promise that an
   external engine has indexed or displayed it.
2. A Shared-by-link release remains anonymously reachable under D2 but emits
   `noindex`, is absent from directory, sitemap, and locale alternates, and is
   not disallowed or individually named in `robots.txt`.
3. Not-public, contained, retired, removed, and tombstoned routes follow D8's
   uniform unknown-page `404` plus `noindex`. An authority outage remains D8's
   neutral `503`, `Retry-After`, and `no-store`, never a stale positive.
4. D13 GET query/filter variants emit `noindex`, canonicalize to the active base
   directory route, stay out of sitemap and locale alternates, and never echo
   visitor query text into metadata or structured data.
5. Locale alternates exist only among mutually current, Listed-public,
   Phase-10-safe releases under exact Phase 24 locale/domain truth. No draft or
   fallback locale becomes search authority.
6. Sitemap `lastmod` is the exact time of a significant released public-content,
   route, safety, or search-presentation change. Build time, request time,
   support activity, progress recomputation, and financial changes are not
   substitutes.
7. Baseline structured data is code-owned `WebPage` plus eligible
   `BreadcrumbList`. `ProfilePage`/`Person` is admitted only when the exact page
   subject is one public-safe person and every emitted property is visibly
   supported. Couples, teams, ministries, projects, aliases without a public
   person subject, and ambiguous or restricted subjects remain `WebPage`.
8. Search JSON-LD contains only current visible released facts. No internal or
   raw source id, legal-name inference, exact location, `sameAs` inference,
   supporter fact, engagement count, D6 progress, D7 Giving state, Field Account
   fact, arbitrary tenant JSON-LD, `DonateAction`, fabricated Project rich-result
   type, retired `SearchAction`, or meta-keyword surface is admitted.
9. The D14 output is a release/effect projection pinned by the D2 Page Release
   Manifest and D8 Route Effect Manifest. It is not an SEO publication head,
   tenant crawler policy engine, page-level reach toggle, or second workflow.
   D3 owns editorial fields; D4/D5 own review/release; Phase 5 renders; Phase 23
   supplies ordinary CMS editing; Phase 24 owns locale/domain truth.
10. Unknown, incomplete, revoked, stale, or generation-mismatched proof removes
    positive search output first, opens one cause-owned exception, and cannot
    fall back to root metadata, another locale, another Site, a previous release,
    or raw CMS/CRM data.

### 30.6 Adversarial preview before founder selection

The likely high-severity concerns are already concrete:

- **privacy and tenant safety:** hidden legal identity, exact geography, raw id,
  wrong host/locale, or another tenant's canonical can escape through metadata,
  JSON-LD, sitemap, cache, or an inherited root head even when visible HTML is
  safe;
- **footguns and operational burden:** editable robots, sitemap, canonical,
  hreflang, schema, keywords, and indexing toggles turn a simple page editor into
  a dangerous SEO console;
- **brittleness and hidden coupling:** separately computed metadata can drift
  from D2 reach, D8 routes, D9 media, D13 topology, or Phase 10 containment;
- **failure and observability:** stale positive sitemap/cache output and external
  crawler lag can outlive local removal, while Search Console actions do not
  prove permanent internet deletion;
- **scale:** parameterized D13 search/filter URLs can create an unbounded crawl
  space unless they are canonicalized and non-indexable; and
- **data integrity and upgrade risk:** mutable metadata, non-reciprocal locale
  alternates, request-time `lastmod`, obsolete `SearchAction`, or generic
  `Person` markup can create contradictory public claims.

If C-prime is selected, the next response must run the full required
category-by-category adversarial review before any ratification. No option is
accepted by this research section.

### 30.7 Founder question

How much control should tenants and page contributors have over how a public
ministry page appears in search engines: **A-prime fully automatic safe search
presentation**, **B-prime full SEO controls**, or **C-prime one release-bound
Public Search Presentation with bounded editorial title and description
(recommended)**?

## 31. D14 official-source evidence — search-ready public releases and social sharing

> **Status: incorporated into ratified Phase 22 D14 on 2026-08-06.** The
> founder selected the C-prime direction, explicitly expanded it so every D2
> **Listed publicly** page is technically ready for Google, Bing, and other
> conforming search engines and every anonymously public page and D11 public
> Ministry Update has a safe, useful social-share presentation, then ratified
> the hardened formulation in §32.8. Section 30 remains the historical option
> record. Nothing below weakens D1–D13 or guarantees third-party indexing,
> ranking, sharing, cache refresh, or removal.

### 31.1 Precision correction: Asym can make a release search-ready, not indexed

Google's minimum technical conditions are that Googlebot is not blocked, the
URL returns HTTP `200`, and the response contains indexable content. Google is
explicit that satisfying those conditions does **not** guarantee crawling,
indexing, serving, a particular title or snippet, or ranking. Bing likewise
states that URL submission and sitemap discovery do not guarantee indexing.
IndexNow `200` means only that a notification was received—not that the URL was
crawled or indexed.

The proposed product language therefore needs two different facts:

- **Search-ready** is Asym-authoritative: the current release passed its local
  reach, safety, route, metadata, crawlability, canonical, sitemap, and public
  response proofs.
- **Discovered / crawled / indexed / shown** are search-provider observations,
  separately through-dated and never collapsed into “SEO working” or “indexed.”

Sources: [Google Search technical requirements](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/technical),
[Google Search Console URL Inspection](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9012289),
[Bing URL Submission](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/URL-Submission-62f2860b),
[Bing IndexNow](https://www.bing.com/webmasters/help/indexnow-0z209wby), and
[the IndexNow protocol](https://www.indexnow.org/documentation).

### 31.3 Reach, discovery, and permalink matrix

| Release surface                                                                                                              | Anonymous dereference                           | Search treatment                                                                                                                                 | Social treatment                                                             | Required stable URL behavior                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Current D2 **Listed publicly** ministry/project page                                                                         | `200`, subject to current Phase 10 and D8 proof | `index,follow`; self-canonical; exact-host sitemap eligible; crawlable from the D13 directory/navigation; locale alternates only when reciprocal | Share and Copy link; complete safe page card                                 | One current D8 canonical route; approved D8 moves redirect `308`; removal follows D8's local removal disposition           |
| Current D2 **Shared by link — public** ministry/project page                                                                 | `200`; explicitly public and reshareable        | `noindex`; absent from sitemap, directory, nav, public feeds, and locale discovery; crawler must be able to fetch the response to see `noindex`  | Share and Copy link; complete safe page card                                 | Stable share URL, but never described as private or unguessable security                                                   |
| D2 **Not public**, protected preview, draft, or removed page                                                                 | No public content response                      | Not sitemap/discovery eligible; generic non-revealing crawler response                                                                           | No public card or public share affordance                                    | No metadata fallback that exposes title, image, identity, designation, or prior release                                    |
| D11 Public-page Ministry Update whose owning page is Listed and whose D3 Feed Binding and current safety proof allow release | `200` at its own immutable update permalink     | Individually index-eligible; self-canonical; sitemap/feed/internal-link eligible                                                                 | Share and Copy link; `article` card for that exact revision/audience release | Stable opaque permalink distinct from the page root; exact release `published_time` and correction-derived `modified_time` |
| D11 Public-page Ministry Update whose owning page is Shared-by-link                                                          | `200` at its own immutable update permalink     | `noindex`; absent from sitemap, directory, nav, public feed discovery, and locale alternates                                                     | Share and Copy link; `article` card                                          | Must inherit the stricter owning-page reach so a post cannot become a discovery backdoor                                   |
| D11 supporter-only/protected Ministry Update                                                                                 | Authenticated/authorized only                   | No public indexing or discovery                                                                                                                  | No anonymous title, copy, image, or rich preview                             | Authentication and current audience authorization guard every deep link and asset                                          |

“Every public post is shareable” therefore requires a stable, independently
addressable D11 public-update permalink. Sharing only the parent page would not
make a specific update reliably shareable or individually indexable. The post
route remains a D11 release projection under the D2/D3/D8/Phase-10 ceiling; it
is not a second CMS document or a weaker publication path.

### 31.4 Proposed C-prime-R search presentation contract for adversarial review

The source evidence supports hardening the selected direction as **one
release-bound Public Search and Share Presentation**, not separate mutable SEO
records. For each exact current public page or update release, one immutable
projection would bind at least:

- Tenant, Site, environment, typed page/update family, locale, D2 resolved
  reach, D8 route generation, D3 Presentation/Feed Binding, D9 approved media
  generation, D11 revision/audience release where applicable, and the current
  Phase 10 public-safety proof;
- the exact absolute canonical URL, reciprocal eligible locale alternates,
  robots result, sitemap inclusion result, crawlable-link topology, visible
  released title/body facts, bounded title/description presentation, and typed
  structured-data result;
- the exact social card type, absolute `og:url`, safe title/description,
  `og:locale`, site name, immutable public image URL, MIME type, dimensions,
  file size, and meaningful alt text, plus compatible `twitter:*` metadata; and
- source provenance, content hash, release time, last meaningful modification
  time, generator version, and positive/negative proof results.

The public response, canonical/head data, sitemap, social metadata, directory
links, and notifications must all project from that same immutable coverage.
No public output may independently reread raw CRM/CMS tables, infer a legal
name or location, inherit root metadata, reuse another tenant's image, or fall
back to a previous positive release when proof is unknown or stale.

Asym can render X-compatible `twitter:*` card metadata through the installed
Next.js 16 API, but the current official X developer documentation no longer
exposes a stable, platform-specific card contract at the legacy card-doc URLs.
Consequently, X preview behavior should be production-probed and described as
compatible/best-effort—not certified from obsolete documentation or promised
as identical to Open Graph consumers.

### 31.5 Bounded tenant and contributor UX

The evidence does not support a full SEO console. A low-noise editor should:

1. generate a safe search/social title, description, and card from the approved
   release by default;
2. allow only bounded, semantic title and description overrides and selection
   of an approved D9 public image (with an optional collapsed social-specific
   override only if the same safety and release proof applies);
3. preview **Search appearance** and **Link preview**, while explaining that
   providers may rewrite text, crop images, cache old previews, decline to
   index, or rank differently;
4. show a plain reach result—**Can appear in search**, **Shareable by link but
   not submitted for search**, or **Not public**—computed from D2 rather than an
   editable checkbox;
5. place safe validation beside the field that needs work and keep healthy
   generated metadata quiet; and
6. expose **Share** plus **Copy link** only for the exact currently public route,
   with a clear warning that recipients can reshare public-by-link content.

If no approved public image exists, generate a neutral, tenant-branded,
content-addressed `1200 × 630` card using only already released safe title/alias
and Site branding. It must not contain the uploader's original filename, EXIF
or embedded metadata, a storage key, exact hidden geography, a raw party id, or
an unapproved prior photo. Keep the derivative within the strictest supported
declared limit (Next.js documents `5 MB` for a Twitter image and `8 MB` for an
Open Graph image) and publish its alt text.

### 31.6 Release, caching, removal, and failure semantics

- Release commits the authoritative publication first. Search/social side
  effects run afterward through D8's idempotent outbox; no Search Console,
  Bing, IndexNow, or social-provider network call may sit inside the release
  transaction or make a successful release ambiguous.
- Add/update/delete notifications carry the exact Site host, canonical URL,
  release generation, and idempotency key. Retries are bounded, inspectable,
  tenant-fair, and never interpreted as provider crawl or index completion.
- Search and social crawlers receive the same public released content and
  claims as people. Bot-tailored hidden identity/content would be both a safety
  defect and a search-policy risk.
- A safety downgrade or D8 removal changes local behavior immediately, removes
  the URL from internal discovery and the next sitemap generation, and emits
  an IndexNow delete/update where configured. Search-console removal/recrawl
  and Meta/LinkedIn inspection may accelerate external refresh but remain
  observed best-effort actions.
- External search indexes, snippets, screenshots, embeds, social caches, copied
  links, and already published social posts cannot be transactionally recalled.
  Immutable derivative URLs prevent stale bytes from masquerading as the new
  card, but old shares can remain visible.
- A metadata/image generation or proof failure suppresses the affected new
  positive search/share projection, preserves the last valid immutable release
  only where D8 and Phase 10 still authorize it, and opens one cause-owned
  exception. It must not silently publish incomplete tags or another release's
  image.

### 31.7 Proof and observability required before calling a release search-ready

Production-shaped automated checks should fetch the exact public URL as an
anonymous user and as supported crawler user agents, then prove:

- expected status and cache behavior; correct Tenant/Site/host/locale; current
  D2 reach; current D8 route; current Phase 10 safety; and absence of protected
  data in HTML, headers, metadata, JSON-LD, image URLs, and error responses;
- one absolute self-canonical URL, only reciprocal eligible locale alternates,
  complete title/description/robots data, visible matching content, crawlable
  internal anchors, and correct sitemap membership/non-membership;
- complete Open Graph and compatibility metadata with the exact permalink,
  correct `website` or `article` type, safe publication times, and no unapproved
  author identity;
- social image `200`, public crawler access, expected MIME type, dimensions,
  file size, content hash, alt text, metadata stripping, and no expiring signed
  URL or cross-tenant storage path;
- deterministic regeneration and invalidation for a changed release, reach,
  route, safety, locale, or media generation; and
- immediate local removal plus eventual outbox evidence without treating
  submission acknowledgement as crawl, index, ranking, preview refresh, or
  deletion completion.

Operational telemetry should keep separate counters/timestamps for **release
generated**, **public proof passed**, **sitemap emitted**, **IndexNow or provider
submission acknowledged**, **crawler observed**, **indexed observed**, and
**removal observed**. Healthy tenants should not need an SEO dashboard ritual;
staff should see one cause-owned exception only when Asym-controlled readiness
is broken, with optional provider observations under a details view.

### 31.8 Risks this evidence sends into the D14 adversarial review

The full adversarial pass should specifically test at least these likely
high-severity failure classes:

- a Shared-by-link page or post becoming searchable through sitemap, locale
  alternates, directory/feed links, structured data, or a canonical pointing to
  a Listed route;
- a removed/restricted subject remaining identifiable through inherited head
  tags, social images, filenames, JSON-LD, provider cache, or error responses;
- a public update becoming a reach-escalation backdoor independent of its owning
  page, D3 Feed Binding, audience release, or current Phase 10 safety;
- cross-tenant or cross-Site canonical, sitemap, IndexNow-key, locale, image,
  cache-key, and metadata contamination;
- request-time sitemap dates, mutable provider status, blind notification
  retries, crawler-induced fan-out, unbounded directory-filter crawl space, or
  social-image generation overwhelming release capacity;
- contributor-facing jargon and unsafe controls that imply false privacy,
  guaranteed indexing, exact ranking, or recallable social sharing; and
- reliance on provider-specific preview behavior without production probes,
  especially where official platform documentation is missing, redirected, or
  materially cached.

This section supplies source evidence for the requested ruthless review. It is
not the review itself and does not name or ratify the final D14 formulation.

## 32. Ratified D14 selected-option adversarial review and hardened decision

> **Status: ratified and adversarially hardened on 2026-08-06.** This section
> reviews the founder-selected C-prime direction plus the explicit requirement
> that eligible public pages be technically ready for Google, Bing, and other
> standards-compatible search engines and that every anonymously public Phase
> 22 page and Ministry Update be safely shareable. It preserves D1-D13 and
> records the exact C-prime-R wording ratified as Phase 22 D14.

### 32.1 Verdict and required precision

The selected direction survives, but only as one **Public Search & Sharing
Presentation Manifest** containing two typed, non-interchangeable results:

- a **Search Presentation** controls only locally authoritative search
  eligibility and search-facing artifacts; and
- a **Share Presentation** controls only the exact public permalink, link-card
  metadata, certified public image, and user-initiated share payload.

They must be compiled from the same immutable public release coverage so their
facts cannot drift, but they cannot be collapsed: D2 **Shared by link — public**
is intentionally shareable while remaining `noindex` and omitted from
directories, navigation, sitemaps, and locale discovery. D2 **Listed publicly**
is both shareable and technically search-index eligible. Not-public, protected,
preview, supporter-only, contained, withdrawn, retired, and tombstoned truth is
neither anonymously searchable nor anonymously shareable.

**Search-ready** is an Asym-owned proof that the current eligible release is
an anonymous `200`, safely server-rendered, internally crawlable, self-
canonical, correctly described, sitemap-covered, and free of known local
indexing blockers. It is not a claim that Google or Bing has discovered,
crawled, indexed, ranked, or displayed the URL. Search providers choose those
external outcomes and may rewrite the displayed title or snippet.

### 32.2 The required public Ministry Update permalink

D11 defines one canonical Ministry Update, immutable Revisions, and exact
Public Page Release Projections, but it does not yet define one authoritative
public permalink. The current public prototype renders unlinked update cards,
while the authenticated donor-feed prototype shares a fictional hard-coded
`https://givehope.app/posts/{id}` URL. Neither is production authority.

D14 therefore requires exactly one stable, opaque, server-resolved Public
Ministry Update Permalink per exact Tenant x Legal Entity x environment x Site
x locale x canonical Update identity. It presents the current admitted D11
public release head rather than embedding a mutable feed position or Revision
number in the public identity. Every page placement links and shares that same
Site/locale permalink; a fragment, query-only identity, copied page-owned post,
raw Update id, and duplicate per-feed canonical are forbidden.

Its effective posture is derived from complete current placement coverage:

1. if at least one current, safe, admitted public placement belongs to a
   Listed-public page, the permalink is Listed/search-ready eligible;
2. if one or more current, safe public placements exist but every placement is
   Shared-by-link, the permalink is public and shareable but `noindex`; and
3. if no current safe public placement exists, the public route has D8's
   privacy-safe `404`/`noindex` disposition and no content-specific card.

This union rule cannot widen a Shared-by-link placement: a permalink becomes
Listed only when the same released update is already presented through at
least one independently authorized Listed-public page. Removal from the last
Listed placement recomputes the current local posture to link-only or absent;
external search and social caches remain separately observed outcomes.

The permalink consumes a D8-compatible append-only Route Generation and Route
Effect Manifest through Phase 5. It does not create a second route authority,
CMS post, audience release path, or publication head.

### 32.4 Hardened low-friction experience

#### Staff and missionary authoring

The existing page or public-update editor contains one collapsed **Search &
sharing** section. Healthy generated output needs no action and creates no
second review queue.

The section shows:

- one read-only result: **Can appear in search**, **Shareable by link; not
  listed in search**, or **Not public**;
- the exact Site, locale, and clean public URL;
- generated, locale-specific Search & sharing title and description, with
  optional bounded edits and **Reset to generated**;
- one optional Share image choice limited to current D9-certified public
  placements and derivatives; if none is selected, the deterministic chain is
  the exact release's social placement, eligible released hero/update media,
  a certified Site card, then a neutral certified fallback;
- accessible **Search appearance** and **Link preview** tabs, explicitly marked
  approximate because providers can rewrite, crop, omit, or cache output; and
- one plain note: search engines decide when or whether a page appears, and
  social networks may temporarily show an older cached preview.

The title, description, and optional certified image selection are ordinary
D3/D11 draft fields and follow the tenant's sole D4/D5 review/release lane.
They may not introduce a hidden identity, exact location, claim, or image not
supported by the visible current public release. Contributors see no editable
canonical, slug, robots, sitemap, `hreflang`, schema, keywords, provider,
IndexNow, storage URL, arbitrary image URL, or indexing switch.

For Shared-by-link, the exact warning is: **Anyone with this link can view and
reshare it. It will not be listed in your directory or submitted in your
sitemap.** No interface calls it private.

#### Visitor sharing

Every current anonymously public page and admitted public Update permalink has
one quiet, accessible, secondary **Share** action. It:

1. invokes `navigator.share({ title, text, url })` only after direct user
   activation when supported;
2. always retains a first-party **Copy link** fallback and may offer bounded
   ordinary provider links that contact the provider only after selection;
3. treats user cancellation as cancellation, not an error;
4. announces Copy success/failure as a status message and exposes a selected
   read-only URL when clipboard access fails;
5. uses visible text, an accessible name, logical focus, keyboard operation,
   adequate touch targets, safe encoding, `noopener`, and a conservative
   referrer policy; and
6. shares the clean current canonical URL with no draft/preview token, access
   key, supporter/donor identity, query-derived search text, hidden UTM value,
   or automatic social post.

No third-party share SDK, iframe, Like widget, tracking pixel, or provider
request loads before deliberate visitor action. Share-sheet opening is not
proof of selected target, completed post, delivery, view, or engagement.

### 32.5 Search, structured-data, social-card, and effect contract

For each admitted exact release, the code-owned compiler produces a complete
initial HTML/head and effect coverage containing:

- an absolute HTTPS canonical on the exact verified Site host;
- unique, useful, locale-correct title and description derived from visible
  safe truth plus only the bounded released overrides;
- a D2/Phase-10-derived robots result, never an editor setting;
- reciprocal alternates only among current safe Listed releases under exact
  Phase 24 locale/domain truth;
- host-scoped sitemap membership and a `lastmod` equal to the last significant
  released content, search/share presentation, route, media, or safety change,
  never request/build time or unrelated financial activity;
- semantic server-rendered headings/body and ordinary crawlable links from the
  current D13 directory and D11 public placements;
- safely serialized, code-owned structured data containing only visible facts:
  `WebPage` and eligible `BreadcrumbList` by default; `ProfilePage`/`Person`
  only for exactly one genuinely public-safe person; and `Article`/`BlogPosting`
  only for an eligible public Update permalink with exact released dates and
  safe visible authorship;
- Open Graph title, description, type, canonical `og:url`, Site, locale,
  eligible alternate locales, and image URL/type/dimensions/alt; compatible
  `summary_large_image` metadata; and
- one content-addressed, same-origin, metadata-stripped D9-certified social
  derivative, normally using the interoperable 1.91:1 large-card shape, with a
  non-expiring public resolver identity while that exact release remains
  authorized.

The Page/Update HTML, canonical, robots, alternate links, JSON-LD, sitemap row,
Open Graph/social metadata, share payload, and card asset all carry or resolve
the same immutable coverage digest. Search and social crawlers receive the same
current public claims people receive; crawler-specific hidden content is
forbidden.

D13 GET query/filter variants are `noindex`, canonicalize to the active base
directory, stay out of sitemaps and locale alternates, and never echo visitor
query text into head, structured data, logs, or share cards. Sitemaps contain
only current canonical URLs intended for search, are deterministically sharded
before protocol limits, and reference accurate significant-release `lastmod`.

The D8 effect outbox performs exact add/update/delete cache, sitemap, internal-
link, structured-metadata, social-metadata, and optional provider-notification
effects after the local release. A provider call never runs inside the release
transaction. Exact-host IndexNow may accelerate Bing and other participating
engines, but acknowledgement proves receipt only. Google's general Indexing API
is not used because ministry pages and Updates are outside its supported
JobPosting/livestream scope.

### 32.6 Failure, removal, observability, and production proof

- Missing, stale, contradictory, revoked, or generation-mismatched authority
  removes or withholds new positive search/share output first. It never inherits
  root metadata, another Site/tenant/locale, raw CMS/CRM/storage truth, an old
  positive release, or a raw media URL.
- A D8/Phase-10 known denial returns the uniform privacy-safe `404`/`noindex`
  result and disables content-specific card/asset resolution. An authoritative
  dependency outage remains the neutral `503`, `Retry-After`, `no-store`
  response and cannot become a stale `200` or false permanent removal.
- Release replacement preserves the last coherent release only while that exact
  release remains currently authorized. A safe certified Site/neutral card
  prevents ordinary image-generation failure from creating an incomplete live
  share result.
- Narrowing, withdrawal, or removal invalidates local positive metadata/assets,
  internal discovery, and the next sitemap generation immediately, then emits
  residual external refresh/removal work. Search indexes, snippets, social
  caches, published posts, copied links, screenshots, and archives cannot be
  transactionally recalled.
- Observability distinguishes local release generation, public proof, sitemap
  emission, crawler fetch, submission receipt, crawl observation, index
  observation, preview refresh observation, and removal observation. Healthy
  tenants see no routine SEO chores; one cause-owned exception explains only
  an Asym-controlled readiness problem.

Production authorization requires contract and journey proof across Tenant,
Legal Entity, environment, Site, host, locale, both Page Families, Update,
every D2/D11 posture, current/stale/contained/withdrawn authority, multi-page
Update placement, route move/tombstone, media replacement/withdrawal, and
deployment skew. It must include:

- raw initial-HTML and `GET`/`HEAD` tests for ordinary anonymous requests and a
  certified matrix of Googlebot, Bingbot, Meta, LinkedIn, Slack, and compatible
  card-crawler user agents without JavaScript dependence;
- cross-tenant/host/locale/id substitution and RLS/grant/cache isolation tests;
- equality of release digest across HTML, metadata, canonical, robots,
  alternates, JSON-LD, sitemap, share payload, and card asset;
- D9 egress assertions proving no original filename, EXIF/location data,
  provider/storage URL, internal id, preview token, or protected fact in HTML,
  RSC/JSON, headers, metadata, JSON-LD, image bytes/URL/alt, sitemap, logs,
  traces, metrics, or errors;
- canonical collision, reciprocal-locale, query crawl-trap, sitemap sharding,
  exact `lastmod`, crawler-burst, tenant-fairness, Core Web Vitals, and cache-
  invalidation tests;
- concurrent release, stale job, outbox replay, ambiguous provider receipt,
  adverse-positive-first containment, and append-only recovery exercises; and
- mobile, no-JavaScript, keyboard, screen-reader, reflow, visible-focus,
  touch-target, native-share cancellation, clipboard-denial, and status-message
  journeys at the project's WCAG 2.2 AA baseline.

### 32.7 Ruthless ordered synthesis

1. **Freeze the reach matrix.** Listed means locally index eligible and
   shareable; Shared-by-link means shareable and `noindex`; stricter truth has
   no anonymous content-specific projection.
2. **Create one stable public Update permalink per Site/locale canonical Update
   identity.** Derive its posture from complete current public placement
   coverage; never use fragments, raw ids, or copied per-feed posts.
3. **Compile one immutable manifest with two typed results.** Search and share
   consume the same exact release facts while preserving different semantics.
4. **Keep tenant work bounded.** Generate everything useful; allow only
   optional locale title, description, and D9-certified image selection inside
   the existing review/release flow.
5. **Make eligible content genuinely crawlable.** Serve meaningful HTML and
   anchors, correct canonicals/alternates/structured data, and exact host-
   scoped sharded sitemaps. Do not create a crawler-only rendering authority.
6. **Make every anonymous public Page and Update safely shareable.** Use native
   Share, Copy link, and click-only provider links without passive third-party
   code or identity-bearing URLs.
7. **Keep external systems asynchronous and non-authoritative.** Sitemaps,
   optional IndexNow, and provider observations improve discovery and diagnosis
   but never block release or prove indexing, ranking, sharing, or removal.
8. **Remove unsafe positive output first.** Local denial, metadata, assets,
   discovery, and sitemap converge from owning facts before residual external
   refresh; do not promise recall of cached/copied material.
9. **Replace prototype seams rather than grandfathering them.** Global root
   metadata, mock/raw-id worker helpers, generic `Person`/location JSON-LD,
   obsolete `SearchAction`, fictional share URLs, inert Share buttons, mutable
   raw CMS media, and serialized original filenames are migration evidence only.
10. **Ship only after complete public-egress and race certification.** A single
    happy-path SEO snapshot is insufficient for a multi-tenant safety surface.

### 32.8 Exact C-prime-R ratified as Phase 22 D14

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — one immutable,
> release-bound, locale-exact Public Search & Sharing Presentation Manifest
> containing non-interchangeable Search Presentation and Share Presentation
> results for every exact current Phase-10-safe D2 Page Release and D11 Public
> Page Ministry Update Release; structurally scoped by Tenant, Legal Entity,
> environment, Site, verified host, locale, Page Family or canonical Update
> identity, D3 Presentation/Feed Binding, D4/D5 release occurrence, D2 reach,
> D8-compatible route and effect generation, D9 media manifest, D11 Revision
> and audience/placement coverage, Phase 10 safety and containment, Phase 24
> domain/locale truth, and exact renderer, compiler, and release generations;
> using people-first generated defaults plus only bounded locale-specific title,
> description, and D9-certified share-image selection inside D3/D11 and
> D4/D5's sole edit, review, and release lane. A current `Listed publicly` Page
> Release is server-rendered, internally crawlable, self-canonical, exact-host
> sitemap- and reciprocal-locale-eligible, locally search-index eligible, and
> publicly shareable; `Shared by link — public` remains anonymously reachable
> and publicly reshareable but emits `noindex` and remains absent from
> directories, navigation, sitemaps, public-feed discovery, and locale
> discovery; Not-public, draft, authenticated-preview, supporter-only,
> contained, withdrawn, retired, and tombstoned truth emits no content-specific
> anonymous metadata, card, or share projection. Every canonical Ministry
> Update receives exactly one stable opaque public permalink per Site and locale
> rather than a feed fragment, query identity, raw id, or copied page-owned post;
> complete current placement coverage makes that permalink Listed only when at
> least one exact safe admitted placement is independently Listed, public but
> `noindex` when every admitted placement is Shared-by-link, and uniformly
> absent when no admitted public placement remains. One code-owned compiler
> produces complete initial HTML/head, exact crawler directives, canonical and
> reciprocal alternate links, significant-release `lastmod`, host-scoped
> sharded sitemap coverage, visible-fact structured data, Open Graph and
> compatible social-card metadata, and one content-addressed same-origin
> D9-certified social derivative with contextual image alternative text; every
> HTML, metadata, JSON-LD, media, sitemap, and share-payload fact resolves the
> same immutable release coverage and current safety ceiling while Search and
> Share outcomes remain distinct. One quiet accessible `Search & sharing`
> section shows generated defaults, approximate search/link previews, current
> Site, locale, clean URL, and honest search eligibility, with optional Reset to
> generated and no editable canonical, robots, sitemap, `hreflang`, schema,
> keyword, provider, route, or arbitrary-image controls; it creates no second
> review queue or routine tenant work. Every anonymously public Page and public
> Update permalink receives one accessible secondary Share action using
> user-initiated native Web Share when supported and first-party Copy link plus
> bounded click-only outbound fallbacks otherwise, with no passive third-party
> SDK, iframe, tracker, draft/preview URL, secret, supporter identity, query-
> derived text, hidden attribution, automatic post, or claim that Asym knows the
> selected target or completed share. Phase 5 serves exact public HTML and
> assets; D2 owns reach, D8 route dispositions/effects, D9/Phase 29 media, D11
> Update/audience truth, Phase 10 safety, Phase 24 domain/locale truth, and D13
> on-site discovery remain independently authoritative. Automatic canonical
> sitemaps, crawler-accessible links, public-response probes, optional exact-
> host IndexNow acceleration, and cause-owned exception monitoring make Google,
> Bing, and other standards-compatible crawlers able to discover and evaluate
> eligible releases, while external crawling, indexing, ranking, title/snippet
> choice, social fetching, cache refresh, sharing, and de-indexing remain
> independently observed best-effort outcomes. Unknown or adverse proof removes
> positive local search/share output first and recovery is append-only — without
> a second SEO/social publication head, page-level indexing switch, shared-link
> secrecy claim, client-side or bot-only content authority, raw CMS/CRM/storage
> reads, inherited root or cross-Site/unsafe-locale fallback, original filename
> or source metadata, arbitrary JSON-LD or remote media, generic `Person`,
> `SearchAction`, `DonateAction`, Google Indexing API misuse, third-party share
> widget, query-variant indexing, request/build-time freshness, mutable current
> truth, destructive rollback, blind provider retry, or any claim that released,
> reachable, listed, search-ready, sitemap-included, submitted, crawled, indexed,
> ranked, share-opened, shared, cached, refreshed, removed, and externally
> forgotten are the same fact.**

The founder ratified this exact formulation as **Phase 22 D14** on 2026-08-06.
The binding interpretation and consequences are recorded in the
[Phase 22 decision log](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md) and
