## 33. Historical D15 option research — Public Ministry measurement and privacy

> **Status:** historical option input incorporated into ratified D15. This
> section does not itself alter D1–D14, authorize runtime collection or replay,
> or change the current privacy posture. The final D15 contract in §36 has
> exactly four interactions and excludes the older directory-result-selection
> proposal below.

### 33.1 Why this is the next dependency-ordered seam

D13 creates public browse/search interactions and D14 makes eligible pages and
Updates discoverable and shareable. That creates a normal product question:
what, if anything, may staff and assigned page contributors learn about public
reach, reading, sharing, and Give-CTA interest? It also creates an immediate
classification problem because a supporter, Googlebot, a social-card fetcher,
an email-security scanner, a browser prefetch, an uptime probe, and an abusive
client can request the same public URL without representing the same behavior.

This decision must precede Phase 22's final observability, cache, contributor-
permission, migration, and launch proof. Once raw URLs, replay frames, visitor
identifiers, or third-party events leave Asym, later narrowing cannot reliably
recall them. Once dashboards depend on ambiguous view or conversion semantics,
changing the event model also becomes expensive.

### 33.2 Current-repo evidence and conflict

- [`apps/donor/openpolicy.ts`](../../../apps/donor/openpolicy.ts) declares
  `analytics: false`, `marketing: false`, no cookie banner, and no preference
  panel for the donor public surface. Its retention text permits de-identified
  aggregate analytics but does not prove that an analytics feature is enabled.
- [`apps/donor/instrumentation-client.ts`](../../../apps/donor/instrumentation-client.ts)
  initializes Sentry Session Replay whenever `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` exists,
  sampling 10% of production sessions and attempting replay for every sampled
  error. `sendDefaultPii: false` and Sentry's default text/media masking reduce
  exposure but do not turn DOM/session recording into body-free aggregate
  measurement or reconcile it with the published analytics-off posture.
- D10 already requires preview to remain absent from public analytics. D14
  separates public Share-action opening from a completed external share and
  prevents passive third-party widgets. D15 cannot reinterpret either fact.
- D7/Phase 13 already own Page Giving Binding, Source Code, cart, checkout,
  accepted contribution, recurring setup, and attribution truth. Phase 22 may
  count a Give CTA selection but cannot invent or duplicate a conversion ledger.
- Phase 31 is the governed future API/connector spine. Any later external
  analytics destination belongs behind a separately certified Phase 31 adapter,
  not a Phase 22 arbitrary-script field or launch-time tag manager.

Sentry's current JavaScript Session Replay guidance describes replay as a DOM-
based session reproduction. It masks text and blocks media by default and makes
network bodies/headers opt-in precisely because privacy configuration is still
required; these defaults are safeguards, not proof that replay is necessary or
appropriate for public ministry pages. [Sentry Session Replay](https://docs.sentry.dev/platforms/javascript/session-replay/)

### 33.3 Current regulatory and platform evidence

The UK ICO's final April 2026 storage/access guidance recognizes a narrow
statistical-purpose exception for aggregate service-improvement analytics, but
requires clear information and a simple free objection path. It excludes
identifying, tracking, monitoring, profiling, advertising, retained individual-
level data, and decisions about a person; individual data must be aggregated
and retained only as long as necessary for that aggregation. This is a useful
privacy-by-design ceiling even where a particular tenant is outside UK scope,
not a substitute for tenant-specific legal review. [ICO statistical-purpose
exception](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-the-exceptions/)

The same ICO guidance says first-party versus third-party and client-side versus
server-side labels do not decide the privacy result; purpose, storage/access,
personal-data handling, transparency, objection/consent, and downstream use do.
[ICO storage and access technologies](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-storage-and-access-technologies/)

Google states that Consent Mode does not provide a consent banner or widget.
Basic mode blocks tags until consent; advanced mode still sends cookieless pings
that can include timestamp, user agent, referrer, consent state, and page-load
signals, and reports may blend observed and modeled results. Therefore “uses
Consent Mode” is not a complete tenant UX, legal, privacy, or truth contract.
[Google Consent Mode](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/10000067?hl=en)

### 33.4 Concrete scenario

A supporter follows a prayer-letter link to a Listed missionary page, reads a
Ministry Update, chooses Share, selects Give, and later completes a recurring
gift. During the same minute Googlebot, a social-preview crawler, an email-
security scanner, an uptime monitor, and a browser prefetch request the page.
The missionary and spouse have separate D1 contributor assignments. Finance and
fundraising staff want to understand whether the public page is useful, while
neither contributor should receive donor identities, individual browsing
history, or a claim that a Share opening or CTA click became a gift.

### 33.5 Options

#### Option A — No engagement analytics

Retain only body-free operational health metrics plus Phase 13 contribution
attribution. This is the simplest and safest posture, but staff and contributors
cannot evaluate page reach, Update readership, Share interest, or CTA use.

#### Option B — First-party aggregates for authorized staff only

Record bounded qualified page views, directory selections, Share-action
openings, and Give-CTA selections and expose delayed aggregates only to
authorized staff. Contributors retain their existing Phase 13/16/21 support
views but receive no page-engagement feedback. This sharply limits disclosure
but may withhold useful ministry-page insight from the people responsible for
the content.

#### Option C-prime — One bounded Public Ministry Measurement Profile with tenant-controlled contributor visibility — Recommended

Each exact Tenant × Legal Entity × Site prospectively chooses **Off**, **Staff
only**, or **Staff + assigned Public Page Contributors**. The quiet guided
default is **Staff only**; enabling contributor visibility previews exactly
which page-level aggregates they will see and never widens financial or supporter
access.

When enabled, Phase 22 records only first-party, release-bound typed occurrences
for qualified page/Update views, directory-result selections, Share-action
openings, and Give-CTA selections. Durable data carries exact Site, verified
host, locale, Page or canonical Update, immutable release, Page Family, action
type, coarse bounded source category, occurred bucket, and event/schema
generation, but no raw IP, user agent, full referrer, query string, persistent
visitor/session identifier, fingerprint, donor/supporter identity, legal
identity, sensitive location, cross-site/device linkage, replay frame, free-form
property, or arbitrary tenant event.

Ephemeral request signals may classify known crawlers, social fetchers, email
scanners, prefetches, monitors, and abuse, then are discarded before durable
storage. Reports are delayed, through-dated, low-count suppressed, purpose-
scoped, and aggregate-only. Staff do not receive an individual browsing timeline.
Assigned contributors see only exact pages they currently may contribute to,
never tenant-wide or supporter-level aggregates. A transparent public notice
and simple free objection path remain available wherever the selected posture or
applicable law requires them.

Phase 13 remains solely authoritative for cart entry, checkout, accepted gift,
recurring setup, settlement, and Source Code attribution. A D15 report may show
a separately labelled Phase 13 aggregate by reference but cannot join a person
or session journey, infer a gift from a CTA click, or create conversion truth.
Public and giving routes prohibit session replay, heatmaps, ad pixels, arbitrary
third-party scripts, cross-site tracking, and hidden tag-manager additions.
Phase 31 may later add an exact separately certified analytics adapter with its
own tenant authorization, consent/objection, egress, deletion, provider, and
observed-versus-modeled-result proof.

#### Option D — Tenant-selected external analytics at launch

Allow Google Analytics, PostHog, Meta, or similar tenant-selected scripts from
the start. This maximizes marketing flexibility but introduces provider code,
cookies or cookieless pings, consent/objection UX, URL/referrer leakage, cross-
border processing, modeled-versus-observed reporting, CSP and performance risk,
provider-specific configuration, and substantial support burden. It also
conflicts with D14's no-passive-widget posture and the current analytics-off
donor policy unless separately redesigned and disclosed.

### 33.6 Recommendation and decision question

Recommend **Option C-prime**. It gives tenants a genuine Off choice, gives staff
useful comprehensible product feedback by quiet default, lets a tenant share
safe page-level aggregates with current assigned contributors, and avoids
turning Phase 22 into a surveillance, ad-tech, replay, or contribution-
attribution system.

The unresolved founder question is: should Phase 22 use **A no engagement
analytics**, **B first-party staff-only aggregates**, **C-prime one bounded
tenant profile with optional contributor-visible aggregates (recommended)**, or
**D tenant-selected external analytics at launch**?

## 34. D15 current research incorporated into the ratified contract

> **Status:** incorporated into ratified D15. This section remains research
> evidence and does not authorize runtime collection, change D1–D14, or cure
> the current donor-policy and Session Replay conflict.

### 34.1 The selected direction survives only after material simplification

The selected C-prime direction is useful, but its original shape still allows
too much ambiguity. A directory selection does not need to be a fifth metric;
it is a bounded source category for a later qualified page load. A request is
not a page view because Next.js may prefetch routes and crawlers, preview
fetchers, scanners, monitors, and abusive clients all request public URLs.
Likewise, a Share control opening is not a completed share, and a Give selection
is not a cart, gift, recurring agreement, settlement, conversion, or donor.

The hardened product therefore has exactly four fixed signals:

1. **Qualified page loads** — a current public Page Release became visible in a
   browser and emitted one best-effort post-render signal;
2. **Ministry Update opens** — a current public Update permalink became visible
   or a visitor explicitly opened the full Update, never merely saw a feed card;
3. **Share menu opens** — a visitor deliberately opened D14's first-party Share
   experience, with no claim that an external destination or post followed; and
4. **Give selections** — a visitor deliberately selected the current D7 Give
   CTA, with no claim about Phase 13 cart, checkout, gift, or payment results.

These are measured interactions, not unique people. D15 provides no visitor,
supporter, donor, session, device, household, journey, reach, bounce, dwell,
scroll, demographic, geography, heatmap, replay, ranking, or conversion metric.
It never joins an occurrence to a Phase 13 Person, Contribution, cart, checkout,
or Source Code. Staff may follow a separately labelled link to already-
authorized Phase 13 aggregate reporting, but the two authorities and coverage
watermarks stay visibly distinct.

Next.js warns that prefetching can execute side effects before navigation, and
Google warns that crawler user-agent strings are spoofable. The report must
therefore say **qualified page loads**, disclose that machine filtering is
best-effort, and never promise human or unique-visitor counts. [Next.js
prefetching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/prefetching) [Googlebot
verification](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/googlebot)

### 34.2 One deliberately small setup

Each exact Tenant × Legal Entity × Site has one prospective versioned Public
Ministry Measurement Profile with three choices:

- **Off** — no D15 occurrence is emitted. Essential security and reliability
  telemetry continues under its independent purpose and body/query-safe
  contract.
- **Staff only — Recommended** — authorized staff see delayed aggregate Page
  and Update activity.
- **Staff + assigned page contributors** — authorized staff retain their view;
  every current D1 Public Page Contributor sees only disclosure-safe aggregates
  for the exact pages they currently may contribute to.

The persisted initial state is **Off**. One setup screen may recommend **Staff
only**, but collection begins only after an authorized tenant actor explicitly
saves it and every launch gate is current. There are no per-page overrides,
metric builders, report builders, custom events, retention controls, threshold
controls, bot controls, provider API keys, JavaScript fields, tag-manager
fields, or external-analytics switches.

The setup preview lists the four signals, the fields that are never collected,
who will see each report, and—only when contributor visibility is selected—the
current page/contributor census. Turning the profile Off stops new D15
measurement prospectively and immediately removes contributor report access.
It does not pretend to disable essential security telemetry or silently destroy
authorized aggregate history before the code-owned retention boundary.

The current donor policy says analytics are off, while the donor runtime enables
sampled Sentry Session Replay whenever a DSN is present. D15 production
activation is therefore blocked until public ministry and giving routes are
proved replay-free, operational telemetry is query/body/DOM-safe, and the
public notice plus simple free objection or stricter applicable consent path
matches actual behavior. `sendDefaultPii: false` is not a substitute for that
proof. [Sentry Session Replay](https://docs.sentry.dev/platforms/javascript/session-replay/)

### 34.3 Minimal data, Supabase, and RLS boundary

`GET`, `HEAD`, rendering, RSC/prefetch, preview, sitemap, crawler, social-card,
scanner, and monitor requests remain measurement-effect-free. A first-party same-origin
POST occurs only after a production public release is visibly rendered or an
exact Share/Give action occurs. Delivery is best-effort and never delays or
blocks content, Share, Give routing, cart, or checkout. No persistent offline
queue retries a visitor action.

Before durable measurement storage, request headers may be examined
ephemerally for abuse control, a coarse source category, and known-machine
classification. Raw IP, user agent, full URL/query, referrer, location,
fingerprint, cookie, local-storage identifier, visitor/session identifier,
supporter identity, donor identity, free-form property, and replay data are
discarded. The short-lived occurrence carries only a random unlinked operation
ID, exact Tenant, Legal Entity, environment, Site, verified host, locale,
Page/Update, immutable release, Page Family, fixed action, bounded source
category, received bucket, and metric/classifier generation.

Occurrences and idempotency material are removed within 24 hours after daily
aggregation. One code-owned 24-month aggregate retention period supports
ordinary comparison without creating a tenant retention matrix. Open daily
buckets may accumulate; sealed daily buckets are immutable and later repairs
use append-only correction deltas. Turning measurement Off does not rewrite
history. A stricter legal deletion, hold, or custody requirement remains with
the owning privacy/custody workflow.

Raw occurrence storage is private and unavailable to browser clients, tenant
exports, contributors, and Phase 31. Aggregate projections carry the complete
Tenant × Legal Entity × environment × Site × host × locale × Page/Update ×
release × metric dimensions. RLS is defense in depth, not the sole authority:
every report read re-proves current Phase 12 staff authority or the current D1
page assignment. It never trusts user-editable metadata, a stale JWT claim, a
historical recipient list, subject identity, spouse/team relationship, Display
Participant status, or Support Assignment. Revocation removes historical and
future report access immediately without deleting the tenant's aggregate fact.
Supabase warns that exposed tables need RLS, JWT authorization data may be
stale, and views require deliberate security posture. [Supabase Row Level
Security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)

Launch does not require partitioning or an event warehouse. Daily aggregate
keys and policy dimensions are indexed; tenant-fair intake, bounded payloads,
rate limits, idempotency, asynchronous aggregation, and measured growth govern
scale. Partitioning is introduced only after observed volume and query plans
justify it.

### 34.4 Calm, honest reports

Staff receive one **Public page activity** report with 7-, 30-, and 90-complete-
day presets, exact Site and authorized Page filters, four metric cards, a calm
trend, and a bounded source breakdown such as **Asym directory**, **other Asym
page or Update**, **external search**, **external social**, and **Other/unknown**.
The raw referrer is never retained, and **Other/unknown** is not filled by
guessing.

Contributors receive the same plain metric definitions for exact currently
assigned pages, but no tenant-wide rollup, source breakdown, visitor timeline,
financial drill-through, or exact sparse cell. Code-owned suppression and
secondary-suppression rules cover every contributor-visible value and allowed
comparison so differencing cannot reconstruct a hidden small number. Suppressed
means **Not enough activity to show safely**, never zero.

Every report states **Data complete through ...** and one of **Complete**,
**Delayed**, **Partial**, or **Unavailable**. An intake or aggregation problem
never displays stale data as current or fabricates zero. Metric definitions and
classifier generation are discoverable without asking tenants to configure
them. An optional compact chart is paired with an equivalent accessible HTML
table, textual trend summary, non-color status, keyboard access, visible focus,
mobile reflow, zoom support, and an export containing only the currently
authorized visible aggregate. W3C guidance requires charts to have equivalent
descriptions/data and programmatic table structure. [W3C complex images](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/complex/)

Analytics products themselves document unavoidable discrepancies caused by
reloads, bots, disabled JavaScript, blocking, time zones, and differing metric
definitions. D15 therefore exposes coverage and definitions rather than a
false accounting-grade total. [Shopify analytics discrepancies](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/reports-and-analytics/discrepancies)

### 34.5 Privacy and external-provider ceiling

The public privacy surface explains the fixed service-improvement purpose and
provides a simple free objection path where the statistical exception is used;
stricter applicable consent requirements still win. A first-party preference
used solely to remember the objection may not become an analytics identifier.
The ICO's current statistical-purpose exception is narrow: aggregate service-
improvement only, clear information, easy objection, no individual monitoring,
no retained individual history, and no advertising or decisions about people.
[ICO statistical-purpose exception](https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/what-are-the-exceptions/)

Phase 22 public and giving routes prohibit session replay, heatmaps, ad pixels,
arbitrary scripts, tag managers, cross-site/device linkage, custom tenant
events, and external analytics at launch. A future provider is possible only
through a separately certified Phase 31 adapter with exact capability, field,
purpose, consent/objection, egress, retention, deletion, region, provider, and
observed-versus-modeled reporting proof. D15 has no generic analytics payload or
tenant API-key field.

## 35. Ratified D15 ruthless adversarial review

Every requested category contains a concern before the controls above are
binding.

## 36. Ratified D15 synthesis and hardened decision

### 36.1 Ordered permanent path

1. **Reconcile truth before collection.** Disable and prove the absence of
   replay on public ministry/giving routes, preserve only independently scoped
   safe operational telemetry, and make policy/objection or consent UX match
   runtime behavior.
2. **Freeze four honest meanings.** Qualified page load, Update open, Share menu
   open, and Give selection are distinct measured occurrences—not people,
   shares, conversions, gifts, or payments.
3. **Ship one setup choice.** Keep the persisted state Off until an authorized
   tenant actor explicitly chooses recommended Staff only or Staff + assigned
   page contributors. Do not add per-page knobs.
4. **Enforce the data ceiling before storage.** First-party post-render/action
   intake only; discard identity and raw request data; private transient rows
   expire within 24 hours; durable daily aggregates expire after 24 months.
5. **Make authorization current.** Staff and contributors receive only exact
   current scope; D1/Phase 12 are re-proved at every read and export; revocation
   is immediate; contributors never get source or sparse drill-down.
6. **Make uncertainty visible.** Daily sealed facts, exact generations,
   append-only repairs, fixed suppression, through-dates, and distinct complete,
   delayed, partial, unavailable, suppressed, and zero states replace false
   real-time precision.
7. **Keep the public journey independent.** Measurement failure never blocks
   public serving, Updates, Share, Give, cart, or checkout and never generates a
   downstream action.
8. **Prove production behavior.** Test Off, every non-human fetch path,
   idempotency, cross-tenant/host/locale/release swaps, revocation, suppression
   differencing, accessibility, partial coverage, TTL, load, concurrency,
   deployment skew, and absence of replay/query/body leakage.
9. **Defer generic analytics.** Any future vendor is a separately certified
   Phase 31 adapter. Phase 22 never embeds a tag manager, pixel, arbitrary
   script, generic event payload, or provider API key.

### 36.2 Ratified C-prime-R

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — one prospective, versioned, Tenant × Legal Entity × Site Public Ministry Measurement Profile with a persisted Off state and one guided choice of Staff only (recommended) or Staff + current assigned Public Page Contributors; measuring exactly four first-party, immutable-release-bound, fixed-schema interactions—qualified visible Page loads, full Ministry Update opens, Share-menu opens, and Give-CTA selections—through best-effort post-render or explicit-action POSTs that never arise from GET, HEAD, render, RSC/prefetch, preview, sitemap, crawler, social-card, scanner, monitor, or provider fetch and never block Page, Update, Share, Give, cart, or checkout behavior. D15 owns only delayed aggregate service-improvement measurement: it never claims unique people, supporters, reach, sessions, journeys, completed shares, carts, conversions, gifts, recurring agreements, settlements, payments, or attribution; D7/D14 and Phase 13 remain independently authoritative, and any separately displayed Phase 13 aggregate retains its own label, authorization, and through-date with no person/session join. Ephemeral request signals may support abuse control, bounded source classification, and conservative known-machine exclusion, but raw IP, user agent, URL/query, referrer, location, fingerprint, cookie or local-storage identifier, persistent visitor/session identifier, supporter/donor/legal identity, free-form property, replay frame, and cross-site/device link never enter durable measurement; unlinked idempotent occurrences are private, aggregate into exact Tenant, Legal Entity, environment, Site, verified host, locale, Page or canonical Update, immutable release, Page Family, metric, bounded source, day, profile, metric-schema, and classifier-generation facts, and are deleted with idempotency material within 24 hours, while sealed daily aggregates use append-only corrections and one code-owned 24-month retention. Every staff or contributor read/export re-proves current Phase 12 or exact D1 page-assignment authority in the server boundary and RLS, with complete structural isolation, immediate revocation, no JWT/user-metadata or relationship inference, no browser/raw-event access, and code-owned disclosure controls; contributors receive only suppression-safe exact-page totals and trends, never tenant-wide, source, identity, event, sparse-cell, or financial drill-down. One quiet setup consequence preview, one accessible Public page activity report, 7/30/90 complete-day presets, fixed plain-language definitions, an equivalent HTML table, Data complete through coverage, honest Complete/Delayed/Partial/Unavailable/Suppressed/Zero states, and cause-owned diagnostics keep administration and missionary use simple. Production activation is proof-gated on replay-free public ministry and giving routes, query/body/DOM-safe independent operational telemetry, truthful notice plus the applicable simple objection or stricter consent path, fixed-schema same-origin intake, tenant-fair rate and size limits, exact release re-resolution, cross-scope and concurrency proof, suppression-differencing proof, retention proof, accessibility proof, and failure isolation. Phase 31 alone may later expose a separately certified external analytics adapter with exact purpose, fields, consent/objection, egress, retention, deletion, provider, region, and observed-versus-modeled proof—without per-page analytics switches, custom metrics or events, report builders, visitor timelines, unique-visitor hashes, funnels, heatmaps, session replay, ad pixels, tag managers, arbitrary scripts, provider API-key fields, raw-log or Sentry backfill, generic analytics payloads, premature event warehousing or partitioning, destructive correction, silent zero-filling, blind retry, or any claim that enabled, collected, queued, received, classified, aggregated, complete, viewed, human, shared, selected, converted, donated, settled, paid, or externally reported are the same fact.**

The founder ratified this exact formulation as **Phase 22 D15** on 2026-08-06.
The binding decision and its permanent architectural consequences are recorded
in the [Phase 22 decision log](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md)
and
[ADR-0132](../../adr/0132-bounded-public-ministry-measurement-and-contributor-visibility.md).

## 37. Ratified D16 research — source-bounded Public Page Writing Assistant

> **Status:** INCORPORATED INTO FOUNDER-RATIFIED PHASE 22 D16 ON 2026-08-06.
> This section records the first-party comparator evidence and product
> deductions used for the D16 adversarial review. The binding decision is in
> the [Phase 22 decision log](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md)
> and [ADR-0133](../../adr/0133-source-bounded-public-page-writing-assistance.md).

### 37.1 Existing Asym boundary carried into this research

- **DOCUMENTED (repository):** Phase 21 D10 already owns the shared
  tenant-controlled AI execution foundation: purpose-specific immutable AI
  Capability Binding Versions, minimum-data AI Egress Manifests, immutable
  Invocation Evidence, server-side capability-certified adapters, no arbitrary
  provider endpoint/model/system prompt, no browser-side provider call, no
  silent fallback, and a complete manual path. Phase 22 may consume that
  foundation for public-profile drafting but owns whether a suggestion is
  accepted into ordinary content truth. See
  [ADR-0099](../../adr/0099-claim-level-expense-truth-and-purpose-routed-tenant-ai.md).
- **DOCUMENTED (repository):** D1 owns contributor authority; D4/D5 own the
  tenant-selected review-and-release lane; Phase 10 remains the non-waivable
  public-egress ceiling. An AI result can therefore be only a proposed content
  change. It cannot submit, approve, release, publish, relax safety, select a
  Designation, or establish a public fact.
- **INFERENCE:** D16 should specialize the shared `public-profile drafting`
  purpose into one bounded writing-assistance contract rather than create a
  second key store, provider picker, chat product, publication workflow, or
  generic agent.

### 37.2 Current primary-source comparator findings

| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Gmail with Gemini          | Google’s July 14, 2026 update says users can refine a draft through a prompt bar with their own precise follow-up instruction and undo or redo edits. It contrasts this with the earlier fixed `Polish`, `Formalize`, and `Shorten` choices. The update says Gmail changes the draft immediately; it does **not** document a selected-text-only or accept-before-apply flow. Earlier Gmail releases exposed `Elaborate`, put a `Polish` shortcut after 12 words, and used swipe gestures on mobile. [Shopify Magic descriptions](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/details/product-descriptions/shopify-magic)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | More supplied facts can improve relevance but do not make output truthful. `Lengthen`, `clarify impact`, or persuasive tone must not manufacture ministry outcomes, needs, locations, dates, beneficiary claims, doctrinal claims, or financial facts. Mobile behavior needs first-class design rather than desktop shrinkage.                                            |

| Microsoft HAX              | Microsoft’s evidence-based library says to make capability and likely error clear; time service to context; support efficient invocation, dismissal, and correction; scope the service when uncertain; explain why it acted; adapt cautiously; provide global controls; and notify users about capability changes. [HAX Design Library](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/haxtoolkit/library/)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Keep assistance quiet and deliberate, make source use visible, preserve the full manual editor, degrade to a smaller safe task when intent or source authority is uncertain, and never introduce silent behavioral changes.                                                                                                                                               |

### 37.3 Useful action set for ministry, biography, and project writing

The comparator products prove that a compact verb-led menu is easier to learn
than a blank chat. The following is a D16 product deduction, not an external
product claim:

#### Quiet primary actions

1. **Fix spelling & grammar** — correct mechanics while preserving meaning,
   names, quoted text, terminology, and voice.
2. **Improve clarity** — simplify structure and wording without adding facts.
3. **Shorten** — preserve the material meaning while reducing length to the
   block’s published guidance.
4. **Change tone** — a deliberately small submenu: **Warm and personal**,
   **Clear and direct**, and **Professional**. Avoid a novelty list of ten tones
   and labels that imply manufactured spirituality, urgency, or persuasion.

#### Contextual actions under **More**

- **Organize my story** for a Missionary Ministry biography or ministry-story
  block;
- **Clarify what our ministry does** for a ministry-description block;
- **Clarify the project need** for a Project/Campaign need block;
- **Explain the expected impact** only from exact supplied source facts;
- **Create a short summary** for an intro or card excerpt; and
- **Tell AI what to change** for one bounded custom transformation instruction.

**INFERENCE:** A generic `Lengthen` button is a hallucination footgun. The
missionary-friendly equivalent should be **Add detail**: first ask the author
for the missing fact or let them select an already eligible fact, then expand
only from that material. If the user supplies nothing new, the assistant may
restructure or elaborate wording but must say that it did not add facts. A
blank block should use a short, block-specific guided interview—not an open
chat—to create a first suggestion.

### 37.4 Recommended quiet interaction model

1. **INFERENCE:** When the tenant has not activated the exact Phase 21 D10
   binding, show no AI setup warning, empty state, provider language, or broken
   control to the missionary. The manual editor remains complete.
2. **INFERENCE:** When enabled, show one subdued, clearly named **Help me write**
   action in the exact narrative block. Selection exposes the same action near
   the editor toolbar. Do not interrupt typing, pop a prompt after a word
   threshold, underline prose with unsolicited AI judgments, or repeatedly
   advertise the feature.
3. **INFERENCE:** Empty or very short blocks open a few page-family- and
   block-specific questions. Existing prose opens the compact transformation
   menu. The advanced custom instruction stays under **More**, not as the first
   thing a hesitant writer must understand.
4. **INFERENCE:** Before remote egress, **What AI will use** lists the exact
   selected text, author answers, and individually selected current public-safe
   facts. Each removable source is visible in plain language. Phase 10-ineligible
   or unproved material is omitted or blocks that invocation; BYOK never waives
   the ceiling.
5. **INFERENCE:** Generate one suggestion in a non-modal preview while the
   original remains unchanged. Offer **Use suggestion**, **Try again**, and
   **Discard**; allow direct editing of the suggestion. **Insert as alternative**
   is useful for full-block drafting but unnecessary noise for spelling or
   grammar fixes.
6. **INFERENCE:** Accepting a suggestion performs an ordinary draft edit and
   enters the editor’s normal undo/revision history. It does not submit or
   publish. If the source block changed during generation, show the current and
   proposed text and require a deliberate reapply; never overwrite newer work.
7. **INFERENCE:** On mobile, use an accessible bottom sheet with the same
   actions and no gesture-only operation. Keep the selected text or block,
   source summary, result, and primary action understandable without a
   side-by-side desktop diff.
8. **INFERENCE:** Loading is cancellable; timeout, revocation, rate limit,
   budget exhaustion, unsupported language, provider ambiguity, or output
   validation failure leaves the original untouched and gives a short manual
   recovery message. No retry silently changes provider, model, credential,
   region, purpose, source coverage, or prompt family.

### 37.5 Accessibility and non-annoyance requirements

- **DOCUMENTED:** WCAG status messages allow an asynchronous result or error to
  be announced without moving focus. [WCAG 2.2 status messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html)
- **DOCUMENTED:** Controls must remain keyboard operable; focus must remain
  visible and not obscured; targets must meet the applicable minimum; and the
  experience must reflow without two-dimensional scrolling at the required
  viewport. [Keyboard](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html),
  [Focus Not Obscured](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html),
  [Target Size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html),
  [Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)
- **INFERENCE:** Use native buttons and an accessible menu/listbox pattern;
  announce `Writing suggestion ready`, generation failure, and source-staleness
  without stealing focus. Preserve selection when possible, provide a labelled
  cancel action, and make original-versus-suggestion differences available as
  text—not color, animation, or strike-through alone.
- **INFERENCE:** Never make a sparkle icon the only accessible name, a swipe the
  only way to invoke or dismiss, a streaming animation necessary to understand
  progress, or AI use necessary to complete, save, preview, submit, or publish
  a page.

### 37.6 Adversarial implications from the comparator evidence

| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

Shopify’s warning demonstrates this is a normal product risk, not an edge case. |
| Destructive replacement                     | A Gmail-like immediate update or late provider result overwrites the author’s prose or a teammate’s newer edit.                                                                                                    | High     | Possible                      | Suggestion-first preview, source-version digest, compare-on-stale, explicit use, normal undo, and no autosave/publish side effect. Word’s replace/regenerate pattern is the safer comparator.                                                                                       |
| Noisy assistance                            | Automatic word-count prompts, repeated sparkles, inline judgments, or a large menu interrupt authors and pressure tenants who enabled the capability for occasional use.                                           | Medium   | Likely                        | One quiet optional action, progressive disclosure, no unsolicited generation or critique, efficient dismissal, and user-visible control consistent with HAX G3/G7/G8/G17.                                                                                                           |
| Source creep and privacy leakage            | Copying Gmail’s broad personalization pattern causes private CRM, supporter, receipt, message, location, or unrelated-page data to leave Asym.                                                                     | Critical | Possible                      | D10 purpose binding plus minimum-data manifest; explicit per-invocation sources; closed source kinds; Phase 10 pre-egress gate; no tools, browsing, retrieval, tenant search, or hidden context.                                                                                    |
| Action and tone sprawl                      | Ten tones, generic translation, SEO, fundraising persuasion, social posts, and an open chatbot create an untestable general writing product and inconsistent missionary voice.                                     | High     | Likely                        | Four primary actions, a few typed block actions, one bounded custom instruction, and only §38's separately pair-certified exact-English-locale translation operation; SEO, Updates, and general AI remain outside D16.                                                              |
| Mobile and assistive-technology failure     | Selection toolbars disappear, bottom sheets trap focus, diffs are color-only, streaming is unannounced, or swipe-only invocation excludes users.                                                                   | High     | Likely without explicit proof | Same semantic actions on all viewports; keyboard and screen-reader operation; announced status; preserved focus; textual comparison; non-gesture alternative; 320-CSS-pixel reflow and target-size tests.                                                                           |

| Synthetic or culturally inappropriate voice | `Warm`, `professional`, or “missionary” tone erases the author’s voice, reinforces cultural bias, or manufactures emotional and spiritual claims.                                                                  | High     | Possible                      | Small neutral tone set; preserve names/quotes/faith terminology; bias and multilingual evaluation; explicit preview/edit; no “more spiritual”, urgency, guilt, donor manipulation, or demographic targeting action.                                                                 |

### 37.7 Research synthesis for the D16 review

The strongest permanent direction combines Gmail’s compact refinement language
and reversible custom follow-up, Word’s exact selected-text suggestion and
explicit replacement controls, Jetpack’s CMS-native fixed transformations and
cancellable generation, Givebutter’s editable-unpublished nonprofit draft, and
HAX’s efficient invocation/dismissal/correction principles. It deliberately
rejects Gmail’s automatic in-place mutation and broad Workspace retrieval,
Jetpack’s large feature surface, Shopify’s publish-adjacent direct application,
and any inference that polished language is accurate.

The launch experience should therefore be **quiet, block-bounded,
source-visible, one-suggestion-at-a-time, explicitly accepted, fully undoable,
mobile-complete, and optional**. `Help me write` improves an ordinary draft; it
never becomes the editor, the author, the safety reviewer, or the publisher.

| Microsoft Azure Translator transparency note       | Microsoft says machine translation can make mistakes; quality varies with the language pair, content, style, and register. It documents risks including lost document context, mixed-language input, literal idioms, missed cultural adaptation, altered titles and relationships, changed negation or numbers, falsified names, unfavorable treatment of religious figures or symbols, omissions, ungrounded additions, offensive wording, and gender, political, and religious bias. Microsoft recommends representative scenario testing, human oversight, and a correction path; it says human evaluation is its most significant and reliable quality measure. [Azure Translator transparency note](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/translator/transparency-note) | Treat English translation as a fallible suggestion, not a language fact. The review warning must name the ministry-specific details most likely to drift. Capability proof must be source-language × exact-English-locale × provider/product/model specific and include bilingual human evaluation.                                                                                                                           |

It separately documents pronoun/context limitations requiring manual review. Confirm one source language, preserve embedded names/phrases, or ask the author to translate separately identified passages.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
