The fundraising model includes Campaign, Gift Designation, Gift Transaction Designation, and related gift objects; Program Management separately includes Program and benefit-delivery records. | Mature nonprofit CRM models do not require an operational program to be represented by a campaign or designation.                                                                                         |
| [Salesforce Gift Designations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sfdo.npc_fr_manage_designations.htm&language=en_US&type=5)                                                                                                                         | A Gift Designation is a fund for a specific gift purpose. Designations can be associated with campaigns and commitments, while Gift Transaction Designations are the allocation source used for rollups.                                                                 | A designation-backed public-purpose page is valid, but it must not become the page's campaign or operational-project truth by implication.                                                                |
| [Blackbaud: Campaigns, Funds, and Appeals](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/rex/content/en-ca/content/bb-cfas.html)                                                                                                                  | Campaign answers what the fundraising effort seeks to achieve, Fund answers how a gift should be used, and Appeal answers how the donor was solicited. A campaign may use multiple funds and appeals.                                                                    | The three axes must not be collapsed into one `fund/project/campaign` identifier.                                                                                                                         |
| [Blackbaud: Add or edit a Fund](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/rex/content/en-ca/content/bb-fund-records-add.html)                                                                                                                 | A Fund controls allocation/reporting by donor intent and may represent a general, restricted, or purpose-specific initiative. It has a stable Fund ID plus optional dates, category, type, goal, and restriction state.                                                  | Some tenants legitimately use a fund as their only durable record for a public purpose; a bounded Designated Purpose arm is therefore useful for compatibility.                                           |
| [Blackbaud SKY synchronization guidance](https://developer.blackbaud.com/skyapi/docs/in-depth-topics/synchronize-data)                                                                                                                                         | List synchronization uses stable pagination cursors, but deleted entities are not returned; Blackbaud recommends inactivation rather than deletion where synchronized continuity matters.                                                                                | A Page cannot infer retirement from record disappearance. Source status/tombstone continuity and explicit disposition are needed for migration and connectors.                                            |
| [PostgreSQL constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html)                                                                                                                                                                         | Table checks can constrain combinations of columns; primary/unique keys identify rows; foreign keys preserve referential integrity; partial unique indexes can enforce uniqueness for only qualifying rows.                                                              | A closed typed subject union can retain real database foreign keys and exactly-one semantics. A generic `{subject_type, subject_id}` pair cannot provide an ordinary FK to three unrelated source tables. |
| [Supabase Row Level Security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)                                                                                                                                                           | Exposed tables require RLS; policies act as row filters, service roles may bypass RLS, views are security-definer by default unless made security-invoker, and policy columns should be indexed.                                                                         | RLS is defense in depth, not a replacement for composite Tenant/Legal Entity foreign keys, explicit grants, server-command authorization, and anonymous projection isolation.                             |
| [USWDS radio guidance](https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/radio-buttons/) and [GOV.UK Check answers](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/check-answers/)                                                                                    | Radio groups suit one mutually exclusive choice and should use clear vertical labels; a final check-answers summary reduces errors and should name the effect of the submit action.                                                                                      | Staff should choose one plain-language subject kind, then one exact eligible record, and review the consequences before starting the private Page.                                                        |

Microsoft has announced that its separate Fundraising and Engagement product is
being retired at the end of 2026. The evidence above therefore relies on the
open Common Data Model's semantic separation and uses the retiring product only
as a concrete illustration; Asym must not treat that product as a longevity or
integration dependency.

### 41.3 Designation fallback verdict

**Synthesis:** the Designation fallback is safe only as an explicitly named
**Fund or designated purpose** subject. It is not safe as a generic
`operational_project` substitute.

The fallback should be admitted only when all of the following are true:

1. Phase 13 owns the exact Designation and marks it eligible to serve as a
   public Page subject through a deliberate, auditable action. Ordinary Giving
   eligibility alone is insufficient.
2. The exact Tenant and Legal Entity match the Page. Site selection remains a
   Phase 22 Page concern and cannot change financial ownership.
3. Phase 10 supplies an eligible public-facing purpose label or alias. Internal
   fund names, worker legal names, GL codes, accounting descriptions, and
   restrictions never become public copy or slugs automatically.
4. Staff knowingly select **Fund or designated purpose** in the Page setup.
   Asym never reclassifies every active Designation as a Project Page candidate
   and never labels the source itself as an operational project.
5. The Page Subject Binding and D7 Page Giving Binding remain separate facts.
   They may intentionally reference the same Designation, but neither defaults,
   infers, or mutates the other.
6. Designation inactivation, succession, or closure opens its exact D8
   cause-owned Page lifecycle case and independently affects D7 Giving
   eligibility. It does not silently remove, retitle, redirect, repurpose, or
   rebind the Page.
7. A Designation that aggregates several unrelated purposes or whose public
   purpose cannot be proven stays unavailable as a subject. Missing eligibility
   never becomes a generic `Project` or a public general-fund page.

This bounded arm gives smaller missions organizations a truthful path when the
fund/purpose record genuinely is all they operate, without forcing them to
manufacture a campaign or project. It does not let a financial record absorb
project, content, lifecycle, permission, progress, or publication authority.

### 41.4 Recommended permanent subject contract

**Synthesis:** harden C-prime into one closed Page Subject Binding with exactly
one of these kinds for a Project/Campaign Page:

1. **Ongoing ministry or project** — one exact organization-controlled Ministry
   Project source record.
2. **Fundraising campaign** — one exact Phase 13 Giving Campaign.
3. **Fund or designated purpose** — one exact, separately public-subject-
   eligible Phase 13 Designation under the constraints in §41.3.

The repository currently has no owner for kind 1. The permanent solution is a
minimal **CRM-owned Ministry Project identity and lifecycle contract** in the
operational ownership layer, not continued inference and not a new Phase 22
content record. It contains only what is necessary to identify and govern the
organization-controlled work: stable opaque identity; Tenant and Legal Entity;
source-owned type and lifecycle; internal label; optional dates; exact external
source references where applicable; immutable version; retirement/successor
meaning; and audit provenance. It is not a project-management suite, CMS
document, Designation, fundraising Campaign, accounting Project, task board,
budget, progress counter, or workflow engine. Phase 22 references the exact
source version through its Page Subject Binding. Presentation copy remains in
D1/D3; public identity remains Phase 10; money and goals remain in their owning
phases.

If that minimal owner does not ship, **Ongoing ministry or project must remain
unavailable**, and Asym must say why. It cannot synthesize an operational
project from a Payload document, `fundId`, title, location, tag, accounting
Project, or campaign description.

The binding itself should have these invariants:

- one immutable Page identity and one closed Page Family;
- one immutable subject-kind value and one exact source identity per binding
  version;
- exact Tenant, Legal Entity, Page, source version/generation, lifecycle
  evidence, actor, reason, and time coverage;
- structurally enforced exactly-one source reference, using direct composite
  foreign keys (or kind-specific subtype tables) rather than an unenforced
  polymorphic ID;
- no source-derived contributor assignment, display participation, reach,
  release authority, Giving destination, progress definition, media, update
  audience, measurement access, or notification audience;
- every D2 Page Release Manifest pins the exact binding version and a
  privacy-safe source snapshot/digest needed to explain historical releases;
  live rendering does not join anonymous traffic to the raw source table;
- a staff correction before the first release creates an audited successor
  binding and invalidates stale previews rather than overwriting history; and
- after the first public release, a different subject requires a new Page
  identity plus D8's explicit lifecycle/successor treatment. An in-place subject
  swap would make URLs, releases, search history, measurement, updates,
  attribution, and donor expectations tell a false story.

Source status and Page disposition remain distinct. A completed Ministry
Project, closed Campaign, or inactive Designated Purpose produces a typed
cause-owned input to D8. It does not automatically publish, unpublish, redirect,
archive, change Giving, change progress, or select a successor.

### 41.5 One clear setup experience

**Synthesis:** users should encounter the domain distinction as three ordinary
answers to one question, not as database terminology.

The staff flow is:

1. **What is this page about?** Show a vertical native radio group:
   - **Ongoing ministry or project** — work your organization carries out;
   - **Fundraising campaign** — a specific fundraising effort; or
   - **Fund or designated purpose** — a fund or purpose supporters may give
     toward.
2. **Choose the exact record.** Search only eligible records of the selected
   kind and current Tenant/Legal Entity. Each result shows a plain label, kind,
   source status, responsible team when authorized, date coverage where
   meaningful, and whether a Page already references it. Raw IDs, GL codes, and
   restricted facts remain hidden.
3. **Check the Page setup.** Show one compact summary with separate rows:
   - `This Page is about`;
   - `Gifts go to`;
   - `Progress shown`;
   - `Who can edit`;
   - `Public reach`; and
   - `Review before publishing` or `Publish after checks`.
     Every independently unavailable item says what remains to be completed; it
     never appears as zero, inherited, or silently defaulted.
4. **Start private Page** creates or advances only the private D1 setup/draft
   path. Selection never publishes, creates a public route, enables Giving, or
   implies that the source itself is public.

Capability-aware progressive disclosure keeps the flow quiet: a tenant without
a Ministry Project source does not receive an empty selector; it sees the two
supported choices plus a short explanation only when relevant. The system does
not expose a tenant-authored subject-type matrix or ask ordinary staff to learn
`DeliveryFramework`, `GiftDesignation`, foreign-key, or polymorphism language.

Contributors see assigned Pages under one dashboard-native **Public pages**
workspace. They may edit authorized presentation fields but cannot change the
subject. Donors see the approved title and content only; internal subject kind,
IDs, record status, and financial configuration are not public metadata.

### 41.6 Migration, export, and portability

**Synthesis:** portability requires typed identity and history, not a CSV that
exports only the current Page title.

- A complete custody export includes stable Page identity, Page Family,
  subject kind, stable source identity, Tenant/Legal Entity/Site scope, external
  source keys where present, binding versions, lifecycle facts, privacy-safe
  historical source snapshots/digests, D7 Giving Bindings as separate records,
  and explicit retired/tombstoned dispositions. Private operational source
  fields are exported only through their owning permissioned package.
- Import uses private staging and an exact typed mapping manifest. Source kind,
  Tenant, Legal Entity, source ID/external key, and current source eligibility
  must all resolve; names and titles are display/help only and never matching
  authority.
- Existing `project-pages.fundId` rows are candidates for the **Fund or
  designated purpose** arm only after exact Phase 13 and Phase 10 proof. They
  are never automatically promoted to Ministry Project or Giving Campaign.
- A legacy record with a missing, duplicated, cross-tenant, inactive, or
  ambiguous source is quarantined with a cause-owned resolution. Missing source
  never becomes a newly fabricated project, a General Fund default, or a
  published Page.
- Reconciliation accounts for every legacy Page and source reference exactly
  once as adopted, transformed, quarantined, retained as inert evidence, or
  retired. Cutover is one source-authority switch; no dual read/write remains.
- Connectors must preserve inactive/tombstoned source identity because vendor
  APIs may not report deletions. Absence from a poll is never a lifecycle fact.

### 41.7 Principal adversarial findings

| Hazard                        | What could go wrong                                                                                                                      | Severity / likelihood  | Permanent prevention                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Meaning collapse              | `fundId`, Campaign, and Project are treated as synonyms, so the page, progress, and gift destination drift together.                     | Critical / High        | Closed kinds, named owners, exact binding, and independent D6/D7 facts.                                                                             |
| Fictional operational project | A CMS title or fund record is presented as real operational work with no owner or lifecycle.                                             | Critical / High        | Minimal Ministry Project source authority or disable that arm. Never infer.                                                                         |
| Designation overreach         | Every active fund becomes a public-page candidate or an internal name leaks publicly.                                                    | Critical / High        | Separate public-subject eligibility, Phase 10 public alias, exact staff selection, no bulk default.                                                 |
| Polymorphic orphan            | Generic `type + id` survives after a source is deleted, changes scope, or points across tenants.                                         | Critical / Medium-high | Closed discriminator plus direct composite FKs or typed subtype tables; source retirement, not destructive deletion.                                |
| Lifecycle coupling            | Closing a Campaign or Designation automatically retires the Page or reroutes gifts.                                                      | Critical / High        | Typed source event opens D8 case; D7 and D2 remain independently authoritative.                                                                     |
| Identity swap                 | Staff repoint a released Page to a new subject while retaining its URL and history.                                                      | Critical / Medium      | New Page identity after first release; explicit D8 successor presentation; no in-place swap.                                                        |
| Duplicate and race creation   | Two staff members create competing Pages for the same source and Site.                                                                   | High / Medium          | Idempotent server command, locked exact-source lookup, explicit current-Page policy, and conflict recovery; do not rely on a preflight query alone. |
| Permission inference          | A project lead, campaign owner, fund manager, contributor, or displayed person gains Page or financial access from the subject relation. | Critical / High        | D1/Phase 12 assignments and capabilities only; source relation grants nothing.                                                                      |
| Migration misclassification   | Legacy fund-backed pages are silently labelled Campaigns or Projects by fuzzy name matching.                                             | Critical / High        | Typed mapping manifest, exact IDs/external keys, private review, quarantine, full reconciliation.                                                   |
| Export lock-in                | Exports omit source kind, stable IDs, binding history, or tombstones, so another system cannot reconstruct meaning.                      | High / Medium          | Versioned machine-readable custody package plus safe human-readable summary.                                                                        |
| RLS/API leak                  | Anonymous clients or service-role code read raw project, campaign, or designation tables.                                                | Critical / Medium-high | Anonymous projection choke point, explicit grants, indexed RLS, composite scope, server-derived actor, negative tests.                              |
| UX category error             | Staff cannot distinguish `about` from `gifts go to`, select the wrong record, or believe Start means Publish.                            | High / High            | Plain-language kind choice, eligible-record search, check-answers summary, precise `Start private Page` action.                                     |
| Over-engineering              | A universal tenant-defined polymorphic subject framework becomes a mini workflow/ontology engine.                                        | High / Medium-high     | Exactly three code-owned kinds, capability-aware choices, no custom kinds or arbitrary relation DSL.                                                |

### 41.8 Required production proof

- Every enabled subject kind has a real owner, stable identity, source status,
  exact Tenant/Legal Entity scope, lifecycle/tombstone semantics, export shape,
  and production-shaped test fixture.
- Database tests reject zero-source, multi-source, discriminator mismatch,
  nonexistent, cross-Tenant, cross-Legal-Entity, and destructively deleted
  references even when application checks or RLS are bypassed.
- Authorization tests prove that subject, campaign ownership, fund management,
  Display Participant, relationship, contributor, and D7 Designation references
  grant no capability beyond an explicit current Phase 12/D1 assignment.
- Lifecycle tests independently exercise active, paused, completed, closed,
  inactive, retired, missing, restored, and successor source outcomes against
  D2 reach, D6 progress, D7 Giving, D8 disposition, D13 discovery, and D14
  search/share without co-moving them implicitly.
- Concurrency tests cover duplicate creation, stale subject selection, source
  status changing during setup/release, pre-release correction, post-release
  swap refusal, retry, and partial failure.
- UX and accessibility proof covers keyboard and screen-reader radio/search/
  summary flow, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% zoom, forced colors, status/error
  announcements, no color-only distinction, understandable terms, and test
  sessions with tenant staff who use project records, campaigns, and funds in
  materially different ways.
- Migration tests classify every current fund-backed Page and mock Project;
  exact source mapping and totals reconcile; unsafe names/slugs/content stay
  private; ambiguous rows cannot release; and rollback never revives a legacy
  public Page or dual source authority.
- Export/import round trips preserve exact subject kind, stable IDs, binding
  and lifecycle history, D7 separation, tombstones, Unicode, locale, and scope
  without relying on names, row order, or undocumented vendor fields.

### 41.9 Research synthesis

The selected direction survives adversarial review only after two important
clarifications. First, **Ongoing ministry or project** needs a minimal canonical
operational source; the repository has none today, and a fund or CMS page may
not impersonate one. Second, the Designation arm is a deliberately selected
**Fund or designated purpose** compatibility path with separate public-subject
eligibility, never a silent Project alias.

The resulting model gives each tenant practical flexibility without creating a
custom ontology: staff answer one understandable question, choose one exact
eligible record, and see a final consequence summary. The immutable typed
binding says what the Page is about. D7 independently says where gifts go. D6
independently says what progress means. D1/Phase 12 independently say who may
edit or release. Source lifecycle independently supplies a cause for D8. That
separation is the permanent fix for the current `fundId` shortcut and is what
makes migration, export, security, and future integrations reliable.

### 41.10 Ratified decision

The founder ratified the following exact formulation as Phase 22 D17 on
2026-08-06:

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — for every Project/Campaign Page, one immutable-versioned, exact Page Subject Binding to exactly one code-owned and owner-certified subject kind: one canonical CRM-owned Ministry Project, one Phase 13 Giving Campaign, or one separately public-subject-eligible Phase 13 Designation presented as “Fund or designated purpose”; with the missing minimal CRM Ministry Project identity and lifecycle contract established in the operational ownership layer and every subject kind unavailable until production-certified; exact Tenant, Legal Entity, environment, Site, Page Family, source identity, source version, lifecycle, actor, reason, and effective-time scope; structurally enforced kind-matched composite foreign keys, deletion restriction, duplicate prevention, release-time source and Phase 10 reproof, and a privacy-safe subject snapshot pinned into every immutable release. Page subject, D7 Page Giving Binding, D6 progress, D1 contributor and display participation, D2 reach and release, D8 route/lifecycle disposition, D9 media, D11 Ministry Updates, D13 discovery, and D14 search/share remain independently authoritative. A pre-first-release correction creates a CAS-guarded successor binding; after the first public release, a different subject requires a new Page identity and explicit D8 succession. Staff receive one quiet, accessible “What is this page about?” setup followed by exact eligible-record search and a plain-language consequence review; missionaries receive a read-only “About this page” summary; donors see only approved public presentation—without a generic `subject_type + subject_id`, arbitrary CRM custom objects, inferred operational projects, fund-as-project relabeling, inferred permissions, inferred Giving or progress, copied operational identity, raw public source access, mutable released subjects, destructive deletion, fuzzy migration, silent substitution, dual authority, or exposed internal identifiers.**

Normative detail is recorded in the
[Phase 22 decision log](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d17--what-exact-subject-may-a-projectcampaign-page-represent)
and
[ADR-0134](../../adr/0134-exact-typed-public-page-subject-bindings.md).

## 42. Ratified D19 research — organization-owned Ministry Assignments and separated support access

**Research and ratification date:** 2026-08-06

**Status:** Complete for the Phase 22 product decision. Runtime behavior remains
subject to the production proof below.

### 42.1 Problem and user outcome

A Missionary Ministry Page often represents more than one person. A husband and
wife may use separate logins while sharing one ministry and one support context;
a project team may have several contributors; a leader or coach may help without
appearing publicly or seeing supporter details. A person-owned Page, household-
owned fund, shared login, or relationship-derived permission cannot express
those ordinary combinations safely.

The desired experience is nevertheless simple: staff choose a person, select
the few applicable consequences, review them in plain language, and save once.
The implementation must preserve the fact that association, public appearance,
page editing, financial access, responsibility, and notifications have different
owners and may be revoked independently.

### 42.2 Repository findings

- Phase 22 D1 already separates Page Subject Binding, Display Participant, and
  Public Page Contributor Assignment and prohibits spouse, team, Support
  Assignment, and subject relationships from inferring page access.
- Phase 21 D19 and ADR-0108 already establish the finance-side pattern: one
  organization-controlled Support Assignment may have multiple Participant
  Memberships, but only Phase 12's request-time PDP grants Support Workspace
  access. Participation never changes balance arithmetic.
- Phase 12 already owns the required exact purpose-, projection-, target-,
  field-, history-floor-, and governance-epoch authorization. Phase 22 must call
  that owner rather than create a page-local ACL or relationship graph.
- Current runtime code is still prototype-shaped: the missionary portal selects
  one person record and donation activity by `missionary_id`, while shared
  operation helpers may use an administrative Supabase client. Those paths are
  migration evidence, not proof of D19 authorization or team support.
- The repository already distinguishes Phase 12 Active Tenant Assignment,
  Phase 21 Support Assignment, D1 contributor assignments, and several other
  assignment concepts. The fully qualified **Ministry Assignment** name is
  therefore required; a bare `assignment_id` would be ambiguous and hazardous.

### 42.3 Primary-source platform findings

| Source                                                                                                                                                                                             | Current documented fact                                                                                                                                                                      | Binding D19 consequence                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Supabase Row Level Security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)                                                                                               | `user_metadata` is user-modifiable, authorization claims can remain stale until JWT refresh, policy columns should be indexed, and service keys can bypass RLS.                              | Do not place participant/grant lists in JWTs or treat service credentials as user authority. Resolve current exact access server-side and prove indexed containment.                      |
| [Supabase API security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api)                                                                                                                    | Data API exposure requires deliberate privileges plus RLS; private schemas are appropriate for server-only objects.                                                                          | Keep raw Ministry Assignment, membership, binding, grant, supporter, activity, and balance relations browser-inaccessible and assert grants in tests.                                     |
| [Supabase Data API grant change](https://supabase.com/changelog/45329-breaking-change-tables-not-exposed-to-data-and-graphql-api-automatically)                                                    | Supabase is moving new tables to explicit Data API grants, with the documented existing-project rollout on October 30, 2026.                                                                 | Treat absent browser grants as a positive, catalog-tested invariant rather than relying on a historical default.                                                                          |
| [PostgreSQL row security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html)                                                                                                            | Permissive policies combine with `OR`; owners and `BYPASSRLS` normally bypass policies; referential-integrity checks bypass row security; `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` changes owner behavior. | Do not accumulate fine-grained relationship policies. Use forced coarse containment, structural same-scope constraints, non-enumerating errors, and the Phase 12 PDP on privileged paths. |
| [PostgreSQL `CREATE VIEW`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createview.html)                                                                                                            | A `security_invoker` view applies underlying privileges and RLS as the caller instead of the view owner.                                                                                     | Any unavoidable exposed view must be invoker-secured and still return only a bounded projection; otherwise keep it unexposed.                                                             |
| [PostgreSQL `CREATE FUNCTION`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createfunction.html)                                                                                                    | `SECURITY DEFINER` functions run with owner authority and require a safe `search_path` and controlled execute privileges.                                                                    | Keep any unavoidable definer function private, schema-qualified, narrowly granted, and free of generic financial lookup behavior; revoke `PUBLIC EXECUTE`.                                |
| [Supabase Auth sessions](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions) and [sign-out](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signout)                                                             | Issued access tokens may remain valid until expiry even after refresh-token or session changes.                                                                                              | Deny-first sensitive-data revocation must recheck the current grant and governance epoch; logout or JWT expiry is not the security control.                                               |
| [Supabase Realtime database changes](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/subscribing-to-database-changes) and [Postgres Changes](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime/postgres-changes) | Private Broadcast can authorize messages; Postgres Changes authorizes subscribers, has scale/ordering constraints, and cannot serve as a complete deletion or revocation protocol.           | Send only an opaque resource/version signal and perform a fresh authorized server read. Never stream raw financial rows or use Realtime as balance authority.                             |
| [Supabase pgTAP](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/local-development/testing/pgtap-extended)                                                                                                        | Privileges, policies, and database behavior can be checked in database-native tests.                                                                                                         | Ship only with catalog and hostile-principal tests for grants, RLS, views, functions, constraints, and bypass paths.                                                                      |
| [PostgreSQL multicolumn indexes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-multicolumn.html)                                                                                                 | Composite B-tree indexes are most useful when leading constrained columns match the lookup shape.                                                                                            | Index and load-test exact Tenant → Legal Entity → Assignment → participant/grant paths instead of accepting recursive per-row authorization.                                              |

### 42.4 Comparable product patterns

- MPDX documents both multiple ministry accounts and coach access, demonstrating
  the real need for one person to work across several ministry contexts and for
  leadership to see a deliberately bounded view. Its broad shared-account
  affordances are useful workflow evidence, not a safe authorization model for
  Asym's field-specific supporter and balance privacy.
- Microsoft Dataverse distinguishes owner teams from access teams. The useful
  pattern is explicit record-scoped collaboration rather than granting access
  merely because people are related; Asym keeps Phase 12 as the sole
  authorization owner instead of importing Dataverse's team ACL model.
- Modern collaboration products consistently use named invitations and
  individual accounts instead of shared credentials, display the exact scope
  before access is granted, and make removal independently reversible. D19
  applies that familiar interaction while retaining finance-specific proof.

Sources: [MPDX ministry accounts](https://help.mpdx.org/article/633-adding-and-managing-ministry-accounts-all-other-orgs),
[MPDX coaching](https://help.mpdx.org/article/510-for-mpd-coaches), and
[Dataverse access teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-access-teams-owner-teams-collaborate-share-information).

### 42.5 Options evaluated

#### A — Person- or household-owned Page and support context

This looks simple for one person or one couple but fails when the household
changes, a teammate joins, one person serves multiple ministries, a project has
no current participant, or the same people need different permissions. It also
turns a relationship into financial authority. Rejected.

#### B — Generic team/relationship graph that inherits all access

This can represent many shapes but becomes an ACL/ReBAC engine inside Phase 22,
duplicates Phase 12, makes revocation difficult to predict, and encourages raw
graph traversal in RLS. Rejected.

#### C-prime-R — Organization-owned Ministry Assignment plus explicit bindings

One stable CRM Ministry Assignment represents the ministry. Separate membership,
display, contributor, support, responsibility, and notification facts can be
created through one calm workflow, but only their owners authorize them. An
optional typed binding written only by Phase 21 through a separately finance-
authorized command composes the Ministry Assignment with support context
without copying finance or granting access. Phase 22 only consumes it. Accepted.

### 42.6 Exact data and authorization contract

- Ministry Assignment identity and lifecycle are immutable/versioned, owned by
  CRM, and scoped to one Tenant and Legal Entity.
- Party Participant Memberships are prospective, effective-dated, append-only
  corrected, and non-overlapping. They record association only.
- Each Missionary Ministry Page references one exact Ministry Assignment through
  D1's source-qualified Page Subject Binding; Project/Campaign Pages retain
  D17's three different typed subject arms.
- A Ministry Assignment is the people/service/optional-Support-Workspace
  context for a Missionary Page. A Ministry Project is D17's initiative/program
  subject for a Project/Campaign Page. D19 adds no fourth D17 arm and never
  auto-links the two.
- A Ministry Assignment has zero or one current Support Binding Version, and a
  Support Assignment has zero or one current Ministry Assignment binding, for
  the same Tenant and Legal Entity and one exact non-overlapping interval. Phase
  21 owns the separately finance-authorized binding command; Page and
  contributor authority cannot select or mutate it.
- The binding does not select the D7 Designation, D6 public progress, a Field
  Account currency, participants, access grants, notifications, or a combined
  balance. Every currency remains independently labelled and authoritative.
- D1 Display Participants and Contributor Assignments, Phase 21 Participant
  Membership, Phase 12 Support Workspace authorization, responsibilities,
  history floors, and notification preferences remain separately versioned and
  attributable to their actual actor and cause.
- All browser-facing data passes a server-owned exact-resource lookup and the
  Phase 12 PDP before enumeration. An unauthorized or stale reference fails
  uniformly and does not reveal whether a protected assignment or field exists.
- Before first public release, a Missionary Page subject correction appends a
  CAS-guarded binding successor. After first release, a different Ministry
  Assignment requires a new Page identity and D8 succession. Retirement
  preserves released history and never silently repoints the Page.

### 42.7 Quiet UX contract

The ordinary staff flow uses one **People & access** drawer or page:

1. Select or invite one identified person.
2. See only choices applicable to this tenant and ministry: **Associated with
   this ministry**, **Shown on the public page**, **Can edit this page**, **Can
   use the Support Workspace**, and **Gets updates**. Its consequence detail
   names the exact D9-enabled modules, fields, and history; activity and balance
   visibility remain independently selectable and may be absent.
3. Use a tenant-safe preset if desired, then adjust explicit choices. Presets
   never hide unavailable fields or imply authority. The minimum-safe support
   preset excludes supporter identity, contact details, evidence, and other
   sensitive fields unless each is separately field-authorized.
4. Review a short natural-language consequence summary naming the Page,
   ministry, support context and fields/history where applicable, effective
   date, invitation, and notifications.
5. Confirm once. The result separates successful local facts, pending delivery,
   and any cause-owned exception, and states **No balance moves. No closed
   history changes.**

The missionary dashboard shows only Pages and support modules currently
authorized for that principal. A spouse or teammate switches among named
ministries and separately ISO-labelled balances without seeing access matrices,
other people's permissions, unavailable controls, or an authoritative converted
grand total. Association or page-edit access can exist without support data,
and support access can exist without public appearance. Missing binding,
disabled Phase 21, D9 module Off, or balance Off renders no support/balance card
or placeholder. Temporary unavailability appears only for an authorized viewer
when D9 selected that exact module and its owning projection reports an outage.

### 42.8 Principal adversarial findings

| Hazard                         | What could go wrong                                                                                                     | Severity / likelihood  | Permanent prevention                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Relationship becomes authority | Marriage, household, assignment membership, display, or editing silently reveals supporter identity or balances.        | Critical / High        | Sole Phase 12 PDP, explicit grants, invariant tests, and consequence-separated UI.                                       |
| Scope omission                 | A binding or request crosses Tenant, Legal Entity, ministry, support assignment, purpose, field, or currency.           | Critical / Medium-high | Repeated composite keys, structural FKs, server-derived target, exact projection grant, and hostile tests.               |
| Stale authorization            | Old JWTs, open sessions, cached pages, deep links, jobs, or Realtime connections outlive revocation.                    | Critical / High        | Live governance epoch/history floor checks, deny-first invalidation, no raw subscriptions, and authorized refetch.       |
| Partial orchestration          | Association saves while invitation, grant, or notification fails and the UI claims everything succeeded.                | High / High            | Atomic local rows plus outbox, independently labelled outcomes, bounded retry, and one residual action.                  |
| Rebinding propagation          | A new Support Assignment inherits old people, grants, balances, notifications, or history.                              | Critical / Medium      | Immutable prospective binding successor, no propagation, explicit retain/end/re-authorize decisions, and contract tests. |
| RLS false confidence           | Table-owner/service paths bypass RLS, permissive policies widen access, or views/definer functions expose owner rights. | Critical / Medium-high | Forced coarse RLS, explicit grants, security-invoker/unexposed views, safe private functions, and bypass-path tests.     |
| Policy-query collapse          | Fine-grained relationship joins in RLS or subscriber authorization become too slow at production size.                  | High / Medium-high     | Coarse indexed RLS, compiled server decisions, bounded pagination, signal-only Realtime, and plan/load proof.            |
| Ambiguous UX                   | Staff cannot predict which checkbox changes page, finance, or notifications and remove too much or too little.          | High / High            | Applicable plain-language choices, safe presets, literal review, independent revoke controls, and comprehension testing. |
| Legacy inference               | `missionary_id`, a shared URL, household, email, or prior portal visibility is treated as a grant.                      | Critical / High        | Private exact mapping manifest, quarantine, one disposition per row, reconciliation, and one-authority cutover.          |

### 42.9 Required production proof

- Composite keys reject cross-Tenant and cross-Legal-Entity Ministry
  participants, Page subjects, Support Bindings, invitations, and grant targets.
- Exclusion/uniqueness tests reject duplicate and overlapping memberships and
  concurrent current bindings under real transaction races.
- An associated, displayed, or contributing person with no support grant cannot
  enumerate or read support activity, balances, Field Accounts, supporter
  identity, or the existence of a protected target.
- A separately authorized spouse or teammate can use their own principal to
  read exactly the allowed fields and history for the exact bound Support
  Assignment; currencies remain separate and through-dated.
- Page access does not imply finance; finance does not imply display, editing,
  review, release, notification, Giving, progress, or money movement.
- Cross-Tenant, cross-Legal-Entity, cross-Ministry-Assignment,
  cross-Support-Assignment, cross-purpose, cross-field, and cross-currency
  hostile requests fail uniformly.
- Old JWTs, cached navigation, open Realtime, queued notifications, stale deep
  links, and in-flight paginated requests all fail after deny-first revocation.
- Catalog/pgTAP checks prove forced RLS, absent raw browser grants,
  security-invoker exposed views, safe owners/search paths, absent `PUBLIC
EXECUTE`, and application-PDP use on service/bypass paths.
- Production-cardinality query plans prove bounded indexed assignment,
  membership, binding, and grant resolution without per-row recursive policy or
  raw Realtime fan-out.
- Concurrent add, end, rebind, revoke, invite, retry, Party merge/split,
  retirement, and worker-crash cases prove idempotency, monotonic revocation,
  immutable history, and residual-only recovery.
- Keyboard, screen-reader, focus, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% zoom, target-size,
  forced-color, mobile invitation/recovery, and plain-language comprehension
  tests pass for singles, couples, teams, coaches, and finance staff.
- Migration reconciles every legacy person, Page, collaborator, portal access,
  and support/fund reference to one explicit disposition. Names, emails,
  relationships, shared URLs, and previous visibility create no inferred fact.

Documentation does not prove the deployed project's grants, RLS owner behavior,
Auth-token lifetime, Realtime connection handling, query plans, or production
isolation. Those remain mandatory activation evidence rather than staff setup
or tenant certification work.

### 42.10 Ratified decision

The founder ratified the following exact formulation as Phase 22 D19 on
2026-08-06:

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — one stable,
> CRM-authoritative, organization-owned, Tenant- and Legal-Entity-scoped
> Ministry Assignment with immutable identity and versioned lifecycle as the
> exact operational subject referenced—not copied—by each Missionary Ministry
> Page; zero-to-many prospective, effective-dated, append-only-corrected Party
> Participant Memberships; and one optional, prospective, immutable,
> same-scope, one-to-one Ministry Assignment Support Binding Version to Phase
> 21’s independently authoritative Support Assignment. Every spouse, teammate,
> leader, coach, staff member, and contributor retains a separate Party,
> principal, login, invitation, Ministry Assignment membership, Phase 21
> Support Assignment Participant Membership, D1 Display Participant and Public
> Page Contributor Assignment, Phase 12 Support Workspace authorization,
> responsibility, history floor, and notification-preference identity. One

> the explicitly selected local facts and outbox intent through bounded safe
> presets and one literal consequence review, allowing multiple separately

> Designation, D6 public progress, notification preference, or the Support
> Binding itself grants no financial access, reveals no supporter identity,

and
[ADR-0136](../../adr/0136-organization-owned-ministry-assignments-and-separated-support-access.md).

## 43. Ratified D20 research — two small code-owned Page Family Semantic Catalogs under D3

**Research date:** 2026-08-13

**Status:** Founder-ratified supporting evidence. The founder ratified the exact
C-prime-R formulation as Phase 22 D20 on 2026-08-13. Runtime behavior remains
unimplemented and must satisfy the production proof recorded below.

### 43.1 Question and constraint

The question is not whether Payload can expose a flexible block builder. It can.
The question is which small, family-qualified semantic sections Asym should ship
for Missionary Ministry and Project/Campaign Pages, and how a tenant can choose a
useful experience without allowing page structure, operational truth, public
safety, or Giving authority to drift.

D3 already settled the architecture: two non-interchangeable family-certified
profiles, immutable profile/catalog/renderer generations, bounded optional
sections, explicit source/edit authority, exact release pins, and no generic
cross-family template. D20 fills the launch catalogs and authoring interaction;
it cannot become another profile resolver, permission system, release workflow,
or source owner.

### 43.2 Current first-party product and standards evidence

All sources were accessed on 2026-08-13. Product dates are included where their
first-party page displayed one.

| Source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Current evidence and D20 implication                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Payload, [Blocks Field](https://payloadcms.com/docs/fields/blocks)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Code supplies the exact eligible block schemas. Payload supports server validation, `minRows`/`maxRows`, field access, localization, conditional eligibility, labels, disabling sorting, and custom editor presentation. Its generic copy/paste persists through browser local storage and can move compatible blocks between documents, so Asym must not expose generic block authority to contributors.       |
| Payload, [Fields Overview](https://payloadcms.com/docs/fields/overview) and [Access Control](https://payloadcms.com/docs/access-control/overview)                                                                                                                                                                                       | Schema fields can drive a deliberate form with validation, descriptions, conditional UI, hooks, and access. UI hiding or a `readOnly` presentation remains insufficient as Asym product authorization; actor- and page-scoped command enforcement is still required.                                                                                                                                            |
| WordPress, [Content-only editing](https://developer.wordpress.org/news/2024/11/how-to-add-content-only-editing-support-to-a-block/) (November 2024) and [Block Locking](https://developer.wordpress.org/block-editor/how-to-guides/curating-the-editor-experience/block-locking/)                                                       | `templateLock: contentOnly` hides layout children and settings while leaving marked content editable. This is direct evidence for content-only contributor authoring, not proof that editor locks are an authorization boundary.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Shopify, [JSON templates](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/templates/json-templates), [Section schema](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/sections/section-schema), and [Blocks](https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture/blocks)                                         | Code-defined template schemas constrain eligible sections, order, presets, static blocks, and limits. Shopify's platform maximums of 25 sections and 50 blocks are ceilings, not appropriate Asym defaults; D20 should remain far smaller and family-specific. Shopify also documents that reducing limits or changing eligibility can invalidate existing content, supporting immutable successor generations. |

Existing entries are not automatically revalidated until republished, and required/hidden field combinations can strand publishing, supporting prospective catalog migrations rather than in-place reinterpretation.                            |
| Raisely, [Understanding Fundraiser Profiles](https://support.raisely.com/hc/en-us/articles/44649205175565-Understanding-Fundraiser-Profiles) (March 27, 2026)                                                                                                                                                                           | Fundraising profiles combine contributor data with a single campaign-designed dynamic page, and types are configured separately. Contributors personalize a bounded profile rather than own the organization's page schema.                                                                                                                                                                                     |

Updates are a separate supporter feed with an independent email choice, supporting D11's non-copied update model. Givebutter's broader story editor also shows why arbitrary video/links/HTML create a larger safety and accessibility burden than D20 needs.    |

The pattern supports task-language contributor groups; its arbitrary media/link affordances and mutable fundraiser goal are not adopted where D6/D7/D9 own those facts.                                                                                                                                                         |
| Neon One, [Create a peer-to-peer fundraising page](https://support.neonone.com/hc/en-us/articles/5054296297357-How-to-create-a-peer-to-peer-fundraising-page) (updated May 12, 2025)                                                                                                                                                    | A narrow title/URL/goal/hero/story flow plus preview is easier for fundraisers than a full CMS. D20 adopts the focused workflow but keeps route, goal, and media truth in their owning Asym domains.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

The combined evidence favors **structured flexibility**: code owns the content
model and safe templates; tenants choose bounded optionality, edit ownership,
and certified arrangement; contributors edit task-named content rather than
layout primitives; source-owned facts remain read-only references.

### 43.3 Current repository evidence

The live checkout disproves any assumption that D20 is only a greenfield schema
choice:

- `apps/admin/src/cms/collections/page-builders.ts` defines one freely sortable
  seven-block catalog—`hero`, `rich-text`, `media-feature`, CTA, FAQ,
  `impact-stats`, and `testimonial`—for both page families. Hero and CTA contain
  author-entered href fields; arrays have no D20 family semantics; the `layout`
  field has no explicit family cardinality or zone contract.
- `missionary-giving-pages.ts` and `project-pages.ts` both call the same
  `buildPageBuilderCollectionFields`. The current `missionaryId` and `fundId` are
  text references with Payload Admin `readOnly` presentation, not D17/D19 typed
  subject authority. The optional `MissionaryProfile` copies identity-like
  fields into another CMS record.
- Page templates copy mutable `defaultLayout` block blobs into pages. The create
  UI requires a template and retrieves a bounded flat list of sources rather than
  a scalable scoped search. Native edit views still embed Payload's generic
  document form; there is no D1 page-scoped missionary dashboard editor.
- `apps/admin/src/cms/public/serialize-published-page.ts` and the package public
  serializer duplicate the same block switch. Unknown blocks can degrade to a
  base record or disappear rather than block a new release. Public media
  serialization still exposes a filename, which D9 explicitly replaces with
  opaque public asset treatment.
- Authenticated preview and public serving use different rendering paths. The
  donor `/workers/[id]` route remains mock-backed with hard-coded story, updates,
  progress, and Give UI, while no corresponding Project route exists.
- Payload's generated Postgres migrations materialize physical block and version
  tables for both families. Existing templates, seeds, fixtures, pages, and tests
  assert the legacy seven-block model, so renaming blocks is a real data migration
  and cannot safely become semantic adoption by assertion.

The existing system is useful migration evidence, not D20 authority. It needs an
additive family catalog and release compiler boundary, explicit legacy
dispositions, one preview/public renderer, and page-scoped contributor commands.

### 43.4 Recommended launch catalog boundary

The candidate catalogs are intentionally shallow and small:

- **Missionary Ministry:** managed public identity/hero; optional Introduction,
  Ministry story, Ministry focus, and Prayer focus; managed D9 media; optional
  managed D6 Support progress; required D7 Give; optional exact D11 Ministry
  Updates feed; locked organization stewardship/disclosure/help.
- **Project/Campaign:** managed D17 kind-qualified subject identity/hero;
  optional Project summary, The need, What this project will do, and bounded
  prospective Expected impact; managed D9 media; optional managed D6 Project
  progress; required D7 Give; optional D11 Updates feed selected by the exact
  Page-scoped Feed Binding and subject/purpose scope; locked organization
  stewardship/disclosure/help.

Every top-level role is zero-or-one except required managed roles; focus, impact,
and media may contain code-bounded internal lists. Launch explicitly excludes
generic FAQ, testimonial, quotation, logo cloud, arbitrary statistic/counter,
map/exact location, form, carousel, countdown, related-page block, arbitrary
external video/iframe/embed, raw HTML/CSS/JavaScript, free CTA URL, alternate
Designation, manual progress, custom fonts/colors/spacing/responsive rules,
nested layouts, tenant queries/conditions, and copied operational truth.

Tenant flexibility is limited to one immutable D3 profile per exact scope plus a
rare complete same-family profile exception. For each optional editorial role,
staff choose `Off`, `Available`, or `Expected`, and, when applicable, `Staff only`
or `Assigned page contributors`; `Expected` creates private guidance and review
evidence, never filler. Staff can choose a certified visual treatment, bounded
list/media limits, localized safe headings, and permitted order inside named
zones. Contributors cannot activate a tenant-disabled role or move a managed
role. A removed optional section leaves the live release and private revision
history intact.

### 43.5 UX/UI conclusion

**Contributor:** one Public pages dashboard lists every D1-assigned Missionary or
Project Page and its exact Live/Draft/In-review state. Editing uses Basics, Story,
Media, Support & giving, and Updates. It shows only applicable editable fields;
managed values are calm source-labelled cards, not disabled inputs. Desktop may
pair the form with exact responsive preview; mobile is a one-column form with an
explicit preview action. Autosave, offline/conflict recovery, review comments,
errors, focus, and status announcements are accessible. The final verb is exactly
`Submit for review` or `Publish changes` under D4, never generic Payload Publish.

**Staff:** separate Missionary and Project family profile screens begin with the
accessible default. A section row explains Required/Optional, Managed/Editorial,
availability, and who may edit. Bounded move controls work without drag. Exact
preview covers desktop/mobile and populated, empty, source-unavailable,
restricted-worker, RTL, and long-locale states. Activation previews affected
future candidates and says that existing live releases do not change.

**Donor:** family identity, disclosure, and Give placement remain predictable;
empty optional sections collapse; hidden D6 progress is absent rather than zero;
an unavailable source uses its owner-defined state; media and headings remain
semantic, responsive, safe, and accessible.

### 43.6 Adversarial conclusion and proof seams

Every requested category has a concern: brittleness, technical debt, edge cases,
footguns, tenant safety, over-engineering, UX friction, hidden coupling, failure
modes, data integrity, security/privacy, scalability/performance, operational
burden, observability, dependency/integration risk, migration/upgrade risk, and
other development hazards. The exact what/why/severity/likelihood/permanent-
prevention matrix is recorded in the
[D20 decision record](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d20-ruthless-adversarial-review).

The permanent proof boundary is:

1. exhaustive family/role contracts and wrong-family/unknown/duplicate/over-limit
   rejection;
2. exact D1 contributor field allowlists with atomic rejection rather than silent
   discard;
3. Tenant/Legal Entity/Site/Page/Page Family isolation across edit, preview,
   media, release, cache, migration, and public response;
4. CAS collaboration, revocation, offline, and profile-change concurrency proof;
5. D6/D7/D9/D11/D17/D19/Phase 10 managed-source state matrices;
6. one candidate/preview/release/public renderer generation and digest parity;
7. AST, link, media, identifier, scope, size, and preview security fuzzing;
8. ATAG/WCAG authoring and public-output proof, including keyboard, screen reader,
   reflow/zoom, target size, RTL/long locales, alt/decorative decisions, and
   caption/transcript gates;
9. maximum-certified content/media/feed/load budgets and exact D18 cache behavior;
10. a complete legacy disposition and shadow-reconciliation manifest that never
    infers managed truth or mutates a live release; and
11. PII-safe compiler/source/convergence diagnostics and synthetic checks that
    make save, candidate, source, render, and cache failures visible.

## 44. Ratified D21 research — complete Public Ministry surface authority cutover

**Research and ratification date:** 2026-08-14.

**Status:** D21 is ratified, amended, and adversarially hardened. This section
preserves the research basis and production-proof boundary; it authorizes no
implementation, migration, public reader change, tenant activation, or issue
dispatch.

### 44.1 Decision boundary and conclusion

D1–D20 establish the target Public Ministry authority, but the repository still
contains a public `/workers` experience, profile editor, CMS collections,
metadata helpers, preview paths, mocks, fixtures, and cache readers that do not
implement that authority. The unresolved question was therefore not how to
design another Page or migration framework. It was how a tenant can move from
the disagreeing legacy readers to the D1–D20 surface without donors seeing two
identities, two route systems, two progress formulas, or two Giving authorities.
Before cutover, every remaining legacy response must first be forced behind one
Phase 5/Phase 10/D8 safety choke point or made safely unavailable; “old coherent
surface” is a required serving property, not an assumption about today's code.

The evidence supports one rule:

> **Incremental adoption is private preparation. Complete-surface cutover is
> the public authority transition.**

The cutover unit is the smallest dependency-closed Tenant × Legal Entity ×
environment × Site × enumerated verified-host-membership generation × locale
or locale-set cohort. A shared route, directory/search, sitemap, canonical,
alternate-locale, or cache artifact must either have an atomically selectable
versioned shard or bring all of its dependents into the cohort. Every
discoverable tenant source and egress item in that surface must have exactly one
proved disposition before one short, current-reproved compare-and-swap advances
the sole reader boundary. “Complete” does not require publishing every old
Page; it requires proving the fate of every item. An unresolved Page may remain
Not public, quarantined, reference-only, or retired without allowing it to
disappear from coverage.

This is narrower than a platform migration engine. D21 owns only adoption
coverage, shadow proof, and the one-time authority transition. Every D1–D20
owner remains independently authoritative before, during, and after cutover.

### 44.2 Current repository evidence

The following code is implementation evidence, not D21 authority:

| Current repository surface                                                           | Observed behavior                                                                                                                                 | D21 consequence                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/mock-data/index.ts` (`getFieldWorkers`)                                    | Builds public worker identity, location, story, image, annualized support, goal, and a demo missionary ID from mock records.                      | The census must classify every mock-derived Page, field, CTA, progress value, and fixture. No mock value may become tenant identity, goal, Designation, or Giving truth.                        |
| `apps/donor/app/(public)/(hero)/workers/workers-client.tsx`                          | Performs browser-side directory search/filtering over `getFieldWorkers()` and links directly to `/workers/{id}` while rendering `QuickGiveInput`. | The current directory, route, and Give surfaces are one legacy authority cohort. They cannot be converted page-by-page while remaining a public fallback.                                       |
| `apps/donor/app/(public)/(solid)/workers/[id]/page.tsx`                              | `generateStaticParams`, metadata, JSON-LD, profile content, and Giving are all derived from the mock worker set.                                  | Shadow and cutover proof must include static route generation, HTML, metadata, structured data, cards, navigation, and Giving—not only a CMS document.                                          |
| `apps/missionary/app/profile/use-profile-page-view.ts` and `profile-primitives.tsx`  | Construct a public path from lower-cased first and last names.                                                                                    | A legacy name-derived route is evidence to disposition under D8 and Phase 10, never a safe slug or subject mapping. Restricted paths cannot redirect in a way that reveals identity succession. |
| `apps/admin/app/web-studio/web-studio-sections.tsx`                                  | Uses local `Public                                                                                                                                | Draft                                                                                                                                                                                           | Private` states, raw goal strings, editable display/location/bio fields, and sample projects. | The current editor vocabulary cannot prove D2 release, D6 progress, D7 Giving, D17/D19 subject, or D20 catalog truth. It must be censused and mapped, quarantined, or retired rather than grandfathered. |
| `apps/admin/src/cms-ui/web-studio/collections/config.ts` and create flows            | Public paths and Page creation rely on soft `missionaryId`/`fundId` values and Payload-oriented collection configuration.                         | IDs, URLs, titles, funds, and visual similarity may not infer a canonical subject, Designation, permission, route, or release. Exact owner-certified mappings are mandatory.                    |
| `apps/admin/src/cms/public/published-content-reader.ts` and `published-page-read.ts` | Provide a useful tenant-scoped published-content boundary over Payload.                                                                           | Reuse the reader boundary as substrate, but cut it over to the Phase 22 gateway contract. Payload `_status` and the legacy reader never become release or cutover authority.                    |
| `packages/lib/seo/metadata.ts` and `json-ld.tsx`                                     | Use global `/workers` URLs and helper-generated worker metadata/structured data.                                                                  | Metadata, canonical, JSON-LD, sitemap, social presentation, and locale/host coverage belong in the same adoption manifest and shadow proof as visible HTML.                                     |
| `packages/graphql/handler.ts`                                                        | Invalidates generic post cache tags with stale-while-revalidate behavior.                                                                         | Existing invalidation is useful mechanics only. D18 current admission and adverse-first convergence remain controlling after the CAS.                                                           |

The repository has durable ingredients—Payload versions and preview, a
tenant-scoped published reader, Next.js public routes, and cache invalidation—
but no current complete D1–D20 authority census, immutable adoption manifest,
surface head, or one-time CAS transition. A partial wrapper around current
files would institutionalize dual authority.
