### 44.4 Binding architecture and data implications

#### Exact cohort and complete coverage

- One immutable-scope **Public Ministry Surface Adoption Case** names Tenant,
  Legal Entity, environment, Site, the immutable enumerated verified-host
  membership generation and digest, and the smallest dependency-closed locale
  set. Page Family is not a smaller cutover boundary when families share
  discovery, routes, sitemap, media, or Giving.
- One prospective immutable **Adoption Plan Version** records the code-owned
  preparation policy and selected bounded choices. Changing it creates a
  successor; it never mutates a reviewed manifest, and exactly one immutable
  plan/manifest pair is selected for each attempt.
- One content-addressed **Adoption Coverage Manifest** reconciles a complete
  source census by count and digest. It covers legacy/mock/static/generic routes
  and aliases; Page records, drafts, autosaves, and versions; templates, blocks,
  globals, and former editors; subject/identity/Designation/fund/campaign/
  locale/source-code/CTA hints; Updates; media; previews; discovery/search/
  sitemap/canonical/robots/social outputs; cache variants; and Giving handoffs.
  Code-global APIs, readers, serializers, fixtures, tests, and import paths are
  certified once in a content-addressed code/schema coverage artifact that the
  tenant manifest pins; they are not duplicated as per-tenant facts.
- Every source item receives exactly one non-overlapping disposition. Missing,
  duplicate, ambiguous, stale, or unsafe truth remains an explicit blocker or
  Not-public outcome; it never becomes zero or an inferred match.

#### Finite dispositions and compatible legacy

The bounded dispositions are:

1. one certified typed D2 release;
2. one frozen, version-pinned compatible-legacy D2 release where D20 already
   permits it;
3. one exact D8 successor, transition, redirect, tombstone, or terminal result;
4. private reference-only preservation and export;
5. quarantine or Not public; or
6. proved retirement.

Compatible legacy is deliberately narrow. It may preserve proved-safe editorial
presentation through the new Phase 5/D18 gateway. It cannot infer, edit, or own
identity, Phase 10 reach, subject, Designation, Giving, progress, media, Update,
route, discovery, search/share, or measurement truth. It is not raw Payload
publication, a generic fallback reader, or a second Page builder. Its next
change uses ordinary D1–D20 commands.

#### Private preparation, shadow, and cutover

- Preparation is additive, cursor-based, chunked, resumable, tenant-fair, and
  non-authoritative. Worker crashes and retries resume residual work rather
  than replaying the whole cohort.
- Candidates pin exact source versions and owner generations. A later
  missionary draft remains saved but is visibly outside the prepared release;
  preparation never silently replaces or destroys it.
- D10 remains the authenticated exact-version human preview. A separate D21
  production-shaped whole-surface shadow renders the actual D20 compiler and
  Phase 5 reader path without public effects. It proves controlled generated
  output for included and excluded routes, identity, content, Giving posture,
  progress posture, Updates, media, directory/search, metadata, sitemap, social
  presentation, redirects/terminal responses, locale, cache variants, and
  restricted-worker behavior. It is not a D10 preview, D2 release, D18 serving
  or convergence observation, public cache warm, or proof that Google, Bing, or
  a social network refreshed.
- The final command re-proves current actor/Phase 12 authority, scope/hosts,
  census/manifest/digests, owner generations, permissions/revocations, schema/
  code/environment, heads, and in-flight change state inside one short
  transaction. The authority-head CAS, immutable receipt, and D18 convergence
  cause commit together. Provider calls and compilation stay outside locks.
- Before the CAS, failure has no public effect. After it, the new authority
  remains the only truth while D18 performs idempotent residual convergence.
  There is no old-reader, mock, Payload, cache, or deployment fallback.

#### Recovery and independently authoritative outcomes

“Restore a previous safe version” means select a prior certified,
generation-compatible D2 release only after current Phase 10, route, subject,
Designation, media, and code reproof. If none is currently safe, the owning
policy returns absence, redirect/transition, or neutral unavailability. A
Vercel deployment rollback is code selection, never content rollback.

Prepared, mapped, reviewed, released, reachable, served, cached, converged,
crawled, indexed, share-cached, gift-ready, donated, paid, and externally
forgotten remain different facts. D21 weakens none of D1–D20.

### 44.5 Quiet, consequence-first UX

Tenant staff enter one conditional **Finish setting up public pages** card for
the visibly named website and language. A private automatic scan runs first.
The workspace has three comprehensible tasks: resolve genuine exceptions,
review the complete prepared site, and start it.

- Healthy items collapse under **Ready to use**.
- The default working view is **Needs a decision**, with one cause-owned action
  such as **Connect the ministry**, **Choose the Giving destination**, **Replace
  this photo**, or **Choose what this old address should do**.
- **Not moving as a current ministry page** shows the exact quarantine,
  reference-only, Not-public, D8 redirect/transition, terminal, or retirement
  outcome without treating it as missing. This is the canonical interpretation
  of the ratified quote's shorthand **Will not be public**, which is inaccurate
  for a public Transition Notice Release.
- Current/prepared responsive preview and a semantic change list show what
  visitors will see; the final review names every Page outcome, old address,
  exact Giving destination, progress posture, directory/search/share result,
  media replacement, and newer draft excluded from the cohort.
- The one final action is **Start using these prepared pages**. If current
  reproof fails, nothing switches and the interface links to the changed fact.

Missionaries remain in their ordinary Public Pages workspace, may continue
editing, and see only task/editor state plus D18's canonical **Public**,
**Updating**, or **Not public** serving state. They never choose a subject,
Designation, restricted classification, redirect, or cutover cohort. Donors see
no migration UI and no mixed surface. Existing carts and copied CTAs continue
to receive final Phase 5/13 revalidation without destination substitution.

Authorized support may inspect scope, generations, digests, proof cause,
controlled convergence, and a reference ID. It receives no Force live, safety
override, raw database repair, or Restore legacy reader command.

### 44.6 Ruthless adversarial review

Every required category has a concern before the D21 hardening:

| Category                          | Concern? | What could go wrong / why it matters                                                                                                                                                                                      | Severity | Likelihood  | Permanent prevention                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Brittleness                       | Yes      | Per-Page switches split one website across mocks, CMS rows, new releases, routes, and caches; source changes stale an earlier green result.                                                                               | Critical | High        | Exact cohort, immutable inputs, resumable staging, complete manifest, final recensus, and CAS reproof.                             |
| Technical debt                    | Yes      | A temporary v2 flag, duplicate serializer, or fallback reader becomes permanent and doubles every future Phase 22 change.                                                                                                 | Critical | High        | One compiler/DTO/gateway/authority path; compatible legacy only as a frozen D2 release.                                            |
| Edge cases                        | Yes      | Duplicate or case-folded slugs, locale aliases, restricted name URLs, missing Designations, withdrawn media, redirect loops, shared templates, concurrent edits, and open carts can produce unsafe or incorrect outcomes. | Critical | High        | Structural uniqueness, exact dispositions, immutable versions, final owner reproof, and production-shaped fixtures.                |
| Footguns                          | Yes      | Publish All, Force live, inferred mappings, free CTAs, blanket redirects, generic Payload writes, service keys, or legacy restoration can expose people or misdirect gifts.                                               | Critical | Medium-high | No override path; server-derived scoped commands; exact owner facts; constrained Payload adapters.                                 |
| Tenant safety                     | Yes      | Scope drift in manifest queries, object paths, host aliases, RLS, workers, or cache keys can expose another organization.                                                                                                 | Critical | Medium-high | Scope-complete composite keys/FKs, explicit grants plus indexed RLS, server-owned scope, hostile cross-tenant proof.               |
| Over-engineering                  | Yes      | A migration DSL, environment clone, arbitrary state matrix, or generic workflow makes a bounded cutover a permanent product.                                                                                              | High     | High        | One code-owned Adoption Case, finite dispositions, three-task UX, narrow adapters, one cutover.                                    |
| UX/UI and user friction           | Yes      | Technical jargon, page-by-page certification, hidden unresolved rows, or two editing systems cause guessing and abandonment.                                                                                              | High     | High        | Automatic healthy preparation, exception-first saved work, plain consequences, one review/action, one missionary editor.           |
| Hidden coupling                   | Yes      | Adoption can accidentally redefine safety, Giving, routes, media, Updates, discovery, search/share, measurement, or caching.                                                                                              | Critical | High        | Reference exact D1–D20 versions/manifests; D21 owns only coverage and cutover evidence.                                            |
| Failure modes                     | Yes      | Worker crashes, lost/out-of-order effects, stale CDN bytes, failed probes, unavailable stores, or unsafe rollback can leave mixed behavior.                                                                               | Critical | High        | Atomic CAS/receipt/outbox, idempotent residual recovery, D18 admission, neutral fail-closed outcomes.                              |
| Data integrity risks              | Yes      | Census omissions, duplicate dispositions, fuzzy matches, in-place overwrite, or check-then-create races create competing truth.                                                                                           | Critical | High        | Count/digest reconciliation, exact IDs, append-only versions/corrections, composite constraints, single-winner CAS.                |
| Security and privacy risks        | Yes      | Identity can leak through old slugs, filenames, EXIF, derivatives, preview, logs, metadata, sitemaps, social cards, or shared caches.                                                                                     | Critical | High        | Phase 10 at preparation/cutover/serve, D9-only media, D10 authorization, complete egress census, redacted evidence.                |
| Scalability and performance risks | Yes      | A giant transaction, synchronous full-site render, static redirect list, or large tenant can time out and starve others.                                                                                                  | High     | Medium-high | Cursor chunks, tenant-fair queues, indexed manifest queries, precompiled artifacts, tiny final transaction, scalable route lookup. |
| Operational burden                | Yes      | Staff recheck healthy Pages or engineers manually repair caches/redirects for each tenant.                                                                                                                                | High     | High        | Deterministic preparation, cause-owned exceptions, saved progress, generated evidence, supported residual recovery.                |
| Observability gaps                | Yes      | CMS Published, job done, purge accepted, response observed, indexed, and Giving executable collapse into one false success.                                                                                               | Critical | High        | Separate immutable facts/timestamps, generation probes, coverage/deadline evidence, honest external states.                        |
| Dependency and integration risks  | Yes      | Payload, Next/Vercel caching, deployment skew, provider limits, and crawler timing can invalidate assumptions.                                                                                                            | High     | Medium-high | Product/version/environment capability pins, narrow adapters, production certification, local semantic authority.                  |
| Migration and upgrade risks       | Yes      | Generic blocks, URLs, stats, testimonials, or `fundId` acquire fabricated D20 meaning; down migrations revive unsafe content.                                                                                             | Critical | High        | Additive versioned schemas, exact dispositions, shadow compile, source export, no destructive down rollback.                       |
| Other development hazards         | Yes      | Stale tabs, double-clicks, concurrent actors, revoked permission, duplicate events, deployment order, deadlocks, or fixture promotion bypass safety.                                                                      | Critical | High        | Current auth, idempotency, CAS/fencing, deterministic lock order, compatible deployment window, race/fault tests.                  |

### 44.7 Required production-shaped proof

The eventual implementation is not acceptable until it proves:

1. zero missing source items, overlapping dispositions, unexplained count
   differences, digest differences, or mock/fixture facts admitted as tenant
   truth;
2. structural Tenant, Legal Entity, environment, Site, host, locale, Page,
   subject, route, and generation isolation, including service-role workers;
3. exact shadow/public compiler parity and fail-closed handling of unknown
   blocks, unsafe media, fuzzy identities, free CTAs, ineligible Designations,
   missing source facts, and excluded routes;
4. Phase 10, Designation, source, actor, grant, schema, and code changes between
   final review and cutover; two concurrent actors; repeated/conflicting
   idempotency keys; crash before/after CAS; lost, duplicate, delayed, and out-
   of-order effects; old browser/RSC/cache/media/deployment requests; and safe
   residual recovery;
5. every old URL reaches exactly one retained Page, one-hop same-Page successor,
   transition, or terminal response with no loop, chain, soft 404, broad
   redirect, identity disclosure, or destination substitution;
6. an existing tab, copied CTA, or cart crossing cutover cannot silently change
   Designation and Page reach cannot substitute for Phase 5/13 eligibility;
7. at least one production-shaped 5,000-Page **minimum test fixture** with
   bounded cursor work, tenant fairness, stable reconciliation, resumability,
   targeted convergence, and a short final transaction; this is neither a
   product limit nor a performance guarantee;
8. keyboard, screen reader, focus, linked error summary, non-color meaning,
   semantic diff, non-iframe preview, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% text, 400% zoom,
   forced colors, reduced motion, touch, RTL/long locale, and interruption/
   resume behavior; and
9. operator evidence that keeps authority activation, current admission,
   convergence requested/accepted/observed/unverifiable, external crawler or
   social observation, and Giving eligibility distinct.

Usability research must include small and large tenant staff, actual Page/
Giving setup responsibilities, varied technical comfort, keyboard/screen-reader
use, and synthetic restricted-worker scenarios. A design fails if staff think
**Ready to use** means already public, missionaries believe they choose the
operational Designation, staff cannot predict route/retirement behavior, or a
participant cannot resume and complete the cohort without developer help.

### 44.8 Ratified exact contract and durable links

The founder ratified the following exact formulation as Phase 22 D21:

> **C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R) — one privately prepared,
> complete-surface Public Ministry authority adoption for each exact Tenant ×
> Legal Entity × environment × Site × verified-host set × locale, composed from
> one immutable-scope Public Ministry Surface Adoption Case, one prospective
> immutable Adoption Plan Version, one content-addressed complete Adoption
> Coverage Manifest, and one short idempotent CAS-guarded Surface Authority
> Cutover. Page preparation may proceed incrementally in private, additive,
> chunked, resumable, non-authoritative staging, but public authority changes once
> for the complete scoped surface; “complete” means every discovered item has
> exactly one proved disposition, not that every old page must become public.**
>
> **The manifest exhaustively covers every legacy, mock, static, generic, or
> copied route and alias; Page, draft, autosave, and version; template, block,
> global dependency, and former profile editor; subject, identity, Designation,
> fund, campaign, locale, source-code, and CTA hint; Ministry Update; media
> original, derivative, URL, metadata, and source filename; preview; directory,
> search, sitemap, canonical, robots, and social presentation; cache namespace
> and variant; Giving handoff; API, reader, fixture, test, and import path. Every
> item receives exactly one source-family-valid, non-overlapping disposition: a
> certified typed D2 release; a frozen, read-only, version-pinned compatible-
> legacy D2 release served only through the new gateway; an exact D8 successor,
> transition, redirect, tombstone, or terminal disposition; private reference-
> only preservation and export; quarantine or Not public; or proved retirement.
> No mock or synthetic fact becomes tenant truth, no missing fact becomes safe or
> zero, and no name, title, URL, `fundId`, profile row, free CTA, or visual
> similarity may infer identity, Designation, publication, progress, media,
> Update, or Giving authority.**
>
> **Compatible-legacy presentation is permitted only where D20 already allows
> it, as an immutable certified D2 release inside the same new reader. It may
> preserve safe editorial presentation but cannot infer or own managed identity,
> restricted-worker reach, Designation, Giving, progress, media, Updates, routes,
> search, or measurement. It is never continued raw Payload publication, a
> generic fallback reader, or a second editing system. Later improvement of that
> Page uses ordinary D1–D20 release and succession commands without another
> migration mode.**
>
> **Exact candidates may be machine-prepared, but staff review only genuine
> exceptions and the complete visitor consequences. The production-shaped D10
> shadow proves every included and excluded route, current/new presentation,
> subject, Giving destination, progress posture, Ministry Updates, media,
> directory/search membership, metadata, sitemap, social presentation, redirect
> or terminal response, locale, cache variant, and restricted-worker outcome
> without public side effects. The selected candidate versions remain immutable;
> newer missionary drafts remain safely saved and visibly outside the prepared
> release rather than being lost or silently substituted.**
>
> **The final cutover re-proves inside one short transaction the current actor
> and Phase 12 authority; complete scope and verified hosts; plan, manifest,
> source census, and content digests; Phase 10 safety and D2 reach; D3/D20 catalog
> and renderer generations; D7 Giving binding; D8 route dispositions; D9 media;
> D11 Updates; D13 discovery; D14 search/share; D17/D19 subjects and
> participants; locale, code, schema, environment, revocation, current heads,
> and in-flight changes. It records the immutable receipt and transactional D18
> convergence cause and advances the one-time pre-/post-Phase-22 serving
> boundary through compare-and-swap. D21 owns only adoption coverage and cutover
> evidence; it creates no second Page release, route, safety, subject, Giving,
> progress, media, Update, discovery, search/share, measurement, or cache
> authority.**
>
> **The database authority transition is atomic; distributed cache, sitemap,
> media, search, social, and external crawler convergence is not. Immediately
> after cutover, the Phase 5/D18 gateway is the sole reader for that exact
> surface, and D18’s request-time current-admission gate prevents superseded
> positive bytes from regaining authority while idempotent, tenant-fair,
> residual-only convergence proceeds. Failure before the CAS has no public
> effect. Failure after the CAS leaves the new authority truthful and opens only
> the remaining convergence work; it never falls back to mock data, raw Payload
> publication, an old cache namespace, or the legacy reader.**
>
> **Recovery may use only “Restore a previous safe version”: a previously
> certified, generation-compatible D2 release re-proved against current Phase
> 10, route, subject, Designation, media, and code safety. If no currently safe
> release exists, the affected scope becomes privacy-safe absent, redirected,
> transitioned, or neutrally unavailable under its owning policy. A Vercel
> deployment rollback is never content-authority rollback.**
>
> **Tenant staff receive one quiet, accessible, exception-first “Prepare public
> pages” experience scoped visibly to the exact website and language, with only
> “Ready to use,” “Needs a decision,” and “Will not be public”; automatic
> preparation of healthy items; cause-owned plain-language actions; an exact
> responsive current/prepared preview and semantic change list; one complete
> consequence review; and one literal “Start using these prepared pages” action.
> There is no repeated page-by-page certification, technical migration
> vocabulary, ambiguous Publish All, high-risk bulk approval, typed confirmation
> phrase, force-live path, or second D4/D5 editorial approval.**
>
> **Missionaries continue using their ordinary Public Pages dashboard and may
> keep editing while preparation occurs. They see only calm, truthful states such
> as Preparing for launch, Ready for launch, In review, Live, or Changes
> requested, plus notice when a newer draft is not part of the prepared site.
> They never choose operational subjects, Designations, redirects, safety
> classifications, or cutover scope. Donors see no migration interface or mixed
> authority: each request resolves wholly through the old coherent surface
> before cutover or the new coherent surface afterward, and Phase 5/13
> revalidates any existing cart or copied Giving action without silently changing
> its Designation.**
>
> **There is no tenant-global enable bit, page-by-page public authority toggle,
> mixed reader, dual read or write, fuzzy adoption, mutable readiness truth,
> silent exclusion, inferred redirect, blanket homepage or organization-fund
> redirect, unrestricted compatibility renderer, traffic-split content canary,
> giant transaction, browser service key, blind retry, destructive rollback,
> legacy restoration, or claim that prepared, mapped, approved, released,
> reachable, served, cached, converged, crawled, indexed, share-cached,
> gift-ready, donated, or externally forgotten are the same fact.**

The normative wording and additional binding interpretation are preserved in
the
[Phase 22 D21 decision](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d21--how-does-a-tenant-replace-the-legacy-public-ministry-surface-without-exposing-mixed-authority)
and
[ADR-0138 — Complete Public Ministry Surface authority cutover](../../adr/0138-complete-public-ministry-surface-authority-cutover.md).

D22's ongoing Public Ministry operations and cause-owned-repair experience was
the next dependency-ordered seam after D21. D21 ratification remains planning
truth only and grants no implementation or production authority.

## 45. Ratified D22 research — quiet derived Public Page operations

**Status:** D22 is ratified, amended, and adversarially hardened on 2026-08-14.
This section records research and planning evidence only; ratification
authorizes no implementation, migration, notification, issue publication, or
production activation.

### 45.1 Research conclusion

One staff workspace is the right direction only when it is a disposable,
permission-filtered read model over D1–D21 owner truth. It must not become a
second review queue, Page-health state machine, universal ticket product, repair
authority, or mutable resolution ledger. The safe information architecture has
exactly three stable views:

1. **To review** references D4/D5 candidates and actions without copying their
   state.
2. **Needs attention** contains only current owner-labelled causes for which the
   current actor can perform one concrete action now.
3. **All pages** is a coverage-labelled, permission-filtered inventory, not a
   wall of health cards.

These are navigation views, not Page states. D5 editorial workflow, D18 public
serving, D7 Giving, and every source-owned outcome remain separately labelled.
One cause may affect many Pages and appear once; several causes on one Page
remain separately owned and actionable. A cause disappears only after fresh
owner proof of correction or supersession—not because someone read, dismissed,
completed, or stopped seeing a task.

### 45.2 Current repository evidence

The repository already contains useful shell mechanics, but none is safe to
adopt as D22 authority without the hardened boundary:

Cross-record foreign keys do not structurally prove a complete Tenant × Legal Entity × Site × locale × Page scope. | Reuse visual or collaboration primitives only after separately proving scope. Task state cannot clear or reinterpret a Public Page cause.                                                                  |

| `packages/api/src/admin/mission-control-tasks/{types,store,service,route}.ts`                                                     | The current model is contribution-specific, filters attention by Tenant and open status, caps at 100, lacks cursor/coverage truth, creates task/link/event sequentially, and authorizes coarse staff roles.                                                                                                         | It is not a Public Pages projection or command seam. D22 needs typed owner adapters, deterministic episodes, atomic/idempotent task linking where used, keyset pagination, and permission-filtered counts. |
| `packages/database/collections/admin-workspace.ts`                                                                                | The visible task demo explicitly uses local transition data and seed identities with a different state vocabulary.                                                                                                                                                                                                  | It is not production identity, authorization, or operational truth.                                                                                                                                        |

D21 cutover must first remove the mock authority.                                                                                         |

The normative cross-cutting boundary already says Mission Control tasks are the
shared staff work model and **Needs Attention** is a projection rather than a
second task system. D22 narrows that rule: a human-actionable cause may link to
one shared follow-up task for collaboration, but task completion never proves
the owner cause is fixed.

No source supports collapsing reviewed, published, publicly served,
gift-ready, cached, indexed, or repaired into one Page state. Nor does any source
support treating task completion, provider acceptance, or an empty derived view
as source-owned resolution.

### 45.4 Required product and data contract

- The ordinary staff row shows Page identity/family/Site/locale, **Visitor
  access**, **Giving**, and only relevant owner work. It has no green success
  banner or technical status chips.
- An actionable detail states, in order: what supporters can see now; whether
  Giving is available; what changed; whether automatic work continues; who owns
  the next step; one literal action; and source through-time only when it affects
  the decision.
- Viewers without the action capability see a permission-safe owner explanation
  in **All pages**, never a disabled authority-bearing button and never a
  **Needs attention** item.
- Cause and impact are separate. Root identity includes complete non-null scope,
  owner domain, stable source reference, contract generation, monotonic owner
  version, responsible-owner generation, action kind, coverage, and recurrence
  episode. Impact membership carries exact Page or Update scope and the
  privacy-safe visitor consequence.
- Actions are finite product commands resolved server-side. Arbitrary stored
  URLs, raw provider errors, owner enums, source filenames, restricted identity,
  and private review content never enter the ordinary projection.
- Projection absence or incomplete coverage is not health. The UI says **Some
  page information is temporarily unavailable**, shows the last complete
  through-time where useful, and keeps public serving and direct owner workflows
  independent.
- Missionaries stay in their D1 Public pages dashboard. D22 grants nothing from
  subject, spouse, teammate, D19 Ministry Assignment, Phase 21 Support access,
  task ownership, or raw database visibility.

### 45.5 Ruthless adversarial result

Every required category contains a concern before the hardening:

| Category                          | Concern? | What could go wrong and why it matters                                                                                                                      | Severity | Likelihood  | Permanent prevention                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Brittleness                       | Yes      | Late, missing, reordered, or incompatible owner facts could remove real work or leave a dead action.                                                        | Critical | High        | Versioned adapters, monotonic updates, complete coverage watermarks, periodic reconciliation, explicit source outage, and execution-time reproof.           |
| Technical debt                    | Yes      | Copying owner enums, permissions, labels, links, and close rules creates a drifting second implementation.                                                  | High     | High        | One finite semantic adapter/action contract, owner commands, reusable presentation primitives, and exhaustive conformance tests.                            |
| Edge cases                        | Yes      | One cause may affect thousands of Pages; one Page may have several causes; causes can recur; Pages, locales, owners, and permissions can change mid-action. | Critical | High        | Cause/impact separation, deterministic episode identity, exact versions, source-owned recurrence/supersession, and current reproof.                         |
| Footguns                          | Yes      | Mark fixed, dismiss, snooze, bulk approve, generic retry/purge, arbitrary priority, or Force live could hide harm or bypass an owner.                       | Critical | Medium-high | Application-read-only projection, finite code-owned actions, no generic/bulk correction, and owner-side authorization plus idempotency.                     |
| Tenant safety                     | Yes      | Rows, counts, filters, URLs, notifications, cache entries, or timing could reveal another tenant or restricted Page.                                        | Critical | Medium-high | Complete structural scope, indexed RLS, security-invoker views, authorization before aggregation, safe copy/cache keys, and hostile isolation tests.        |
| Over-engineering                  | Yes      | A configurable health, workflow, assignment, SLA, or case product duplicates D1–D21 and becomes a second authority.                                         | High     | High        | Exactly three views, a disposable read model, finite owner adapters, and existing owner/communication systems.                                              |
| UX/UI and user friction           | Yes      | Status-chip overload, technical language, empty alarms, disabled actions, whole-row activation, and desktop-only tables train staff to ignore genuine work. | High     | High        | Independent plain-language facets, one literal action, progressive disclosure, stable routes, mobile cards, accessible feedback, and quiet healthy states.  |
| Hidden coupling                   | Yes      | Review, Giving, safety, media, route, search, cache, and adoption changes could silently redefine D22 or be changed through it.                             | Critical | High        | Versioned privacy-safe owner contracts, stable action kinds, no raw-table joins, and no D22 owner writes.                                                   |
| Failure modes                     | Yes      | Lost events, partial task creation, stale views, owner outages, revoked permissions, or ambiguous commands could hide, duplicate, or misapply work.         | Critical | High        | Transactional occurrences, atomic/idempotent task linkage, inspect-before-retry, reconciliation, honest unavailable states, and current reproof.            |
| Data integrity risks              | Yes      | Nullable or tenant-only keys, arbitrary JSON, mutable resolution, and out-of-order close events could corrupt counts and current truth.                     | Critical | High        | Complete non-null same-scope keys, deterministic uniqueness, typed references, monotonic CAS, append-only owner evidence, and no D22 close field.           |
| Security and privacy risks        | Yes      | Titles, aliases, safety causes, former routes, comments, exports, logs, and notification copy could identify a restricted worker.                           | Critical | High        | Phase 10 before enumeration/counting, privacy-safe manifests, field allowlists, opaque references, redacted logs/tasks, and separately authorized evidence. |
| Scalability and performance risks | Yes      | Request-time cross-domain joins, one item per affected Page, hard caps, offset pagination, and unindexed RLS could collapse at tenant scale.                | High     | High        | Incremental materialization, root grouping, keyset pagination, partial/current indexes, tenant-fair processing, and production-shaped load proof.           |
| Operational burden                | Yes      | Staff could spend time triaging healthy automation, duplicates, owners, retries, and stale rows.                                                            | High     | High        | Zero setup, human-actionable-only membership, source-derived owner/action, automatic source-owned removal, grouping, and private operator runbooks.         |
| Observability gaps                | Yes      | Staff could read an empty view as healthy while operators cannot trace lag, mismatch, dropped events, invalid actions, or notification storms.              | Critical | High        | Coverage/through-time UI and privacy-safe lag, backlog, digest mismatch, stale-action, denied-access, task-orphan, and rebuild telemetry.                   |
| Dependency and integration risks  | Yes      | Payload, Supabase, Vercel/CDN, Giving, media, search/social, and notification behavior can drift independently.                                             | High     | Medium-high | Capability/version-pinned owner adapters, explicit unknown outcomes, circuit breaking, local semantic truth, and no provider outcome as repair proof.       |
| Migration and upgrade risks       | Yes      | Reusing legacy attention JSON or Payload `_status` can revive old authority, strand causes, and duplicate notifications.                                    | High     | Medium-high | Additive versioned cause contracts, typed adapters, shadow rebuild plus count/digest parity, cursor cutover, and projection-only rollback.                  |
| Other development hazards         | Yes      | Stale tabs, double clicks, duplicate events, clock/deployment skew, task races, unauthorized deep links, and Realtime refetches can defeat the happy path.  | Critical | High        | Current authorization, CAS/idempotency, deterministic locks/keys, compatible rollouts, signal-only Realtime, kill switches, and race/fault tests.           |

### 45.6 Required production proof

1. Prove every cause adapter's source owner, visitor consequence, action,
   clear/reopen predicate, recurrence, and privacy projection through contracts.
2. Prove nonexistence-indistinguishable isolation across Tenant, Legal Entity,
   Site, locale, host, Page Family, Page, restricted worker, role, field, row,
   impact, count, filter, search, export, subscription, cache, notification, log,
   and privileged projector path.
3. Prove one root cause affecting 300 Pages becomes one owner action and one
   eligible notification with 300 permission-filtered impacts, while several
   causes on one Page remain independent.
4. Prove task completion/dismissal/suppression cannot hide an active cause and
   owner correction removes it even when task state is stale.
5. Fault-test duplicate, missing, out-of-order, reopened, and superseded owner
   versions; incomplete coverage; source/queue/projector outage; partial task
   creation; stale tabs; permission revocation; simultaneous actors; and
   accepted-but-unobserved commands.
6. Prove twenty automatic retries or projection rebuilds emit no new human
   notification; only an eligible owner or material-impact transition produces
   the exact successor intent.
7. Prove 100 healthy Pages produce no attention item, badge, email, or success
   wall and that incomplete coverage is never shown as zero.
8. Load-test D21's production-shaped 5,000-Page minimum plus bursty
   one-cause-many-Page and many-cause-one-Page data with stable indexed plans,
   keyset pagination, tenant fairness, reconciliation, and measured supported-
   tenant headroom.
9. Usability-test representative small-tenant generalists, reviewers, finance,
   safety, contributors, spouses/teammates, support, and restricted-worker
   scenarios. Each participant must correctly identify what supporters see,
   whether Giving works, who acts, and what follows the action without Phase
   codes or technical coaching.
10. Verify keyboard, screen reader, stable focus, concise polite status
    announcements, 320-CSS-pixel reflow, 200% text, 400% zoom, forced colors,
    reduced motion, touch, RTL/long locale, interruption recovery, and public
    non-disclosure.

### 45.7 Ratified decision

The founder ratified the exact C-prime-R formulation. Its binding
interpretation, role consequences, all-category adversarial analysis, proof
gates, and implementation order are preserved in the
[Phase 22 D22 decision](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d22--how-does-staff-manage-ongoing-public-pages-work-without-a-noisy-second-workflow)
and
[ADR-0139 — Derived Public Page operations with cause-owned actions](../../adr/0139-derived-public-page-operations-with-cause-owned-actions.md).

D22 is planning truth only. D1–D21 remain unchanged, and no runtime,
notification, migration, issue-publication, or production action is authorized.
The next dependency-ordered seam was D23 Public Pages setup/settings. Section
46 records its subsequently selected and hardened candidate; D22 evidence does
not decide or ratify D23.

## 46. Ratified D23 research — derived Public Page setup and settings

**Status:** The exact C-prime-R was founder-ratified on 2026-08-14. This section
records research and planning evidence only and authorizes no implementation,
migration, notification, issue publication, or production activation.

### 46.1 Research conclusion

The winning direction is not one universal settings record. It is one calm
staff experience that composes exact source-owner facts, tells the user which
scope and consequence they are changing, and delegates each amendment to one
owner command. “Easy to change” means a prepopulated one-setting task with
authoritative readback; it does not mean mutable flags, broad switches, or a
global save bar.

The UX has two modes over the same projection:

1. **First setup** foregrounds only Publication Reach for each Page Family and
   Review & Release. Missing tenant choices are visibly different from safe
   fallback behavior. Built-in and optional features remain quiet.
2. **Ongoing settings** presents four compact groups, one literal **Change**
   action per row, exact owner-supplied effects, and links to Page-owned or
   separately owned workflows rather than pretending every Public Page fact is
   a global setting.

D23 remains disposable and non-authoritative. D2–D20 and Phase 21 D10 own the
settings and versions; D21 owns surface preparation/activation; D22 owns
operational work; and Page/Update owners retain their exact per-item choices.

### 46.2 Current repository evidence

The live worktree contains several useful cautionary examples but no current
D23 authority model:

| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

Every D23 read/change needs server-resolved complete scope, typed validation, current fine capability, owner version/head, CAS, idempotency, and authoritative readback. |
| `supabase/schema.sql:13-26`                                      | Stores untyped `org_settings JSONB` on the secret-bearing Tenant row beside payment/provider settings.                                                                          | The Tenant row is not a safe browser read surface or universal Phase 22 profile. Keep owner-specific typed versions and heads outside a generic JSON blob.                                         |
| `apps/admin/app/(app)/feed/org-updates/page-client.tsx:199-216`  | Waits 800 ms and reports **Settings saved** without authoritative persistence.                                                                                                  | D23 cannot use delay/toast success. It reports success only after owner readback of the exact successor/head.                                                                                      |
| `packages/auth/context.ts:241-379`                               | Resolves one Tenant plus coarse roles/memberships.                                                                                                                              | Phase 12 fine-grained read/change capabilities and exact Legal Entity/Site/environment/locale/Page-Family scope are genuine prerequisites, not client-side fields.                                 |
| `apps/admin/src/cms-ui/web-studio/flows/tenant-picker.tsx:31-77` | A super-admin browser picker loads up to 200 Tenant rows and has no Legal Entity, Site, locale, Page Family, or owner capability boundary.                                      | Reuse neither its authority nor all-at-once loading. D23 scope is server-authorized, URL-addressable, bounded, and dimension-aware.                                                                |
| Payload preferences and current mock public-worker records       | Store editor/UI state or demonstration content rather than immutable Phase 22 owner facts.                                                                                      | They may supply shell patterns only; a Payload preference, CMS publish state, or mock value never becomes D23 configuration truth.                                                                 |

A repo-scoped semantic index search returned obsolete paths such as
`src/types/database.ts` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; those files do not exist in
the current checkout. Direct `rg` and source reads above therefore remain the
authority for this decision. No stale indexed result is used as architecture
evidence.

### 46.3 Setup and settings UX evidence

All sources below are first-party and were checked on 2026-08-14.

| Primary source                                                                                                                                                                     | Current guidance or observed product behavior                                                                                                                         | D23 implication                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cloudscape, [Onboarding](https://cloudscape.design/patterns/general/onboarding/)                                                                                                   | Surface only the information needed at the current step, let the user request deeper guidance, and use progressive disclosure for generalists and specialists.        | First setup shows the three deliberate choices; built-in and optional settings stay summarized and expandable.                                                             |
| Cloudscape, [Defaults](https://cloudscape.design/patterns/resource-management/create/defaults/)                                                                                    | Defaults reduce friction only when transparent and consistent with actual runtime behavior; automatic and dynamic behavior must say what and when the system applies. | Label organization choices, built-in defaults, safe fallbacks, creation seeds, Off, and unavailable states separately. Never display an unset fail-safe as a saved choice. |
| Cloudscape, [Page edit](https://cloudscape.design/patterns/resource-management/edit/page-edit/) and [Unsaved changes](https://cloudscape.design/patterns/general/unsaved-changes/) | Edit experiences should preserve current values and protect work when users navigate away.                                                                            | Prepopulate every owner form, preserve failed input, protect dirty forms, and return to the exact prior scope/row.                                                         |
| Carbon, [Forms](https://carbondesignsystem.com/patterns/forms-pattern/)                                                                                                            | Ask only for necessary information, group related tasks, use predictable single-column forms, and disclose optional inputs only when relevant.                        | Use one setting per form and four scannable summary groups; do not build a settings matrix or overloaded modal.                                                            |
| GOV.UK, [Check answers](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/check-answers/)                                                                                              | Provide a specific Change link per section, preserve entered answers, return directly to the summary, and use a button label that states the action.                  | Each row has a uniquely named action, a changed/unchanged consequence review, and a descriptive commit such as **Use Shared by link for new Project pages**.               |
| GOV.UK, [Complete multiple tasks](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/complete-multiple-tasks/)                                                                          | Simplify a journey before adding a task list and use the fewest useful statuses.                                                                                      | D23 has no persistent checklist, progress percentage, or completion authority; first setup is a small derived list of choices still missing.                               |
| Cloudscape, [Selection in forms](https://cloudscape.design/patterns/general/selection/)                                                                                            | Use the control that matches single, multiple, or boolean choice and reveal related content consistently.                                                             | Reach/review modes use radios with visible descriptions, not ambiguous instant toggles. Optional groups expand consistently.                                               |

The exact row anatomy is therefore:

1. plain-language question;
2. current effective value;
3. source meaning;
4. exact **Applies to** scope;
5. **What this changes**;
6. **What this does not change**;
7. existing-item consequence and effective time;
8. authorized last-change evidence; and
9. one literal owner action.

The summary does not promise that every setting is “future only.” D2, D4,
D6, D11, D12, D13, D15, and D16 have different settled effect boundaries, so
the owner adapter supplies the consequence preflight for each command.

### 46.4 Comparable product evidence

Comparable systems support the need for guided setup and defaults, but also
show the coupling D23 must avoid:

| Product evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Observed behavior                                                                                                                                                     | D23 lesson                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Salesforce, [B2B Store Setup Considerations](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=commerce.comm_store_setup_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5) and [Commerce automated setup](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=commerce.comm_quick_start.htm&language=en_US&type=5) | Uses a simplified guided path, lets users customize locale/language/currency later, previews before go-live, and asks users to review changes before automation acts. | Keep initial setup short, amendments easy, consequence review explicit, and setup distinct from D21 activation.                             |
| HubSpot, [User preference presets](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/user-management/manage-user-preferences-with-user-groups) and [Permissions guide](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/user-management/hubspot-user-permissions-guide)                                                               | Separates permission to edit account defaults from other administrative powers and lets defaults reduce repeated setup.                                               | D23 uses setting-specific read/change capabilities and creation seeds without inferring broader authority.                                  |
| Neon One, [Campaign Landing Page](https://support.neonone.com/hc/en-us/articles/25282456197901-Creating-a-Campaign-Landing-Page)                                                                                                                                                               | Campaign creation, page editing, donation-form selection, theme choice, and Publish are spread across a campaign workflow.                                            | D23 should link directly to the owner task and return, not reproduce every Page editor or publish action inside settings.                   |
| Blackbaud, [Create a donation page](https://webfiles-sc1.blackbaud.com/files/support/helpfiles/guided-fundraising/content/donation-pages-create-a-donation-page.html)                                                                                                                          | One mutable Draft/Active/Archived status controls constituent access and whether the page accepts donations; archived pages redirect to a default donation page.      | Treat this as a coupling warning: D2 reach, D7 Giving, D8 disposition, D18 serving, and D21 adoption must remain independent facts in Asym. |

These comparisons are behavioral evidence, not architecture templates. D23
keeps the low-friction setup advantages while rejecting mutable Page status as
combined publication, Giving, lifecycle, or activation authority.

### 46.5 Supabase and PostgreSQL evidence

| Primary source                                                                                                                                                                       | Current documented behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | D23 requirement                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Supabase, [Securing your API](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/api/securing-your-api)                                                                                                | Postgres grants decide whether a role can reach an object; RLS separately decides which rows it may access. Exposed tables/views without RLS remain reachable when grants allow them.                                                              | Define explicit grants/revokes and RLS together. Do not assume enabling RLS or using `authenticated` is a complete permission model.                 |
| Supabase, [Row Level Security](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security)                                                                                | Views use creator authority by default; Postgres 15+ supports `security_invoker`. User metadata is unsafe for authorization, app-metadata/JWT claims can be stale, UPDATE requires a matching SELECT policy, and policy columns should be indexed. | Use current server/Phase 12 facts, security-invoker views, indexed policies, and command-time reproof; never trust user-editable or stale JWT scope. |
| Supabase, [Securing your data](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/secure-data)                                                                                                | Secret/service-role keys bypass RLS and must never reach the frontend.                                                                                                                                                                             | No browser service role and no privileged read accepted as proof of the current actor's authority.                                                   |
| PostgreSQL, [Row security policies](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html) and [CREATE POLICY](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-createpolicy.html) | Table owners and `BYPASSRLS` roles normally bypass policies; permissive policies combine with OR and restrictive policies with AND; `USING` and `WITH CHECK` govern existing and proposed rows separately.                                         | Test actual application roles, keep privileged projectors confined, and prove both visibility and mutation constraints.                              |
| PostgreSQL, [Constraints](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-constraints.html)                                                                                              | Unique and composite foreign-key constraints provide cross-column identity; cross-row assumptions do not belong in a `CHECK`.                                                                                                                      | Use owner-specific complete-scope heads and composite same-scope references, not nullable generic profiles or cross-row checks.                      |
| PostgreSQL, [UPDATE](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-update.html)                                                                                                        | `UPDATE ... RETURNING` reports rows actually advanced.                                                                                                                                                                                             | A CAS head update returning zero rows is a visible stale conflict, never success.                                                                    |
| PostgreSQL, [Serialization failure handling](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html)                                                       | Serialization/deadlock recovery retries the complete transaction rather than an isolated statement.                                                                                                                                                | Retry the bounded owner command from the beginning and combine it with content-bound idempotency.                                                    |
| PostgreSQL, [Multicolumn indexes](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/indexes-multicolumn.html)                                                                                  | B-tree indexes are most effective when leading equality predicates match the query, while excessive wide indexes are costly.                                                                                                                       | Measure predicate-aligned scope/head/history plans under RLS; do not create one speculative mega-index.                                              |

The safe initial read is a private/no-store server composition using bounded
parallel or batched owner ports. A disposable materialized summary is a later
measured optimization, never the source of authorization or mutation truth.

### 46.6 Accessibility and comprehension evidence

WCAG 2.2 requires labels/instructions, identifiable and correctable errors,
programmatically determinable relationships, usable status messages, reflow,
visible/unobscured focus, and minimum target sizing. Relevant first-party
guidance includes [Labels or Instructions](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/labels-or-instructions.html),
[Error Prevention](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/error-prevention-all),
[Status Messages](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html),
[Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow),
[Focus Not Obscured](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum),
and [Target Size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum).

D23 therefore requires native controls, visible labels, fieldset/legend for
choice groups, error summary plus linked field errors, restrained live-region
status, preserved focus/input, no sticky control obscuring focus, non-color
meaning, complete mobile feature parity, and robust long-locale/RTL behavior.

Usability certification must include a teach-back, not only task completion.
Representative staff must correctly explain:

1. the active organization/Legal Entity/Site/locale context;
2. whether a chosen change affects existing Pages, drafts, queued work, or only
   newly created items;
3. whether anything becomes public because of setup;
4. who reviews or acts next;
5. why progress/Giving/subject/people remain Page-owned; and
6. how to recover from concurrent or uncertain change outcomes.

Release targets are zero wrong-scope or unintended-publication changes, no
critical accessibility blockers, and at least 90% unassisted completion for
first setup and one later amendment in representative moderated tests. The
90% value is a product acceptance target, not a claim from an external source.

### 46.7 Proof and synthesis

The all-category risk analysis and thirteen exact certification gates are
preserved in the
[ratified D23 decision](./phase-22-public-ministry-pages-decision-log.md#d23--how-does-an-authorized-tenant-admin-set-up-and-later-change-public-page-defaults-without-guesswork-or-a-second-source-of-truth)
and [accepted ADR-0140](../../adr/0140-derived-public-page-setup-and-settings.md).

The permanent order is:

1. classify the finite setting inventory and reject global/per-item/automatic
   facts that do not belong in D23;
2. establish owner version/head/read/consequence/command contracts plus Phase 2
   exact scope and Phase 12 capabilities;
3. prove complete-scope isolation and authorization before controls;
4. build the three-choice initial setup and four-group summary;
5. add one-setting amendment, authoritative readback, conflict/ambiguity
   recovery, and source-owned history;
6. link without absorbing D21, D22, and per-page workflows;
7. classify and retire legacy settings authority without dual write; and
8. certify security, concurrency, failure, scale, observability,
   accessibility, localization, and staff comprehension.

D23 is ratified as the exact C-prime-R. D1–D23 are binding, and this evidence
adds no runtime, migration, issue, notification, or production authority.

## 47. Ratified D24 research — attribution-preserving Staff-authored Page Revisions

This section records the evidence behind the founder-ratified Phase 22 D24
C-prime-R. Ratification creates planning truth and the corresponding ADR and
glossary boundary, but no product, schema, migration, issue, notification,
implementation, or production authority.

### 47.1 Research conclusion

An authorized staff member may need to correct organization-owned Public Page
presentation content, but "staff can edit" is unsafe if it means an elevated
overwrite. The smallest coherent design is an ordinary D1 Page Revision with
proved staff authorship: it preserves the exact source and displaced work,
advances the one Page-and-locale working head only through compare-and-swap,
and continues through the existing D4/D5 review lane and D2 release command.
Staff authorship alone grants no approval, release, reach, subject, route,
Designation, progress, Giving, media, Ministry Update, or Phase-10 authority.

The quiet UX keeps **Approve & publish** and **Request changes** primary in the
review surface. **Edit page** is a secondary action. Before staff supersede
another contributor's active or submitted work, the UI identifies the exact
source and author, says what remains preserved, warns about newer work, and
asks for one short contributor-safe reason. Routine edits to the staff
member's own working revision need neither a takeover modal nor a reason.

Raw content and restricted identity must not enter logs. |

### 47.4 Ruthless adversarial result

The principal risks are critical lost updates, cross-tenant or over-broad staff
authority, accidental review/release bypass, Payload access or lock bypass,
cross-store partial completion, dangling references after version pruning,
fabricated legacy authorship, retry duplication, revocation races, notification
noise, and unbounded history/diff work. The permanent controls are:

1. one immutable successor edge and one coherent working head per exact
   Page-and-locale scope, advanced by expected-head CAS;
2. commit-time reproof of Phase 12 capability, complete scope, lifecycle,
   Phase-10 ceiling, editable-target allowlist, source digest, and head;
3. a private, inert Payload content prepare followed by one short operational
   provenance/head/outbox transaction, with orphan reconciliation rather than
   a false cross-store atomicity claim;
4. request-bound Payload calls with `overrideAccess: false` and
   `overrideLock: false`, plus server-side commands and no browser write path;
5. content-bound idempotency, inspect-before-retry recovery, and one
   notification intent only when a committed staff successor actually
   displaces active or submitted contributor work;
6. retention-pinned semantic revisions, bounded normalized changed-target
   summaries and digests, indexed keyset history, and privacy-safe telemetry;
7. commit-time revocation/retirement rejection while preserving attributed
   history and quarantining unfinished scratch; and
8. migration that classifies unproved legacy actors honestly and removes any
   competing direct-authoring path before cutover.

### 47.5 Ratified hardened contract

**Ratified C-prime-amended-and-hardened (C-prime-R)** is one
attribution-preserving Staff-authored Page Revision path inside D1's sole
working-revision contract. A separately Phase-12-authorized staff Page editor
may deliberately create one immutable successor from the exact current live
release, working revision, or submitted candidate, with source, actor,
authority path, base, displaced work, semantic comparison, and safe takeover
reason preserved. A CAS-guarded commit advances the single Page-and-locale
working head only after current authorization, scope, lifecycle, safety,
profile/catalog, editable-target, source-digest, and expected-head reproof.

The successor remains private and uses D4/D5's existing candidate and review
lane plus D2's sole release authority. It cannot publish, approve, widen reach,
resolve D22 readiness, change a managed operational reference, or bypass Phase 10. Taking over another contributor's active or submitted work is a secondary
consequence-reviewed **Edit page** action; all displaced work stays attributed,
inspectable, and recoverable, and autosaves remain quiet non-authoritative
scratch. Payload stores content and versions only, while the Phase 22 server
boundary, Phase 12 authorization, operational CAS, durable provenance,
idempotent recovery, and retention contract own product truth.

The ratified contract forbids in-place overwrite, destructive restore, head rewind,
silent merge, last-write-wins, a generic staff role, native Payload publication,
browser mutation, a second review queue, branch/merge UI, autosave notifications,
raw-content logging, blind retry, or any claim that edited, saved, reviewed,
approved, released, reachable, notified, or operationally corrected are the
same fact. The exact ratified formulation is authoritative in the Phase 22
decision log and ADR-0141.

D24 is ratified as the exact C-prime-R. D1–D24 are binding, and this evidence
adds no runtime, migration, issue, notification, or production authority.

## 48. Ratified D25 research — cause-gated actionability with bounded, recoverable editorial work

**Status:** The founder ratified the exact adversarially hardened C-prime-R as
Phase 22 D25 on 2026-08-14 after requiring that it not burden the database or
become needlessly complex. D1–D25 are binding planning truth, and this section
grants no implementation, migration, retention, deletion, issue-publication,
notification, or production authority.

### 48.1 Unresolved source requirement

The original Phase 22 prompt's missionary edit-proposal workflow explicitly
requires a decision for an abandoned draft, an old base, a classification
change, and worker departure. The settled decisions cover exact bases,
concurrency, review, safety, release, routes, migration, operations, and
attributed successors, but none establishes the complete lifecycle of work that
never reaches release. Without D25, age, actionability, recovery, evidence
retention, and eventual erasure could collapse into mutable Payload status or an
arbitrary timer.

### 48.4 Database-minimal result

D25 needs no new authoritative persistence:

| Fact class                                                                                                                                  | Correct home                                                   | D25 behavior                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Working head, immutable revision, candidate, review/withdrawal occurrence, release, actor/provenance, digest, idempotency, owner generation | Existing D1/D2/D4/D5/D24 operational truth                     | Read and re-prove; do not copy or reinterpret                                                                                                                  |
| Authored bytes and versions                                                                                                                 | Private Payload store                                          | One coalesced mutable recovery slot beneath the sole head; immutable non-autosave version sealed before a deliberate D1 revision or candidate can reference it |
| Currently permitted actions and one safe cause                                                                                              | Pure server resolver; optionally D22's disposable presentation | Derive at read time; re-prove inside the owning command; never persist as status                                                                               |
| `stale`, `expired`, `archived`, `actionable`, recovery tier, retention class, per-actor branch, expiry timer                                | Nowhere                                                        | Forbidden D25 persistence                                                                                                                                      |

The launch save policy is code-owned, not tenant-configurable: a trailing
two-second dirty-aware debounce, a 15-second maximum wait, explicit **Save
draft**, safe-navigation/editor-handoff flush, digest-based no-op suppression,
one in-flight write per Page/locale/head generation, and late-write fencing.
Unsafe close/navigation keeps visible unsaved input and warns honestly rather
than claiming an unreliable flush. Autosave emits no operational revision,
audit occurrence, outbox event, notification, or activity-feed item. Deliberate
save, submission, decision, withdrawal, and release retain their exact semantic
occurrences.

A candidate can never reference the mutable autosave row. A deliberate command:

1. seals exact editor content as an immutable non-autosave Payload version;
2. normalizes and hashes the content;
3. creates the D1 revision and candidate reference and advances the exact head
   through one idempotent, short CAS-guarded operational command; and
4. leaves a failed pre-commit version structurally inert for bounded orphan
   reconciliation rather than guessing distributed atomicity.

Reference-safe cleanup remains the bounded D24 reconciler, not a second D25
engine. Native blind pruning is disabled for these Page collections. The
reconciler walks small tenant-fair keyset batches, quarantines only scratch or
inert prepares, point-checks that no canonical revision references the exact
version and no ambiguous command may still commit it, then deletes only if proof
remains complete. Unavailable or contradictory proof skips deletion and opens a
private exception. Age may select unreferenced scratch for inspection; it never
changes editorial actionability or proves erasure eligibility.

### 48.5 Action-specific and UX result

One candidate-level **stale** status is incorrect. A source change can prevent
approval while still permitting current-authorized view, request-changes,
rejection, withdrawal, or D24 editing. The resolver therefore answers per
action and the command re-proves the same facts at commit. D22 displays one
source-owned cause; it does not persist or close it.

The recovery action is **Review saved changes**, not **Update and resubmit**.
Recovery opens a current-authorized same-scope successor; the separate existing
D4 action then says **Submit for review** or **Publish changes**. This prevents a
single button from silently combining recovery, submission, review, and
release.

Healthy users see **Saved privately** and a subtle timestamp. Real save failure
stays visible with **Retry saving**. A changed base says:

> **Your earlier changes are saved, but this page has changed since then. Review
> them against the current page before submitting again.**

A staff blocker says:

> **This submission can't be approved yet because the page changed after it was
> submitted. The submitted version is still saved.**

Age alone produces no warning, task, notification, **Needs attention** item, or
queue movement. Old valid candidates remain in **To review** until an existing
D4/D5 decision or explicit withdrawal. Terminal/reference history remains
secondary and permission-filtered.

### 48.6 Adversarial conclusion

All 17 requested categories have a material concern. The binding detailed
review appears in D25 of the decision log. The cross-cutting hazards are:

- a second persisted workflow masquerading as safety;
- one durable draft per actor becoming hidden branches;
- 300 ms shared-Postgres update/log amplification;
- a mutable autosave version becoming a candidate source;
- Payload's blind version cap deleting referenced bytes;
- age creating authority, queue noise, or retention decisions;
- broad invalidation hiding actions that remain independently valid;
- unsafe cross-Page, cross-locale, cross-family, or cross-subject reuse;
- former-contributor or browser-storage disclosure;
- cleanup racing a deliberate submission; and
- UI copy collapsing saved, submitted, approved, released, and public.

The permanent answer is not more database state. It is one coherent head, one
coalesced recovery buffer, immutable deliberate sources, reference-safe bounded
cleanup, action-specific current proof, append-only successor/withdrawal facts,
and a quiet D22 presentation over existing owners.
